molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families acquire useful polar motifs, but reactive bonds, strained-looking bridges and unspecified stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: Node n-0db88abff519 produces recognizable medicinal-chemistry fragments within heavily edited ring systems: indoles with cyano/enamine or amidine groups, acceptor-rich heteroaromatics, aryl-linked saturated amines, cyclic amides and fluorinated carbonyl/imino heterocycles. All five supplied tasks were read; the digest's tasks_without_trajectories list is empty. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Digest ring_closure_rate spans 0.9563 to 0.9782 and aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.954 to 0.9736; these are fractions of strings containing the indicated features, not fractions of atoms or measures of ring diversity. The chemistry has abundant rings and aromatic atoms, with multiple families across seeds but substantial congeneric concentration within them. Passive RDKit inspection of every supplied Child and Parent trajectory gives Child median heavy-atom counts of 25, 34, 30, 34 and 28 in the stated task order. Size changes relative to Parent n-559d25e9c9c7 are mixed, and smaller molecules do not uniformly accompany better recorded endpoints. Plausible motifs coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, thiols, unusual arene bridges, unsaturated small rings and oversized assemblies. All task stereocentre_rate values are 0.0, despite many apparent stereogenic centres. Charged_rate is 0.0 except 0.0011 in the final task; neutral SMILES do not imply an absence of protonatable amines. These are connectivity-based chemical judgments, not measured stability, synthesis, affinity or mechanism activation. Reproducible structural counts, exact observed seed endpoints, input hashes and digest-molecule descriptors are in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-07-improve-L01-molecular.audit.json, generated by the adjacent audit.py with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6 environment. Counts in this report refer to trajectory occurrences, excluding initial molecules unless stated otherwise; ring-size checks use RDKit-perceived rings.

per_task.generated_character: The main products are compact, mostly aromatic indole/aniline relatives, with a median of 25 heavy atoms and digest mean SMILES length 40.9. The best molecule, at 0.4572645941803378, has 24 heavy atoms, an indole NH, a phenyl group, two methoxy substituents, a carbon-bonded nitrile and an exocyclic anilinoalkene. A thiol-substituted alkene analogue reaches 0.4455495560238204. Another leading family combines an N-hydroxy-N-aryl amidine with an unusually bridged aromatic system, reaching 0.4451945621839941. Late seed-2 molecules retain the aromatic/amidine framework but add N-F, N-Cl and halomethyl ethers. This is a real change in functional groups from the Parent: carbon-bonded nitriles occur in 105 Child proposals versus none in the Parent, while the passive amide flag falls from 705 to 46. Both streams retain the same median heavy-atom count. The straightforward substituted-indole connectivity is more synthetically recognizable than the short bridged or heteroatom-halogen variants; no route or stability evidence is supplied.
liabilities: The thiol-bearing alkene, N-hydroxyamidine and exocyclic enamine introduce potential reactivity or tautomeric uncertainty; their scores do not establish storage stability or a synthetic route.
Late N-F/N-Cl substitutions and halomethyl ethers raise chemical stability concerns without surpassing the best simpler indole. The bridged amidine structures also require geometric scrutiny.
Unassigned stereogenic features and unspecified alkene/imine geometry remain in the more elaborate families; the digest contains no stereochemical assignments.
missing_features: The compact aromatic framework and connected polar substituents seen in the leaders are missing from the fragment tail and incompletely preserved in ring-expanded late congeners.

The favorable carbon-bonded cyano/enamine arrangement is absent from the leading amidine family, while the best cyano molecule lacks that family's amidine. The visible scores support alternative heteroatom arrangements and do not identify a further mandatory heterocycle or functional group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Its higher-scoring descendants retain compact aromatic extent while changing the carbonyl-linked functionality to cyano/enamine, thiol-alkene or amidine arrangements. The Child's upper observed score quartile contains only 22-27 heavy atoms; the low tail includes water, ethene and FSSF at 0.0. Removing aromaticity from part of a late amidine framework accompanies a score of 0.09690882872436221. These observations favor a connected, compact aromatic scaffold with suitably placed heteroatoms, not indiscriminate ring addition. Several different bridged amidine connectivities share 0.4451945621839941, so the records do not establish a unique preferred topology. Parent and Child best values remain close in seeds 0 and 1, while seed 2 changes from 0.4484138510190879 to 0.4031937733859023; replacing amides with other nitrogen chemistry is not a uniform score improvement.

per_task.generated_character: This stream consists largely of densely substituted polyheteroaromatics. The best family has a fused aza/oxa carbonyl core joined through sulfur to a phenyl-pyridyl system. The leader has 34 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, two carbon-bonded nitriles, an O-cyanate and a formate ester. Equally scoring congeners substitute thioformate, formate or acetate groups. Other seeds produce bulkier carbonyl-rich fused nitrogen heterocycles with aryl ethers, sulfur-containing chains and extensive halogenated substituents; the final seed-2 examples include 46-47 heavy atoms. Relative to the Parent, mean heavy-atom count falls from 51.13333333333333 to 36.89885057471265 and mean SMILES length from 94.56436781609196 to the digest's rounded 67.2. Nevertheless, 142 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms and the largest contains 113. Recognizable heteroaryl connections coexist with much less routine combinations of cyanates, thioesters, peroxides and heteroatom-halogen bonds.
liabilities: Aryl cyanates and formate/thioformate esters are chemically consequential reactive or hydrolyzable handles, not interchangeable benign decorations. Their stability and synthesis have not been demonstrated.

Late products combine heavy halogenation, multiple carbonyl derivatives and sulfur-containing chains; some contain S-F or O-O connections. Reduced average size still leaves a substantial oversized tail.

The dominant family is highly aromatic and mostly flat; alternative seeds add substantial conformational or topological complexity. Neither drawing style nor RDKit sanitization establishes a practical synthesis.
missing_features: The connected heteroaromatic acceptor arrangement is absent from the low-scoring fragments; abundant heteroatoms alone do not recreate it.

The listed high scorers offer little evidence of a substantially different core that retains the favorable arrangement while replacing the cyanate/formate/thioformate decorations with less reactive chemistry. Their equal scores do not reveal an exact missing decoration or required target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy/cyano polyaryl carbonyl compound scores 0.5418375031378128, whereas the thioaryl-linked, cyano-rich fused family reaches 0.6329826640983849. Tiny C=NOC, FF and other fragments remain at 0.5, showing that this floor is not evidence for useful molecular chemistry. The upper observed quartile has a median of 33 heavy atoms; late larger decorated heterocycles score around 0.595-0.597. The visible gradient therefore associates better scores with an intact acceptor-rich aromatic arrangement, without demonstrating a benefit from repeated appendage growth. Four different cyanate/formate/thioformate/acetate examples have exactly 0.6329826640983849, so their extra chemical liabilities are not distinguished by those values. The best cyano-rich seed rises from its Parent endpoint 0.6199818405862896, but the other Child seed endpoints, 0.5981257463267743 and 0.5965492580010727, are below their corresponding Parent values 0.6092799188640974 and 0.616992140985949.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are aryl-rich amines of moderate size, not nitrogen-poor fragments. The leader at 0.9999991193494832 has 29 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings, a tertiary piperidine, a secondary amine linker, a benzocyclobutene unit, an aryl thiol and carbon-bound fluorine and chlorine. Another leading family contains a bridged diazabicycle, two aryl groups, phenol, methoxy and aminomethyl substituents. These contain recognizable medicinal-chemistry building blocks, although the compact bridged arrangements are more demanding. The overall median is 30 heavy atoms versus 31 for the Parent; digest halogen_rate is 0.992. Late seed-2 output also contains N-chloro/N-bromo derivatives and tiny ClCl or CN(Cl)Cl. N-halogen-containing proposals increase from 82 in the Parent to 223 in the Child. Amine chemistry is already abundant; introducing a basic ring nitrogen cannot be described as a missing general capability here.
liabilities: The leading piperidine/benzocyclobutene molecule has three RDKit-detected unassigned atom stereocentres; the bridged phenol/aminomethyl leader has four. Apparent geometry and stereochemistry need more support than a connectivity-only score.

Aryl thiols and late N-Cl/N-Br groups introduce reactivity concerns. The stream includes both ordinary aryl halides and chemically distinct nitrogen-halogen bonds; they should not be treated as the same kind of fluorination or chlorination.
The benzocyclobutene and cage-like aza ring systems may be synthetically accessible in suitable cases, but no route or conformational feasibility evidence is supplied for these particular products.
missing_features: The low tail lacks the connected aromatic/nonacylated-amine combination present in the high scorers, or masks nitrogen with carbonyl/sulfonyl groups. The high scorers already supply this chemistry, so no additional necessary basic centre is established.

The high-scoring connectivities lack specified configurations and explicitly explored protonation states. Their neutral SMILES can still encode protonatable amines; the records do not show which charge state or stereoisomer would be favored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low-scoring sulfonyl/disulfide fragment scores 0.00024675866379847753, and a carboxylic-acid, amide and N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine product scores 0.0006269216484658979. In contrast, every molecule in the upper observed quartile has an ordinary nonacylated amine structural flag, two aromatic rings and 23-32 heavy atoms. This supports a local preference for connected aryl/amine architecture and accessible amine functionality rather than larger, heavily acylated or sulfonylated assemblies. The nearly saturated scores do not establish a unique linker, thiol requirement, preferred stereoisomer or measured binding affinity. Parent best values 0.9959491085611949 and 0.9964552366323939 become 0.9999951970568197 and 0.9999991193494832 in seeds 0 and 1, while seed 2 changes from 0.9912887882944748 to 0.9697141867217297. The more reactive late amine substitutions do not provide a consistent improvement over the simpler leaders.

per_task.generated_character: Products are nitrogen-rich cyclic amides attached to aromatic groups, with a median of 34 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 56.6. One leading family carries a nine-membered triaza ring with two amide carbonyls, N-methyl substituents and two aryl groups, including an ethoxy-substituted aryl. The best molecule, 0.23402322695167738, has 29 heavy atoms and adds a short oxygen bridge across one arene; the phenol-bearing congener at 0.2338090388900024 has 31 heavy atoms and avoids that bridge. Another leading family, at 0.2339383623102592, has 35 heavy atoms and a fused/bridged nitrogen-rich aromatic framework joined to lactam and amine rings. Late products add further N-N or N-O connections. Compared with the Parent's median of 33 heavy atoms, size changes little, but mean perceived aromatic-ring count increases from 2.1528735632183906 to 2.7333333333333334. The ordinary amides and ethers are plausible fragments; the unusual short bridges and dense polycycles make whole-molecule synthesis much less certain.
liabilities: The short arene oxygen bridge is not an ordinary benzofuran motif. It creates a small constrained cycle whose geometric and synthetic feasibility cannot be inferred from sanitization.
Medium-sized cyclic diamides and densely fused aza/lactam systems can demand difficult cyclizations and stereochemical control; the leading examples leave their detected atom stereocentre unassigned.

Late N-O and additional N-N closures alter chemical roles as well as connectivity. Their presence should be evaluated individually; an N-O bond alone is not proof of instability, but these particular ring assemblies lack route evidence.
missing_features: The low fragments lack connected amide, amine and aromatic features; the favorable families preserve those roles but do not establish a specific missing ring, substitution position or external reference structure.

The supplied leaders do not consistently preserve a simple feasible topology while varying the relative placement of those functional groups. A phenol-bearing example already scores nearly as highly as the short oxygen-bridged structure, leaving no visible requirement for that additional bridge.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, while the cyclic diamide/aryl and bridged lactam/aryl families approach 0.234. Methane, HCN and NOCl are at 0.0. All molecules in the upper observed quartile have an amide-type carbonyl/nitrogen connection and 29-40 heavy atoms, supporting retention of a connected nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic arrangement. The arene oxygen bridge at 0.23402322695167738, the unbridged phenol family at 0.2338090388900024 and the more fused family at 0.2339383623102592 have very similar scores; extra ring complexity is therefore not evidence of a chemically meaningful gain. Parent seed-1's recorded best is 0.24321515648721753, above the corresponding Child value, while seeds 0 and 2 move from 0.22270606177144964 and 0.23035161967494103 to 0.2229315869550826 and 0.2339383623102592. Increased aromatic complexity is not uniformly associated with a better endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by fluorinated carbonyl/imino nitrogen heterocycles, usually retaining a fused aromatic core, with a median of 28 heavy atoms and digest mean SMILES length 53.3. The best molecule at 0.5387819611321613 has 29 heavy atoms: an N-fluorinated imino/lactam core, a fluorinated thiol-containing alkene chain, a substituted cyclobutene and an ester ending in another thiol. Other leaders have phenolic aryl groups, a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring, or a ring-expanded carbonyl-rich heterocycle with aminophenyl and pyrrolyl substituents. These are chemically more unusual than their moderate size alone suggests. Relative to the Parent, proposals with a perceived ring of at most four atoms increase from 91 to 378, and O-halogen-containing molecules from 77 to 231. N-halogen-containing molecules decrease from 534 to 279, so the change shifts liabilities rather than removing them. The leading cyclobutene/thiol structure has three unassigned atom stereocentres.
liabilities: Most leading fused examples contain N-F; the seed-0 leader additionally contains a C(=O)-O-Cl group. These bonds have different reactivity implications from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine and are not validated by a favorable score.

Fluorinated substituted cyclobutenes, unsaturated sulfur rings, multiple thiols and ester handles make stability and synthesis questionable. The increased small-ring frequency is an observed topological change, not proof of useful three-dimensional shape.

Atom configurations and alkene geometry are unspecified in the fluorinated sidechains and small rings. The top examples do not establish which realizable stereoisomer the recorded connectivity represents.
missing_features: The low and oversized products do not consistently preserve the compact carbonyl/nitrogen scaffold and positioned carbon-bound fluorine associated with the higher scores. More heterocycles or more fluorine atoms alone do not establish the same arrangement.

Many favorable structures lack a comparably supported combination of that arrangement with ordinary stable heteroatom bonding and specified stereochemistry. The trajectories do not identify a further required amine, stereoisomer or target-specific scaffold, and they do not show that N-F, O-Cl or a strained small ring is necessary.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: A large repeated heteroaromatic/carbonyl assembly with 53 heavy atoms scores 1.5125441317900776e-37; a 47-heavy-atom indole/carbonyl assembly scores 7.32209661742749e-28. Compact fluorinated families instead reach roughly 0.5, whereas elemental fragments remain extremely poor. The most informative local comparison is the leader's fluorinated thiol sidechain at 0.5387819611321613 versus the otherwise corresponding late sidechain without that carbon-bound fluorine at 0.36175063935602336. This supports a position-sensitive fluorination association within this family, not a general rule that any fluorine bond helps. Replacing the terminal thiol of either the sidechain or ester appendage with fluorine gives the two listed examples at 0.5202350897378943. A ring-expanded example without N-F still reaches 0.5260004789707542, so N-F is not established as necessary across the observed chemistry. Parent endpoints 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.6025252354500499 become 0.5079089834520303, 0.5329941377390867 and 0.5387819611321613; the greater prevalence of small rings does not track a uniform score gain.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Favorable structures coexist with electrophilic N-halogen and O-halogen links. For example, CN(c1ccc(F)c2c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n(C)c12)C1C(F)C=C(C(=O)OCl)SN1F scores 0.5079089834520303 and contains both N-F and acyl O-Cl. COc1c(C)c(OCF)cc2c1cc(C(=NF)Nc1ccccc1)n2Cl scores 0.3785808023129121 and places halogens directly on nitrogen. Elsewhere, the highest listed aryl/piperidine/secondary-amine molecule has ordinary nonacylated amine connections without N-halogen substitution. The output therefore shows access to conventional functionality, but no consistent preservation of it as graphs change; favorable scores alone do not certify these reactive bond types.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve ordinary heteroatom bonding while retaining useful polar functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: General chemical transformations should make it possible to preserve donor/acceptor roles and connected shape while changing reactive heteroatom substitutions into chemically coherent alternatives. Bond-level chemical context must distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens from nitrogen- or oxygen-bound halogens. This is a general stability and accessibility gap; it supplies neither a preferred scaffold nor an assumed objective reward for any replacement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: CCOc1ccccc1N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccc2cc1O2 includes a short oxygen bridge across an arene and scores 0.23402322695167738. The phenol-bearing CCOc1ccc(CC)cc1N1CCN(C)C(=O)CN(C)C(=O)C1c1ccccc1O scores 0.2338090388900024 without that bridge. C=Cc1cc2c3cc(C(=N)N(O)c4ccccc4)n2COc1c3C adds another constrained aromatic bridge at 0.4451945621839941. The fluorinated cyclobutene/thiol leader supplies a different small-ring liability. The digest's high ring_closure_rate documents abundant ring generation, so the missing capability is feasibility and controlled topology, not creating rings at all.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates ring closures without demonstrating that the resulting geometry is chemically realizable or useful.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring modification needs chemically informed closure, opening and simplification options that retain connected functional groups while respecting ring geometry and unsaturation. Assess particular bridges and strained-looking arrangements rather than banning every small or medium ring. The observed near-equal values provide no basis for assuming extra closures are inherently beneficial, and no particular ring size is prescribed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The listed leader CC(CCN1CCCCC1CNC1Cc2cc(Cl)ccc21)c1ccc(F)cc1S has three RDKit-detected unassigned atom stereocentres, and COc1cc(O)cc(CC2c3cc(F)ccc3C34CCC(CN3)N2C4)c1CN has four. Cn1c(=N)n(F)c(=O)c2c(C=CC(F)S)n(C3C=CC3(F)C(=O)OCS)c(F)c21 has three, together with unspecified sidechain alkene geometry. These are actual recorded high-scoring connectivities; the records supply no preferred stereochemical assignments.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical choices unspecified even when its products contain multiple apparent stereogenic features.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information when present and provide consistent, realizable configuration choices when edits create or alter stereogenic atoms or double bonds. Molecular identity should retain those distinctions. The need is to represent the chemical alternatives coherently; usefulness of any isomer must come from available feedback rather than an assumed target answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes late O and FSSF at 0.0, C=NOC and FF at 0.5, and ClCl at 0.007765472974341367. At the opposite size extreme, CCOC(=O)c1ccc(O)c(-n2cc3c(c2C(=O)C2=CC=C(O)C(n4c5c6c(c4c4c5c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n4C)C=CC6)=CC2)c(=O)n(C)c(=O)n3C)c1 has 53 heavy atoms and scores 1.5125441317900776e-37. The same supplied streams contain compact connected leaders with recognizable aromatic, amine or carbonyl roles. Another stream still contains 142 proposals above 50 heavy atoms despite a reduction in its mean size. Tiny fragmentation and redundant molecular growth therefore persist alongside useful bounded molecular families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Structural variation does not consistently maintain a coherent molecular scale and connected set of useful functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make structural variation capable of retaining connected functional roles while changing core connectivity or substituent placement, and provide ways to simplify repeated appendages. General chemical coherence and observed feedback should guide which scale works. The evidence does not justify a universal molecular-weight cutoff, fixed formula, task-specific size target or preferred fragment library.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The reference is DST, the Differentiable Scaffolding Tree of Fu and colleagues, which makes discrete molecular editing differentiable. A molecule is first rewritten as a tree whose nodes are whole substructures, single atoms and intact rings, rather than individual bonds and atoms. The identity of each terminal node, and whether that node exists at all, is then relaxed from a discrete choice into a continuous probability vector, which turns the tree into a smooth object that can be differentiated. A scoring surrogate reads the relaxed tree and its gradient is followed uphill, shifting probability mass toward the substructures the surrogate believes will raise the score. The optimized probabilities are then sampled back down to a discrete tree, and a real molecule is assembled from that tree by choosing attachment atoms and bond orders. The surrogate itself is in two parts: a graph encoder pretrained on unlabeled molecules by predicting masked-out substructures and frozen thereafter, plus a small linear readout refitted on the objective's own scored observations after every batch of feedback.
approach.novelty: Being a root, its commitments are the concrete form it gives that idea. Published versions of this method assume a surrogate trained on a large pool of already-scored molecules, which is unavailable here, so this node splits the surrogate in two: an encoder learned only from unlabeled structure and frozen, and a small ridge readout carrying all the task-specific signal, refitted from as few as ten labels and updated after each batch. It restricts each optimization to at most two terminal substitutions and two expansion sites and holds the interior of the starting molecule fixed, which guarantees a chemically intact product but also bounds how far any single proposal can travel from where it began. Starting molecules are drawn from the scored archive with an exponential preference for high rank rather than greedily. Twenty-two gradient steps are taken per optimization under one frozen surrogate version, so the target does not move underneath the ascent, and the diversity-selection objective of the original published method is deliberately not imported.

nodes.hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained masked-substructure graph encoder, fit a regularized linear readout to current-task accepted scores, ascend that fixed surrogate through relaxed leaf identities and leaf/expansion existence variables of observed molecules' scaffolding trees, and stochastically sample and assemble new structures from the optimized variables while preserving their internal scaffold context.

finding_summary.headline: Mid-field at 0.3619: the structural gradients ran cleanly and pointed the wrong way on average
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now knows that this style of surrogate-gradient construction executes faithfully at this budget, and that the surrogate is systematically optimistic. It is fitted in sample to a few hundred points, it is ascended to a strictly higher prediction every single time, and the molecules assembled from that ascent still average worse than the molecules they were built from. The failure is not in the gradient step, which is verified, but in the two lossy translations after it: from relaxed probabilities to a sampled tree, and from a tree to an assembled molecule, where roughly a quarter of attempts fail outright. At 0.3619 against a field spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits well clear of the undirected search methods and well short of the leader, which suggests that a learned model of structure is worth having but that a point estimate with no uncertainty is the wrong thing to ascend, since ascent drives proposals precisely into the region where the fit extrapolates worst. What stays open is whether calibrating the readout, with a posterior rather than a point prediction or an explicit penalty for distance from the fitted data, would close the optimism gap, and whether the fixed-interior constraint that keeps the chemistry clean is also what caps the score.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.361872161920233 on the single screening seed, placing this root in the middle of the thirteen-root field. Per objective: 0.5890616392238477, 0.42602011617052177, 0.380138751942517, 0.23408968632790841 and 0.18005061593636776. Every observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. Masked-substructure pretraining cut held-out loss from 5.444202465850716 to 0.9686623942998355 over 30000 steps, publishing the checkpoint at step 27000. All 150 readout fits used only prior same-objective observations, growing from 10 to 300 records. All 175 structural optimizations ended with a surrogate prediction strictly above their own starting relaxation, with all four gradient families active at every one of the 3850 steps. From 6268 sampled trees, 1450 valid novel context-preserving molecules were assembled; the remainder were 3712 duplicates and 1106 failed assemblies, of which 732 had no compatible attachment point and 374 failed kekulization. The result the run turns on is the transfer gap: 380 of 1450 proposals beat their generating source, but the mean actual score change relative to that source was negative on all five objectives, ranging from -0.00180775181701 to -0.108386772041, while the surrogate's relaxed gain was positive throughout. Predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time, and chronological prediction error reached 0.135969779 on the worst objective against an in-sample residual of 0.0515970171356 on the same one.

molecular.headline: Clean, fully ring-bearing drug-like chemistry that never leaves the scaffolds it was handed
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically respectable output of the three nodes examined. Every single proposal on every objective contains a ring closure and essentially all contain aromatic atoms, with a ring closure rate of 1.0 and aromatic rate of 0.986 to 1.0 across the five sets, no cumulated double bonds anywhere, and molecules of ordinary size at mean SMILES lengths of 41 to 80. The recurring pieces are real medicinal chemistry: quinolines, indoles, oxadiazoles, tetrazoles, piperazines, morpholines, pyrimidines and aryl amides. The cost of that cleanliness is visible in the same molecules. Because the interior of the starting structure is held fixed and only terminal units are edited, each objective's whole trajectory orbits the scaffolds present in the ten supplied starting molecules, so the top-scoring sets read as decoration series rather than as searches. Stereocentres are absent throughout, and a recurring set of reagent-grade functional groups shows the substructure alphabet carries no notion of stability.

per_task.generated_character: A single elaborated core: a methylated pyrimidinedione fused to a pyrrole, N-linked to a benzoate ester and carrying an oxadiazolyl ether, decorated with pyridines, pyrimidines and thiophenes. It is a direct elaboration of one of the supplied starting molecules.
liabilities: an anionic phenolate carried as a scoring feature inside the top-scoring entries
formaldehyde-acetal OCO fragments appearing in the low-scoring entries
densely fused biaryl-on-biaryl decoration pushing molecules past 100 SMILES characters
missing_features: a scaffold hop away from the elaborated core, which the fixed-interior rule forbids by construction
saturated linkers that would break the near-planar all-aromatic character of the whole series
defined stereochemistry at the few sp3 centres the series does contain
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole top twelve sits in a 0.003 band from 0.5863 to 0.5890616392238477 against a starting best of 0.548381482770623, so the gradient is genuinely being followed but into an extremely flat region. What separates the top from the 0.534 to 0.540 bottom is the oxadiazole ether and the N-aryl substitution; the low entries are the plain methoxy-indole carboxanilide with only small oxygen decorations.

per_task.generated_character: A dichlorophenyl sulfenamide on a proline-like pyrrolidine, joined through an aminal carbon to a morpholine or thiomorpholine and to a biaryl aniline. The halogen rate on this objective is 0.9828, so essentially every molecule carries chlorine or bromine.
liabilities: acid chlorides carried through most of the top twelve, which are reagents rather than compounds
sulfenamide S-N bonds as the load-bearing feature of the entire top-scoring family
aminal carbons bearing two nitrogens, which are hydrolytically unstable
a fluoromethyl ether decoration appearing on the highest-scoring entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces whatever the S-N linkage is contributing to the score
an ordinary secondary or tertiary amine of the kind this target class rewards, in place of the aminal
defined stereochemistry, though the pyrrolidine and benzylic centres here are real stereocentres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single largest jump in the set comes from adding one thiol to the dichlorophenyl ring, taking 0.38644405836045415 to 0.42602011617052177. Across the top twelve the pattern is aryl halide plus S-N linkage plus a basic saturated amine ring. The lowest entries are the sulfonamide versions of the same molecules, which is telling: replacing the S-N sulfenamide with a proper sulfonamide costs more than an order of magnitude.

per_task.generated_character: A 4,5-dihydropyrazole bearing a furyloxy-phenyl group and an aminomethyl link to a pyridine or pyrimidine. Compact molecules at a mean SMILES length of 41.4, all ring-bearing and all containing aromatic atoms.
liabilities: free thiol and free aryl iodide substituents introduced as terminal decorations
a bare phosphorus substituent on nitrogen in one of the final proposals
an N-Cl bond appearing in another of the final proposals
one top-scoring entry carries a cumulated allene, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: polar solubilising groups anywhere on the scaffold, absent from the entire series
an aromatic five-membered ring in place of the partially saturated pyrazoline core
defined stereochemistry at the pyrazoline sp3 carbon, which is a genuine stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The furan-2-yloxy phenyl on the pyrazoline is fixed across the entire top twelve, so the whole gradient runs through the small amine cap: a pyridyl aminomethyl reaches 0.377 to 0.380 while a piperidine, morpholine or plain phenyl cap on the identical scaffold collapses to 1e-5 or below. That is an unusually sharp cliff for a single-group change, and the search found the right side of it early and then stopped moving.

per_task.generated_character: A tight decoration series on one supplied starting molecule: a methylquinoline benzyl ether linked to the anilide of an N-methylpiperidine carboxamide, with an added imidazolidine ring on the aniline. Every top entry shares that exact skeleton.
liabilities: an aliphatic aldehyde as the highest-scoring terminal group, reactive and metabolically labile
N-hydroxy piperidines appearing in the low-scoring entries
methylthio ether decorations appearing on the late proposals
missing_features: a second scaffold family, which the fixed-interior constraint prevents this generator from reaching
carboxylic acid or other strongly polar termini, absent from the entire series
defined stereochemistry at the two substituted piperidine ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top twelve span 0.1749 to 0.18005061593636776, a 0.005 band, and the best is only 0.013 above the best supplied starting molecule at 0.1678386594791329. What moves the score is the small terminal group on the piperidine, aldehyde or acetyl or primary amide, together with the added imidazolidine on the aniline; entries lacking that added ring sit at 0.118.

per_task.generated_character: Methoxy-indole carboxamides derived from a supplied starting molecule, decorated with aziridinyloxy groups, fluorines and small azoles. The score span is extreme, best 0.23408968632790841 against a median of 9e-06, so the overwhelming majority of proposals are effectively zero.
liabilities: a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen in the single best-scoring molecule, not a medicinal chemistry substituent
N-O aziridine ethers recurring through the top-scoring entries
peroxide linkages present in every one of the final six proposals
aminal carbons replacing the amide throughout the terminal cohort
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry this class of objective rewards
an amide or other stable connectivity retained through the late proposals instead of an aminal
defined stereochemistry, which this class of objective is built around
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single best molecule differs from its neighbours mainly by a trimethylsilyl group on the anilide nitrogen, which reads far more like the objective being gamed than like real signal. Below it, entries that keep the indole-2-carboxamide intact score 0.07 to 0.19; once the amide is replaced by an aminal carbon the scores fall to 1e-13 and below, and that is exactly where the whole final cohort ends up.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimization holds the interior of a starting molecule fixed and edits at most two terminal units and two expansion sites, and every objective's top-scoring set is a decoration series on one of the ten supplied starting scaffolds, in one case spanning as little as 0.003 in score across twelve entries.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can only decorate the structures it is given; it cannot originate a core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator built this way is bounded by whatever chemistry it was seeded with, and the cleanliness of its output is bought with that bound. It would need an operation that replaces or rebuilds interior substructure, or a route to assemble a molecule from primitives with no starting structure at all, before it could reach a scaffold nobody handed it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 175 structural optimizations ended above their own starting relaxed prediction, yet the mean actual score change relative to the generating molecule was negative on all five objectives, and predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time.
transferable_gaps.gap: The learned score model is systematically optimistic about its own edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ascending a point-estimate surrogate fitted to a few hundred labels drives proposals precisely into the region where it extrapolates worst, so the ascent is self-defeating. A generator needs the surrogate to carry uncertainty and to pay a cost for distance from its fitted data, so the ascent stops where the model stops knowing anything.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 6268 sampled trees, 1106 failed assembly, 732 of them with no compatible attachment point and 374 failing kekulization, and a further 3712 were duplicates, leaving 1450 usable proposals from all that effort.
transferable_gaps.gap: A quarter of everything the optimizer designs cannot be built into a molecule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The relaxed representation is not closed under assembly: it can place substructures that the attachment rules then reject. A generator should make attachment compatibility and aromatic ring closure part of the space being optimized, so that gradient effort is never spent on trees that cannot become molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Acid chlorides, sulfenamide S-N bonds, aminal carbons, N-O aziridine ethers, peroxide linkages and a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen all appear among the highest-scoring molecules, several of them as the load-bearing feature of an entire top-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reagent-grade reactive functionality is proposed as if it were finished substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substructure alphabet was learned from unlabeled corpus statistics and carries no notion of stability or synthetic accessibility, so an unstable primitive that happens to score gets refitted into the readout and then reinforced. A generator needs those primitives filtered, or the assembled molecule screened, before a proposal is allowed to spend an evaluation and enter the archive it is later fitted on.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across all 1450 proposals on all five objectives, while the emitted molecules routinely contain substituted pyrrolidines, piperidines and pyrazolines whose ring carbons are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configuration is never expressed in any proposal.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The tree representation encodes substructure identity and connectivity but not configuration, so stereochemistry cannot be proposed, optimized or even represented in the relaxation. A generator addressing shape-sensitive properties would need stereo as a variable inside the continuous relaxation, not merely as a tag on the final string.

nodes.method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by drawing atom, bond, path and ring edits, normalizing their molecular identities, and directly evaluating the first full batch allowed by inverse-motif memory. Both inverse signs from the same selected transition must match to veto a fresh neighbor. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score is worse, and a separate archive retains the best score. The current deletion choices remove one leaf atom or contract one degree-two atom, so removal of a longer pendant substituent requires several separately evaluated transitions. Identity normalization, memory lifetime and accepted-score selection are already established parts of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing deletion menu with a whole pendant-branch choice. When the deletion operator is drawn, it may remove an entire acyclic substituent attached through one single bond to a ring atom, while retaining every ring atom and the connections among retained atoms. Single-leaf choices remain in the same menu, and the operator keeps its existing allocation weight. This adds direct compact neighbors that no existing one-step removal can reach. The earlier sulfur sibling filtered local valence; this experiment changes the size of a permitted deletion and does not inherit or add that filter.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the Parent's existing uniformly sampled leaf-deletion menu with whole multi-atom acyclic branches attached by one non-ring single bond directly to a ring atom, so the same deletion-operator allocation can emit a compact neighbor in one edit while retaining the complete ring framework.

finding_summary.headline: Whole-branch deletion produced compact neighbors, but every score replica regressed.
finding_summary.insights:
A lack of eligible branches was not the bottleneck: the Parent already had branch opportunities in 399 of 435 states, and the extension successfully turned such opportunities into new evaluated neighbors. The added prunings usually lost source score, rarely won their batch and were followed by regrowth whenever selected. Those observations help explain why immediate reductions of several atoms did not produce a lasting shift toward smaller sampled molecules under the unchanged accepted-score walk.

The experiment separates direct access to compact analogues from retaining useful score. Its complete method loses score in every seed, although that loss cannot be assigned solely to the pruned candidates because the changed menu also changes later sampling and trajectories. The molecular assessment remains dominated by sulfur-rich polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds and unresolved ring geometry and stereochemistry. Ring-preserving removal alone does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results:
The expanded menu was available in 391 of 435 actual batch-start states. It selected 83 whole-branch edits, all graph-valid; after seven duplicate exclusions and seven tabu vetoes, 69 prunings reached evaluation. Each removed 2-14 heavy atoms in one step, averaging 3.75 atoms and 2.10 rotatable bonds, while retaining every ring atom and bond. The recorded menus, uniform selection, graph edits and identity joins passed the audit, including exact original behavior in all 55 deletion draws where no added branch was available.

Eight of the 69 evaluated prunings beat their source, and four became the next current state. All four later grew again. Typical emitted size remained essentially unchanged at 33.21 heavy atoms, compared with 33.20 for Parent. All three seeds completed their five 300-evaluation tasks; sampling cost was also similar at 12.14 versus 12.15 attempts per ten-member batch.

Mean macro final Top-1 fell from 0.520918 to 0.456635, a paired mean change of -0.064283. The three seed changes were -0.020009, -0.101316 and -0.071524. Every task mean declined, with the largest losses in DRD2 and sitagliptin. The intended neighborhood expansion and immediate size reduction occurred, while the score-retention hypothesis failed on the supplied panel.

molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich polycycles and reactive heteroatom bonds persist despite some recognizable aromatic amide families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete corresponding Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7322 to 1.0, while charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These counters indicate SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, measured basicity or feasible stereochemistry. The output remains chemically close in broad character to the Parent: compact fused aromatic carbonyl compounds, large decorated nitrogen heterocycles, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl systems and sulfur-rich cages. Several seeds change detailed scaffolds, giving moderate diversity across the panel, but each late trajectory mainly varies a related family. The more conventional indole or aza-indole amides coexist with multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, sulfur-carbon triple bonds, N-Cl/N-F/O-F bonds, peroxides and extensive constrained ring closure. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor and drug-like quality weak; recognizable fragments do not make these complete structures accessible. Score changes differ across seeds and do not consistently accompany a move toward more conventional chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family contains moderately sized fused aza-aromatic amides or thioesters, with ethyl/methyl groups, hydroxymethylthio or bromomethylthio substituents and N-Cl on the fused pyrrolic nitrogen. More conventional indole carboxamide and thioester relatives also score well. Other seeds move into bridged thione/amine systems or unsaturated sulfur-rich frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9678 and halogen presence is 0.8678. Compared with the Parent's indole, benzofuran N-chloroamide and aryl-ketone families, the current high region preserves compact fused aromatic/carbonyl arrangements while changing ring nitrogen and sulfur linkages. Whole-molecule plausibility is compromised by N-Cl, O-F, N-O and unusual sulfur chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl, O-F, bromomethylthio and thioester groups create reactivity or stability concerns in otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffolds.
Late multiply bonded sulfur and dense bridged thione/amine structures have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable amide and thioester alternatives preserving the favorable fused aromatic arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, O-halogen and N-O substitutions.
Accessible alternatives to the late bridged or sulfur-rich ring systems and explicit configurations where stereocentres arise are absent from the shown high/final series.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-chloro aza-aromatic fluoroanilide scores 0.42749549733373915 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.39905049777278273. Its nonfluorinated anilide relative scores 0.4103264278932849. An indole thioester and corresponding amide score 0.404945686740228 and 0.39004142494831223, respectively, showing a favorable region without N-Cl on that indole. In contrast, disrupting the carbonyl into a hydroxyalkyl thioether gives 0.04016039186228654, and an expanded partially saturated ring system scores 0.016326676663027142. Compact aromatic/carbonyl placement appears favorable, while reactive N-Cl is not demonstrated to be universally necessary. The other current seeds do not improve over their paired Parent maxima.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-2 molecules are very large substituted fused nitrogen diones linked to sulfur/nitrogen-rich heterocycles. They carry a long brominated polyene or imine-containing side chain, an alkyl-S-O-CH2 substituent, propyl and fluoroalkyl groups. Other seeds generate related diones with polyamines and N-Cl, or expanded nitrogen heterocycles with thioesters, imines and cyclic alkynes. Aromatic-token presence is 1.0 and mean SMILES length is 73.5, consistent with visibly extensive substitution but not itself a size descriptor. This resembles the Parent's heavily decorated heterocyclic chemistry; the latest structures remain difficult complete synthetic targets with labile heteroatom combinations and extensive flexibility.
liabilities: Long halo-polyene chains, imines, thioesters and S-O/N-S combinations add flexibility, reactivity and chemical-compatibility concerns.
Expanded or highly constrained heterocycles and unspecified fluoroalkyl stereochemistry reduce confidence in accessible molecular shape.
missing_features: Compact stable versions of the favorable heterocyclic arrangement are poorly represented among the late, extensively decorated molecules.
Conventional replacements for the alkyl-S-O linkage, reactive imine/haloalkene combinations and unusual heteroaromatic ring arrangements remain underexplored.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-2 molecule scores 0.5966573573049399, below the paired Parent maximum of 0.6092182584436399; the other paired current maxima are also lower. Early altered imino/carbonyl or sulfur-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.528153827722535. A substantially smaller related heterocycle without the long halo-polyene side chain still scores 0.5940462840248751, so extensive growth is not shown to be necessary. Multiple alkyl and fluoroalkyl variants tie at 0.5926433232056583. Disrupting the peripheral aromatic heterocycle into the final expanded N/S ring lowers the score to 0.5373314793543317. Retained heterocyclic arrangement appears more consistently important than the precise long substituents.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leaders combine halogenated aromatic rings, methoxy or methylthio substitution, an aminomethyl-substituted aziridine, and a small nitrogen/sulfur ring containing a sulfur-carbon triple bond. Additional sulfur centres carry sulfur-sulfur or sulfur-carbon double bonds with further substituents. Every proposal contains aromatic, halogen and ring-closure tokens. Seeds 1 and 2 instead reach other bulky aromatic amine/sulfur assemblies, including dense bridged N/S cages. Relative to the Parent's already unusual sulfur/amine frameworks, the high seed-0 chemistry preserves the aromatic/basic-amine pattern but intensifies sulfur-valence and ring-strain concerns. These are highly implausible complete synthetic targets, despite recognizable aryl and amine fragments.
liabilities: A sulfur-carbon triple bond in a small ring, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding raise severe stability and geometry concerns.
Aziridine strain, unspecified substituted-ring stereochemistry and bulky halogenated aromatic surfaces further limit drug-like plausibility.
missing_features: Stable, conventionally bonded realizations of the favorable aromatic/basic-amine spacing are missing from the displayed high-scoring family.
Less strained saturated-ring alternatives with explicit configurations are underrepresented; neutral SMILES alone do not establish relevant amine protonation.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The sulfur-triple-bond/aziridine family reaches 0.9296093497966158 versus the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.8856242185485628. Methoxy versus methylthio and fluoromethyl versus chloromethyl versions share 0.9296093497966158. Increasing the aziridine ring size yields a related molecule at 0.9063259998534903. Early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives remain low, including 0.007468397818197266. The observations support a later aromatic/amine arrangement but do not establish that the extraordinary sulfur bonding is chemically useful. Current seeds 1 and 2 reach lower maxima than their paired Parent trajectories and end in different sulfur-rich families.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 gives moderately large, heavily bridged carbonyl compounds with aza-aromatic and ethoxyphenyl rings, a cyclic carbamate or lactam, hydroxyl-bearing junctions and an oxygen-rich macrocyclic bridge. These are more recognizable than the sulfur-rich final seed-2 cages, which contain N-O, N-N and unusual hydroxylated hydrogen-bearing sulfur. Seed 1 also explores cyclic cumulated unsaturation and peroxide-containing relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9586, ring-closure presence is 1.0 and cumulated-double-bond presence is 0.1471. Compared with the Parent bridged N-O/carbonyl families, ring and heteroatom elaboration persists rather than yielding clearly simpler chemistry.
liabilities: Macrocyclic closure, hydroxyl-bearing ring junctions and constrained unsaturation leave strain and stereochemical feasibility unresolved.
Peroxide motifs and dense N/O/S networks add potential instability without consistently favorable scores.
missing_features: Accessible simpler ring systems preserving the aromatic/carbamate arrangement are underexplored relative to elaborate macrocyclic and bridged alternatives.
Stable replacements for peroxide, N-O/N-N and unusual sulfur linkages, together with defined ring-junction configurations, are absent from much of the late output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best bridged aza-aromatic carbamate scores 0.20739224495838143, close to but below the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.2107445781802027. A less extensively bridged aryl cyclic-carbamate relative already scores 0.2038246232140464. Ring-opened or polyene/peroxide variants score 0.12532962632028227 and 0.1317529051523964. Retaining aromatic surfaces with a constrained carbonyl-containing arrangement appears favorable. The final N/O/S-rich bridged family remains near 0.17, including 0.17660664388632322, and shows no clear benefit from the additional heteroatom complexity. The score range does not isolate a unique missing target fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecules are compact nonaromatic sulfur-rich cages with ketone or lactone, aldehyde, N-fluoroamidine/cyclic urea-like functionality and multiple constrained sulfur-carbon bonds. Related high products include sulfur imine functionality, thiols and small unsaturated sulfur rings. Seeds 0 and 1 also contain densely fused sulfur/carbonyl cages, sometimes partly aromatic. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7322 over the whole panel, but the displayed leaders themselves lack aromatic atoms in their SMILES graphs. Compared with the Parent, detailed ring connections and halogen placement change while unusual sulfur valence, reactive N-F and unspecified stereochemistry remain prominent. The complete structures have very poor apparent synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur, constrained small sulfur rings and dense cage junctions create severe chemical and geometric concerns.
N-F, aldehyde and reactive sulfur functionality coexist without stereochemical specification or evidence of whole-molecule synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Stable conventional frameworks retaining the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement without multiply bonded sulfur cages are not demonstrated among the leaders.
Chemically less reactive alternatives to the N-F/aldehyde combination and explicit configurations at cage junctions are absent from the shown comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-2 cage scores 0.4547680704346094 versus 0.4484554129767839 for its paired Parent; current seeds 0 and 1 have lower maxima than their Parents. The low sulfur/carbonyl cage at 4.906706964908493e-09 shows that sulfur-rich complexity alone is insufficient. In the final family, a related lactone-containing cage scores 0.06842623585263305, whereas the ketone/sulfide arrangement reaches the maximum. Changing the N-fluoroamidine connection gives 0.10586430855837528 or 0.1578665537398357. Local carbonyl, nitrogen and ring connectivity therefore matters strongly, but the evidence does not show a stable accessible realization of that favorable arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes a sulfur-carbon triple bond in a small ring, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Methoxy/methylthio and fluoromethyl/chloromethyl variants of the same sulfur-rich family tie at 0.9296093497966158, while sulfur-rich cage complexity also occurs at very low scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still produces high-scoring molecular arrangements through highly unconventional sulfur bonding.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide ordinary carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur linkages that preserve existing attachment geometry, and distinguish chemical feasibility from scalar-score agreement. Stable counterparts of the favorable aromatic/amine and carbonyl arrangements are a general generator capability still missing from these leaders.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High or final digest molecules contain N-Cl, N-F, O-F, peroxide, alkyl-S-O and dense N-O/N-N networks. An indole thioester at 0.404945686740228 and its amide counterpart at 0.39004142494831223 show that more conventional carbonyl linkages can already reach part of the favorable region.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reactive nitrogen, oxygen and sulfur linkages remain entangled with otherwise recognizable aromatic carbonyl chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand stable matched alternatives around recurring carbonyl and heteroaromatic attachment patterns, while representing reactive-bond and functional-group compatibility independently. Avoid equating familiar individual fragments with a stable complete molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure presence is 1.0 and stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 in every digest. The leaders include substituted aziridines, hydroxyl-bearing macrocyclic junctions and dense sulfur cages, while cumulated-double-bond presence reaches 0.1471 in one proposal set.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits abundant ring closures without resolving three-dimensional feasibility or stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make accessible ring sizes and less constrained fused or spiro alternatives available, with consistent configuration assignment and stereoisomer variation where applicable. Score sensitivity to those configurations cannot be inferred from the present unspecified structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A decorated heterocycle reaches 0.5966573573049399 while a substantially smaller related molecule reaches 0.5940462840248751. A bridged aromatic carbamate at 0.20739224495838143 has a less elaborated relative at 0.2038246232140464. Multiple alkyl/fluoroalkyl variants share 0.5926433232056583.
transferable_gaps.gap: Large side chains and increasingly elaborate ring systems are sampled more extensively than chemically simpler alternatives with comparable observed scores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate compact substituents, fewer ring connections and simpler linkers around the existing favorable arrangements. This would expose stable accessible chemistry within score-tolerant regions rather than concentrating late proposals on additional molecular complexity.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates direct molecular sampling from a task-local neural flow policy with two rounds of graph crossover and mutation. It learns from the exact token trajectories and real scores of accepted molecules through trajectory balance, a jointly learned normalizer and regularization toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. Accepted graph discoveries re-enter the same replay archive. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior selects which fresh graph offspring receive evaluations while retaining the first fresh-policy handoff. Its reusable prior is chosen along the unchanged unlabeled training trajectory by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique molecular yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. Online replay currently samples the full accepted archive by global score rank.
approach.novelty: Add a scaffold-balanced mixture to accepted trajectory replay: keep half of each trajectory's original rank probability and allocate the other half equally among available core families, preserving rank preference within each family. This changes which genuine accepted trajectories train the policy, with every accepted label and exact serialization retained. The lineage's other children changed prior preparation or graph posterior selection; none changed replay allocation. Other campaign experiments balanced breeding parents or survivor populations and lost score despite broader core use. This experiment tests a different path, the distribution of neural learning credit over the full accepted archive, and explicitly checks later policy behavior rather than treating extra scaffold counts as success.

nodes.hypothesis: Sample accepted trajectory-balance replay from an equal mixture of inherited score-rank probabilities and uniform scaffold-group mass with the inherited conditional rank probabilities preserved within each group.

finding_summary.headline: Scaffold-balanced replay broadened learning exposure and reached the policy, while completed-seed endpoints worsened
finding_summary.insights: Extra archive coverage did reach neural learning and subsequent sampling, so the result rules out a purely cosmetic entropy increase. It also exposes the allocation tradeoff: on the same accepted histories the mixture cuts expected graph-origin mass from 72.53% to 59.12% and reduces high-score rank emphasis, while giving much more replay to lower-ranked policy and initial records. Some transfer measures and average policy scores improve, yet those changes coexist with fewer novel raw candidates and weaker completed-seed best results. Broad replay therefore does not establish better endpoint search. The chemical assessment reinforces the distinction: plausible cyclic amines coexist with peroxide, N-halogen and constrained unsaturated-ring families, so family breadth does not certify useful functional context. The terminal failure is a separate inherited canonicalization weakness exposed by one emitted molecule; it explains the missing third formal score and does not explain the losses in the two successful seeds. A complete three-seed score-benefit conclusion remains unavailable.
finding_summary.results: The declared replay mixture ran in all 449 executed feedback states. Actual distinct scaffold groups per 32-member update rose from 17.87 to 23.26, with broader exposure in all fifteen task sessions. Graph-origin replay received less probability, but its average sampled trajectory log-probability increase rose slightly from 0.169 to 0.176 nats and more later policy emissions occupied previously trained graph families. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.205 to 0.238. This did not improve every output measure: raw valid-novel yield fell from 66.59% to 64.74%, duplicates increased, and emitted scaffold coverage narrowed slightly. Both formally successful seed endpoints fell, by 0.02618 and 0.06224. The third seed completed its oracle calls but failed on the final canonical-identity feedback join, leaving its formal macro score unavailable.
