per_task.generated_character: The pooled leaders are seed-1 aminoquinazoline-like structures bearing an oxygen-fluorine substituent and peroxide, peroxyhalogen or oxygen/sulfur attachments. Their aryl partner contains an extra short closure across the nominal aromatic framework; RDKit identifies two four-membered rings in the leading 23-heavy-atom molecule, alongside the two six-membered aza-aromatic rings. This is not an ordinary phenyl-substituted quinazoline despite the familiar-looking aromatic SMILES. A separate high example has a more conventional substituted aminoquinazoline/aryl-ether framework with a thiophene-linked oxime ether. Other seeds explore larger nitro-containing heteroaromatic assemblies. The child median is 38 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with 36 and four in the Parent, and 177 of 870 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals. Parent high families also combined aminoheteroaromatics and carbonyl/imine linkers, but the new leading neighborhood prominently exhibits peroxide/O–F and short-ring chemistry.
liabilities: O–O single bonds occur in 66 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals; O–halogen bonds occur in 54 versus seven. Leading cited molecules directly contain O–F and O–O–halogen connections.

The high family with two four-membered rings formed by a short aromatic-framework closure has major geometric and synthetic questions. Ring-closure markers alone do not establish conventional aromatic ring systems.

The full set includes very large linked molecules, reaching 114 heavy atoms. Their extensive aromatic/heteroaromatic assembly and charged groups leave physical-property balance and synthesis unestablished.
missing_features: Matched, synthetically credible alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/donor/aryl arrangement are not established for the leading peroxide/short-ring family. A different conventional high example shows that the upper score region is not restricted to that problematic connectivity.
Controlled independent changes to linker geometry, ring size and peripheral oxygen functionality are underrepresented among the near-identical leaders.

The output does not demonstrate a uniquely missing target functional group. Its visible limitation is chemically credible realization of useful arrangements, rather than a general shortage of heteroaromatics.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains a diaryl fused nitrogen/carbonyl framework whose dicarbonyl-ring nitrogen is connected through an N–N bond to N-methylpiperazine. Methoxy, isopropyl, aldehyde and extra ring-fusion variants decorate the aromatic portion. The leader has 37 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered carbonyl-containing ring. per_task.generated_character: Two quite different families occupy the upper digest. Seed 1 produces an N-methylaminomethyl-substituted azetidine attached through its nitrogen to a fluorinated, partly saturated fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocyclic network; the leader has 25 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited structures near 0.8796240145542753 combine O–F, peroxide or peroxyhalogen functionality with a useful aminoaza-aromatic framework; a more conventional oxime-ether/aryl-ether example reaches 0.8713274281080406. Elsewhere, high families include hydroxyallenes, dicarbonyl N–N attachments and multiple thionoesters. C=S functionality occurs in 209 of 870 proposals in one set versus 32 Parent proposals. Favorable observations thus coexist with chemically sensitive alternatives, without establishing those alternatives as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible functional-group bonding within favorable molecular neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent functional-group alternatives that preserve useful surrounding aryl, donor, acceptor and amine relationships. Distinguish carbonyl from thionocarbonyl, ordinary ether from peroxide or O–halogen, and carbon-linked amines from N–N or N–O attachments. Use current-session accepted feedback to compare actual alternatives rather than equating parser validity or a high score with chemical persistence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aminoaza-aromatic leader contains two four-membered rings produced by a short closure across its aryl partner. Other high examples include an azetidine with a fluorinated polyheterocyclic attachment, a bridged pyrrole/tertiary-amine core and rearranged carbonyl-ring systems. Every digest gives stereocentre_rate 0.0; unassigned centres occur in 196 of 690 observed first-task proposals and 180, 608, 501 and 441 of 870 proposals in the remaining sets, with assigned centres in none.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring topology and stereochemical representation do not provide adequate control of the geometry of complex output.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support credible ring closure, expansion and contraction together with explicit configurations for existing stereogenic centres. Keep geometry, saturation and connectivity changes distinguishable so accepted feedback can evaluate defined chemical alternatives. The current absence of specification does not establish a benefit for any chosen configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited low tails include methane, dihalogen/peroxide fragments, a cyclic peroxide and long polyene or polar assemblies. One complete set has 177 of 870 proposals above 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals and reaches 114 heavy atoms. Yet smaller carbonyl/piperazine examples can sit near much larger relatives in another upper tail, and some larger heteroaromatics are favorable. The evidence therefore supports context-dependent useful size rather than a universal small-molecule rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some size-changing proposals fragment away or overbuild useful connected molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent accepted core and its useful local polar-group arrangement. Avoid relying on tiny fragments or repeated assembly of whole motifs, and let accepted observations determine the appropriate complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest repeatedly revisits hydroxyallene/heteroaryl amines, aminoaza-aromatic peroxide/short-ring variants, bridged aryl amines, dicarbonyl/piperazine assemblies and aminomethyl or thionoester-rich heterocycles. Different seeds access different families, but much of each upper neighborhood changes peripheral atoms or ring closures. Nonchiral Murcko counts in the four fully covered child sets are 713, 523, 702 and 545; such graph counts include local edits and highly elaborated assemblies, and the partially observed first set cannot be treated as full-panel coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful core diversity remains uneven within the leading neighborhoods despite a varied overall ring repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted chemical families and enable core replacements that retain useful spatial and electronic relationships among aromatic groups, amines, donors and acceptors. Assess core and functional-group diversity directly rather than relying on a new string, peripheral decoration or an additional ring closure as evidence of a useful new family.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent constructs fresh graph-edited offspring from accepted scored parents, then uses an accepted-feedback fingerprint Gaussian process and correlated posterior draws to select each batch. Candidate strings also serve as the keys for temporary uniqueness, emitted exclusions and matching later scores. Its graph checker returns a reparsed molecule with the spelling produced just before that parse, which can leave the stored graph and its identity key out of step.
approach.novelty: Require a stable molecular identity before a candidate enters the pool. Keep already consistent identities, normalize a changing spelling only when the new spelling survives confirmation and still describes the original checked graph, and reject representations that remain inconsistent through the existing bounded generation loop. Earlier siblings altered chemical edits or parent allocation. This change leaves the generated graph and selector intact and extends an earlier identity-repair idea to the newly observed case of alternating representations.

nodes.hypothesis: Admit generated pool candidates only under a parse-and-serialize-stable canonical identity, normalizing stable aliases and rejecting representations that remain inconsistent on confirmation.

finding_summary.headline: Two pool identities stabilized; every evaluated molecule and score stayed unchanged
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a correction at the pool interface that preserves the represented graphs and the search trajectory under the installed parser. Its demonstrated benefit is stable bookkeeping: the only corrected entries were unselected, and their fingerprints were unchanged. A separate read-only replay rejected all 59 unstable representations recorded in the sibling with carbonyl preservation, including one that sibling had emitted. Five of those unstable representations retained the same fingerprint after another parse, showing why fingerprint equality cannot substitute for the registered identity test. The child itself produced no unstable candidate and never evaluated a renamed identity, so empirical failure prevention and accepted feedback under a changed key remain open. Its unchanged emitted chemistry still contains reactive heteroatom-halogen and peroxide bonds, concentrated aromatic ring families and unspecified stereochemistry. Identity consistency does not resolve those chemical limitations.
finding_summary.results: Both known stable aliases were normalized, reducing disagreements between stored pool identities and their molecules from two to zero. Across 75,484 otherwise valid checked attempts, 75,482 identities stayed unchanged and two received confirmed spellings of the same graphs. Independent checks found no admitted identity instability, graph modification, new identity collision or feedback mismatch. Neither corrected pool member was selected. All 435 pools reached 160 candidates, and all 4,350 generated evaluations retained the parent’s exact molecule and score order. Mean final-best score across three seeds remained 0.544374, with population standard deviation 0.013310; every paired task and seed score difference was zero, within the supplied 0.002 non-inferiority allowance. The offspring parent-beating rate also stayed at 565 of 4,350, or 12.99%. Identity checks consumed 7.28 seconds in aggregate, and the added receipts increased diagnostic log size from 98.24 MB to 147.13 MB. Recorded total wall time was lower, but these historical runs do not isolate the incremental runtime cost.

molecular.headline: Parent chemistry persists: aromatic polycycles, halogenated amines and carbonyl heterocycles, with reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated molecule/score order matches Parent n-fc2c108a5253 in every supplied task/seed trajectory. The emitted chemistry therefore remains the same. All objectives have trajectories; each digest covers 900 molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. This is a ring-rich, mostly aromatic output with several distinct seed-dependent families: compact bridged heterocycles, linked carbonyl heteroaromatics, aryl-substituted saturated amines, and larger aza rings. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9943 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are fractions of SMILES containing the indicated text features, not fractions of atoms or measured ring counts. Both the charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral SMILES still contain potentially basic amines, and the lack of stereochemical labels does not mean the graphs are achiral. Recognizable medicinal chemistry fragments coexist with oxygen-halogen bonds, nitrogen-halogen bonds, peroxide chains, crowded aminal centres, unusual ring junctions, and occasional very small or extensively concatenated products. Structural diversity is moderate across the full panel but much narrower within the highest-scoring excerpts. Synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly absent: familiar substructures are present, while complete routes, stability, and stereochemical control are not established. The score-gradient statements below describe associations in the supplied molecules and scores; they do not establish an unseen target structure, experimentally measured activity, or an intrinsic score benefit from repairing a chemical liability.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are compact but densely fused or bridged aromatic heterocycles carrying an aryl/heteroaryl carbonyl appendage and small alkyl substituents. The leading structure has an ethyl/methyl-substituted nitrogen-containing polycycle with an O-methylene bridge and a ketone connected through methylene to fluoropyridine. Other high examples replace that connection with an aroyl group or a thioester. The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide is recognizable conventional chemistry; later structures also include N-fluoro amides and fused N-N or N-O rings. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.5, with ring-closure rate 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.9724, and halogen presence 0.869. These are mostly substantial multi-ring molecules, with small fragment outliers. The leading ketone is more chemically interpretable than some heteroatom-rich variants, but its unusual bridged core would still need a credible synthesis and structural assignment. Chemistry and associated scores are unchanged from the Parent.
liabilities: N-fluoro amides, N-N/N-O ring linkages, and a thioester introduce different reactivity or stability concerns; they should not be treated as interchangeable examples of ordinary aryl fluorination or amide chemistry.
Unusual short bridges and ring junctions complicate synthetic planning and geometry, while the SMILES provide no explicit stereochemical specification.
Ethene and the N-chloro imine demonstrate loss of essentially the entire multi-ring feature combination even late in the trajectory.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragment products lack the aromatic/heteroaromatic surfaces and carbonyl-bearing connection jointly present in the higher-scoring molecules.

The output does not establish broad, synthetically routine alternative cores that retain this compact feature arrangement; the best excerpt stays close to an unusual bridged family. An additional unseen target-specific group cannot be inferred from the observed scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; the leading bridged heterocycle/fluoropyridyl ketone scores 0.4463521672202675. The high aroyl analogue scores 0.4349635367667153, and the thioester analogue still scores 0.4238198477630873. The common observed association is a compact aromatic carbonyl-bearing assembly with small substituents, not one uniquely established linker chemistry. The late N-fluoro-amide/N-N-ring product scores 0.3630045684864706, whereas the final ethene and the N-chloro imine fragment score 0.0. Ring-free fragments do not express the combination retained by the better molecules. These comparisons do not establish that added bridges, thioesters, or N-halogen bonds are independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules join carbonyl-bearing O/N heteroaromatic ring systems through an NH connection. The leading family also carries an aryl cyanate substituent, a short annulated carbon bridge, an aryl halogen, and an O-O-Cl chain. The final excerpt contains still more nitrogen-rich fused/linked dicarbonyl heterocycles, including N-F, N-Cl, and oxygen-chlorine substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.4 and the maximum is 248: the full trajectories include much larger concatenated aromatic assemblies than the leading compact representatives. Ring-closure and aromatic presence are both 0.9885; halogen presence is 0.7851. The familiar carbonyl heterocycles and NH linkage are embedded in molecules whose reactive substituents and complex annulation make overall synthetic plausibility questionable. The Parent has the same chemistry and score order.
liabilities: O-O-Cl and O-O-F chains combine peroxide and oxygen-halogen bonds; these are chemical reactivity liabilities despite their high objective scores.
Late N-halogenated dicarbonyl heterocycles and oxygen-halogen substituents raise further stability and synthetic-handling concerns.
Short annulated bridges, extensively repeated heterocyclic units, and large aromatic surfaces complicate synthesis and molecular properties; SMILES validity alone does not resolve those concerns.
missing_features: The tiny low-scoring molecules lack the linked aromatic surfaces, NH connection, and distributed carbonyl/heteroatom acceptors present in the higher-scoring family.

The highest excerpt poorly covers chemically ordinary replacements for the unusual peripheral bonds while preserving the same compact core geometry. The fluoromethyl example shows one such alternative; the scores do not identify a required unvisited scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623, compared with 0.6324703199409752 for the leading linked heteroaromatic product. Small methylamine and molecular chlorine examples both score 0.5, so that floor does not demonstrate useful molecular features. Within a closely related high-scoring core, the O-O-Cl-bearing structure scores 0.6300605077662029 and the fluoromethyl replacement scores 0.6293992623616929. Replacing its aryl bromine with methyl retains 0.6300605077662029. Thus the observed score is compatible with the linked heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement while distinguishing these reactive or halogen substituents only weakly. It does not establish a need for peroxide-halogen chemistry or increasing molecular size.

per_task.generated_character: The better products are medium-sized aryl-rich amines with saturated nitrogen-containing rings and flexible benzylic or alkenyl connections. One high-scoring family contains a saturated diaza ring with a crowded aminal centre, an exocyclic amine, an N-alkyl substituent, and substituted aromatic ends. Another has spiro-connected aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, and an aryl thiol. Mean proposal SMILES length is 60.2; ring-closure presence is 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9782, and halogen presence 0.9874. These molecules already contain basic-amine opportunities; a lack of ring nitrogens is not their general limitation. Some spiro-amine frameworks are recognizable medicinal chemistry, while the crowded aminals, occasional O-Cl groups, chloromethyl substituents and undefined stereochemistry make the full products less routine. The same structures and scores occur in the Parent.
liabilities: Crowded aminal centres, including a carbon bearing an exocyclic amino group and both ring nitrogens, require scrutiny for stability and synthetic accessibility.
Aryl thiols, O-Cl substituents, and N-chloromethyl groups occur alongside otherwise recognizable amine frameworks; high scores do not establish their suitability.
No explicit charge or stereochemical labels are present. Potentially basic nitrogens are encoded neutrally, so the emitted strings do not document a protonation-state or stereoisomer exploration.
missing_features: Low-scoring aryl fragments and the final truncated aminal fail to retain the aromatic-appendage/amine/geometry combination expressed by the better molecules.

The spiro and substituted saturated-ring products lack stereochemical specification. Their graphs can encode different spatial arrangements, but the trajectories do not test whether a particular stereoisomer improves this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminal/aryl/amine assembly scores 0.9914038363125457 and the spiro-amine/aryl-thiol example 0.9908331648929692. A small halogenated aromatic fragment scores 0.001421581552029289. A particularly useful local comparison retains the aryl ends and enamine-linked core: the ring N-methyl analogue scores 0.981088217863691, while its N-formyl analogue scores 0.48797702544581545. That change alters nitrogen electronics and hydrogen-bonding capacity. The final smaller product retaining the diaza ring and fluorinated aromatic end but losing the other aromatic appendage scores 0.011495655106721757. The visible gradient favors the combined aromatic surface, amine character, and connecting geometry. It does not imply that every amine, extra halogen, or additional nitrogen independently helps.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring products are medium-to-large cyclic assemblies containing alkyl-substituted pyridyl or quinolyl groups, a benzofused carbonyl heterocycle, and N-methylated aza rings or macrocyclic connections. Carbonyls, aromatic nitrogens, tertiary amines or amidic nitrogens recur; oxygen and sulfur substitutions appear among neighboring products. The final excerpt includes unsaturated, nitrogen-rich larger rings bearing quinoline-like appendages. Mean proposal SMILES length is 55.9; ring-closure presence is 0.9943, aromatic presence 0.9885, and halogen presence only 0.269. This family is much less dependent on halogen decoration than the others. The individual functional groups are often familiar, but constructing the complete fused/bridged larger-ring arrangements would require deliberate synthetic planning and stereochemical control. Chemistry and its score trajectory remain identical to the Parent.
liabilities: Large and sometimes bridged aza rings create conformational and ring-closure challenges; their existence as valid graphs is not a synthesis.
Serial changes interconvert tertiary amines, amides and urea-like connections, changing basicity and donor/acceptor patterns along with ring geometry.
Bulky repeated aromatic appendages and unspecified stereochemistry add uncertainty even though this family has fewer obvious heteroatom-halogen liabilities than several other outputs.
missing_features: Low-scoring chains lack the coupled heteroaromatic/carbonyl/cyclic-nitrogen arrangement that is present in the better products.

The highest excerpt provides limited alternative, synthetically straightforward ring topologies retaining that feature arrangement, and it does not specify stereochemistry at newly substituted or bridged centres. The observed scores do not identify a particular missing target scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329, whereas the leading pyridyl/benzofused dicarbonyl/aza-ring assembly scores 0.22405709718343647. A related analogue without the extra methylene between the N-methyl nitrogen and carbonyl scores 0.21884002370946612; this changes both ring size and amine-versus-amidic character, so those effects cannot be separated. Ethane scores 0.012461119656980673 and the small acyclic amide 0.025605696979529788. The common higher-scoring feature set is the combined aromatic heterocycle, nitrogen-rich ring and carbonyl arrangement, rather than amide presence alone. The larger final molecule carrying repeated quinoline-like appendages scores 0.1754730092490373, below the more compact final dicarbonyl aza-ring example at 0.21037674112349405; repetition and size alone do not ensure higher score.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of compact fluorinated aryl compounds attached to an N-alkylated fused dicarbonyl heterocycle, with aminomethyl or aminoethyl substituents. The top example has a free primary amine, aryl fluorine and fluoromethyl groups, and the carbonyl-bearing heterocycle; neighboring examples include N-F substitution. Another seed finishes with more extensively fused heteroaromatics bearing thiol/hydroxyl groups and small fluorinated carbocycles, without the same pendant primary amine. The leading aminomethyl compound contains comparatively conventional functional groups; N-fluoro congeners, very large repeated cores and unsaturated small rings elsewhere are less straightforward. The Parent emits the same chemistry with the same scores.

Small unsaturated carbocycles, thiol substituents and cumulated-double-bond examples require chemical scrutiny; these are not evidence of an intrinsically inaccessible whole output.
Large repeated heterocyclic/aromatic assemblies show that the emitted chemistry does not reliably remain within the compact size and feature balance seen in the better family.

The output lacks a broad set of chemically stable scaffold alternatives preserving that arrangement. Where small saturated carbocycles create stereochemical choices, these are unspecified; a stereochemical score benefit has not been demonstrated.

Its close aryl-chloro analogue scores 0.5064928497454653: replacing that aryl chlorine with fluoromethyl accompanies an increase within this particular family. Let observed feedback determine which combinations matter without assigning task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 94.4 and maximum 248. Other supplied records include the very large repeated-core molecule Cn1c(=O)c2c(-c3ccccc3)n(-c3cc4cc(c3O)C(n3c(=O)c5c(-c6ccccc6)n(-c6cc(C(=O)OCCl)ccc6O)cc5n(C)c3=O)OC4=O)cc2n(C)c1=O at 1.6758614448245604e-53, and the final fragment C=C at 0.0. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a SELFIES variational autoencoder on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freezes it. A complete Gaussian state contains both the semantic latent and the variables that determine categorical decoding, so each state produces one reproducible molecule. During an objective, a Gaussian process learns from the fingerprints and scores of that session's accepted molecules. Parallel pCN chains sample the Gaussian prior weighted by the GP probability of beating the best observed score. The Parent randomly takes a novel batch from retained chain states and submits the exact molecules used for prediction.
approach.novelty: Add empirical elite-threshold conditioning: after each feedback message, use the 90th percentile of accepted scores as the probability threshold. This asks whether a molecule can enter the observed upper score region even when an isolated record lies far above the decoder's predicted scores. The proposed causal change is a less extreme threshold that changes which pCN transitions are accepted. This lineage has only its root so far; its incumbent threshold is the direct comparator, and no sibling has tried an elite-percentile threshold.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the observed-maximum threshold in the Parent's GP-probability pCN target with the linearly interpolated empirical 90th percentile of unique accepted current-session scores, so the same prior-preserving sampler conditions on entering an observed elite score region instead of exceeding an isolated incumbent.

finding_summary.headline: Elite conditioning changed sampling but lowered the single-seed mean score to 0.391
finding_summary.insights:
An extreme incumbent tail can be relaxed enough to materially redirect sampling without improving record discovery. The paired receipts rule out an inactive cutoff, unaccepted labels or prediction/submission mismatch as explanations for this score result. Lowering the cutoff changed relative preferences: it accepted 5,401 moves the incumbent rule would reject, and rejected 1,103 moves that rule would accept. The effect therefore includes which molecular transitions are preferred, as well as the overall acceptance rate.

On the two sessions that motivated the intervention, the elite target became permissive: mean retained-minus-prior log elite probability was only 0.087 for drd2_docking and 0.021 for sitagliptin_mpo. Their scores moved in opposite directions. This narrows the next question to how much record-seeking pressure is useful, and whether the GP can distinguish useful molecular arrangements within the decoder's reachable space. The molecular assessment finds abundant rings and familiar medicinal fragments, but inconsistent whole-molecule assembly and control of functional-group placement in both runs; threshold relaxation leaves those generator limitations open. These chemistry observations suggest further hypotheses, not a proven cause of the score loss. One seed establishes the logged behavioral effect but cannot establish the reliability of the score tradeoff, GP calibration or equilibrium mixing.
finding_summary.results:
The intended threshold and sampling effects occurred. All 145 fitted cutoffs exactly matched the accepted-score 90th percentile and lay below the incumbent. On 4,640 identical prior probes, the mean standardized threshold deficit fell from 5.193 to 1.057, and the fraction more than three posterior standard deviations below the cutoff fell from 66.49% to 0.43%. Retained states showed the same direction in every round. Replaying both rules with the same proposals and random draws changed 6,504 of 36,800 accept/reject decisions (17.67%); every actual update followed the elite rule. All 1,450 submitted molecules retained exact prediction identity and filled the budget.

The seed-0 mean final-best score fell from 0.433167 to 0.390832, a decrease of 0.042335. The largest change was drd2_docking, which fell from 0.867722 to 0.572905. median_2 fell from 0.171784 to 0.167839. Gains on zaleplon_mpo (0.340635 to 0.375713), deco_hop (0.573265 to 0.574331) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.212429 to 0.263373) did not offset those losses. This is confirmed mechanism activation with a negative score result on the one available seed.

molecular.headline: Abundant rings and medicinal fragments coexist with awkward connectivity and no defined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers every supplied objective for seed 0: each digest contains 300 evaluated structures, including 290 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally broad, spanning ordinary aryl heterocycles, saturated amine rings, fused and bridged systems, lactams, ethers and esters, alongside long polyenes and unusually connected nitrogen, sulfur and phosphorus groups. Most molecules have a substantial medicinal-chemistry-sized skeleton, but very small fragments and much larger, highly decorated structures also occur. Ring chemistry is abundant: the per-task ring_closure_rate spans 0.9828 to 0.9966, and aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.7793 to 0.8897. These are SMILES presence rates, not perceived ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths span 44.6 to 46.4; text length is not molecular weight. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0 despite structures containing potentially stereogenic tetrahedral centres. The lack of stereochemical specification does not imply that all structures are planar. The parent trajectories show the same broad mixture of recognizable fragments and awkward assemblies. There are chemically interpretable individual proposals, but broad structural diversity and accepted SMILES do not establish a feasible synthesis, an ordinary closed-shell state, or stability. Score-gradient readings below are associations within these trajectories; they do not identify hidden target structures or prove that any particular functional group caused a score.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring proposals are mostly moderately sized ring assemblies with aromatic carbon, ring nitrogen or oxygen, and limited peripheral substitution. Evaluation 149, score 0.37571328785207686, joins a fused N-methyl N/O aromatic system to an alcohol-bearing side chain and a fluorinated unsaturated aza ring with an amino substituent. Evaluation 185, score 0.33690534619560325, is a much more conventional methylimidazole bearing benzyl and chlorobenzyl-thioether substituents. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already scores 0.3051048083696145. The low end includes an extensively benzylated, peptide-like amide assembly with unusual sulfur at evaluation 11 and a large polyunsaturated ring assembly at evaluation 179. The late set still mixes exotic phosphorus/sulfur structures with the aryl-thiophene thioamide and unsaturated lactone at evaluation 299. Synthetic plausibility is therefore mixed rather than uniformly poor.
liabilities: The high-scoring fused imine structure at evaluation 110 includes a small, densely connected nitrogen ring; several other high structures also have unusual unsaturated ring closures that complicate a plausible synthesis.

Evaluations 223 and 268 carry conjugated aldehyde substituents. Evaluation 299 combines an aldehyde, thioamide and unsaturated lactone, so a useful score does not remove potential chemical reactivity.
The late phosphorus species at evaluation 295 and bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur at evaluation 296 are unusual valence environments for an ordinary medicinal series.
missing_features: The set lacks consistent elaboration of the compact, chemically conventional heteroaromatic arrangements already represented by the imidazole and initial indole carboxamide; many alternatives change ring topology and appendage size at the same time.

No uniquely required absent functional group can be inferred. The evident gap is reproducible control of scaffold size and substituent polarity, rather than absence of rings, nitrogen, carbonyls or halogens.
Configurations are unspecified at the alcohol-bearing and other tetrahedral centres; the trajectory provides no stereochemical comparison from which to infer a preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.37571328785207686 and the digest median is 0.011458. The larger, flexible amide-rich structure at evaluation 11 scores 4.062031856671369e-45, while evaluation 179 scores 9.963756221572277e-36. Together with the high aromatic examples, this supports a preference for a bounded scaffold size and a coherent aromatic/heteroatom arrangement over indiscriminate molecular growth. Smallness alone is insufficient: the initial alkyl bromide scores 8.305895500294491e-10. Carbonyls are not an established requirement because the best proposal lacks one. The fluoro/chloro matched pair at evaluations 223 and 268 has the identical score 0.3365357296869613, so halogen identity is not a differentiating signal in that pair. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.340634631669846 with an aryl-substituted diazacycle bearing a small N/O ring; the child maximum has a more fused aromatic core, while the parent and child share the 0.33966649739182625 sulfur-containing heterocycle at evaluation 111. The higher maximum does not coincide with removal of questionable ring connectivity.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is rich in aromatic and heteroaromatic rings with multiple nitrogen functions, usually on moderately sized to larger scaffolds. Evaluation 247, score 0.5743310208126858, contains linked and fused aza-aromatic systems joined through an extended unsaturated N-N-containing segment. Evaluation 253, score 0.5664592760180995, has a recognizable aryl amide and indole, but its intervening carbon also bears a nitroso group. Evaluation 191 combines a biphenyl amide with imine/hydrazone chemistry, while evaluation 218 combines an aryl amide, a saturated diazacycle, a thiourea and a fused N/O heteroaromatic ring. Familiar synthetic fragments are present, but the output does not define a consistently straightforward series. The low examples include unsaturated sulfone-linked rings, a saturated cyclic sulfone with a fused N/O ring system, and the morpholine-containing sulfone at evaluation 299.
liabilities: Nitroso substitution at evaluation 253, extended imine/hydrazone connectivity at evaluations 247 and 191, and the allyl thioether/thiourea combination at evaluation 218 warrant chemical scrutiny before treating these as ordinary stable analogues.

The final evaluation-296 structure has a very elaborate polycyclic assembly containing bracketed hydrogen-bearing sulfur, ester/amide groups and a carboxylic acid; a recognizable morpholine appendage does not make the full assembly straightforward to synthesize.
missing_features: The upper structures suggest value in specific aromatic nitrogen and donor/acceptor arrangements, but systematic chemically stable versions of those arrangements are missing from the bounded high-scoring set.

The evidence cannot identify a missing target decoration or a required scaffold replacement: broad structural classes already overlap in score, and the apparent sulfone association has a strong parent counterexample.
Defined stereochemistry is absent even in substituted indole side chains and saturated fused systems.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest median is 0.520459. Aromatic nitrogen-containing assemblies at evaluations 247, 191 and 158 sit above the nonaromatic or less aromatic sulfone-rich structures at evaluations 50, 170 and 299, whose scores are 0.25758568374594853, 0.26375771547557075 and 0.26539368531376917. Yet the tiny propionitrile at evaluation 41 still scores 0.5, and the extended polyene/amide structure at evaluation 99 scores 0.5609057782404998. Thus the narrow upper score differences do not establish a general size penalty, and the low sulfone examples do not establish that sulfones themselves are disfavored. In fact, parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.5732649174777824 at evaluation 218, is an aryl sulfone attached to a nitrogen-rich heterocyclic assembly. The child maximum replaces that chemistry with a more extensively conjugated aza-ring assembly, without a clear improvement in apparent synthetic plausibility. The shared evaluation-158 structure scores 0.5644679320458192 in both trajectories.

per_task.generated_character: The useful upper examples combine aromatic surfaces with nitrogen-containing linkers or saturated nitrogen rings. Evaluation 87, score 0.572904722089471, is an arylpiperazine connected to an N-hydroxy, unsaturated amino fragment and a phosphine-substituted phenyl group. Evaluation 29, score 0.31273900914359654, carries a dimethylaminopropylamino chain on a methoxybenzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered carbocycle; the small ring is chemically consequential. Evaluation 18 contains a tetrahydroisoquinoline-like tertiary amine, and evaluation 135 combines a secondary amino linker, an aryl ether, a pyridine and an oxime. The low end contains aryl imines, amides, conjugated nitrogen systems and thioethers without an equivalent exposed saturated amine arrangement. The overall output still spans small fragments, ordinary medium-sized scaffolds and much larger polyunsaturated assemblies.
liabilities: The best proposal contains an arylphosphine and an N-hydroxy unsaturated amino unit. Their possible chemical liabilities are separate from the supplied score.

Evaluation 29 has an unusual fused unsaturated four-membered ring; evaluation 255 adds a pyridinium group and an amino carbon attached to pyrrolidine, giving a different charge and aminal environment from a simple tertiary amine.
Hydrazone-like connectivity, nitro groups and extended unsaturation remain in late proposals; the broad output does not establish a stable or synthetically coherent amine series.
missing_features: Reliable construction of accessible aliphatic amine centres at controlled positions relative to aromatic surfaces is underdeveloped. Such centres are present, so this is a problem of their arrangement and recurrence, not absolute absence.

Chemically uncomplicated versions of the useful aryl/amine arrangements are not consistently represented among the strongest child examples: phosphine, N-O, oxime and unusual small-ring features accompany them.

The observed cationic or nitrogen-rich structures do not by themselves specify a useful protonation state; amide, imine, aromatic and saturated amine nitrogen must remain chemically distinct in this reading.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.572904722089471, but the digest median is 0.007702. The amine-bearing structures at evaluations 29, 18 and 135 score 0.31273900914359654, 0.2586499693063822 and 0.21811628298646404, whereas the aryl imine at evaluation 212 scores 0.00011879516001877162 and the simple phenoxypropyl amide at evaluation 55 scores 0.00033303319833196673. This supports an association with the chemical state and placement of nitrogen near aromatic groups, rather than nitrogen count alone. It is not sufficient: the final N-N-linked diazacycle at evaluation 299 scores only 0.0014980745212506842. Parent n-a08278654dda's strongest structure at evaluation 208, score 0.8677224451996757, combines an aminopropyl group and a tertiary cyclic amine with benzene, ether and thiophene elements; its evaluation-267 structure, score 0.7993263925636829, also has saturated aliphatic amines. The child retains individual amine-bearing hits, including the shared 0.31273900914359654 structure, but its maximum adds unusual phosphine/N-O chemistry and remains below those parent values. No binding pose or measured protonation state was supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger proposals combine multiple rings with carbonyl-containing or ether-containing motifs: lactams, esters, cyclic amide/urea-like units, aryl ethers and oxygenated aromatic rings. Evaluation 257, score 0.16273417606729546, is an elaborate polycyclic amine/imine and lactone assembly with a dihydroxybenzene element. The late evaluation-295 structure, score 0.16095095675340096, is a more compact N-methyl pyrrole fused to a lactam ring, with a phenyl substituent and an oxazoline ring. Evaluation 242 is a benzene-fused medium-ring lactam bearing a methyl ester and benzyl substituent; evaluation 151 is an oxygen-linked aromatic cyclic ketone assembly. The fixed initial structure at evaluation 7 contains a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyls, phenyl substitution and a hydroxybenzoate ester, and remains the highest-scoring structure in the child trajectory. At the other extreme are formaldehyde and a long acyclic brominated polyene containing multiple nitrogen linkages.
liabilities: Evaluation 257 obtains an upper-set score with a complicated bridged ring system and an imine; this is less straightforward medicinal chemistry than its recognizable amine, phenol and ester fragments imply.
The acyclic evaluation-116 structure combines extensive unsaturation, bromination and N-N linkages. Evaluation 80 has adjacent positively charged nitrogen atoms in an unusual ring system.

The final evaluation-296 polycycle remains large and densely connected, with several imine-containing rings; late output is not uniformly represented by the more conventional lactam at evaluation 295.
missing_features: The output lacks consistent preservation and controlled variation of the organized aromatic/heterocyclic and carbonyl/ether arrangements already visible in the initial and stronger generated molecules.
Ring and oxygen atoms are plentiful; the unresolved feature is their specific connectivity and spacing, which the score comparisons cannot reduce to a single required heterocycle or carbonyl count.
Potentially stereogenic benzylic and ring-junction centres, including that in evaluation 295, remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial evaluation-7 score is 0.1678386594791329; no child proposal exceeds it. The best generated score is 0.16273417606729546 and the digest median is 0.109215. The low formaldehyde score of 0.008773280079294957 and acyclic polyene score of 0.015539494866471998 contrast with the ring-rich, oxygenated upper structures. The latter low example is not merely too small, supporting an association with organized ring and functional-group topology. Carbonyls are common in the upper set but not obligatory: the aryl-ether/imidazole structure at evaluation 248 scores 0.1566926618156574. Parent n-a08278654dda reaches 0.1717839775079566 with an aromatic, oxygenated polycycle containing several amide carbonyls. The child reproduces the parent's evaluation-260 polycycle at its evaluation 257 with the same 0.16273417606729546 score. This looks like broad coverage of the same oxygenated ring chemistry, with additional unrelated structures rather than evidence for a new missing functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest proposals are moderately sized but chemically varied: an N/O polycyclic amidine connected to an aldehyde-bearing cyclic enol ether at evaluation 182; a vinylpyridine with an oxime ether and thiol/hydrazone segment at evaluation 256; a polyenynyl cationic aza ring attached to an aminopyrazole at evaluation 123; and unsaturated imide/lactone or imide/ether ring systems at evaluations 17 and 77. They are not a coherent conventional amine-amide series. The bottom end includes both heavily decorated large ring assemblies and sprawling chains with multiple phenyl groups, boron or phosphorus, many unsaturated bonds and several polar functions. Familiar functional groups are available, but their combined architectures often look difficult to make and chemically delicate.
liabilities: Evaluation 182 combines an aldehyde, cyclic enol ether and amidine-containing polycycle; evaluation 256 adds oxime-ether, thiol/hydrazone and enol functionality. Their scores do not demonstrate stability or a practical route.

The shared parent/child cationic structure at evaluation 123 contains an undercoordinated bracketed positive nitrogen; direct graph inspection identifies radical character, so it should not be interpreted as an ordinary protonated amine.
The bromomethyl group and multiply unsaturated medium/large rings in evaluation 17, and the very elaborate ring connectivity at evaluation 52, create additional chemical and synthetic concerns.
missing_features: The set lacks a repeatedly expressed, chemically uncomplicated combination of modest scaffold size and organized polar ring/linker functionality; high values are attached to structurally disparate and often delicate assemblies.

No specific absent pharmacophore is supported by these molecules alone. Nitrogen, carbonyls, ethers and halogens all occur among very low structures as well as some higher ones, so their presence cannot identify the missing arrangement.
Defined stereochemistry is absent from the polycyclic and substituted ring structures, but the available scores cannot establish a stereochemical preference.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 182 scores 0.26337307291649803 and evaluation 256 scores 0.22480871596011054. They exceed parent n-a08278654dda's maximum, 0.21242900824222632, which belongs to the same cationic polyenynyl/aminopyrazole structure found at child evaluation 123. The higher child maximum therefore has a more oxygenated cyclic amidine/enol-ether arrangement, but still carries an aldehyde and unusual ring connectivity. The very large structures at evaluations 52 and 167 score exactly 0.0, while the benzyl-rich nitrogen-containing structure at evaluation 172 scores 1.5436686042133222e-64. Modest size and an integrated polar arrangement appear more compatible with the upper region than extensive hydrophobic or polyfunctional growth; this is not a clean matched-pair inference. Halogens alone are uninformative: the best proposal is unhalogenated, whereas the multiply fluorinated late evaluation-297 structure scores 2.151807787068372e-13. The digest median is reported as 0.0, but the trajectory includes many tiny nonzero scores, so that rounded median is not an exact-zero count. Late evaluations 299 and 300 remain at 1.981355285913548e-05 and 1.397896131843601e-05 despite amine/heterocycle content.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring and aromatic token presence are high, yet upper examples include ONC(=CCc1ccccc1P)N1CCN(c2ccccc2F)CC1 with phosphine and N-O chemistry, and Cc1cc(OC(F)F)ccc1C(=O)NC(Cc1c[nH]c2ccccc12)N=O with a nitroso group. More conventional chemistry is demonstrably available in Cc1ncc(SCc2cccc(Cl)c2)n1Cc1ccccc1. The deficit is therefore the reliability of whole-molecule assembly, not absence of useful fragments. Unusual groups occur at both high and low scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably assemble familiar medicinal fragments into chemically uncomplicated, interpretable whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs stronger control of functional-group compatibility, ordinary valence/electronic states and ring connectivity while retaining its broad de novo scaffold coverage. It should be able to vary an existing useful arrangement without incidentally adding reactive or exotic groups. This chemical plausibility gap does not justify assuming that every such group universally lowers the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1cccc2c1C=C2NCCCN(C)C scores 0.31273900914359654, and Cc1ccc(F)cc1OCCNCC(CC=NO)Cc1ccccn1 scores 0.21811628298646404 in their supplied session, whereas CCCC(=O)NCCCOc1ccccc1 scores 0.00033303319833196673 in that same session. The latter still contains nitrogen and an aromatic ether, but its nitrogen is an amide. The corresponding parent's strongest structures also carry saturated aliphatic amines. The child clearly can emit such centres; the missing capability is repeatable control of their attachment and environment, not simple nitrogen enrichment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve the chemical state and placement of amine nitrogen relative to aromatic surfaces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator should be able to retain or vary an aliphatic amine centre, its substitution and its spacing from a ring independently of wholesale scaffold changes. Distinguish that chemistry from amides, conjugated imines, aromatic nitrogen and unusual formal charges. Which nitrogen environment to retain must come from current-session observations, without an objective-specific motif rule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact organized examples such as Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 score well relative to the acyclic C=COC(=CC=CC#CCC)NC=NC=C(Br)C=NNN=NC(Br)=CC=O in their shared trajectory. Elsewhere large decorated structures reach tiny scores. However, C=CC=C(C(=O)C=CCNCC=C(CC=C)NC(=O)c1cc(C(C)NCc2cnc(C)[nH]2)ccc1O)c1cccnc1C(C)=NON has recorded scores 0.5609057782404998 and 2.241116085184792e-33 in different sessions. Thus a universal small-molecule or ring-count preference would contradict the evidence. A fluoro/chloro matched pair is present, but most cited upper structures differ by much more than a controlled substituent change.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable independent control of scaffold topology, molecular extent and polar-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo variations that change a substituent or ring connection while preserving the rest of a chemically meaningful size and donor/acceptor arrangement. Molecular growth, contraction and polarity changes should be controllable dimensions whose value is learned from the local scores. Broad ring coverage already exists; simply increasing ring or heteroatom occurrence does not fill this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied proposal-set stereocentre_rate is 0.0. Cn1c2ccccc2c2oc(C(O)CC3=NC=CC(N)C=C3F)cc21 contains an unspecified alcohol-bearing centre, and Cn1cc(C2=NCCO2)c2c1NC(=O)CC2c1ccccc1 contains an unspecified substituted tetrahedral ring carbon. Both appear among the higher-scoring proposals. This is absent stereochemical specification, not proof of absent three-dimensional shape or proof that a particular enantiomer would score better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces potentially stereogenic structures without representing defined tetrahedral configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs the capacity to retain and deliberately vary valid explicit stereochemical assignments when its scaffolds create stereogenic centres. No preferred configuration can be prescribed from these trajectories; any utility would have to be established from permitted current-session feedback.

nodes.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on unlabeled molecules and selects its checkpoint by the number of valid, connected, distinct ancestral molecules under a fixed sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts a fresh adaptable flow policy and keeps that selected prior frozen. Accepted molecular trajectories train the policy through trajectory balance and prior regularization. The search alternates one neural batch with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a scored breeding population and supply a protected first descendant; crossover and seven atom/bond mutation families build temporary offspring pools, and an accepted-score fingerprint posterior selects the remaining evaluations. Accepted graph discoveries can then breed again and train the neural policy. The graph atom-replacement step chooses an atom uniformly and substitutes an element allowed by its current bond valence; a fully bonded carbonyl carbon consequently has no replacement option.
approach.novelty: At those otherwise unsuccessful carbonyl-carbon replacement sites, add one direct reversal of a qualifying secondary amide: A-C(=O)-NH-B becomes A-NH-C(=O)-B while both attached fragments and the molecular formula remain intact. This makes the opposite arrangement of the amide donor and carbonyl acceptor available without passing through independent destructive substitutions. The same-parent graph children moved nitrogen within aromatic rings or matched crossover attachment contexts; neither supplied this amide-orientation move. The new move retains the inherited selection of atoms and operators and adds no protection gate over ordinary replacements.

nodes.hypothesis: Rescue otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replace_atom choices with a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic carbon-substituted secondary amide, preserving its molecular formula and both attached fragments.

finding_summary.headline: Amide reversals reach evaluation without a local score gain, despite higher endpoints
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes a working, evaluated amide-orientation channel, and rules out failure to construct the move as the explanation for its weak measured utility. It does not support the proposed local score benefit. Exposure narrows sharply after construction: 46 admitted reversals remained unevaluated, including every crossover-derived reversal. Two direct pairs cannot establish which amide environments might benefit more broadly. The higher endpoints also occur amid changed pool competition, random-number consumption and later search feedback; they cannot be attributed to a favorable amide reversal when neither observed direct pair wins. The molecular assessment reinforces the narrower chemical interpretation: familiar medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive linkages, small-ring cumulenes and unspecified configurations. Conserving one amide and its attached fragments does not resolve those broader quality gaps. A useful next causal question is whether valid local alternatives fail mainly through limited evaluation exposure or through context-dependent score neutrality; the present panel leaves that distinction open. The ancestry audit also shows why crossover parent labels must be followed through subsequent deletions before interpreting parent-relative scores.
finding_summary.results: Across all three seeds and five objectives, 51 selected secondary-amide sites produced 51 valid, distinct-from-source reversals with the registered formula, fragment and ring preservation. That is 0.420% of 12,153 atom-replacement attempts. Thirty-six were sole mutations of accepted parents and 15 followed crossover. Across all three seeds and five objectives, 51 selected secondary-amide sites produced 51 valid, distinct-from-source reversals with the registered formula, fragment and ring preservation. That is 0.420% of 12,153 atom-replacement attempts. Thirty-six were sole mutations of accepted parents and 15 followed crossover. Forty-eight products entered temporary pools; only two were evaluated, both as sole reversals. The zaleplon pair tied at 0.273668, while the deco_hop pair fell from 0.594245 to 0.580622. There were no direct wins, one tie and one loss, with mean difference −0.006811. Overall graph parent-beating yield fell from the logged Parent reference of 452/2,850 (15.86%) to 389/2,850 (13.65%). Correcting an inherited crossover attribution error raises the Parent count to 453 and leaves the Child count unchanged. All batches filled and all 150 fresh-policy handoffs had real fresh-parent contribution. Meanwhile, mean endpoint score rose from 0.550198 to 0.570186; the paired seed changes were +0.042122, +0.022690 and −0.004846, with the largest mean task gain in deco_hop.

The experiment establishes a working, evaluated amide-orientation channel, and rules out failure to construct the move as the explanation for its weak measured utility. It does not support the proposed local score benefit. Exposure narrows sharply after construction: 46 admitted reversals remained unevaluated, including every crossover-derived reversal. Two direct pairs cannot establish which amide environments might benefit more broadly. The higher endpoints also occur amid changed pool competition, random-number consumption and later search feedback; they cannot be attributed to a favorable amide reversal when neither observed direct pair wins. The molecular assessment reinforces the narrower chemical interpretation: familiar medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive linkages, small-ring cumulenes and unspecified configurations. Conserving one amide and its attached fragments does not resolve those broader quality gaps. A useful next causal question is whether valid local alternatives fail mainly through limited evaluation exposure or through context-dependent score neutrality; the present panel leaves that distinction open. The ancestry audit also shows why crossover parent labels must be followed through subsequent deletions before interpreting parent-relative scores.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom links, small-ring cumulenes and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The complete supplied panel covers all five tasks and seeds 0, 1 and 2: each task has 900 accepted trajectory records, including 870 optimizer proposals. No task lacks trajectories. Both this node and Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 were read across that panel. The output contains recognizable aryl ethers, nitriles, benzimidazoles, quinazolines, saturated amines, lactams, sulfonamides and indoles, together with unusually connected sulfur/oxygen groups and extensively rearranged unsaturated rings. Digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9644 to 0.9954 and aromatic-marker rates from 0.7103 to 0.9747; these are string-level presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived rings. Ring chemistry and aromatic chemistry are abundant. The complete output spans many frameworks, although each seed's upper tail often concentrates on a particular family. Practical-looking building blocks coexist with questionable assembled structures, so broad diversity does not establish broadly plausible synthesis. Every digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of the optimizer trajectories finds molecules with unspecified atom stereocentres in counts of 351, 251, 451, 316 and 378 in the brief's task order, with no assigned atom centres; absence of stereo annotation therefore does not mean the output is achiral. Structural counts below are derived from the supplied molecular records, and all scores are existing trajectory scores. The digest's final excerpts are seed-2 samples, not a summary of every seed's final state.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 structure is a medium-sized nitrile attached to an unsaturated seven-membered oxygen ring, with phenyl, aryl ether, pyridyl and aminomethyl functionality. RDKit reads 24 heavy atoms and three rings, two aromatic. Its relatives interchange ether, sulfur, O-S, S-S and peroxide linkages while retaining much of that arrangement. Seed 1 instead produces N-alkoxycarbonyl or N-acyl benzimidazole-like cores bearing a halogenated anilinomethyl substituent, with an N-O-containing ring-expanded relative also near the top. Seed 0 follows phenolic hydroxycyclobutene/imine structures joined to an expanded nitrogen-containing ring. Thus the pooled leaders do not describe the whole seed panel. The optimizer's median heavy-atom count is 25 in both this node and the Parent. The Parent's seed-0 leaders were fused aza-ring structures with unusual O/N/S attachments; its other seeds included aryl carboxamides and nitrile-containing unsaturated rings. The current molecules retain moderate molecular scale and aromatic/polar combinations while changing their assembly. The ether/nitrile and halogenated heterocycle families contain recognizable synthetic fragments, but the unusual heteroatom bonds and ring arrangements make feasibility uneven.
liabilities: Peroxide, O-S, S-S and N-O connectivity occurs among favorable examples. Those bonds change the chemical class and possible stability of the linker or ring; their accepted scores do not establish interchangeable synthetic behavior.
The hydroxycyclobutene/imine and expanded aza-ring output, and the fused cumulated-double-bond example, raise geometry and chemical-persistence questions beyond simple SMILES validity.
RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 351 of 870 optimizer proposals and assigned centres in none. The leading seven-membered oxygen-ring example itself has an unspecified centre.
missing_features: A more complete series of chemically credible alternatives preserving the favorable aromatic, polar and linker relationships is not demonstrated. The distinct favorable nitrile/ether and N-acyl heterocycle families do not reveal one uniquely missing required group.
Defined configurations are absent at the substituted oxygen-ring centre and in other saturated ring variants. The observed scores do not identify a preferred configuration.
Controlled compact core and linker changes remain incompletely represented: the late duplicated nitrile ring and fused cumulene do not retain the leading score despite retaining recognizable pieces.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryloxy nitrile leader scores 0.48839749189747395, the related O-S linker 0.47582689034774595, and the sulfur linker 0.46457806514522626. The peroxide-linked relative still scores 0.4526205390674507. The N-alkoxycarbonyl benzimidazole and its N-O ring-expanded relative each score 0.4588069837338257 despite lacking the leading family's nitrile. These observations associate higher scores with particular medium-sized connected aromatic/polar arrangements; they do not make nitrile or an unusual heteroatom linkage a universal requirement. Methane, hydroxylamine and the much larger polyol/amide assembly have scores of 0.0, and an overgrown amino/amidine-rich assembly scores 7.335113523278365e-48. A late structure duplicating the unsaturated nitrile-containing ring scores 0.26198042135705957, while a fused cumulated-double-bond variant scores 0.18422963024144726. The pooled median is 0.152555. Relative to the Parent, the sampled maximum decreases in seed 0 from 0.49151859442707624 to 0.4412371986661207, and increases in seeds 1 and 2 from 0.4163503402962837 and 0.46457806514522626 to 0.4588069837338257 and 0.48839749189747395. The chemistry changes differ by seed; these comparisons do not isolate the cause of those score changes.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-0 family consists of anilinoquinazolines with fluorine/chlorine substitution, methoxy or amino groups, and oxygen-linked side chains. The best molecule has 32 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-membered rings. Its aminomethoxy substituent contains an N-Cl bond; many nearby leaders instead carry an aryl peroxide, and some add an O-Cl group. A favorable ether-linked relative lacks the peroxide and N-Cl linkage. Seed 1 explores quinazoline/carbonyl arrangements with nitrile-bearing thiophenes, acylated amines and piperazinones, sometimes in very large linked assemblies. Seed 2 samples linked pyrimidine, benzimidazole and pyridyl regions with nitrogen-rich connecting rings and N-N attachments. The median size is 33 heavy atoms, compared with 36 for the Parent, with a median of four rings in both. Parent seed 0 favored a different sulfonamide/aza-ring family; Parent seed 1 already had linked quinazoline/piperazinone chemistry, and Parent seed 2 had aminoalkyl aza-aromatic structures. Conventional heteroaromatic and amide components are readily recognizable, but the high-ranking peripheral chemistry is not consistently plausible as a stable finished compound.
liabilities: The highest-scoring molecule contains N-Cl, several near-leading molecules contain O-O, and one contains O-Cl. Carbon-bound chlorine elsewhere in these molecules is a different chemical environment and should not be conflated with those heteroatom-halogen bonds.

Read-only graph perception finds O-O bonds in 130 optimizer proposals, compared with 135 in the Parent. The concern persists across a substantial sampled family and is not confined to a single isolated low-score example.
Expanded linked assemblies and unusual nitrogen-rich rings complicate geometry and synthesis. RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 251 optimizer proposals, with none assigned.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives around the favorable aza-aromatic attachment pattern are only partly demonstrated. An ether-linked high example exists, so the missing capability is consistent coverage of credible alternatives, not the mere ability to emit an ether.
Useful core/attachment diversity is uneven across seeds: the strong anilinoquinazoline family does not establish a similarly successful alternative core in the seed-2 nitrogen-rich neighborhood.

Specified stereochemistry is absent for substituted alkyl side chains and more complex saturated variants. Nothing in the displayed scores identifies the preferred configuration or a uniquely absent functional group.
