per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are arylpiperazines with flexible alkyl linkers to another aromatic group or an N-aryl five-membered heterocycle. The brominated/chlorinated leader has 32 heavy atoms and four rings, three aromatic, and a six-carbon linker to piperazine. A simpler high example is a fluorophenylpiperazine linked through five carbons to phenyl. Seed 0 instead explores aryl-substituted saturated diazepane amines attached to fused aromatic/imine systems, including indole and thiol groups. Seed 1 retains heavily fused or bridged aryl/ether/amine structures. This node's median size is 28 heavy atoms and five rings, compared with the Parent's 30 heavy atoms and four rings. The Parent already emitted the same leading seed-1 and seed-2 families; the main change among those leading structures is in seed 0. Accessible saturated amines and aromatic surfaces are abundant. The digest charged-marker rate of 0.008 does not measure basic-amine coverage: the neutral SMILES of arylpiperazines and other saturated amines can contain protonatable centres. Simple arylpiperazine/linker assemblies look synthetically recognizable, whereas the densely bridged variants require substantially more scrutiny.
liabilities: Long flexible chains, repeated aromatic surfaces and substantial halogen substitution leave physical-property balance unestablished. High accepted scores are not measurements of solubility, selectivity or practical exposure.
Thiol-bearing relatives and extensively fused or bridged structures introduce chemical-persistence and synthetic-geometry questions that the SMILES and scores do not resolve.

RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 451 of 870 optimizer proposals, with none assigned. This primarily concerns the broader substituted and polycyclic output rather than every quoted linear arylpiperazine.
missing_features: No uniquely absent pharmacophore can be inferred from an upper tail already near the observed score limit. Saturated basic-amine candidates and aromatic surfaces are present.

Defined configurations are absent in the fused and bridged amine families, and a controlled series of linker geometries is not established by the displayed leaders. The linear-linker leaders themselves need not contain a tetrahedral stereocentre.
Compact alternatives that retain the favorable aromatic/accessible-amine arrangement without multiplying large arms are incompletely controlled.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl/heteroaryl hexyl-piperazine leader scores 0.9999999657062248, its thiol-substituted relative 0.9999999149875901, and the simpler fluorophenylpiperazine/pentylphenyl molecule 0.9999993790262016. The extra heteroaromatic ring and extensive halogenation are therefore not demonstrated necessities. The Parent already has the same leading seed-2 value and the same seed-1 maximum of 0.9999943278368041; the seed-0 maximum changes from 0.98747470209114 to 0.9999971866054931 with the altered amine/aromatic family. The pooled median is 0.724445. At the low end, an N-acyl/sulfonyl aromatic molecule scores 3.8021829379963674e-05, a nitro acylhydrazone 4.1105044111594925e-05, and a sulfonamide/hydroxamate 5.916130606141068e-05. A piperazine whose nitrogens are tied into thiourea and amide environments scores 0.00015556264858674598. This supports a distinction between accessible amines and electronically deactivated nitrogen, while the different whole structures prevent a causal assignment to basicity alone. Duplicating large aromatic/amine arms produces a late score of only 0.046770493414912545. The observed preference concerns the connected aromatic/amine/linker arrangement, rather than maximizing nitrogen or molecular bulk.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecule is a methylenedioxy-fused benzodiazepinone-like system attached to an aryl sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine. It has 32 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered imine/lactam ring. Related seed-1 leaders contain bromomethyl or bromoethyl heteroaromatic lactams and chlorinated biphenyl groups joined to the sulfonylpiperazine. Seed 2 favors an indole-containing oxygen ring linked through an ether to a fused nitrogen/dicarbonyl system; late examples replace a ring carbon with oxygen or nitrogen. Seed 0 produces fused aromatic/dicarbonyl systems with sulfur-oxygen ring links. The median size is 32 heavy atoms and four rings in both this node and the Parent. The leading seed-1 and seed-2 structures and scores are retained from the Parent, while seed 0 changes from more sulfonylmorpholine-bearing assemblies to the sulfur/oxygen-linked fused family. Lactam, sulfonamide, piperazine and indole components are familiar medicinal chemistry, but their detailed ring assembly and some late substitutions make synthetic plausibility uneven.
liabilities: Alkyl bromides occur in several favorable relatives, and an O-O bond occurs in a favorable indole-linked oxygen ring. Those changes introduce distinct possible reactivity concerns and cannot be treated as chemically neutral decoration.

O-O single bonds occur in 47 optimizer proposals, compared with 50 in the Parent. The compact leading diazepinone lacks that liability, so the judgment concerns inconsistent quality within the output.
The fused/linked carbonyl systems and acetal-like centres have unresolved configurations. RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 316 optimizer proposals and none assigned.
missing_features: Stable and configurationally specified variations of the indole-linked oxygen-ring family are incompletely demonstrated. The peroxide and O-N replacements do not establish an objective-required group.

Compact core replacements that retain the useful lactam, aromatic and amine relationships remain incompletely covered. The leading diazepinone already shows that the larger brominated biaryl architecture is not universally necessary.
The structures do not identify a uniquely missing target-like scaffold or preferred stereoisomer; stereochemical specification and controlled functional-group placement are the observable gaps.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact diazepinone/sulfonylpiperazine leader scores 0.26493557493264663. Larger bromomethyl and bromoethyl biphenyl relatives score 0.24793630350691426 and 0.24551078459035605, showing that the additional aryl and alkyl-bromide groups are not prerequisites for the strongest sampled value. The indole/oxygen-ring/dicarbonyl molecule scores 0.2371358719187444; its O-O-containing ring relative still scores 0.23322188283655107 and the O-N-containing relative 0.23035022137995856. These local similarities show that a chemically concerning peroxide remains near a favorable conventional ether-containing member. Acetylene, a long acyclic polyamine and a small nitrile/amidoxime-like compound each score 0.0. The long hydrocarbon chain attached to a polyol ring scores 0.034938562148434216; a simpler late fused lactam scores 0.16539457330816304. The pooled median is 0.156797. Parent and child share the same maxima in seeds 1 and 2, while seed 0 changes from 0.21407396945703827 to 0.21286009496455266 with a different leading assembly. The observed gradient supports particular connected aromatic/carbonyl/nitrogen arrangements, without establishing a universally required ring, halogen or extra nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 structures are compact sulfonyl/sulfinyl nitrogen compounds bearing fluoroacetyl groups and highly unsaturated carbon frameworks. The best molecule has 26 heavy atoms, one five-membered carbon ring and no aromatic ring by RDKit perception. It contains an acyclic allene/polyene segment and a five-membered ring with consecutive cumulated double bonds; the nitrogens are acylated or sulfur-bound rather than ordinary free alkylamines. Aromatic relatives occur in the same high family, including an aniline and a benzyl-substituted sulfonamide-like arrangement. Seed 0 instead favors compact nitrogen-rich fused rings with pyridyl/imine and oxime-ether functionality. Seed 2 samples carbonyl-rich chains with sulfur/nitrogen attachments, acylurea-like units or a carboxylic/carbamic mixed-anhydride linkage, connected through oxygen to unsaturated nitrogen rings. The median size remains 24 heavy atoms, as in the Parent. Parent seed 0 had a different oxygen/nitrogen bicyclic family, Parent seed 1 already had sulfonyl/sulfinyl unsaturated-ring structures, and Parent seed 2 included indole-linked ureas. The current output therefore has polar groups and compact scaffolds, but the high seed-1 family is particularly questionable as isolable finished molecules.
liabilities: The five-membered cyclic cumulene is a strong geometry and persistence concern inferred from its connectivity. Small-ring cumulenes are known to impose substantial geometric strain; this contextual concern is supported by the primary study [Strain estimates for small-ring cyclic allenes and butatrienes](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16839152/). No stability or strain value is assigned here to a generated molecule.

The digest cumulated-double-bond rate is 0.1207, corresponding to 105 optimizer strings; the same string-level check finds 4 in the Parent panel. The aromatic-marker rate is 0.7103 despite the ring-closure rate of 0.9644, consistent with extensive nonaromatic unsaturated-ring exploration rather than absent rings.

Sulfenamide-like S-N attachments and mixed-anhydride connectivity in the late carbonyl-rich molecules raise additional chemical-context questions. They are chemically different from ordinary thioethers, amides and carbamates.
RDKit finds unspecified atom stereocentres in 378 optimizer proposals and none assigned. The leading sulfinyl structure itself has an unspecified atom stereocentre.
missing_features: Chemically persistent alternatives that preserve the compact favorable polar-group arrangement while avoiding severely constrained cumulated unsaturation are not consistently demonstrated. A less-unsaturated ring relative is present, so this is incomplete coverage rather than total absence.

Defined configurations at substituted saturated atoms and sulfinyl centres are absent, and relevant double-bond geometry is not established by the cited strings. The data do not establish a preferred configuration.

The output does not reveal a uniquely absent target pharmacophore. Nitrogen, fluorine, carbonyl and sulfur functionality are already represented; their useful arrangement remains incompletely resolved across the different seed families.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A leading N-Cl-containing molecule scores 0.9389438334932467, a peroxide-containing relative 0.9361879682516134, and a related ether-containing molecule without those bonds 0.9310417418501142. An indole-linked oxygen-ring member scores 0.2371358719187444 while its peroxide-containing relative remains at 0.23322188283655107. O-S, S-S and mixed-anhydride examples also occur in the cited output. Concerning chemical classes therefore survive in favorable neighborhoods alongside more conventional alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group changes do not consistently retain chemically credible local bonding around otherwise useful molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide context-sensitive edits that retain useful surrounding aromatic and polar relationships while offering coherent amide, ether, amine and sulfur-group alternatives. Distinguish peroxide formation, heteroatom halogenation, sulfenamide formation and mixed-anhydride formation from changes within ordinary functional-group classes. Use the available accepted feedback to compare the actual alternatives; their presence alone does not establish a reason to remove every occurrence of a heteroatom or halogen.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One complete supplied panel contains 105 strings with a cumulated-double-bond marker, versus 4 in its Parent panel. Its leading cited molecule, scoring 0.43965957023019037, has a five-membered cyclic cumulene and no aromatic ring. A less-unsaturated five-membered-ring relative still scores 0.3542726928004173. Elsewhere, the cited fused cumulated-double-bond variant scores 0.18422963024144726 beside a conventional aryloxy/nitrile leader at 0.48839749189747395. The structural concern is tied to specific ring/bond relationships, rather than ring presence alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-size and bond-order changes do not consistently preserve credible geometry, and can concentrate output on small-ring cumulenes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring contraction, expansion, fusion and bond-order changes chemically coherent as joint local transformations. Maintain access to saturated or conventionally unsaturated alternatives that preserve the useful substituent arrangement. Let current-session observations determine which geometries and saturation states are useful, while keeping the consequences of small-ring cumulene formation distinguishable from ordinary ring edits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories identifies unspecified atom stereocentres in 351, 251, 451, 316 and 378 proposals in the brief task order, and assigned centres in none. The cited structures include substituted oxygen rings, chloroalkyl side chains, fused or bridged amines, acetal-like centres and a sulfinyl centre. Several simple aromatic or linear-linker leaders are achiral, so the gap concerns the structures that actually admit configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configurationally rich molecules are emitted without explicit stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configurations where chemically defined and preserve those specifications through local structural changes. Provide coherent configured alternatives around accepted arrangements and compare them through available feedback. The absence of specified configurations establishes missing representation, without identifying a universally favorable stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited zero-score examples include methane, hydroxylamine, acetylene, a long acyclic polyamine and a large repeated sulfur/amide assembly. A duplicated aromatic/amine-arm structure scores 0.046770493414912545 despite near-limit values for simpler arylpiperazine/linker members. Conversely, the compact 32-heavy-atom diazepinone-containing molecule scores 0.26493557493264663, above larger brominated biaryl relatives in its displayed family. The observations support context-dependent molecular scale.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing output can destroy a useful connected arrangement through extreme fragmentation or duplication of large motifs.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore growth, contraction and linker changes that retain a coherent core and useful donor, acceptor, accessible-amine and aromatic relationships. Include alternatives between tiny fragments and multiplication of whole favorable arms, allowing accepted observations to determine useful size for the current objective without any hidden-task identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Different seeds produce aryloxy nitriles, N-acyl benzimidazoles, anilinoquinazolines, arylpiperazines, fused lactams and compact sulfur/nitrogen frameworks, yet the upper excerpts repeatedly decorate one neighborhood. Small local alternatives sometimes retain useful scores, while whole-fragment growth or electronic-context changes do not. The cited arylpiperazine/linker member scores 0.9999993790262016, whereas a piperazine with its nitrogens incorporated into amide and thiourea environments scores 0.00015556264858674598. These whole structures do not isolate a causal property, but they show why nitrogen count or a shared ring name is insufficient chemical coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad graph variety is not accompanied by consistent coverage of useful core and functional-group arrangements within each leading chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted core families and explore core, linker and attachment alternatives that preserve useful functional-group placement and electronic context. Represent the distinctions among accessible saturated amines, amide nitrogens, heteroaromatic nitrogens and other polar environments when generating alternatives. Assess chemical variety through those relationships as well as the existence of a new molecular graph.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two highest-scoring earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current elites, preserving their original accepted strings and scores. The policy fits all selected sequences with equal weight toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward. It takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps and uses the final policy to sample complete SMILES; chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refill the next batch. A passive uniform-history comparator measures the retained score-ordered replay mechanism without contributing to training.
approach.novelty: Add best-prefix checkpoint restoration to online adaptation: after following the existing bounded Adam update path, keep the visited policy and matching optimizer state with the lowest training loss, including the unchanged starting state as an option. This addresses the observed cases where the final iterate has already made the selected examples fit worse. The change selects which completed update prefix survives; it uses the same targets, examples, equal weights and gradient calculations. Earlier siblings changed prior learning, replay membership or retention, and equivalent training strings. None tested whether the last online iterate should be replaced by a better state already visited during the same update. A comparison with the discarded final iterate will establish activation separately from later molecular novelty and score.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain the policy and matching Adam optimizer checkpoint with the lowest unchanged combined current-and-historical augmented-target mean squared error among the starting state and every iterate visited by the inherited bounded online update, choosing the earliest exact tie instead of automatically retaining the last iterate.

finding_summary.headline: Earlier checkpoints lowered training loss but reduced final scores in all three seeds
finding_summary.insights:
Useful earlier prefixes are much more common than endpoint-versus-start checks alone reveal: 132 of the 142 nonterminal interventions occurred even though the discarded endpoint was already better than the starting checkpoint. Selecting the best visited fitting loss is therefore an active intervention, but it is insufficient to improve this molecular search. The seven zero-progress updates all occurred at the beginning of the task with the largest score loss. Suppressing those early parameter changes, or more generally discarding useful momentum and learning progress, is a plausible contributor; the experiment does not isolate either explanation. The discarded endpoint is a same-path training comparator, not an evaluated alternative molecular trajectory.

The preserved objective still has positive, unattainable log-probability targets in 1,217 of 4,425 training-row exposures, and historical-group error worsened in 148 of 420 nonterminal replay updates despite lower combined loss. Better combined fitting therefore does not imply that each historical example improves. Broader observed core coverage also rules out a uniform collapse of sampled core diversity as the sole account of the score decrease. The chemistry assessment finds abundant aromatic and cyclic medicinal-chemistry motifs, but recurring high-score families, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth remain. This narrows the next question to the relationship between retained update progress, these fixed targets and useful future proposals, rather than assuming the last iterate or simple core scarcity was the main utility bottleneck. Checkpoint-loss equality is supported on identical tensor shapes; the inherited larger diagnostic tensor has small numerical discrepancies beyond the registered tolerance on 32 updates and should not be substituted for that criterion.
finding_summary.results:
The intended checkpoint intervention happened. Of 435 updates followed by new proposals, 142 retained an earlier policy and matching Adam state: five initialization updates and 137 later feedback updates. Every intervention produced a measurable parameter difference from its discarded endpoint. On those same update paths, terminal-minus-selected mean squared error averaged 0.202718, summing to 28.785889. All 450 updates, including 15 terminal updates, retained the minimum logged loss on the fixed training tensor. Seven early sitagliptin updates retained their starting state. Targets, training membership, equal row weights and the executed Adam rule remained unchanged.

Final benchmark performance declined despite that lower fitting loss. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.513272 to 0.487621, a paired mean change of -0.025651; the individual seed changes were -0.036109, -0.010057 and -0.030788. Population standard deviation increased from 0.001984 to 0.012470. Four of five task means fell, led by sitagliptin from 0.288538 to 0.197063; drd2 was essentially unchanged. Both algorithms delivered all 4,350 novel accepted optimizer proposals. Canonical-novel yield among raw draws rose from 51.81% to 52.79%, and distinct chemical-core coverage increased on four tasks. Those coverage improvements did not provide the predicted score gain.

molecular.headline: Rich aromatic and cyclic chemistry, but recurring high-score cores, unspecified stereochemistry and occasional uncontrolled molecular growth.
molecular.overall_character: The read trajectories cover every listed objective. These molecules are predominantly recognizable medicinal-chemistry scaffolds: aryl and heteroaryl amides, fused heteroarenes, sulfonamides, ethers, hydrazones and saturated nitrogen heterocycles. The optimizer proposal ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9747 to 0.9989 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9391 to 0.9954; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant text markers, not perceived ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 37.8 to 51.1 characters and are not molecular-weight measurements. Structural diversity is moderate across the complete trajectories and seeds, with much narrower families among many high-scoring samples. Ring formation, aromatic nitrogen and basic cyclic amines are demonstrated capabilities. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, including outputs with complex saturated ring junctions, so molecular chirality is often left unspecified. The explicit charged_rate does not measure whether neutral amines can protonate. Conventional scaffolds look synthetically plausible, but highly elaborate ring assemblies, unusual heteroatom linkages and extreme hydrocarbon growth make the overall synthetic reading questionable. Stability, ionization, solubility and synthetic-route concerns below are structural interpretations, not measured properties. Parent comparisons describe observed chemistry and recorded scores only; they do not establish mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The highest digest samples are compact, predominantly planar aza-carbazole-type fused heteroarenes whose ring nitrogen bears a methylene carboxamide joined to a methoxyphenyl or methoxypyridyl group. They contain an amide donor/carbonyl acceptor, an ether and variably placed pyridine-like nitrogens. Other trajectories include azaindole ester/carboxamides and arylamine, sulfonamide and hydroxy-fused-arene families. The worst samples are much larger assemblies with extended hydrocarbon ester tails, bulky saturated nitrogen rings or elaborate oxygenated ring systems. Amide formation and substitution of an available heterocyclic building block are plausible synthetic disconnections for the leading series; the fused aza-core still requires an appropriate precursor. Relative to the Parent, the leading chemistry in seed 1 changes from substituted pyrazole carboxamides to aza-carbazole acetamides, while seed 0 retains the same leading azaindole ester/amide family. This is a change in scaffold arrangement within already abundant ring chemistry.
liabilities: The leading aza-carbazole family has a substantial planar aromatic surface, leaving aqueous behavior and solid-state packing uncertain.
Very long alkyl ester appendages and oversized multifunctional assemblies are still proposed despite their extremely small recorded scores.
Late proposals include hydrazides, a free aryl thiol and adjacent phenols; these add unassessed chemical behavior beyond the leading amide series.
missing_features: The poor proposals often lose the compact combination of aromatic heteroatom placement, an amide linker and limited peripheral bulk seen in the stronger examples; merely retaining aromatic rings does not preserve that arrangement.

The highest digest samples give little coverage of alternative ring topologies carrying a comparable donor/acceptor arrangement, although the Parent supplies a distinct high-scoring pyrazole-amide family.
A specific absent target motif cannot be identified from this score span; the supported gap is reliable coverage of balanced compact arrangements rather than absence of ring or nitrogen chemistry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxypyridyl aza-carbazole acetamide and the methoxyphenyl diaza analogue both score 0.46671988179915697. A closely related methoxyphenyl aza analogue scores 0.46331566856387824, while other aromatic-nitrogen placements score 0.4418627361103939. The visible neighborhood supports particular heteroatom positions within a compact aromatic-amide arrangement, without a simple benefit from adding more nitrogens. The initial methoxyindole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the large ring/amine assembly scores 9.068393833650252e-27 and the long-chain indole ester scores 3.13726955652741e-24. Final proposals still range from a larger aminopolyaryl amide at 0.0009912168585955116 to a more compact diarylamine carboxamide at 0.41220436185971376. The Parent seed-1 leading pyrazole carboxamide scores 0.4697065314067379, so the Child examples do not show that this fused core is uniquely required.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large polyaromatics with dense fluorine substitution. A prominent family is an aryl acylhydrazone connected to a diarylamine; another combines pyridyl and phenyl rings with a thiazolylmethoxy linkage. A further family uses an aryl thiourea connected through an aminomethylene/imine chain to another arene or azaarene. Final samples add bromine, nitro groups and additional aromatic nitrogens. The optimizer halogen_rate is 0.8724, consistent with this strong substitution bias. Hydrazone condensation, thiourea formation and ether connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry, although dense positional substitution and undefined imine geometry complicate the identity of a physical product. Parent trajectories already contain polyfluoroaryl hydrazones and thiourea/imines; the Parent seed-1 leading thioalkyl-pyridyl aminoalkyl family is replaced among the Child leaders by thiazolylmethoxy-pyridyl chemistry.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces and extensive fluorine or heavier-halogen substitution increase hydrophobic structural burden; aqueous properties were not measured here.
Hydrazones and imines introduce possible hydrolysis, geometric-isomer and tautomer concerns, while thioureas add further tautomeric and chemical variability.
Nitro substitution persists in the final thiourea/imine molecules, so substantial chemical liabilities can coexist with scores near those of the leading examples.
missing_features: The high-scoring examples provide limited coverage of less halogen-loaded, more conformationally varied versions of their recurring aromatic donor/acceptor arrangements. Their scores do not establish whether those alternatives would be favored.
The leading acylhydrazone and thiourea/imine series do not specify the configuration of their imine bonds; a defined geometric chemical identity is missing from those strings.
The available gradients identify local aromatic substitution patterns, but cannot establish a unique missing target-specific scaffold or a universal linker requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading fluorinated acylhydrazone scores 0.6010573047491092. Closely related benzoyl substitution patterns score 0.5989441930618401 and 0.597835391953039, making local fluorine placement/addition a visible source of small changes within this family. The distinct thiazolylmethoxy compound scores 0.5999139813405677 and the aryl thiourea/imine scores 0.5966118931649093. Thus several linkers can support similar recorded values. The fluorophenyl sulfonyl cyanide scores 0.25700280112044815, a larger polyaryl sulfone 0.26617434238528986 and a cyclic-sulfone thiourea 0.286193233770192; trifluoromethane scores 0.5004402958788305. These observations do not support a monotonic molecular-size or general-quality interpretation. The Parent seed-1 aminoalkyl pyridine reaches 0.6039526921879863 with a different linker arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of alkyl-substituted indoles attached to piperidine rings whose free tertiary nitrogen carries a haloarylalkyl group. These are medium-to-large molecules combining aromatic hydrophobic surfaces, an indole NH and a potentially protonatable aliphatic nitrogen. Another strong family contains phenolic spirocyclic amine polycycles with chloroaryl ether-containing appendages; final samples also carry primary amines, alcohol/phenol groups and related saturated-ring changes. The leading indole/piperidine connectivity looks compatible with conventional heterocycle assembly and N-alkylation, while the spiro/fused products pose greater ring-construction and stereochemical demands. Low examples are aromatic amides, oxalamides, hydrazones and sulfonamides, often with their nitrogen functionality conjugated to carbonyl or sulfonyl groups. The Parent also generated strong aryl cyclic amines, but its leading families included piperazine/pyrrolidine arrangements and flexible alkyl diamines. The Child visibly explores more indole-centered and spiro/bridged cyclic amine chemistry.
liabilities: Alkyl tails, multiple aromatic surfaces and halogens give many leading compounds considerable hydrophobic burden alongside their basic nitrogen.
Complex spiro/fused ring assemblies are incompletely specified without stereochemistry, and their scores do not demonstrate an accessible synthesis of a defined isomer.
Formal neutral SMILES do not resolve protonation state for these amines; actual ionization and assay behavior remain unmeasured.
missing_features: The weak sulfonamide/amide examples lack the free aliphatic nitrogen environment and spatial aromatic/basic-group combination repeatedly present among the stronger molecules. The generator already demonstrates that capability in its leading families.
The saturated spiro and fused structures lack specified relative or absolute stereochemistry despite ring junctions and substituents that can create distinct stereoisomers.

There is limited high-score evidence for preserving the observed aromatic/basic arrangement while reducing bulky alkyl and halogen appendages; the trajectories do not establish which smaller alternatives would retain the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propylindole/tertiary-piperidine haloarylalkyl molecules score 0.9999999595806517, and a phenolic spirocyclic amine scores 0.9999996167758578. The low anisamide/heteroaryl sulfonamide scores 1.9828327575562915e-05; its piperidine nitrogen is sulfonyl-bound, so the ring does not supply the same free aliphatic amine environment as the leading piperidines. A neutral aryl oxalamide scores 3.0069171067466083e-05. This supports the joint arrangement of an available aliphatic basic center and aromatic surface in these trajectories. It does not establish that a basic nitrogen alone suffices: the initial molecule with a free N-methylpiperidine, amide and hydroxamic-acid group scores 0.0003786988088202195. These are recorded objective values, not binding affinities, and the molecules alone do not identify a unique receptor interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large heteroatom-rich ring assemblies: fused aromatic carbonyl heterocycles bearing sulfonamide-linked morpholine or diazacycles, as well as benzodioxole-containing aryl heterocycles. The leading molecule combines an aryl-fused oxygen heterocycle, a ketone/exocyclic imine and a morpholine sulfonamide. Related samples include lactams, piperazines, aryl ureas and fused azaarenes. Their amide and sulfonamide connections are synthetically recognizable, though the imino-carbonyl and densely substituted fused cores need closer chemical definition. The worst samples include a small chlorinated N-hydroxyformamide, flexible peptide-like chains, long alkyl chains and small imino heterocycles. Parent leaders more often combine aryl/fused carbonyl cores with substituted piperazine sulfonamides, while the Child seed-0 leader retains a morpholine sulfonamide and other Child seeds sample broader aryl heterocycles. Both generations contain the constituent ring and polar-group chemistry.
liabilities: Leading and near-leading structures include imino-carbonyl and quinone-like dicarbonyl systems with additional stability, tautomeric or redox questions.
A sulfonyl-bound morpholine or diazacycle nitrogen is chemically different from a free basic amine; a count of nitrogen rings would conceal that distinction.
Some late molecules accumulate fused and pendant aromatic rings without preserving the stronger examples' full polar arrangement.
missing_features: The lowest samples omit the combined aromatic framework, carbonyl/sulfonyl acceptor pattern and cyclic polar substituent found in stronger structures; adding a small heterocycle or a flexible amide chain does not recreate that arrangement.

Late proposals do not consistently retain the combined polar fused-core and substituted diazacycle/sulfonamide arrangements seen among Parent and early Child leaders. These substructures are available, but their useful joint configurations are not consistently represented.
The exocyclic imine of the leading structure lacks a defined geometric state, and the provided examples do not establish a more specific missing target motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The morpholine-sulfonamide imino ketone scores 0.20325754327905224 at evaluation 91, followed by a fused diazacycle sulfonamide/lactam at 0.20120147126513588 and a piperazine/heteroaryl sulfonamide at 0.19718878121013778. In contrast, the ring-free chlorinated N-hydroxyformamide scores 0.007693218186208301, the peptide-like molecule 0.025041397240195853 and a small imino sulfur heterocycle 0.0345361852497211. Several rings plus a spatially organized aromatic/polar combination distinguish these higher examples; many amide groups alone do not. A late polyaryl piperazinyl carbonyl heterocycle scores 0.18230155742745996, whereas the simpler benzyl tetrahydroisoquinoline scores 0.11757927025044308. The Parent fused carbonyl/arylpiperazine sulfonamide reaches 0.2354681799202668. These comparisons support arrangement-sensitive chemistry rather than an unobserved universal functional-group requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The isolated stronger molecules are compact-to-medium nitrogen-rich heteroarenes and carbonyl-linked aryl compounds. The leader is a methylamino/methyl-substituted triazine carboxamide attached to a dimethylphenyl group. Other examples include an amino/hydroxy fused heterocycle with a saturated tertiary nitrogen, a fused azaarene N-oxide carboxamide, aryl/furanylmethyl oxalamides and an aryl/pyridyl oxalamide. These have recognizable amide or oxalamide synthesis opportunities and limited peripheral bulk compared with the worst outputs. The broader trajectory also emits very long hydrocarbon chains, elaborate steroid-like esters, peptide-like assemblies and large nitrogen-containing rings. Parent leaders include pyrazole carboxamide alcohols, fused azaheteroaryl benzamides and aryl acylhydrazones; the Child shifts toward aminotriazine carboxamides and oxalamides. Compact heteroatom-rich chemistry is present in both generations, but widely different and oversized structures persist through final evaluations.
liabilities: Extreme hydrocarbon growth produces very large flexible or macrocyclic structures, including a zero-scoring nitrogen ring with extensive alkyl content.
Other poor samples accumulate peptide-like donor/acceptor arrays or elaborate polycyclic ester frameworks, so excess polarity and complexity are also represented.

Furan, N-oxide, adjacent oxalamide carbonyls and tautomeric amino/hydroxy heteroarenes introduce distinct chemical behavior among the stronger molecules; none has demonstrated stability, solubility or a completed synthesis here.
missing_features: Much of the output lacks the simultaneous limited hydrocarbon burden, positioned nitrogen heteroatoms and compact carbonyl-linked donor/acceptor arrangement found among the isolated stronger examples.

The final molecules do not consistently preserve or closely explore the aminotriazine and oxalamide arrangements already associated with higher observed scores; chemically distinct oversized families continue to appear.
Specified stereochemistry is absent even in complex saturated-ring outputs, although the shown scores do not establish that a particular stereochemical motif is required.
The sparse, structurally heterogeneous higher examples leave any unique missing target-specific group indeterminate.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminotriazine carboxamide scores 0.26223613784124133 against a digest median of 1e-06. The fused amino/hydroxy heterocycle scores 0.20803336453696816 and the azaarene N-oxide carboxamide 0.198169175615563. The dimethylphenyl/furanylmethyl oxalamide scores 0.19770893824865138, while its less methyl-substituted aryl counterpart scores 0.13923463506082193; this local comparison supports tuned composition within a compact polar framework, not simply making every molecule smaller. The pyridyl oxalamide scores 0.18652622280944445. The enormous hydrocarbon-rich nitrogen ring and elaborate steroid-like ester each score 0.0, and a final long-chain aryl heterocyclic ketone scores 4.064637608571372e-56. Compactness and heteroatoms are insufficient by themselves: a final small aryl/azaaryl acetamide scores 0.002351936446697417. The Parent fused azaheteroaryl benzamide reaches 0.30950439639437716 with a different topology. The heterogeneous maxima do not identify one missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest task reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Strong phenolic spirocyclic amines and later fused-ring products contain saturated junctions and substituted ring atoms without tetrahedral stereochemical notation. Leading hydrazone and imine strings also leave their double-bond geometry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not supply defined stereochemical alternatives for its complex saturated-ring products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve chemically coherent stereochemical states as part of proposed molecular identity, including relevant ring-junction and imine alternatives. Available feedback can then distinguish defined structures; these trajectories provide no evidence favoring a particular isomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The high-score excerpts repeatedly show aza-carbazole acetamides, haloarylalkyl indole-piperidines or polyfluoroaryl hydrazones. Full trajectories and Parent examples contain alternative useful pyrazole amides, substituted diazacycle sulfonamides and other cyclic amines. Broad global chemical variety coexists with narrow local high-score families.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring molecular support often contracts to substituent variants of a small number of ring and linker families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain score-supported alternatives in core topology and linker connectivity as chemically distinct generative support, so new accepted identities can explore more than aromatic nitrogen positions, halogen substitutions and peripheral alkyl changes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest examples include a long-chain aromatic ester scoring 3.13726955652741e-24, a hydrocarbon-rich nitrogen macrocycle scoring 0.0 and a final long-chain heteroaryl ketone scoring 4.064637608571372e-56. Compact heteroaryl amides and oxalamides occur among stronger examples, while substantial alkyl and ring burden can still accompany high-scoring basic amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control hydrocarbon and scaffold growth while retaining compact polar arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled changes in substituent size, linker length and polar-group placement around multiple retained cores. Use the observed score context to maintain a suitable size/polarity balance within each chemical family, without imposing one molecular-size preference on all feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring acylhydrazones and thiourea/imine chains recur, an imino-carbonyl ring leads another excerpt, and late samples add nitro groups, hydrazides or a free aryl thiol. Conventional amide and ether connections are also demonstrated elsewhere in the generated set, so these alternatives are chemically within the generator's reach.
transferable_gaps.gap: Some strong aromatic arrangements are explored mainly through geometrically or chemically ambiguous linkers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Broaden chemically coherent linker and tautomer alternatives around score-supported aromatic arrangements, preserving their actual donor/acceptor environments and geometric identity. Treat the recorded objective value and the chemical definition or plausible stability of a product as separate observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Strong indole-piperidine and spirocyclic examples contain free aliphatic amines, whereas weak piperidine sulfonamides place nitrogen next to sulfonyl groups. Elsewhere compact aromatic amides outperform peptide-like chains despite abundant nitrogen and carbonyl groups in both. The structures show that heteroatom presence alone does not capture the useful chemical configuration.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve ionization-relevant nitrogen environments together with their supporting ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and explore the full local ring/linker/functional-group environment, distinguishing free amines, amides, sulfonamides and aromatic nitrogens as chemical states. Let the available score feedback determine which complete arrangements remain useful.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted scored molecules using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It keeps a small population of high-scoring parents, while an archive of all accepted observations trains a fingerprint Gaussian process. Correlated draws from that model select which fresh offspring receive evaluations. The Parent also checks that each pool molecule has a stable canonical identity, so uniqueness and later feedback use consistent keys. Its edits readily change individual atoms, but offer no direct way to reverse an intact amide between two attached fragments.
approach.novelty: Add a direct orientation reversal of an acyclic secondary amide. Keep both attached fragments and the complete amide group, and exchange which fragment connects through nitrogen and which through the carbonyl carbon. The move becomes available when the existing atom-replacement draw lands on an eligible carbonyl carbon whose ordinary replacement menu is empty. Earlier siblings protected carbonyl endpoints, retained ring cores, or relocated nitrogen within an aromatic ring. This experiment changes the direction of a complete amide relationship, giving the existing learned selector a new local alternative without growing or trimming the molecule.

nodes.hypothesis: Enable a direct formula-preserving reversal of an acyclic secondary amide at an otherwise empty carbonyl-carbon replacement site, exchanging the nitrogen-side and carbonyl-side attachment relationships while retaining both external fragments.

finding_summary.headline: Eight evaluated amide-reversal descendants retained the edit, but mean score fell by 0.02036
finding_summary.insights: Failure to generate, preserve or evaluate a reversed amide is ruled out as the explanation for the missed score target. The direct comparisons show limited measured benefit: three source pairs tie, including the leading sampled amide pair, and the only incumbent gain combines two edits. The largest task-level loss occurred in docking, where 20 reversal-bearing candidates entered pools but none was selected. That loss cannot be read as an observed penalty on a scored reversed amide; opening an empty-menu action changes later random draws, pool composition and search history even when the new alternative is unselected. A contribution probe that distinguishes the local alternative's value from these trajectory changes remains informative. The change also does not establish globally better chemistry. Eligible-amide-containing emissions increased from 328 to 563, yet measured nonaromatic C(=O)-N coverage stayed nearly flat at 1,669 versus 1,667 molecules, and mean heavy-atom count increased from 33.39 to 35.43. The molecular assessment associates the weak docking seed with a less aliphatic-amine-rich branch and still finds reactive linkages, oversized repeated cores and unspecified stereochemistry. These are descriptive associations, not causal functional-group effects. The evidence supports a narrowly correct local transformation with sparse direct score exposure; broader utility and practical chemical quality remain open.
finding_summary.results: Every one of the 120 selected eligible sites produced a checked, identity-changing reversal while preserving formula, size, the complete local amide and both attached fragments. Of 95 pooled descendants, 93 retained the reversed orientation; all eight descendants selected for evaluation retained it. Two later edits destroyed the amide, and a double reversal returned to an already seen molecule and was rejected as a duplicate. Of four evaluated sole reversals of accepted parents, one improved its source score by 0.011119 and three tied; none created a new incumbent. A reversal followed by deletion produced one incumbent gain, improving its real parent's score by 0.049026, but that gain cannot be assigned to the reversal alone. All 15 task/seed sessions completed their budgets with no invalid or duplicate oracle submissions. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.524013, a decline of 0.020361 instead of the registered minimum gain of 0.002. Population standard deviation across seed means fell from 0.013310 to 0.007408. Every seed's macro score declined; the 15 paired task outcomes comprised three wins, eight losses and four ties. The inherited identity checker also rejected two unstable candidates before pooling, while every admitted identity remained stable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heterocycles retain useful amides and amines, but reactive bonds, oversized repeats and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: Read the complete Child and Parent panels for seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output is dominated by substituted aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, with secondary amides, cyclic carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles, ethers, amines and halogens. Saturated and bridged nitrogen rings are well represented in some streams; ring chemistry is not missing. Digest ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9747 to 0.9931, and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.9414 to 0.9885. These are SMILES-text presence rates, not ring counts or fractions of atoms that are aromatic. There is moderate structural variety across seeds, but each seed repeatedly revisits its own ring family. Plausibility is mixed: conventional secondary amides and aminomethyl heterocycles coexist with N-halogen bonds, O-halogen bonds, peroxides, unusual ring fusions and very large repeated heterocycles. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0: no explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is recorded, although several saturated ring structures contain potential stereocentres. Almost entirely uncharged strings do not establish absence of protonatable amines. Size and functional-group descriptions below are structural readings of the supplied SMILES; reported objective values are existing trajectory values. The chemical observations do not establish synthesis routes, binding poses or activation of the registered mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly moderate-sized substituted fused heterocycles: mean SMILES length 46.5, with ring and aromatic presence both 0.9839 and halogen presence 0.9713. The leading seed-1 molecules are indoles connected by a secondary carboxamide to fluoropyridine, carrying methoxy, ethyl, vinyl and additional aryl halogen substituents. The leading cited molecule contains 26 heavy atoms. Both amide orientations occur. Seed 0 instead develops more extensively fused, N-methylated rings with imine or oxime linkers; seed 2 includes rearranged sulfur-containing fused rings and N-N-containing acyl linkers. These alternatives are much less conventional than the straightforward indole amides. The end of seed 2 still includes a peroxide-bearing, N-fluorinated amidine analogue and a small carbamoyl fluoride fragment.
liabilities: Near-leading molecules contain N-Br or N-F bonds, including a benzene-fused four-membered nitrogen ring. Chemical parseability does not establish its stability or synthetic accessibility.
Other cited proposals contain peroxide, hydrazine-like N-N or imine functionality, and terminal proposals can collapse to small reactive fragments instead of preserving the ring system.
missing_features: Retention of a complete heteroaromatic partner and intact secondary amide is inconsistent across proposals, although the leading seed shows both and the fragmented tail lacks them.

Chemically conservative variation around the leading ring/amide relationship is limited compared with ring contraction and N-halogenation. An absent target-specific scaffold or a required amide direction cannot be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Seed-1 evaluations 164 and 189 retain the same substituted fragments but reverse the secondary-amide orientation; both score 0.41605207864642335. The chlorine alternatives also tie at that value. Evaluations 250 and 269 are another opposite-orientation pair tied at 0.41003927643747895. Thus the observed series supports retaining the substantial heteroaromatic/amide architecture and changing substituents, but demonstrates no score preference between these sampled amide orientations. The contracted-ring compound with N-Br and N-F at evaluation 288 still scores 0.4136551925282466, so the score does not cleanly separate chemically conventional amides from reactive alternatives. Tiny F, FF and carbon fragments score 0.0; the final carbamoyl fluoride scores 3.5259015803172243e-12. Relative to Parent, seed 0 moves from a fused heterocyclic ketone at 0.4463521672202675 to an oxime-bearing best at 0.3779802455230667; seed 1 reaches the intact-amide series at 0.41605207864642335 versus Parent 0.4126819838532174. Seed 2 remains in unusual fused-ring/acyl chemistry, with best 0.3957609793331631 versus Parent 0.4163503402962837.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest output stream: mean SMILES length 102.5 and maximum 235; ring and aromatic presence are both 0.9885. Seed 0 produces fused aza-aromatic and pyrone-like carbonyl/ether rings connected through aminomethyl or amidine groups, often with long unsaturated ether tails. Its best cited molecule has 39 heavy atoms. Seed 1 combines aza-aromatic carbonyl/oxygen rings, multiple aryl/alkenyl halogens, an ethynyl group and an O-C#N cyanate linkage; its best has 46 heavy atoms. Seed 2 repeatedly joins fused nitrogen heterocycles containing cyclic carbonyl groups into very large assemblies; the final cited molecule has 59 heavy atoms. Conventional heteroaromatic substructures are recognizable, but the complete substituted polyenes and repeated assemblies have questionable practical accessibility.
liabilities: Long polyene and imine/oxime-ether tails have unspecified geometric isomerism and chemically sensitive unsaturation; several high-scoring analogues add N-F or multiply halogenated carbon centres.

The seed-1 cyanate linkage and the large, densely fused or repeated nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies require chemical scrutiny. Ring richness and a nonzero score do not supply a plausible route to these complete molecules.
missing_features: Compact arrangements that retain the productive heteroaromatic/carbonyl combination without repeated cores are not reliably maintained: a compact amidine example already scores close to the extended best, while the final seed-2 structures remain much larger.

The long unsaturated high-scoring series lacks defined alkene geometry and a consistent set of conventional, stable linkers. The trajectory does not establish that filling this practical chemistry gap would raise the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic carbonyl-rich molecule scores 0.548381482770623, while small CF, N#CCl and C#C fragments sit at 0.5. The seed-0 polyene ether reaches 0.6330703012912482, and the much smaller amidine-connected ring pair at evaluation 269 reaches 0.625077399380805. Consequently, the visible gradient rewards retained combinations of heteroaromatic/carbonyl environments but does not establish that a long tail or simple growth is necessary. The seed-1 halogenated cyanate reaches 0.6260015065397522; the huge final seed-2 assembly scores 0.6019296607531901. The Parent also generated elaborate carbonyl/aza-ring chemistry, including reactive O-halogen or N-halogen decorations. Parent/Child best values are 0.6004556752278376/0.6330703012912482 in seed 0, 0.6324703199409752/0.6260015065397522 in seed 1, and 0.6083454583246726/0.6049270072992701 in seed 2. The chemistry changes differently in each seed; persistent size and reactive-group liabilities are visible on both sides.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic hydrophobic groups are combined with substantial saturated ring chemistry, rather than purely flat aromatic scaffolds. Mean SMILES length is 67.4; ring presence is 0.9897, aromatic presence 0.9816 and halogen presence 0.9908. Seed 0 develops fluoromethoxyphenyl groups, cyclobutanes, secondary/tertiary amines and bridged nitrogen rings with phenols and chlorine. Seed 2 develops medium-sized fused/spiro nitrogen rings linked through methylene to aryl sulfones or sulfoxides; its best contains 30 heavy atoms. Seed 1 instead favors brominated carbocycles, aryl sulfides/thiols and an aniline, with little of the unconjugated aliphatic amine character seen in the strongest other seeds. These are recognizable medicinal-chemistry ingredients, but strained polycycles, crowded halogenated aminals and unspecified configurations make many complete molecules questionable.
liabilities: Several high-scoring structures combine three- or four-membered nitrogen/carbon rings, congested bridgeheads and halogen-bearing aminal carbons. They require conformational and stability assessment beyond their accepted SMILES.
Dense halogen substitution, exposed phenols/thiols and variable sulfoxide configurations complicate chemical development. The low-score tail also includes reactive sulfonyl or sulfinyl halides.
missing_features: The seed-1 branch does not consistently combine aromatic hydrophobes with accessible nonacylated aliphatic amines, a combination present in the stronger Child seeds and in Parent best molecules. Aromatic aniline nitrogen or sulfonamide nitrogen is chemically different from that amine environment.

Explicit stereochemical specification is absent even in the bridged/spiro and substituted small-ring series. Their intended three-dimensional arrangement is unresolved by the supplied strings, and no score advantage from choosing a configuration has been measured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading seed-2 cyclic-amine/aryl-sulfone molecule scores 0.9706475574822273, and the seed-0 polyamine with phenol/methoxy aromatics scores 0.9696022091086564. A carboxylic-acid/amide/sulfonamide molecule scores 0.0005876222816323224, while aryl sulfonyl bromide alone scores 0.0004426865581623269. The existing pattern associates substantial aromatic groups combined with nonacylated aliphatic amines and constrained ring shape with higher scores; amines alone are insufficient, since the initial piperidine-containing hydroxamate scores only 0.0003786988088202195. The seed-2 final aryl-depleted sulfur-containing analogue scores 0.3075949875612589, and seed 1 reaches only 0.7565380379187507 in its sulfide/thiol series. Parent best molecules carry aliphatic amines with aromatic groups in all seeds, at 0.9908331648929692, 0.9512348232667347 and 0.9914038363125457 respectively. The Child preserves that broad chemistry in seeds 0 and 2 but follows a less amine-rich branch in seed 1. These associations do not identify a receptor contact or isolate a causal functional-group effect.

per_task.generated_character: Moderate-sized, nitrogen- and carbonyl-rich polycycles dominate: mean SMILES length 56.8, ring presence 0.9931 and aromatic presence 0.9874. Seed 0 favors an alkylquinoline attached to a partially saturated bicyclic ring system with N-methyl lactam groups; the best cited molecule has 28 heavy atoms. Seed 1 combines phenyl and oxygen-containing fused aromatic rings with nitrogen-rich cyclic dicarbonyl scaffolds, including N-F substitution. Seed 2 uses alkylquinoline connected through N-O to a cyclic dicarbonyl amine system, sometimes extending that linkage to O-O-N. These streams explore saturated as well as aromatic rings but converge on related N-alkylated carbonyl ring families. The seed-0 leader is comparatively conventional; the N-halogen, N-N and peroxide-containing relatives weaken overall synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: N-F bonds, peroxide-containing O-O-N linkages and multiple N-N bonds occur among high-scoring examples, making score-based apparent quality a poor stand-in for stable, makeable chemistry.
Complex fused or bridged carbonyl-rich rings have unspecified stereochemistry, and terminal expansion can add redundant aromatic material without a corresponding higher recorded score.
missing_features: Stable alternatives retaining the observed aromatic-to-carbonyl/amine relationship are incompletely explored relative to N-F, N-N and O-O-N variants. The seed-0 best already shows that such reactive linkages are not necessary to reach this local score band.

Changes in ring topology and linker arrangement without simply appending another aromatic core remain limited within each converged family. The observed Parent and Child structures support alternative arrangements, but not a specific unseen target scaffold.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent keeps every accepted score in a task-local archive for a fingerprint Gaussian process, but allows only the sixty-four highest-scoring accepted molecules to remain in its breeding population. It samples parents from three preferred score bands, generates a fresh pool through graph crossover and mutation, and selects evaluations using correlated posterior draws. Accepted offspring immediately compete for survival and can breed in later batches. This gives a functioning learning loop, while chemically distinct lower-scoring parents can disappear from the breeding population before their descendants are explored.
approach.novelty: Allocate survivor places in rounds across molecular cores: the best member of each core competes in the first round, the second-best members in the next, and so on until the existing population is full. Within a round, higher real scores win; the final survivors return to score order for the existing parent sampler. This protects several accepted core families while retaining the incumbent. The recorded lineage has tested posterior selection of generated offspring; this experiment changes the accepted molecules available for future breeding, with the inherited parent-draw rule intact.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted breeding molecules by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, prioritizing each core's best member before any core's next member, then restore global score order for the unchanged parent sampler.

finding_summary.headline: Core-round survival broadened breeding, but protected records never bred and all three score replicas fell.
finding_summary.insights:
Preserving a low-ranked core and exploring it are separate events under the unchanged sampler. Of the 542 protected offspring, 116 survived into a later breeding state, but all remained below the sampled score bands. Six were still retained when the experiment ended and had first received protection in the terminal batch. The broader breeding came through changes to stronger analogues and the ranks of other survivors, rather than descendants of the directly protected records. A local support-promotion trace confirms that this indirect route can produce a parent-beating child, but such participation did not offset the overall loss in productive evaluations.

The actual trajectory also changes the apparent opportunity: on the already diversified Child states, only two incoming molecules were rescued from immediate greedy rejection, while 1,058 newcomers that local greedy selection would accept were excluded. Both rescued newcomers stayed outside breeding support. This narrows the result to a strong redistribution of survivor competition, with little evidence for the hoped-for exploration of protected weak parents. Mean generating-parent strength and mean offspring score both fell, so the smaller average parent deficit is not evidence of better candidates. The molecular assessment still finds repeated oversized heterocycle assemblies, tiny fragments, reactive bonds and constrained ring systems. Core coverage increased without resolving those chemical limitations. The passive greedy lists use existing labels only; they provide no alternate descendants or scores for an independently executed search.
finding_summary.results:
All 4,365 retention calls matched the declared core-round rule, preserved the incumbent and respected the 64-member capacity. Among 3,540 capacity-limited contests, 1,606 changed the local greedy survivor set and added one represented core; 1,266 also changed the immediate breeding support. Mean cores actually used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 24.20, and all fifteen final populations contained 64 distinct cores. There were 12,012 actual parent uses outside greedy breeding support reconstructed from the same accepted history. Those uses contributed to 326 evaluated offspring, including 35 best-parent beats and two incumbent gains.

The direct protection route remained unused: none of the 602 records retained against local greedy eviction, including 542 evaluated offspring, subsequently entered the breeding bands. Overall strict best-parent beats fell from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 526/4,350 (12.09%), and incumbent gains fell from 218 to 175. Mean final-best score fell from 0.544374 to 0.514684, a paired change of -0.029690. All three seed deltas were negative, as were all five task means. The retention mechanism and changed breeding support are confirmed; the intended score improvement was not observed.

molecular.headline: Large repeated aromatic assemblies coexist with compact but reactive carbonyl, amine and fluorinated ring families
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete paired Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9138 to 0.9862 and ring-closure presence from 0.9644 to 0.9908. Charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters report SMILES features, not aromatic atom fractions, actual ionization or feasible stereochemistry. The output spans compact aza-lactams and aryl carbonyl compounds, large aromatic heterocycle assemblies, polyamines attached to constrained rings, expanded cyclic dicarbonyl systems and fluorinated imino/carbonyl polycycles. Tiny fragments coexist with extensive repeated-module growth. This is especially visible in deco_hop, with mean SMILES length 105.0 and maximum 242; high and final molecules contain many linked aromatic or nitrogen-dione units. Compared with the Parent, broad chemical themes persist while ring topology and substituents change. N-F, peroxides, cumulene imines, unusual sulfur bonding and unspecified ring junctions remain material limitations. Overall synthesis is questionable and drug-like quality weak, although some conventional carbonyl and amine subseries are much more plausible than the extreme products. Diversity across seeds is moderate, with related families dominating late output.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule is a moderately sized aryl-substituted aza-lactam with alkyl groups and an O-linked cumulated imine side chain. Other high members are fused oxygen/nitrogen heterocycles carrying aryl thioester, ketone or amide groups. Seed 2 retains indole-carboxamide and fused lactam relatives. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9793 and halogen presence is 0.8184. The core carbonyl/heteroaromatic chemistry is recognizable, but N-O bridges, cumulene imines and unusual fused-ring arrangements complicate complete synthesis. Compared with the Parent ketone/amide and sulfur-containing ring families, the successful region still centres on bounded aromatic carbonyl structures.
liabilities: Cumulated imine, N-F and thioester functionality introduces reactivity or stability concerns despite familiar carbonyl fragments.
Constrained oxygen/nitrogen ring fusion, occasional peroxide-containing relatives and tiny fragmented products limit chemical coherence.
missing_features: Stable alternatives to the cumulated imine and N-O-containing fused linkages are underrepresented around the favorable aryl/carbonyl arrangement.
Configurations of stereogenic lactam or fused-ring centres and geometric isomers are unspecified; a unique required target fragment cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best aryl aza-lactam/cumulated-imine molecule scores 0.4470018114651393 versus the Parent seed-1 maximum of 0.4126819838532174. Fluorinating its terminal imine nitrogen gives 0.41930905650182426. Other current seeds have lower maxima than their paired Parents, although fused aryl thioester and ketone members reach 0.4238198477630873 and 0.4207408531749377. Tiny fluorosulfur, hydrocarbon and fluoroalkene fragments score 0.0. The evidence favors the complete aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over fragment-sized products and does not show a general need for reactive nitrogen fluorination.

per_task.generated_character: The highest seed-1 structures are large multiaryl aza-heterocycles containing cyclic carbonyl or imino groups, ether links, fluorinated aromatic partners and a fused cyclic sulfide. Closely scoring variants add more aromatic rings, aryl peroxide connections or hypochlorite O-Cl. Seeds 0 and 2 generate repeated nitrogen-dione/aza-aromatic assemblies with carbonyl, N-N, ester or thioester links, including N-Cl/N-F variants. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9862 and halogen presence is 0.7586. The Parent also generated expanded heterocyclic assemblies; the current high region remains heavily aromatic and often much larger than conventional small-molecule frameworks. Whole-molecule synthesis is doubtful despite recognizable individual rings.
liabilities: Large repeated aromatic assemblies create severe size, solubility, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
Peroxide, O-Cl, N-halogen, thioester and constrained unsaturation variants add chemical instability or reactivity.
missing_features: Compact accessible versions of the favorable heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the very large late products.
Stable replacements for aryl peroxide, N-halogen and labile multicarbonyl/thioester linkages are not systematically demonstrated at comparable attachment geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best seed-1 assembly scores 0.6112877583465819 versus the paired Parent maximum of 0.6324703199409752; all current paired maxima are lower. Contracting its cyclic sulfide ring gives the same 0.6112877583465819. Larger peroxide/polyaryl variants score 0.6104792370120253 or 0.6100296233601354, so their added complexity is not consistently rewarded. Related ordinary versus cumulated unsaturation variants tie at 0.6087949743003997. Tiny hypochlorite, fluorinated and nitrogen fragments score 0.5. The recurring heteroaromatic/carbonyl arrangement matters, but these plateau-like differences do not establish a need for repeated module growth or reactive linking groups.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest seed-0 family combines fluorinated/chlorinated aromatic rings, a branched polyamine side chain and a tightly fused nitrogen/sulfur ring system. Its exocyclic carbon-sulfur double bond is attached to a sulfur atom that also has ring bonds, rather than being an ordinary terminal thione. A carbon analogue and less fused nitrogen-ring relatives also score well. Seed 1 contains aminoalcohol/cyclobutane compounds with aryl peroxide, while seed 2 favors bulky halogenated aryl amines and cyclic aminals. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9747 and halogen presence is 0.9908. The Parent already reached high scores with aromatic amines; the current strongest family adds more unusual sulfur and constrained geometry.
liabilities: Multiply substituted sulfur with a carbon-sulfur double bond and tightly fused small rings raise stability and geometric concerns.
Aryl peroxides, heavy halogenation, excessive aromatic/amine growth and unspecified stereochemistry remain liabilities across the seeds.
missing_features: Stable conventionally bonded ring systems preserving the successful aromatic/polyamine spacing are underrepresented despite the favorable matched carbon analogue.
Defined ring-junction and side-chain configurations, together with relevant amine protonation alternatives, are absent from the displayed comparisons.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The current maximum is 0.9588472066915413 versus 0.9908331648929692 for Parent seed 0; the other current paired maxima are also lower. In a matched related pair, the carbon-based exocyclic-methylene ring scores 0.9397317511626203, above the sulfur counterpart at 0.8659731726809178. Thus unusual sulfur is not necessary for a high-scoring aromatic/polyamine arrangement. Early acidic amide chemistry scores 0.000719339566735797, and small isolated aromatic or oxygenated fragments also score poorly. A large doubled amine/aryl final product scores 0.04592415123929657, showing that adding another similar module can lose the favorable arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 family links a quinoline or naphthalene-like aromatic group through a short alkyl chain to an expanded nitrogen-rich cyclic dicarbonyl system. It contains several N-methyl groups, an exocyclic amino/enamine region and, in relatives, a saturated version of that region. Other seeds retain fused aromatic lactam/dione frameworks. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and ring-closure presence is 0.9908. The most successful current family is comparatively recognizable and less densely fused than many other outputs, although a large heterocyclic ring still requires controlled synthesis. The Parent seed-2 chemistry already combined an aza-aromatic group with an expanded nitrogen/carbonyl ring.
liabilities: Expanded N-methyl-rich cyclic carbonyl systems may be conformationally complex and synthetically demanding.
Growth into more fused frameworks and fragment-sized proposals adds complexity or loses the intact favorable arrangement without a consistent score benefit.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
