approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from accepted, score-ranked survivors using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. A fingerprint Gaussian process learned from all earlier accepted scores selects each evaluation batch by correlated posterior draws over the fresh pool. The Parent also verifies stable canonical identities before pool admission, normalizing confirmed aliases without replacing the checked graph. Its bond-change move alters bond order; it has no direct move that shifts an intact side group to a neighboring aromatic position while keeping the whole molecule's composition.
approach.novelty: Add intact pendant-branch relocation to the existing bond-change menu: detach an acyclic side group from an aromatic carbon and reconnect that same group to an adjacent aromatic carbon bearing a hydrogen. This exposes substitution-position alternatives while preserving the group, ring framework and formula. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation or survival, protected all first-parent rings, redirected halogen growth, protected carbonyl atoms, or stabilized identity keys. None tested this positional move in their fresh graph pools. A different graph-walk lineage evaluated ten such moves but retained none; this experiment tests whether the Parent's existing learned pool selection can put a useful positional alternative into accepted breeding ancestry.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_bond menu with relocation of an intact single-attachment acyclic branch from an aromatic carbon to an adjacent hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon, exposing positional isomers to the inherited fresh-pool selector while preserving the branch, ring framework and molecular formula.

finding_summary.headline: Positional moves reached useful breeding ancestry, but the panel score fell slightly
finding_summary.insights:
The fresh-pool selector and accepted-survivor breeder can carry a useful positional edit into later ancestry, resolving the earlier graph-walk experiment's absence of retained relocation winners. The demonstrated benefit is narrow: two of 13 evaluated one-atom moves improved their parents, while none of seven evaluated multi-atom moves did. Keeping a larger branch intact therefore establishes access to positional alternatives without establishing better scores. A score-neutral methyl relocation also entered extensive later ancestry, so immediate parent improvement and later usefulness are different observations.

Two final-best molecules have recorded relocation ancestry, but subsequent edits and crossover prevent assigning their endpoint gains to a conserved moved group. Changing the option menu also changes the search path, so the paired panel measures the complete method; it supplies no scores for unselected alternatives. The molecular assessment still finds concentrated aromatic polycycles, reactive heteroatom bonds, strained ring arrangements and unspecified stereochemistry. Local formula and ring conservation did not resolve those chemical limitations, and the panel loss leaves the registered score-benefit expectation refuted even though construction, evaluated positional access and useful breeding ancestry are confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
All 368 sampled branch reconnections preserved the registered atom and bond counts, molecular formula, branch composition and aromatic ring framework. Of the 365 moves that changed molecular identity, 362 reached pools and 20 were evaluated with the relocated attachment still present. The evaluated set contained 13 one-atom and seven multi-atom branches. Two moves beat their generating parents; both moved fluorine. Sixteen evaluated products survived their batch, and 14 were chosen as breeding parents 979 times across 972 later attempts. One fluorine shift increased its source score from 0.382775 to 0.394039, raised the incumbent, and was reused in 444 attempts with 85 later accepted descendants. Every evaluated multi-atom move scored below its best generating parent.

Mean final-best score across three seeds was 0.542797, versus 0.544374 for the Parent: a paired change of -0.001577, which misses the required +0.002 gain. Seed variation decreased from a population standard deviation of 0.013310 to 0.004718, but the paired seed changes were mixed. All 435 pools filled to 160 candidates and all 4,350 proposed evaluations were accepted. Stable identity bookkeeping was preserved; its inherited guard rejected seven unstable representations before pool admission.

molecular.headline: Aromatic polycycles and halogenated amines dominate; reactive bonds, strained ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and Parent trajectories were read; no objective lacks trajectories. Each current task digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The output contains substantial aromatic and heteroaromatic ring systems, carbonyl-rich aza rings, halogenated aryl groups, saturated amines, and seed-dependent fused or bridged families. Ring-closure text rates range from 0.9736 to 0.9931 and aromatic-atom presence rates from 0.8966 to 0.9862. These are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not atom fractions or measured ring counts. Charged and stereocentre text rates are 0.0 throughout. Neutral strings nevertheless contain potentially basic amines, and graph inspection identifies unassigned stereocentres in several leading products. There is moderate diversity across the complete panel, with much narrower families within individual seeds and their high-scoring excerpts. Familiar medicinal fragments coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide or N-O linkages, unusual small ring annulations, crowded aminal centres, and occasional extensive duplication of ring systems. Compared with Parent n-213e85380e04, the leading chemotypes have changed, but these broad chemical liabilities remain. Synthetic plausibility is questionable rather than uniformly absent: plausible substructures do not establish a route to each full structure, its stability, or its stereochemistry. The comparisons below use recorded molecule-score associations only. They do not identify an unseen target structure, establish experimental activity, or attribute changes to the algorithm mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The better products are compact multi-ring molecules with small alkyl substituents and a separate aryl or pyridyl surface. One family retains indole carboxanilide or N-hydroxyamide chemistry; another combines a nitrile, hydroxymethyl ether, fluoropyridyl appendage and a fused unsaturated carbocycle or imine ring. The leading molecule has an O/N-containing benzofused ring, an annulated unsaturated four-membered carbocycle, and an aryl N-formyl substituent carrying an N-S-F connection. The higher cyano/imine examples also contain a four-membered fused ring. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.7, with ring-closure presence 0.9828, aromatic presence 0.9747 and halogen presence 0.8632. The small fragments are outliers, not the dominant output. The Parent led with a bridged aromatic ketone/fluoropyridyl family; the current leading structures retain comparable compact aromatic character while redistributing the polar groups and ring connectivity. Neither set establishes routine synthesis for its unusual core.
liabilities: The leading N-S-F connection, an N-fluorinated heteroaromatic analogue, and N-O-rich variants deserve separate chemical scrutiny; they are not ordinary aryl fluorination.
The fused unsaturated four-membered rings impose geometric and synthetic constraints despite their valid molecular representations.
Late products can either lose almost the entire substantial scaffold or concatenate it into much larger low-scoring assemblies.
missing_features: The very small low-scoring products lack the combined aromatic surfaces, compact scaffold and distributed polar groups present in the better products; the very large repeated products fail to retain that compact arrangement.

The high-scoring excerpt provides limited chemically routine alternatives preserving these spatial relationships without short unsaturated ring annulations or unusual heteroatom bonds. The scores do not identify an additional mandatory target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The leading annulated aryl/formamide product scores 0.4567167360350841, while two differently connected cyano/imine/fluoropyridyl products both score 0.4423126980074005. The brominated and chlorinated N-hydroxyamide congeners also have the same recorded score, 0.42927028031283077. These examples support a compact aromatic/polar-group arrangement without identifying a uniquely required carbonyl, nitrile or halogen. Hydrogen peroxide, molecular fluorine and the small cyclic peroxide each score 0.0. At the opposite size extreme, a late concatenated cyano/heteroaryl product scores 4.0536924658459062e-22 despite repeating features present in better molecules. The Parent seed-0 leading ketone scored 0.4463521672202675; the changed leading chemistry does not establish that the new N-S-F linkage or small ring is independently beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The output is dominated by aromatic, nitrogen-rich carbonyl heterocycles, frequently joined to more aromatic rings or repeated heterocyclic units. The leading compact family carries a diaryl thioketone connection, aza-heteroaromatic rings, short O-containing annulation, an N-fluoromethyl substituent and a fused dicarbonyl core. Nitroso substituents, long unsaturated chains, thioketones and short O/N annulations create distinct stability or synthetic challenges; their coexistence should not be conflated with ordinary carbonyl heterocycle chemistry.
Extensive aromatic repetition and unspecific alkene or ring stereochemistry complicate interpretation of the whole molecules.

The highest molecule has an N-fluorinated ring nitrogen, an exocyclic N-fluoro imine and a substituted fluorocyclobutane; nearby products have an imino NH and an unsaturated five-membered carbocycle. Another high family combines fluorinated unsaturated oxygen rings with N-formyl, urea-like and amidine/imine connections. The best excerpt has imines and amidic nitrogens but lacks the pendant primary aliphatic amine prominent in the Parent leading aryl/dicarbonyl family. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.6, ring-closure presence 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.8966 and halogen presence 0.7425. This output includes more nonaromatic unsaturation than the other leading families, not an absence of rings. Its carbonyls and fluoroalkyl chemistry are recognizable components, but N-F bonds, aldehydes, enol ethers and densely substituted small rings make the complete products less routine. The cyclobutane centres and relevant alkenes are not stereochemically specified.
liabilities: Ring N-F and exocyclic imine N-F bonds are chemically different from aryl or alkyl C-F bonds; their presence at the high end does not establish ordinary medicinal suitability.
Aldehydes, alkenyl ethers and imine-rich connections add reactivity or hydrolytic-stability questions.
Densely substituted small carbocycles have unresolved stereochemistry, and late repeated-core molecules demonstrate that the output can lose the compact feature balance entirely.
missing_features: The current leading excerpt lacks the pendant primary aliphatic amine combined with a compact fluorinated aryl/dicarbonyl core seen in the Parent higher-scoring family. This is an observed lost chemotype, not evidence that appending an amine to the present core must help.
Low-scoring repeated-core and extra-aldehyde products fail to maintain the compact substitution and polar-group balance shared by their better relatives.

Chemically stable alternatives to N-fluorinated imine or ring-nitrogen substitution, and explicit stereochemical alternatives for the substituted carbocycles, are poorly represented among the leading products. No unseen target-specific group can be inferred with certainty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.0020944534688323298. The leading cyclobutane/N-fluoro-imine product scores 0.5046700396010708, compared with 0.5021772038235389 for its imino-NH counterpart. The nearby unsaturated five-membered-ring counterpart scores 0.4824086736309621; several connectivity, hydrogenation and substitution changes accompany that comparison, so no single ring-size effect is isolated. Replacing the fluorine on the substituted cyclobutane carbon with another aldehyde in the imino-NH family gives the final product at 0.009842960423191969. A late product concatenating the related heterocycle/carbocycle motif scores 3.061073839484404e-28. The observed gradient therefore distinguishes compact substitution/polarity combinations sharply and does not reward simply adding more carbonyls or repeating the core. The Parent leading aminomethyl/fluorinated-aryl/dicarbonyl molecule scored 0.5845583988949146. Its primary-amine arrangement is absent from the current leading excerpt, but these different scaffolds do not isolate an amine-addition effect.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-scoring structures contain N-F, imine N-F, N-Cl/N-Br, O-Cl, N-O-F and N-S-F connections. A methyl ester and its carboxyl O-Cl analogue have the identical recorded score 0.6013814616755793, so feedback does not always distinguish an ordinary peripheral group from a reactive alternative.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish ordinary carbon-bound halogens from reactive heteroatom-halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically ordinary substitutions that preserve the surrounding scaffold and polar-group role while distinguishing the atom and bond context of a halogen edit. Treat stability-aware alternatives as a generator capability to test, without assuming that a generic halogen removal increases score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes late repeated-core products at 4.0536924658459062e-22 and 3.061073839484404e-28 while their compact related families reach 0.4423126980074005 and 0.5021772038235389. Another output has mean SMILES length 94.4 and maximum 247, showing that large assemblies remain accessible; these are string lengths, not molecular weights.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve compact feature arrangements when it combines substantial ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide connected scaffold recombination and simplification options that retain useful aromatic/polar-group arrangements without automatically duplicating large cores. Adapt size changes to observed feedback rather than imposing a universal preferred size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring excerpts include fused unsaturated four-membered rings, a chorded carbon bicycle with fused four-membered rings, short O/N annulations, and crowded aminal polycycles. Less exotic aza/carbonyl and aryl/amine structures also receive high recorded scores, so these unusual closures are not a demonstrated general requirement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator offers limited routine ring-topology alternatives within several of its leading chemical families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make accessible ring-framework alternatives that retain approximate substituent spacing and functional-group identity without introducing short strained closures. Assess geometry and synthetic interpretability alongside graph validity; more rings or more distinct strings alone do not establish useful coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has stereocentre text rate 0.0. The cited leading aminal/benzylic-amine molecules and aldehyde-substituted cyclobutane molecules contain unassigned tetrahedral centres on direct graph inspection, and unsaturated side chains also lack specified geometric alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not demonstrate explicit stereochemical exploration of its substituted saturated and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Retain chemically meaningful stereochemical annotations and make bounded, valid stereoisomer alternatives accessible when edits create or preserve stereogenic centres. The current observations establish a coverage gap, not a measured score benefit from assigning a particular stereoisomer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has charged text rate 0.0 despite cited secondary amines, tertiary cyclic amines, flexible polyamines and imine/amidine-like groups. Thus the missing representation capability is not a universal absence of nitrogen or potentially basic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not document chemically justified alternative ionization states for the amines they already contain.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve plausible ionization alternatives in a chemically controlled way when relevant functional groups are present. Establish how those alternatives relate to downstream normalization before assuming the neutral proposal strings imply missing evaluator protonation or a score penalty.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Parent leading compact fluorinated aryl/dicarbonyl family contained a pendant primary amine; the current corresponding leading excerpt instead concentrates on aldehyde-bearing carbocycles, imines and N-F groups. Elsewhere, conventional methyl ester chemistry and reactive O-Cl chemistry share the same score, while multiple seed-specific high families remain recognizable variants of their own unusual core.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain distinct useful functional-group families while changing ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support moves that retain intact polar groups and their attachment context across meaningful scaffold alternatives, so familiar functional-group families remain accessible during structural changes. Use observed feedback to determine where retention helps; neither adding the same group everywhere nor preserving every incumbent ring is implied.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent molecular prior and chooses its prepared checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid, connected, distinct molecular yield, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts an adaptable copy of that prior and an accepted-only archive; trajectory-balance updates with a learned normalizer and fixed-prior regularization transfer real graph feedback into later neural sampling. One direct neural batch alternates with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population and supply a protected descendant at the first graph handoff. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations construct temporary novel offspring pools, and accepted-score fingerprint posterior function draws choose the remaining evaluations. The atom-replacement mutation currently changes one element at one site, so moving a ring nitrogen while retaining composition requires multiple separately sampled substitutions.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with a direct positional exchange between a pyridine-like nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same aromatic six-member ring. The exchange moves the nitrogen while preserving the formula, ring connectivity and substituent attachment positions, making a new local arrangement available in one edit. Earlier Children in this lineage changed prior preparation, replay, flow credit or neural sampling. This Child changes graph generation. A previous graph-walk experiment established that this exchange can yield scored positional isomers but exposed very few of them and missed its score target; the new question is whether the Parent's larger temporary pools and posterior selection turn that same positional channel into useful accepted descendants.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing graph replace_atom option menu with a direct formula-preserving exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, retaining the ring connectivity and substituent attachment framework.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per objective. The molecules include linked and fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, aryl sulfonamides, lactams, ethers, imidates and fluorinated urea/hydrazine chains. This is broad chemical exploration with concentrated upper-score families, rather than a shortage of rings or nitrogen. In the fixed objective order, the digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9874, 0.9885, 0.992, 0.9943 and 0.9874; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9655, 0.9667 and 0.8437. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the markers, not fractions of their atoms that are aromatic. Read-only RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 30, 33 and 25, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2. The corresponding Parent medians are 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 heavy atoms, and 3, 4, 4, 4 and 3 rings. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts in the current proposals are 655, 600, 588, 641 and 532, although many represent local ring edits or enlarged assemblies rather than independent useful core families. Conventional makeable-looking fragments coexist with N-Cl bonds, O-O bonds, imines, hydrazine-derived linkages, strained small rings, conjugated enlarged rings and highly charged oxygen environments. The digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0 on every objective; graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals respectively. Thus unspecified stereochemistry is a real representational gap, rather than evidence that the molecules are all achiral. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are mixed. The recorded scores support chemical associations within these samples; they do not establish a synthesis, a binding pose, or a causal contribution from any particular generator edit.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant upper family has a phenyl ring joining a diazine bearing an imidate or imine to a conjugated seven-member oxygen ring. The two highest digest examples each have 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic six-member rings and one nonaromatic seven-member oxepin-like ring. Other high entries replace the imidate with an amidine-containing aryl ether, change diazine nitrogen positions, or use a methoxyindole-carbonyl-imidazole-pyridyl assembly. These are moderately sized, largely unsaturated molecules, with polar groups placed on an extended ring framework. Their functional groups are chemically recognizable, but the imidates, imines and conjugated enol-ether ring make stability and synthetic handling less routine than for ordinary aryl amides. The full proposal median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; tiny fragments and much larger branched structures also occur. Compared with the Parent, the upper chemistry shifts from fused aza-ring/amide and unusual sulfur-containing families toward linked diazine/oxygen-ring imidates. The median aromatic-ring count falls from three in the Parent to two here, while median total ring count stays at three.
liabilities: The leading imidate/imine and conjugated oxygen-ring combinations warrant scrutiny for hydrolysis, tautomerism and chemical stability; their recorded scores do not measure these properties.

Late examples introduce ring expansion, a small imine-containing ring or thiol substitution without retaining the highest recorded scores. Increased ring or heteroatom complexity is not itself evidence of improved chemistry.
The full proposals include N-Cl and O-O bonds, and the large low-score assemblies can contain multiple unspecified stereocentres.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the connected aromatic framework and polar handles shared by the upper families; the largest poor examples lack their moderate size and limited elaboration. Those features are not preserved consistently across the output.

The upper excerpt shows conventional carbonyl chemistry mainly in a separate indole family, while the dominant linked-ring series relies on imidates, imines and amidines. Equally favorable, chemically varied polar-group arrangements within that same linked framework are not established by the shown molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.0 to 0.49065338146265813, with median 0.163735. The two cited diazine nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813, so these examples do not show a universal preference for relocating a ring nitrogen. The analogous imine scores 0.4786541264696099, and the alternate diazine imidate scores 0.4789131426105757. Contracting the oxygen ring gives 0.46746448265590934; the cited less-unsaturated seven-member version gives 0.38212123769975087. The separate indole-carbonyl family reaches 0.4586023950591373. Together these observations favor a moderate molecular size and particular ring/polar-group arrangements, with both heteroatom placement and saturation mattering locally. Methane scores 0.0, whereas a 50-heavy-atom multiring amide/ether assembly scores 2.2628488414681176e-49. Neither minimal fragments nor accumulation of rings and polar groups reproduces the upper-score chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The upper excerpt is concentrated on an anilinoquinazoline-like scaffold: a fused aromatic diazine/benzene system linked through NH to a substituted phenyl ring. Methoxy or other alkoxy groups, halogens and a terminal aryl formaldimine recur. The highest example has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-member rings, but also an O-N(Cl)-ethyl substituent containing both N-O and N-Cl bonds. A simpler dimethoxy member has 24 heavy atoms. The fused aza core, arylamine link and ordinary ethers are plausible synthetic building blocks; the N-chlorinated hydroxylamine ether and formaldimine are less conventional final medicinal functionality. Another trajectory ends with nitrogen-dense fused systems, small fused rings and multiple explicitly negative oxygens. The current full median is 31 heavy atoms and four rings, compared with 36 heavy atoms and four rings in the Parent. The Parent upper chemistry included larger linked quinazoline-like systems and carbonyl-bearing piperazine derivatives, so the current prominent family is a smaller connected aza-aromatic arrangement, not newly acquired aromaticity.
liabilities: N-Cl-bearing hydroxylamine ethers and terminal methylene imines introduce reactive functionality into the strongest-scoring family. Even the simpler dimethoxy analogue retains the imine.

Some final structures combine heavily fused small rings with alkoxide-like and N-O anions; the cited multiply negative molecule has no accompanying counterion in its SMILES. Charge and valence validity do not establish a plausible dominant chemical state.
The full optimizer set contains 121 molecules with an O-O bond, and its charged-marker rate is 0.2264. These features are materially present rather than isolated textual curiosities.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring sulfonyl or nitrogen-rich structures lack the specific aryl-NH-diazine connection and alkoxy substitution context shared by the upper molecules. Total aromaticity and nitrogen content do not substitute for this local arrangement.

The highest excerpt does not show broad coverage of different cores retaining an equally favorable attachment pattern; it mostly repeats one aza-aromatic family with peripheral variations. Chemically conservative alternatives to its reactive peripheral groups are only partially represented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.2712455185234365 to 0.9410803537101116, with median 0.579468. The N-Cl-containing leader scores 0.9410803537101116 and its cited less-fluorinated analogue scores 0.9369083259163363. The simple dimethoxy scaffold and several chlorinated alkoxy or thioether variants all score exactly 0.9331819976312673 despite differing size and local reactivity. That plateau is consistent with emphasis on the common scaffold and attachment pattern, with limited discrimination among these peripheral groups. A stilbene-sulfone chain terminating in a hydroxamate scores 0.2712455185234365, and a multiaryl sulfone/sulfonamide structure scores 0.29444616217051867. They supply rings and polar atoms without reproducing the upper anilino-aza-ring context. The cited terminal nitrogen-rich fused structures score 0.6068151045584474 and 0.5985804416403786, showing that more ring nitrogens and more fusion alone do not reproduce the leading arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The upper molecules combine substantial aromatic surfaces with accessible aliphatic amines. The highest example is a 23-heavy-atom dibenzocycloheptane-like tricycle bearing a dimethylaminoethyl chain, phenol and amino substituents. Other high examples use a fused pyrrole/aryl framework with an N-methylpiperidine or dimethylaminoalkyl group. Another seed produces halogenated polycyclic amines carrying an aziridine and an aminoethyl branch. The final excerpt also contains aryl ethers linked to N-methylpyrrolidine or piperazine. These families have recognizable medicinal amine/aromatic organization, although some constrained cores are synthetically demanding and the aziridines deserve separate scrutiny. The full median is 30 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings, matching the Parent on these descriptors. The Parent leading examples included long-linker arylpiperazines and bridged oxygen-containing aryl amines; the prominent current examples shift toward compact aryl tricycles with shorter aminoalkyl connections. The charged-marker rate of 0.0103 does not imply a shortage of potentially basic centres: ordinary neutral amine SMILES are abundant.
liabilities: The halogenated polycyclic family includes an aziridine, adding a strained nitrogen-containing three-member ring to an already constrained scaffold.

Potential tetrahedral stereocentres occur in 601 of the 870 optimizer proposals, while the digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. The leading amino-substituted tricycle itself has an unspecified tetrahedral centre.

Some high examples combine several amines with phenol, aniline or thiol groups and complicated fused/bridged frameworks. Their ionization, chemical stability and synthetic tractability are not determined by the recorded scalar scores.
missing_features: Several weak chemotypes lack a comparably accessible aliphatic amine in the aromatic framework. Amide, sulfonamide and pyrrole nitrogen do not reproduce the same chemical environment, even when the molecules contain multiple nitrogen atoms.

Stereochemically specified versions of the constrained amine-bearing cores are absent from the proposal strings. Their possible three-dimensional alternatives remain unresolved; the shown scores do not establish which configuration, if any, would be preferable.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 3.8021829379963674e-05 to 0.9971131223195837, with median 0.265948. nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible original strings from a memory of thirty-two earlier elites. Historical fitting weights decrease with previous training exposure while current and historical groups retain their total loss shares. The policy fits weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, projecting each positive target independently to zero, using bounded clipped Adam updates and retaining the final policy. It then samples complete SMILES directly from the adapted policy and submits the first valid, canonically novel identities in sample order, refilling when necessary and discarding surplus draws.
approach.novelty: Add progressive spacing of repeated molecular cores during admission. The first new molecule with a ring-and-linker core is admitted immediately. Once that core occupies k places in the current batch, its next admission requires k+1 further distinct valid draws of that core; intervening draws are discarded. Other newly encountered cores can therefore reach the same batch, while a dominant core remains admissible and no randomness is added. Earlier siblings diversified retained training memory or balanced choices of breeding parents. This change acts directly on fresh policy samples before oracle submission, leaving both training membership rules and token generation intact. Same-stream admission receipts will show whether additional cores actually reach evaluation. The earlier diversity experiments also warn that spacing a productive family can weaken exploitation.

nodes.hypothesis: Deterministically thin repeated atom/bond-typed Murcko cores within each suggestion: after k molecules of a core have been emitted, admit its next member only on the (k+1)-th distinct valid canonical-novel draw of that core since its preceding emission, resetting that per-core interval after admission; first occurrences and identity-keyed acyclic or extraction-fallback draws pass immediately.

finding_summary.headline: Core thinning delivered broader molecular batches, but final Top-1 fell despite higher AUC.
finding_summary.insights:
The experiment resolves the delivery question: additional cores already present in fresh policy samples can reach the oracle without losing the first-come batch's core support. That delivery was often unproductive. Of the 242 additional core representatives, only six improved the actual incumbent: four on zaleplon and two on docking. Deco-hop received 116 additional core representatives without an incumbent improvement from any of them. Its previously dominant phenyl/anilinoquinazoline core was evaluated 54 times instead of 160 and reached a lower best score. This is compatible with diluted exploitation, although unscored discarded molecules cannot identify the value of any particular forgone proposal.

Coverage is also a poor predictor of the magnitude of the final change. Sitagliptin gained only seven batch-level cores yet had the largest mean endpoint loss. Admission changes alter later feedback and therefore later generated streams; a same-stream comparison isolates immediate delivery, not the complete search that would have followed different admissions. The higher AUC and lower endpoint further separate earlier progress from the final objective.

The chemical assessment narrows what broader coverage did not repair. Productive functional-group attachment arrangements remain inconsistently preserved, and the many structures with potential stereochemistry still have no specified configurations. Those are open chemical capabilities, not established causes of this score loss. Useful next evidence would need to show that broader admission preserves productive local series or transfers their attachment chemistry, rather than using core count as a proxy for usefulness. The utility claim is rejected while the admission and delivery mechanism is confirmed.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism ran correctly and changed which constitutional cores reached evaluation. Across 435 batches, it rejected 436 eligible repeated-core draws in 167 batches. Comparing each recorded stream with its first ten valid novel structures, actual batches gained cores 159 times and never lost a previously represented core. Mean core count increased from 9.106 to 9.662, delivering 242 additional batch-level core representatives and changing 304 canonical output identities. Mean core concentration fell from 0.133 to 0.110. All state transitions, original-string provenance and paired behavior before the first intervention passed the passive audit.

All fifteen task sessions completed their budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.522705 to 0.508247, a paired change of -0.014458 against the required +0.002 increase. Seed changes were +0.009826, -0.032176 and -0.021023; population dispersion across seed scores changed from 0.020072 to 0.019593. Task mean changes were -0.014692 for zaleplon, -0.014459 for deco-hop, -0.005454 for median-2 and -0.037685 for sitagliptin; docking decreased by only 0.000000211 near its ceiling. Recorded mean AUC nevertheless rose from 0.405593 to 0.430066, chiefly through earlier progress on docking and zaleplon.

Broader batches required more work. Raw draws increased from 35,568 to 36,880, and batches needing extra sampling increased from 16 to 28. Raw duplication rose from 32.21% to 34.50%, while validity fell from 91.79% to 91.11%. No generation limit was exhausted. Recorded generation time rose from 24.75 to 37.90 seconds across the panel, including 10.38 seconds for core extraction and 0.52 seconds for receipts; the interval gate itself took 0.009 seconds.

molecular.headline: Broad aromatic and heterocyclic chemistry, but undefined stereochemistry and uneven preservation of productive functional-group arrangements.
molecular.overall_character:
Node n-33f9aab34e21 produces recognizable medicinal-chemistry families: fused azaaromatics and indoles bearing amides or carbamates, decorated anilinoquinazolines, arylpiperazines and other saturated ring amines, and arylsulfonylpiperazines. It also produces long-chain, peptide-like, unusually connected and highly elaborated polycyclic structures. Across the five covered tasks, each digest contains 900 accepted records, including 870 optimizer proposals across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Ring-closure text rates range from 0.9816 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom text rates from 0.9379 to 0.9943; these are molecule-presence counters, not fractions of atoms or RDKit ring counts. Halogen text rates range from 0.3161 to 0.8. The global output is constitutionally broad.

The passive RDKit 2023.09.6 audit reads all 30 supplied child and Parent trajectories, totaling 9,000 accepted records. Every child optimizer record parses, which establishes accepted-structure validity rather than raw-generation validity or makeability. Child median heavy-atom counts in the fixed task order are 24, 33, 28, 23.5 and 24; median perceived ring counts are 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3. Distinct atom/bond-typed Murcko keys, with each acyclic identity counted independently, are 577, 473, 626, 749 and 792, versus Parent counts 542, 360, 598, 740 and 791. These are full-panel constitutional coverage measurements, not evidence about admission activation or utility. The diverse global inventory coexists with much narrower families among the digest best molecules.

All five digest stereocentre text rates are zero. The structural audit finds potential tetrahedral centres in 1,159 of the 4,350 child optimizer appearances, with no assigned centres; 722 appearances have potential double-bond stereochemistry, with none specified. Counts are appearances across independent sessions, not distinct compounds. The Parent also has no assigned centres. Saturated and bridged ring construction therefore does not establish stereochemical definition. The ordinary aryl-amide, heteroaryl and piperazine members look synthetically plausible at the motif level, while unusual neutral sulfur valence, small imine rings, N-N/N-O arrangements and complex unassigned polycycles make the overall makeability judgement mixed. No synthesis route, isolated stereoisomer, biological activity or score causality is established by these records. The audit and its exact digest witnesses are recorded in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0012-02-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json, generated by the adjacent .audit.py. All five objectives have trajectories; none is omitted.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are predominantly compact aromatic amides and carbamates, with indole/other fused azaaromatic cores, pendant phenyl or pyridyl groups, and occasional partly saturated heterocycles. Median size is 24 heavy atoms and 3 rings; 593 optimizer appearances contain an amide substructure. The digest best molecules have 23-26 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings. The best, an acetamidoindole bearing a phenyl-substituted isoxazoline, scores 0.48839749189747395 and has an unspecified tetrahedral centre. Other strong examples are an acrylamido methoxyanilinoquinoline and alkynyl or allyl carbamates on a phenyl-substituted fused diazole. Their ordinary aromatic amide chemistry is plausible; the smaller imine-ring and oxygen-rich ring variants deserve individual synthetic assessment. In contrast, the low end includes long hydrocarbon chains, an extensively substituted polycyclic lactone/acid, and a large multiaryl sulfonamide. Relative to the Parent, the accepted inventory has more core keys, 577 versus 542, and more appearances with potential unassigned centres, 167 versus 86, while its median size stays 24 heavy atoms.
liabilities: Large hydrocarbon appendages and crowded multiaryl or polycyclic structures broaden size and conformational burden well beyond the compact high-score examples.

Acrylamides and other conjugated carbonyls, N-O heterocycles and the small imine-ring analogue require contextual reactivity and synthesis assessment; their presence is not itself evidence of an invalid or low-scoring molecule.
missing_features: Many weak proposals fail to retain the compact placement of carbonyl-linked nitrogen and fused aromatic donor/acceptor sites present in the best examples. These groups are demonstrably producible; their productive arrangement is inconsistently preserved during growth or scaffold changes.

The isoxazoline family supplies tetrahedral shape without specifying its configuration. The records do not test whether stereochemical definition changes this objective, and they do not identify a unique absent target ring or substituent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The gradient supports compact composition and precise carbonyl/heteroaromatic attachment rather than ring count alone. Moving the acetamide around the same indole/isoxazoline family gives 0.48839749189747395 versus 0.4767312946227961. On the shared fused-diazole carbamate, the methyl-extended alkynyl group scores 0.4546547989309981, the allyl group 0.4226489847472999, and the terminal-alkyne variant in the final excerpt 0.33748438760743243. These are local associations, not independent effects of unsaturation. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Elaborating an otherwise related aromatic carbonyl compound with a long dicarbonyl chain gives 1.978240337577409e-21, while the 49-heavy-atom multiaryl sulfonamide scores 1.2150684990266398e-23. The final simple diaryl thioamide scores 0.0002269799216711376. Parent terminal best-so-far values were 0.43351949803907636, 0.4767312946227961 and 0.5; child values are 0.48839749189747395, 0.42312329948394145 and 0.4546547989309981. The changed chemistry accompanies mixed seed outcomes.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic proposal set: median 33 heavy atoms, 4 perceived aromatic rings, and a halogen text rate of 0.8. The pooled digest best molecules all come from seed 2 and are dimethoxy anilinoquinazolines with fluorinated aniline substituents and phenyl, pyridyl or thiophenyl arms. Their sizes are 28-34 heavy atoms; most have 4 aromatic rings, with one additional cyclobutane in an elaborated analogue. These are recognizable heteroaryl coupling/amination motifs, though the many aromatic rings and halogenated appendages merit physical-property scrutiny. The full trajectories also include nitro-rich hydrazone/heteroaryl families and fluorinated triaryltriazines in the other seeds; the best excerpt is not representative of every seed. The child has 473 core keys versus the Parent's 360, and its largest exact core appears 62 times versus 160. Quinazoline-containing appearances are 221 versus 341, so broader constitutional coverage coexists with strong local family recurrence.
liabilities: Substantial aromatic and halogen loading and occasional long or bulky appendages create plausible solubility and conformational liabilities; no measured solubility is supplied.

Nitro-rich hydrazones in other seeds and unusual N-N/N-O-containing structures require more synthetic and stability scrutiny than the ordinary anilinoquinazoline members. RDKit parsing alone cannot distinguish those cases.
missing_features: The best excerpt explores aryl identity and fluorination around a persistent dimethoxy/anilino attachment pattern much more than alternative alkoxy arrangements. More extensive alkoxy decoration occurs in the Parent's strong family but is absent from this best excerpt; its causal benefit is untested.

Weak aromatic proposals often lack the particular donor/acceptor and substituent geometry retained in the strong anilinoquinazolines. Aromaticity is already abundant, and the records do not establish a missing universal heterocycle or basic amine requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best pyridyl/difluoroanilino member scores 0.6462372658560631, versus 0.6457672152926415 for its phenyl analogue; adding a further aniline fluorine gives 0.6460892049127344. These differences do not support a simple more-halogen rule. Low-score molecules remain aromatic and often similarly sized, but rearrange the heteroaromatic/linker pattern or introduce sulfone-rich extensions: the benzodioxole/sulfone/unsaturated ester scores 0.2948214550303749, and an elaborated 46-heavy-atom quinazoline with a benzylsulfone extension scores 0.3716299019607843. The final seven-membered cyclic-amine substitution on a related quinazoline scores 0.6061725138485887. The Parent's strongest seed-2 family included more extensive alkoxy decoration and reached 0.6669492630755185; the child reaches 0.6462372658560631. The other child seed endpoints, 0.588961510530138 and 0.6146044624746451, also sit below the corresponding Parent records. Extra accepted core variety does not by itself identify a better chemical answer.

per_task.generated_character: The strong molecules are aromatic anchors joined to nonacylated aliphatic amines, especially arylpiperazines with benzyl/phenylalkyl substituents, and phenolic fused-ring amines joined through alkyl diamine chains. The digest best molecules have 23-31 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings, combining 2-3 aromatic rings with saturated nitrogen rings. Methoxy, thioether, nitrile, fluorine and methyl substituents decorate these families. The full proposal median is 28 heavy atoms and 4 rings. A conservative structural proxy finds a nonaromatic, nonconjugated amine site in 587 optimizer appearances versus 530 in the Parent, and piperazine occurs in 220 versus 201. Basic ring-amine chemistry is therefore plainly present. Parent and child strong families overlap chemically, while later child examples also include bridged phenolic amines and an unusual neutral hydrogen-bearing sulfur ring. Ordinary arylpiperazines are plausible medicinal structures; the complex bridged and unusual sulfur members are less straightforward.
liabilities: Several strong members combine multiple aromatic surfaces with long flexible alkyl chains and multiple amine sites. Those features imply possible physical-property and conformational liabilities that a nearly saturated recorded score does not characterize.

The final sulfur-containing ring has an unusual neutral sulfur bonding pattern, and the more intricate bridged amines leave multiple centres undefined. They should not inherit a makeability claim from the simpler piperazine series.
missing_features: Some low-score ring-containing molecules lack the nonacylated aliphatic amine/aryl attachment context recurrent among the strong molecules, even when they contain a saturated nitrogen ring. This is an attachment-chemistry gap in part of the output, not a generator-wide absence of amines.

The branched and bridged proposals lack assigned stereochemistry. Potential tetrahedral centres occur in 435 child appearances versus 192 in the Parent, with none assigned in either. No score experiment here establishes a stereochemical benefit.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy-substituted biphenyl/piperazine/phenylpropyl molecule and its methylthio counterpart both score 0.9999998674084429, and the branched pyridylalkyl piperazine scores 0.9999998517131371. High scores tolerate considerable aromatic decoration and linker variation around exposed aliphatic amine sites. A low-score heteroarylamide still contains a piperidine ring, but its nitrogen is directly sulfonylated; it scores 1.9828327575562915e-05. The acidic nitro-heteroaromatic amide scores 1.8588450134335675e-05. Counting ring nitrogens without their bonding context misses the observed separation. These are structural associations, not measured pKa values, docking contacts or experimental activity. The final phenolic ring amine scores 0.9971900592268141, whereas the unusual sulfur-ring proposal scores 0.31554657771518013; they are not a matched molecular pair. Parent and child seed endpoints are all already very near the numerical ceiling, so the records cannot resolve a new required pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output is dominated by arylsulfonylpiperazines: naphthylsulfonyl groups on N-methyl/N-ethyl/N-propyl piperazine, and benzodioxane or benzodioxepine arylsulfonyl groups on arylpiperazines. These combine saturated diaza rings, aromatic surfaces, sulfonyl oxygen acceptors and, in some members, ring ethers. Most digest best examples have 20-28 heavy atoms and 3-4 rings; a larger 38-heavy-atom heterocyclic example also appears. Median proposal size is 23.5 heavy atoms and 3 rings. The conventional sulfonylation and N-substitution motifs look plausible; some oxime/hydrazone and polycyclic departures are less straightforward. The full child inventory is broad, with 749 core keys versus 740 in the Parent. Nevertheless, piperazine appearances are 186 versus 231 and sulfonylpiperazine appearances 82 versus 102.
liabilities: Small azide and unusual N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl fragments are chemically unlike the ordinary sulfonylpiperazine series and need separate handling and synthetic assessment.
Some final alternatives add hydrazone/oxime bonds or complicated unassigned polycycles. They expand structures without demonstrating that the strong series' functional arrangement has been retained.
missing_features: Weak fragments and rearranged piperazine/oxime proposals often omit the sulfonyl-linked aromatic and diaza-ring relationship seen near the top. Sulfur, aromaticity or a cyclic amine alone does not reproduce the supported arrangement.

The modest strong-series scores and narrow N-substitution/aryl-position changes do not establish a unique absent bridging group or target scaffold. The observable shortfall is incomplete retention and exploration of the whole successful attachment pattern, despite broad unrelated core coverage.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-methyl naphthylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.23735633163877068, compared with 0.207375126170294 for N-ethyl and 0.20874143036171652 for N-propyl. Alkyl growth is not monotonically rewarded. The benzodioxane-sulfonyl arylpiperazine scores 0.21430090054520579, and its ortho-chloro analogue 0.21766212246744293. A bis-sulfonylpiperazine still scores 0.20796528955536797 despite lacking the ordinary free amine environment of the N-methyl member. The common association is the assembled aryl-sulfonyl/diaza-ring topology rather than a universal basicity requirement. Weak examples include the acyclic allyl azide at 0.0, N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide at 0.007693218186208301 and urea at 0.008404548427654986. A final tolyl N-methylpiperazine without the sulfonyl-linked aromatic component scores 0.14832850691857688. Parent versus child endpoint records are 0.2125118592516207 versus 0.21766212246744293, 0.20428349275442803 versus the same value, and 0.2588686674995393 versus 0.23735633163877068. The best seed-2 family changes from a more elaborate bis-sulfonyl arrangement in the Parent to a simpler naphthyl sulfonamide in the child.

per_task.generated_character: This output is constitutionally dispersed rather than trapped in one scaffold: 792 core keys among 870 optimizer appearances, compared with 791 in the Parent. Median size is 24 heavy atoms and 3 rings. The best molecule is a fluorinated anilide connected through a branched chain to an oxalamide, with 26 heavy atoms, one aromatic ring and an unassigned tetrahedral centre. The next is an N-sulfonyl imidazoline carrying fluorophenyl and methyl-benzoate groups, with 25 heavy atoms and 3 rings. Other strong examples include a guanidino/amino-substituted tetrahydroisoquinoline, compact oxygen/nitrogen ring systems, and nitrogen-rich heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds. Ordinary amide and sulfonamide motifs are plausible, but the more intricate ring connections require individual synthetic assessment. The low end includes multiaryl hydrophobes, long-chain thioether esters, and large peptide-like structures. Potential unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 288 child appearances versus 274 in the Parent.
liabilities: Large peptide-like structures and long hydrocarbon-rich appendages occupy opposite extremes of polarity and flexibility, while both can have negligible recorded scores.

Acylated nitrogens, guanidines, cyclic amidines, thioureas, oximes and nitro heterocycles have different bonding and likely ionization/reactivity contexts. Treating their nitrogen counts as interchangeable would obscure the chemistry, and no measured ionization or stability data are supplied.
missing_features: Many proposals contain fluorinated aryl groups, nitrogen or carbonyls separately without the compact connected polar architecture shown in the stronger examples. The widely different strong scaffolds do not reveal a unique missing target-specific motif.

The best branched anilide and several fused or bridged examples lack specified configuration. Primary aliphatic amino substructures occur in 24 appearances, so total absence of that functionality would be a false diagnosis; its useful attachment context and any stereochemical score dependence remain unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched fluoroanilide/oxalamide scores 0.3085499097640706, the fluorophenyl sulfonylimidazoline 0.3034617343186778, and the nonfluorinated guanidino fused-ring molecule 0.2711448282680827. These examples support moderate size with specific nitrogen/carbonyl/aryl arrangements, but do not isolate fluorination, a free primary amine or one ring class as necessary. Adding fluorines to the sulfonylimidazoline/benzoate family gives 0.18136420222115457, below the less fluorinated member. The low digest examples include a 47-heavy-atom multiaryl structure and a 61-heavy-atom peptide-like structure, both at 0.0; simply adding aromatic or polar material is insufficient. Final fluorinated, heteroatom-rich structures can also be weak: the diaryl pyrazole carboxamide scores 0.00017370401130919412. The reported digest median is 0.0; this rounded summary is not a count of exact-zero records. The Parent's best seed-2 fluoroaryl N-sulfonylamide had a secondary aminoacetyl chain and scored 0.32609684308650033, whereas the child's best anilide/oxalamide has acylated nitrogens and scores 0.3085499097640706. This is a changed polar-linker arrangement, not an isolated amine comparison. Seed 0 retains the same 0.2711448282680827 guanidino structure; seed 1 changes from a carbonyl/thioamide-rich family at 0.26424211308214746 to a heteroaryl thiourea/piperazine at 0.16873483388608349.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five supplied stereocentre text rates are zero. Passive perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 1,159 of 4,350 optimizer appearances and potential double-bond stereochemistry in 722, with no specified instances. The digest includes unassigned centres in strong isoxazoline, branched arylalkylpiperazine, fused-ring amine and branched anilide examples. These are observed representation omissions, not demonstrated explanations for score shortfalls.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits many stereogenic structures but shows no ability to specify their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to represent and vary configuration where the generated graph permits it, preserving full molecular identity and letting its own accepted feedback establish usefulness. Additional ring cores or saturated atoms alone do not supply this capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aryl-linked, nonacylated ring amines occur among digest molecules scoring 0.9999998674084429, while a ring nitrogen directly sulfonylated in a heteroarylamide occurs at 1.9828327575562915e-05. In a different supplied score context, an arylsulfonylpiperazine scores 0.23735633163877068 and a bis-sulfonylpiperazine remains at 0.20796528955536797. These comparisons have multiple structural differences; they show why neither adding nitrogen nor globally avoiding sulfonamides is an adequate chemical prescription.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not consistently preserve the attachment context that makes its amine, carbonyl and sulfonyl motifs chemically distinct.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to learn connected functional-group environments and support modifications that keep a rewarded ring/linker arrangement while varying nearby functionality. Whether nitrogen is aliphatic, aryl-bound, acylated or sulfonylated must remain visible to that task-local learning; no particular amine or sulfur motif should be imposed across objectives.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Compact best examples include 23-26-heavy-atom fused aromatic carbonyl compounds and 18-28-heavy-atom nitrogen/carbonyl-rich compounds. The supplied low-score witnesses include a 49-heavy-atom multiaryl sulfonamide at 1.2150684990266398e-23 and a 61-heavy-atom peptide-like structure at 0.0, while small acyclic urea and unusual N-hydroxy fragments are also weak in their own score contexts. Size is not sufficient: similarly sized aromatic sulfone and anilinoheterocycle structures also differ substantially in recorded score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent local control over growth and truncation around its productive molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need to preserve locally supported size and connected polar/aromatic arrangements while exploring controlled growth, shortening and linker changes. Local accepted evidence should determine useful ranges; a universal size cutoff or extra heteroatom rule would discard the distinction visible in these molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One supplied panel expands from 360 Parent core keys to 473 child keys, yet all twelve digest best examples retain a dimethoxy anilinoquinazoline pattern while largely varying aryl identity and halogen decoration. A stronger Parent member in that family had a different, more extensive alkoxy arrangement. Another panel has 749 child keys but only 82 sulfonylpiperazine appearances versus 102 in the Parent. These are accepted-output associations, not proof that any discarded or ungenerated molecule would improve a score.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad constitutional output is not accompanied by equally broad preservation and variation of productive peripheral chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need support for transferring and varying peripheral functional groups and their attachment geometry across related observed cores, alongside coherent local series within a core. Core novelty alone cannot create missing decoration combinations, and each combination must earn its value from actual feedback rather than a named objective template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest witnesses include an unusual neutral hydrogen-bearing sulfur ring at 0.31554657771518013, an allyl azide at 0.0, an N-hydroxy/trichloromethyl formamide at 0.007693218186208301, and intricately connected unassigned polycycles. Conversely, an N-O-containing isoxazoline scores 0.48839749189747395. The mixture supports contextual chemical scrutiny rather than treating every N-O bond, unusual atom or ring as categorically undesirable.
transferable_gaps.gap: The valid output does not consistently distinguish conventional medicinal structures from unusual bonding and difficult-to-define polycycles.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need chemical plausibility that considers complete bond and valence environments, plausible assembly and stereochemical definition, beyond successful SMILES parsing. Any such capability should preserve supported heterocyclic chemistry and be checked against the actual generated structures rather than a blanket functional-group ban.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

Passive every-raw-return provenance and structural receipts, exact gate-state/count partitions, measured core/gate/receipt regions, and a same-stream first-come admission comparator that never supplies proposals or oracle labels

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two highest-scoring earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current elites with their original accepted strings and scores. The policy fits every selected sequence with equal weight toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward. Up to twelve clipped Adam steps produce the policy that directly samples complete SMILES; chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refill the next batch. A passive uniform-history draw measures the retained score-ordered selector without supplying training examples.
approach.novelty: Add diminishing exposure weights within the selected historical group. Each historical molecule receives a weight inversely proportional to one plus the number of previous fitting batches that used its original identity. Rescale those weights so history keeps exactly the same total share of the loss and current elites keep their existing weights. This shifts influence toward strong historical examples that have been fitted fewer times. The earlier scheduling sibling changed which records trained; this experiment changes the influence of the same selected records. The adaptation siblings tested target normalization, checkpoint restoration and historical-direction protection. None tested cumulative fitting exposure as a loss weight. A chronological weight audit and a comparison with equal-weight gradients on the same policy state will establish whether the redistribution reaches the actual update. Subsequent useful molecules and scores will determine whether it helps search.

nodes.hypothesis: Within the fixed selected historical replay group, weight each original accepted identity inversely to one plus the number of earlier task-local updates that executed at least one optimizer step with that identity selected, and renormalize those weights to preserve the Parent historical loss share; keep current-elite weights, selected membership and fixed augmented targets unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Less repeated-history influence changed learning, reduced duplicate draws and gave uneven endpoint gains.
finding_summary.insights:
Redistributing influence can change search without broadening replay membership. The child replayed 536 distinct session-local historical identities versus the Parent's 540, and its ordinary mean fitting count actually increased. Yet records with at least ten previous fitting uses received total loss coefficient 13.01 instead of 26.50 under equal weighting on the same child stream. This separates reducing repeated influence from selecting less-repeated records. The cost is a smaller effective historical batch: 4.18 rows on average despite five selected rows.

The effect does not establish better protection of every remembered molecule. Historical squared error fell from 85.86 to 84.09 on the child's fixed tensor, but 906 of 2,100 historical row exposures worsened, compared with 834 in the Parent. Both upward and downward likelihood moves occurred, and 489 historical exposures still had positive, unattainable log-probability targets. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, leaving no skipped-fitting interval that demonstrates forgetting. The positive endpoint result is therefore compatible with weaker exploitation, slower progress in some objectives and a better late discovery in one seed.

Chemical coverage also moved unevenly: distinct docking cores increased from 431 to 537 while deco-hop cores decreased from 392 to 372. The molecular assessment shows familiar ring-rich medicinal chemistry, recurring analogue families and unresolved attachment arrangements. It also finds frequent questionable nitrogen chains in one seed, N-hydroxyaminal linkages and missing stereochemical specification. The counter reduced repeated loss influence; it did not resolve those chemical limitations. The open question is whether this endpoint benefit persists while preserving earlier useful progress and coherent chemistry, rather than whether the weighting can alter learning.
finding_summary.results:
The intended weighting reached the real updates. All 405 nonterminal batches with unequal historical fitting counts reduced the weighted prior-use mean and changed gradient direction. Across the 420 historical batches, the same selected records had mean prior fitting count 4.610 with equal weights and 3.356 with the actual weights. Every first backward pass matched the weighted diagnostic exactly, and all 450 updates changed policy parameters. Current loss coefficients, total historical share, accepted targets, original strings and memory rules remained intact. Separately combining group gradients produced small numerical discrepancies in 31 updates; these do not replace the direct agreement between the weighted objective and the real backward pass.

Subsequent raw duplicate draws fell from 40.78% to 36.22%, novel yield rose from 51.81% to 55.90%, and batches needing further sampling fell from 41 to 29. All fifteen tasks completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.513272 to 0.517655, a paired gain of 0.004383. The three seed changes were +0.001516, -0.007474 and +0.019107. Four task means increased, including an almost unchanged near-ceiling docking endpoint; sitagliptin decreased. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.419605 to 0.406769, so the higher final endpoint did not come with faster useful discovery across the budget. Terminal updates are excluded from the generation conclusions.
