molecular.headline: Recognizable medicinal families dominate the leaders, with unresolved stereochemistry and extreme low-scoring growth
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Against Parent n-15499bde2e65, the output retains broad conventional aromatic, amide, sulfonamide and amine chemistry, while changing which families dominate individual seeds. High-scoring compounds mostly have familiar neutral C/N/O/S bonding and plausible medicinal scaffolds. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9759 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token presence from 0.9494 to 0.9908. Charge-token presence is low but nonzero; such tokens include nitro and other formal-charge representations and do not demonstrate appropriate protonation of basic amines. Stereocentre-token presence is 0.0 throughout. Structural diversity is broad, including fused heteroaromatics, cyclic and acyclic amines, sulfonamides, carbonyl-rich rings and occasional carbohydrate, lipid or peptide-like products. Apparent synthesis is plausible for many leading structures, with important exceptions among reactive and elaborate outliers. The low-scoring tail includes tiny fragments, very long alkyl chains, oversized multiaryl or peptide-like assemblies and isolated unusual valence patterns. These are not uniformly useful drug-like molecules, even when familiar groups recur. The report describes this output and its score associations without assigning mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The high-scoring region contains moderately sized aromatic carbonyl compounds: a fused aza-aromatic nitrile bearing isopropoxy and fluoroanilide groups, indole carboxamides, diaryl ureas, and a naphthyl/azine carboxamide attached to morpholine. Another strong family contains arylidene nitrile and amide or enamide connectivity. These are mostly recognizable synthetic targets; the activated unsaturated nitrile compounds have potential electrophilicity and unspecified alkene geometry. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9897 and mean SMILES length is 38.8. The Parent also favored indole/carboxamide chemistry, including an N-methyl benzylamide; the current seeds broaden those carbonyl arrangements rather than revealing a wholly new chemical class.
liabilities: Activated unsaturated nitrile/carbonyl groups may be electrophilic, and their alkene geometry is unspecified.
Large multiaryl assemblies, highly lipophilic chains and occasional phosphonium or cationic aza-aromatic variants extend beyond the properties of the favorable neutral series.
missing_features: The high-scoring carbonyl/nitrile region lacks systematic stable alternatives to the activated arylidene nitrile linkage, with explicit alkene geometry where applicable.
Compact aromatic carbonyl arrangements are not consistently retained in the broader proposal stream; no unique missing target pharmacophore follows from the displayed examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best fused aza-aromatic nitrile/anilide scores 0.475614712250357. The Parent maximum was 0.5280588545286916 in a related indole carboxamide family, although the current maxima improve over the other paired Parent seeds. A cyanoacrylamide and a changed enamide connection tie at 0.4697065314067379. Very large aromatic assemblies and long aliphatic chains score poorly, as does the small thioaldehyde-amide at 5.6865747950850954e-18. A final chlorinated cyanoacrylamide scores only 0.01086772025284379 despite sharing the broad functional-group class. The visible gradient supports bounded size and specific aromatic/carbonyl/nitrile arrangement, not simply adding nitriles or rings.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 concentrates on a large fused nitrogen heteroaromatic lactam with aryl substituents, alkoxy or methylthio groups and ester, ketone or amide side chains. Fluorinated phenyl rings are common. Other seeds reach aza-heteroaryl/aniline and nitrile-rich families, including pyrrolidine-substituted heterocycles. Aromatic and ring-closure token presence are both 0.9908, and halogen presence is 0.6575. These generally have conventional bonding and plausible synthetic building blocks, but some are densely aromatic and heavily substituted. Compared with the Parent hydrazone/anilino, polyaryl and sulfur-containing families, the current strongest seed uses a more consistent fused aza-lactam core.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic surface, fluorinated phenyl groups and long acyl substituents can increase lipophilicity and reduce solubility.
Some other-seed hydrazone or highly substituted multiaryl products introduce isomerism and reactive functionality despite generally conventional chemistry.
missing_features: Broader compact scaffold alternatives retaining the favored nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic attachment pattern are underrepresented among the highest-scoring molecules.
The late family does not establish which peripheral aromatic, alkyl or halogen groups can be simplified without losing the useful core arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best acyl-substituted fused heterocycle scores 0.6258169934640523 versus the paired Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.5913471190523991. The shift is not uniform across seeds. Ester/alkoxy/methylthio variants tie at 0.6134179161860822, and different alkyl ketone lengths tie at 0.6118800461361015. Highly fluorinated aryl sulfone chemistry can be low, including 0.28938327467739233, while tiny fragments remain near 0.5004. Thus halogenation or molecule size alone does not explain the favorable region; the fused nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement and its attached aromatic groups appear more consequential than several peripheral substitutions.

per_task.generated_character: Leaders are recognizable aromatic basic-amine compounds. Seed 1 combines a branched aryl ketone chain with an N-substituted piperidinol bearing chlorophenyl groups; other leaders use arylamino piperidines, piperazines and aminoalkyl chains. Seed 2 grows long N-alkyl substituents on aryl aminoalcohols. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9655 and halogen presence is 0.7621. The Parent likewise produced high-scoring aryl cyclic amines, so the broad chemical preference persists with changed ring/linker arrangements. Most leaders have plausible synthesis and ordinary valence, but flexibility, lipophilic bulk and stereochemical ambiguity remain substantial.
liabilities: Multiple chlorinated aromatic groups, long N-alkyl chains and high flexibility create physicochemical and metabolic liabilities.
Unspecified stereochemistry and occasional triazene or other reactive outliers limit confidence in a single well-defined drug-like structure.
missing_features: Explicit stereoisomers are absent for the branched aryl ketone and aminoalcohol centres, and the recorded formal charges do not establish relevant amine protonation comparisons.
Compact alternatives retaining the favorable aromatic/basic-amine spacing are not consistently preferred over long flexible N-alkyl growth in the output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched aryl-ketone/piperidinol compound reaches 0.9999813374312453; the Parent already had nearly saturated scores in other aromatic amine families. Shorter and longer aminoalkyl linkers remain high at 0.997268353359776 and 0.9962324225164898. A conventional piperazine/piperidine member scores 0.9924474921980659. In contrast, a nitro/triazene aromatic compound scores 4.147282724618086e-05 and a urea lacking an accessible aliphatic basic amine scores 9.929936367613832e-05. The observations favor particular aromatic/basic-amine arrangements, but high scores also persist in long-chain dialkylaminoalcohols, including 0.9547669836456144. They do not establish that lipophilic growth improves overall molecular quality.

per_task.generated_character: The best current molecules are aryl sulfonamides attached to piperazine or larger diazacycles, with benzyl benzodioxole, fused aza-aromatic or carbonyl-rich ring partners. A separate high seed-2 family combines an indole-derived fused system, cyclic diones and a methoxyphenol group. Aromatic-token presence is 0.969 and ring-closure presence is 0.9977. These are mainly moderate-sized conventional medicinal frameworks with plausible sulfonylation, alkylation and heterocycle chemistry. Compared with the Parent's aryl pyridone, fused sultam and small sulfonylpiperazine leaders, the current high series retains the same broad aromatic/polar-ring balance while varying attachment topology.
liabilities: Repeated aromatic or sulfonamide addition can increase size and polarity without retaining the favorable attachment pattern.
Nitro-containing, highly charged or hydrazone/guanidine outliers remain in the final proposals, alongside otherwise conventional structures.
missing_features: The best aromatic/polar-ring arrangements have only limited close, simplified alternatives among a much broader stream of less relevant structures.
Defined configurations are absent for the fused saturated indole/dione products; the relatively shallow score differences do not identify a unique missing target fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenylsulfonyl/benzodioxolylmethyl piperazine reaches 0.23462432156460183, compared with the Parent seed-0 maximum of 0.20090425134085538. A larger related aryl sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.21309769595029335, so extra aromatic structure is not uniformly helpful. A distinct fused indole/dione family reaches 0.22658333225959595. Long aliphatic amide/ester, carbohydrate-like and small heteroaryl-thiol examples score 0.028602577589751366, 0.034558175818806845 and 0.03934229877866326. These contrasts support a combination of aromatic topology and polar carbonyl/sulfonamide/amine groups rather than any one group alone.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are chemically heterogeneous but mostly recognizable: a diaryl amide/hydroxamic acid, a fluorinated pyrimidinone linked through an aniline to a saturated N/S heterocycle, an aminoalkyl sulfonamide/thiourea, and a benzylated cyclic dione with bromohydrin. Other moderate examples contain amides, aminoalcohols or nitrogen heterocycles. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9494 and ring-closure presence is 0.9759, but the low tail includes very long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like polyamides, elaborate oxygenated polycycles and glycoside/phosphorus hybrids. The Parent also showed diffuse polar aromatic chemistry and severe low-scoring growth. Most leading functional groups are synthetically familiar; growth extremes and unspecified chiral centres are the clearer deficiencies.
liabilities: Unbounded-looking alkyl, peptide-like and heavily functionalized growth produces molecules far outside the size and flexibility of the moderate leaders.
Hydroxamic acid, thiourea, hydrazide and bromohydrin motifs introduce possible chelation, reactivity or stability liabilities, while some late products are highly charged or excessively polar.
missing_features: Consistent compact polar frameworks combining the successful carbonyl, nitrogen and aromatic arrangements are not retained across the broad late proposal stream.
Explicit stereochemical alternatives for the beta-amido centre, hydroxyl-bearing centres and substituted saturated rings are absent; the evidence cannot establish which configuration would matter.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best hydroxamic-acid/amide compound scores 0.26666251850768685, while the fluorinated heterocycle scores 0.26418329062741386 and the sulfonamide/thiourea 0.2614162589649832. The current maxima are below their paired Parent maxima. The digest reports a median of 0.0, and the quoted long-chain, elaborate polycyclic and peptide-like outliers include exact zero scores. Final proposals remain low, from 1.7518667402413673e-13 to 0.0005874138015716985 in the shown excerpt. Moderate-sized polar arrangements are more favorable than these extremes, but the diverse leaders do not establish a necessary fluorination pattern, basic centre or single target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest outliers include very long hydrocarbon chains, peptide-like polyamides and large oxygenated or multiaryl assemblies, with exact zero or extremely low scores. Other tasks retain high scores in long-chain dialkylaminoalcohols, so scalar feedback alone does not establish that growth is useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently keep molecular size and repetitive growth near the chemically useful region it has already reached.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide compact analogues, chain shortening and removal of repeated substituents while preserving recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Control chemical complexity independently of occasional high scores assigned to lipophilic growth.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every current digest reports stereocentre-token presence of 0.0, despite high-scoring branched aryl ketones, aminoalcohols, beta-amido hydroxamic acids and fused saturated ring systems. Activated unsaturated nitrile compounds also lack specified alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic molecules without explicitly representing their configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow configuration assignment and variation for eligible stereocentres and geometrical isomers, maintaining those identities consistently. The existing trajectories do not establish stereochemical score sensitivity, so any benefit remains an empirical question.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Recognizable aryl carbonyl, fused aza-lactam, sulfonyl cyclic-amine and polar heterocyclic families appear among the leaders, while final proposals can return to unrelated very low-scoring structures. Activated nitrile, hydroxamic acid, thiourea and triazene variants coexist with more conventional alternatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad scaffold diversity is not consistently accompanied by stable close alternatives around favorable local chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate chemically stable matched alternatives that retain useful attachment geometry and donor/acceptor placement, including replacements for reactive unsaturation and labile heteroatom linkages. This would make the favorable regions chemically interpretable without narrowing generation to a named objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Fused aza-lactam ester/alkoxy/methylthio variants share 0.6134179161860822, alkyl ketone variants share 0.6118800461361015, and a compact sulfonylpiperazine at 0.23462432156460183 exceeds a larger related member at 0.21309769595029335.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves considerable chemical simplification unexplored where the observed score tolerates peripheral changes.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make smaller substituents, fewer aromatic attachments and stable carbonyl/linker variants readily available around established cores. Near-equivalent score regions can then contain simpler and more plausible compounds rather than mainly additional molecular decoration.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including an aromatic nitrogen/carbon exchange that preserves molecular formula. After normalizing identities and rejecting duplicates, it submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local motif changes. It moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move worsens the current score, using canonical text order for exact score ties. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Among equally best accepted neighbors, choose the one whose local motif counts differ most from the current molecule, then use canonical order if that structural comparison also ties. The distance accounts for motif multiplicity and normalizes by the combined motif counts. This gives an equally scored change in local chemical environments priority over canonical spelling and may expose a different next neighborhood. The earlier tie-selection siblings preferred fewer heavy atoms; this rule can choose smaller, equal-sized or larger graphs. It reuses the Parent's existing motifs without changing the generation or tabu rules and adds no history policy.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the neighbor with greatest multiset-Jaccard distance between its inherited radius-one motif occurrence counts and the current source's counts, then use canonical lexical order for any remaining tie.

finding_summary.headline: Motif-distance ties changed 20 walk states, but the panel score fell
finding_summary.insights: The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. It also shows why larger local structural steps are insufficient evidence of more useful exploration. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Twenty later archive gains occurred in the affected continuations, compared with 26 in the corresponding recorded parent histories, but the overlapping paths prevent assigning a causal gain to each tie choice. The rule sometimes chose smaller molecules and sometimes larger ones. The molecular assessment finds that some equally scored differences introduce reactive attachments or unusual sulfur connectivity, while conventional ring and carbonyl families remain available. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.
finding_summary.results: Twenty choices among equally best accepted molecules changed the next walk state, and all 20 increased exact motif distance from the current molecule without giving up the accepted maximum score. Eighteen occurred at the same score as the source, one during an improving move and one during a worsening move. Nineteen choices had actual continuations; one was terminal. Twenty choices among equally best accepted molecules changed the next walk state, and all 20 increased exact motif distance from the current molecule without giving up the accepted maximum score. Eighteen occurred at the same score as the source, one during an improving move and one during a worsening move. Nineteen choices had actual continuations; one was terminal. The rule encountered 40 exact maximum ties, compared with 26 in the parent, while preserving canonical fallback and the original feedback, archive and memory rules. Plateau episodes contained 60 equal-score moves, each visiting a distinct motif profile within its episode, compared with 49 such moves in the parent. Coverage per move was unchanged, and the longest plateau grew from six moves to nine. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.519947, a paired loss of 0.001812 against the required gain of 0.002. One seed improved slightly and two declined. Only deco_hop endpoints changed; the other four task endpoints were identical in every seed.

The experiment rules out failure to exercise the selector: it changed real, scored next states and was followed by 600 later accepted proposals after removing overlap between the recorded histories. It also shows why larger local structural steps are insufficient evidence of more useful exploration. The extra plateau profiles came with extra plateau moves, and longer equal-score episodes still appeared. Twenty later archive gains occurred in the affected continuations, compared with 26 in the corresponding recorded parent histories, but the overlapping paths prevent assigning a causal gain to each tie choice. The rule sometimes chose smaller molecules and sometimes larger ones. The molecular assessment finds that some equally scored differences introduce reactive attachments or unusual sulfur connectivity, while conventional ring and carbonyl families remain available. Greater distance between local motif counts therefore supplies neither compactness nor chemical plausibility. The direct selection mechanism is confirmed; its proposed overall score benefit is refuted on this panel. What remains open is whether a distance that distinguishes useful structural alternatives from score-insensitive local decoration can improve later search; this experiment does not settle that broader question.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aryl/carbonyl families coexist with reactive attachments, oversized decorations and undefined sulfur cages
molecular.overall_character: Node n-4341f3da1e57 was assessed from all supplied trajectories for all five tasks and all three seeds; the digest has no tasks_without_trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposals are branched, ring-rich molecules: every task has string-level ring_closure_rate 1.0, while aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0. These are presence counters, not aromatic atom fractions. Charged and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0 throughout. The chemical range includes comparatively conventional fused aromatic amides, decorated oxo/thioxo azaheterocycles, aryl compounds carrying primary and cyclic amines, bridged N/O lactams, and densely connected fluorinated sulfur cages. Diversity is moderate across these families but the displayed leaders repeatedly vary the same local frameworks. Rings, aromatic groups, carbonyls and amines are already accessible. The recurring deficiencies are stable heteroatom connectivity, economical substitution, and defined feasible stereochemistry. Many leading sulfur-rich graphs have weak synthetic credibility, although some indole amides have recognizable conventional chemistry. Passive parsing with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6 environment succeeded for every supplied child and parent trajectory molecule. All atom, ring and functional-bond counts below are derived directly from those observed graphs; ring counts use toolkit perception and do not certify geometry or synthesis. The passive descriptors, input hashes and comparison receipts are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-06-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json, produced by the adjacent molecular-audit.py. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, every replica retains the same best molecular identity set on four tasks. The changed best identities are confined to deco_hop, whose chemistry is described below. This is an output comparison, with no judgement about mechanism activation.

The maximum-scoring benzofuran has 26 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, but also an N-chloroamide and a chlorinated amino-bearing carbon. nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The reference is Augmented Hill-Climb, a molecule generator that writes SMILES one token at a time, like a small language model, and is nudged toward the objective by rewriting its own probabilities. First a prior is trained on an unlabeled corpus of molecules, learning only what valid chemistry looks like and nothing about any objective. For each objective a fresh copy of that prior becomes the policy, while the original stays frozen as a reference. After each batch of molecules comes back scored, only the best-scoring half is kept, and the policy is pushed so that the log-likelihood it assigns to each of those elite sequences moves toward a fixed target: the frozen prior's log-likelihood for the same molecule plus a constant times the observed reward. That target is what makes it a hill-climb rather than a policy gradient - the update is a squared regression onto an explicit number, so a molecule that scored well becomes proportionally more likely to be written again while the frozen prior keeps the policy anchored to real chemistry. New candidates are then sampled directly from the updated policy, canonicalised, and any invalid or repeated ones replaced by sampling more. Low-scoring molecules contribute nothing to the update at all.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the update's aggressiveness, its scope and its recovery behaviour open, and this implementation pins all three down. Elites are the top-scoring half of each batch, five of ten, with at least one always retained, so the update never sees an empty training set. The reward multiplier is fixed at sixty and each update is twelve clipped-gradient steps, which is a deliberately sharp commitment: the fixed regression target moves the elite likelihood a long way per batch rather than nudging it. Scope is strictly the batch just scored - no historical replay, no randomized SMILES augmentation, no reuse of earlier elites - so the policy is always chasing its most recent feedback and the root deliberately declines the replay variants that the same method family usually adds. The molecules supplied at initialization are treated as the first scored batch, so the policy is already adapted before it emits anything. Invalid or already-seen samples are replaced by continued sampling from the same policy rather than any fallback, and the exact token sequence that produced each submitted structure is stored and reused for training, so the likelihood being raised belongs to the molecule that was actually scored.

nodes.hypothesis: A corpus-trained autoregressive SMILES policy is adapted independently in each objective by Augmented Hill-Climb on only the current scored batch elites, fitting policy log likelihood toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward, and proposes new molecules by direct token sampling from the updated policy.

finding_summary.headline: Elite-only likelihood sharpening saturates one objective completely and collapses on another, placing fifth of thirteen roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a sharp picture of when elite likelihood sharpening pays. Among the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits fifth at 0.4766, but the aggregate hides the real signal: this method produced both the strongest single-objective result in this group and the weakest. Where a learnable structural motif exists and is reachable from the corpus prior, sharpening onto it is extremely effective - one objective is essentially solved. Where the reward distribution collapses, it has nothing to work with: on the weakest objective the median score across the entire run was exactly zero, its mean elite squared error was 4.94 against 735 on the objective that saturated, and the only two updates in the whole node that increased loss were both from that run. An elite half selected from ten molecules that all score zero is an arbitrary five, and the policy then drifts back to generic prior chemistry. That is a concrete, actionable characterisation of the method's failure mode and a strong argument that any Development on this lineage should target the low-signal regime - a reward transform, a ranking that survives ties, or the historical replay the root deliberately declined - rather than the update rule itself. A second caution: elite likelihood rose in only 111 of 150 individual updates even though the aggregate is clearly positive, so single updates are noisy and the mechanism works on average rather than reliably. Still open: one seed, no paired comparison, no anchor decision, and no evidence on whether the drd2_docking saturation reflects a genuinely easy objective or a policy exploiting it.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4766 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.6029 on deco_hop, 0.99999961 on drd2_docking, 0.1844 on median_2, 0.1428 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4532 on zaleplon_mpo. That drd2_docking figure is effectively a saturated objective and the highest single-task result among the three roots examined here; the sitagliptin_mpo figure is the lowest. All observables behaved as intended and the falsifier was not triggered. The corpus prior learned well - token-normalized next-token loss fell from 4.5609 to 0.5625 on a fixed 4096-sequence holdout over 29742 steps on 1268755 sequences - and was verifiably frozen thereafter, with the prior checkpoint hash and zero prior-parameter changes recorded across all 5 initializations and all 150 updates. The update mechanism did what it claims: mean elite squared error fell from 201.89 to 110.54, decreasing in 148 of 150 updates, and mean elite sequence log-likelihood rose by +2.321 while non-elite log-likelihood fell by -1.052, confirming the update is genuinely selective rather than raising everything. All 750 training members were verified to be the current batch's top-scoring half, with zero historical replay anywhere. Generation stayed healthy: 10492 of 11632 sampled sequences were RDKit-valid, a rate of 0.902, and all 145 rounds filled a batch of exactly ten valid novel molecules with zero rejections at the evaluator.

molecular.headline: The most conventionally drug-like molecules of the three roots, converging hard onto one clean series per run when the reward has signal
molecular.overall_character: This generator writes real medicinal chemistry. Ring-closure rate is 0.983 to 0.997 and aromatic-atom rate 0.948 to 0.997 in every run, cumulated double bonds are essentially absent at 0.000 in four runs and 0.003 in the fifth, and molecules are compact, with mean SMILES lengths of 36.0, 36.7, 37.4, 42.6 and 57.9. The unstable-motif tail that the other roots in this trio produce - peroxides, hypervalent sulfur, strained C=N-O rings, allenes - is largely absent here, because the corpus language prior anchors every sample to chemistry it has actually seen. The characteristic behaviour is convergence: in each run where the reward carried information, the twelve best molecules are one clean series permuted by substituent, exactly the mode collapse an elite-only likelihood update should produce. Two systematic limits remain. Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five runs, so a series built entirely on a substituted saturated ring is emitted with no configuration at all. And where the reward is degenerate the convergence simply does not happen and the output reverts to unrelated commodity structures from the prior - long alkylamines, alkyl phosphonates, tiny saturated heterocycles - alongside the useful chemistry. One run also shows the generator learning to pile on cheap score-raising decoration, reaching a halogen rate of 0.824 and a charged rate of 0.228 in polyfluorinated, nitro-bearing, N-oxide chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: Clean, small, almost entirely aromatic amides: indole and azaindole 2-carboxamides coupled to tetrahydroisoquinoline or isoindoline, plus a family of anthranilamide-aminopyridines. Mean SMILES length is 36.7 and halogen rate only 0.155, so the run built its score from ring and amide chemistry rather than from decoration.
liabilities: Nitro-substituted heteroaromatics recurring in the zero-scoring tail
A quaternary phosphocholine-like surfactant sampled straight from the prior
Oversized multi-aryl condensation products in the tail that consume oracle calls
missing_features: No fluorinated aniline of the kind present in the best supplied starting molecule
No stereochemistry anywhere in the run
No saturated three-dimensional core - almost every winner is flat
No basic amine side chain on the winning series
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 0.453 winner is an anthranilamide with an aminopyridine, and the eleven behind it are a single indole-2-carboxamide-tetrahydroisoquinoline series permuted by methyl, ethyl, ethoxy, methoxy and ring-nitrogen position, spanning 0.380 to 0.443. Replacing the amide with a sulfonamide on the same skeleton drops the score from 0.453 to 0.380 and then to 0.246, so the carbonyl is doing real work and the policy found that and then explored around it.

per_task.generated_character: A tetrafluorinated biaryl carbohydrazide series decorated with nitro groups, pyridine N-oxides and trifluoromethyl. Halogen rate reaches 0.824 and charged rate 0.228, both by a wide margin the highest anywhere in this node, and the aromatic rate is 0.997 - almost every heavy atom is in an aromatic ring.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones throughout the winning series, a reactive and metabolically labile motif
Multiple nitro groups combined with pyridine N-oxides on the same molecule
Perfluorinated aromatic rings that would be far outside ordinary lead-like property space
missing_features: No purinedione or fused bicyclic imide core from the starting molecules
No saturated linkers, and no stereochemistry on anything sp3
No basic ionizable nitrogen to balance the electron-poor rings
No structural alternative to the acylhydrazone once it was found
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best sit within 0.586 to 0.603 and share the same acylhydrazone-tetrafluorobiaryl skeleton, differing only in which electron-poor group decorates which ring. The losing tail is plain unfunctionalised aromatics - diphenylmethane, coumaric acid, a diarylmethanol - sitting at the 0.500 floor that trivial structures occupy. So the gradient rewards piling electron-withdrawing decoration onto a fixed skeleton, and the policy learned exactly that.

per_task.generated_character: A textbook arylalkylamine series: 3-aryl piperidines and ring-expanded azepanes, N-alkylated with propyl or butyl, paired with a chloro- and fluoro-substituted phenethylamine or a strained azetidine amine. Mean SMILES length is 36.0, the shortest of the five runs, and these are the most conventionally drug-like molecules anywhere in the three roots examined.
liabilities: Strained azetidine amines used as primary-amine bioisosteres throughout the top
Ring-expanded azepanes and azocanes of doubtful synthetic accessibility
Alkyl fluoride chains attached to the ring nitrogen, which would be metabolically labile
missing_features: No stereochemistry on the 3-aryl saturated ring centre, which is where the real pharmacology of this series sits
No scaffold alternatives explored once the series was found
No polar or solubilising substituents anywhere on the saturated ring
No aromatic ring systems beyond a single substituted benzene
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Eleven of the top twelve score at least 0.99999 and every one of them carries the same pair: an N-alkyl saturated cyclic amine and a second basic nitrogen on a halogenated aromatic. The tail at 4e-05 to 4e-04 keeps aromatic amides, nitro groups and ureas but has no basic aliphatic nitrogen at all, so the objective has a hard structural switch. The run was effectively saturated by round 28 and the remaining budget went into permuting alkyl chain length and halogen position on an already-solved series.

per_task.generated_character: Aryl sulfonamides and piperazine or tetrahydroisoquinoline amides - ordinary lead-like medicinal chemistry with mean SMILES length 37.4, no cumulated bonds and no obviously unstable motifs. A sulfonyl-tetrahydroisoquinoline motif recurs across the top but does not dominate it the way the winning series does in the other runs.
liabilities: A sulfoxonium-like charged sulfur group appearing in the final batch
An unbranched C18 alkylamine sampled directly from the prior and submitted
An alkyl phosphonate diester with no relevance to the chemistry being searched
missing_features: No fused aminal cage of the kind this objective's strongest chemistry uses
No stereochemistry on the sp3 ring centres produced
No convergence onto a single elaborated series across 29 rounds
No electron-rich alkoxy-substituted biaryl arms
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top twelve span 0.161 to 0.184 and are only loosely related, while the 0.014 to 0.040 tail is long-chain aliphatics, an alkyl phosphonate, a tiny imidazoline and a saturated terpenoid. So the gradient rewards aromatic sulfonamide content over aliphatic bulk but is shallow throughout, and the run never found a step large enough for the elite update to lock onto - the final batch scores 0.099 to 0.139, below the top twelve.

per_task.generated_character: Generic prior chemistry that never organised into anything: phthalimides, benzylamines, triazole acetamides, aryl sulfonamides and oxadiazoles, all unrelated to one another. The molecules are individually plausible - ring rate 0.983, aromatic rate 0.948, no cumulated bonds - but there is no series here at all, which is the visible signature of an update with no reward signal to sharpen.
liabilities: Long dialkylamino thiol chains sampled from the prior in the zero-scoring tail
Azo linkages between aromatic rings paired with bis-cationic quinolinium centres
Acyclic diester and diacid chains with no relation to the objective
missing_features: No trifluoromethyl-substituted aromatic ring on the winning molecules
No beta-amino amide or fused triazolopyrazine motif
No stereochemistry, although the chemistry this objective rewards is stereodefined
No compact saturated fluorinated heterocycle
No convergence of any kind across 29 rounds
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The median score across the entire run is exactly zero and the best is 0.143. Only three molecules clear 0.10 and the twelfth-best is already at 0.031, so the elite half of a typical batch is five molecules that all scored zero and carry no ordering. The final batch scores 0.0, 0.004, 0.0, 0.0004, 0.0 and 0.00003, and those six molecules share nothing structurally with the top of the run - the policy had drifted back to prior-typical output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the three runs where the reward carried information, the twelve best molecules share a complete skeleton and differ only in alkyl chain length, halogen identity or ring-nitrogen position. In one of them eleven of the top twelve exceed 0.99999 on the same series, and the last rounds of the budget were spent permuting decoration on chemistry that was already saturated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator collapses to one skeleton and then only permutes substituents on it
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Raising the likelihood of elite sequences directly narrows the sampling distribution, so once a series is found the generator can no longer reach anything else. A generator needs a diversity term, a likelihood ceiling per motif, or periodic resampling from the unadapted prior, so that budget remaining after a series is exhausted is spent on a different region rather than on redundant analogues.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the run whose median score across all 290 evaluations was exactly zero, mean elite squared error was 4.94 against 735 in the run that converged, the only two loss-increasing updates in the whole node came from it, and its final six molecules scored at or near zero while sharing no structure with its own best. That run also shows no series at all, in contrast to every run that had signal.
transferable_gaps.gap: A degenerate reward distribution leaves the update with nothing to learn from
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Selecting the top-scoring half is meaningless when the whole batch scores the same, so the elite set becomes an arbitrary sample and the update pushes the policy toward noise. A generator that adapts from feedback needs a signal that survives ties - a ranking over the whole history, a reward transform that spreads a collapsed distribution, or a fallback to pure exploration when within-batch variance vanishes.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Stereocentre rate is exactly 0.000 in all five independent runs across 1450 molecules, including a run whose entire winning series is built on a substituted saturated ring carbon where configuration determines the chemistry, and another whose target chemistry is explicitly stereodefined.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is ever produced, including on series that are defined by it
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The token vocabulary and the sampling procedure produce flat connectivity only, so the model cannot express, learn or sharpen configuration even when the feedback rewards it. A generator needs stereochemical tokens present in the prior's training data and preserved through canonicalisation, so that two configurations of a skeleton are distinguishable candidates rather than the same string.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In one run the generator drove the halogen rate to 0.824 and the charged rate to 0.228, converging on perfluorinated biaryls carrying nitro groups and pyridine N-oxides, with all twelve best within 0.017 of each other. It found that adding electron-poor substituents to a fixed skeleton moved the score and kept doing so rather than changing the skeleton.
transferable_gaps.gap: Cheap decoration is exploited in place of structural change
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A likelihood update rewards whatever raises the number, and substituent decoration is the cheapest available move because it changes few tokens. A generator would need property-space constraints applied to its own output distribution, so that a mode built entirely from extreme decoration is penalised before it consumes the remaining budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 11632 sampled sequences, 1140 failed to parse, a validity rate of 0.902, and 4781 further proposals were rejected as duplicates or invalid during refill. Among the structures that did pass, the low-scoring tails contain unbranched C18 alkylamines, alkyl phosphonate diesters, a phosphocholine surfactant and bare four-atom heterocycles - prior-typical output with no relevance to any search.
transferable_gaps.gap: Around a tenth of what the generator writes is not a molecule, and some of what is remains commodity chemistry
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling ancestrally from a language model has no mechanism to keep drawn sequences inside a useful region of chemistry, so budget goes to parsing failures and to generic corpus material. A generator needs constrained decoding that guarantees a parseable structure, plus a property or complexity filter applied before submission, so that invalid and trivially irrelevant draws are replaced without paying for them.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

retained_mechanisms: Unlabeled corpus next-token training of a recurrent autoregressive SMILES prior with fixed-holdout checkpoint selection
Independent objective policy initialization from a verified frozen prior
Current scored-batch top-half elite selection and fixed prior-log-likelihood plus scaled-reward squared-residual updates

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a molecular autoencoder from unlabeled molecules, freezes it, and searches its 24-dimensional latent space with CMA-ES. It samples a Gaussian, deterministically decodes each point into a molecule, and evaluates valid new identities. Each accepted score stays attached to the exact point that generated that molecule. It collects two protocol batches into one scored generation, then uses the better samples to move the Gaussian mean, adapt its full covariance, and control its step size through cumulative paths. High-scoring initial molecules supply geometric starting locations, while subsequent adaptation uses scores of actual decoded offspring.
approach.novelty: Make each completed protocol batch a CMA generation, allowing the next batch to use the feedback that just arrived. This changes the delay between observation and distribution adaptation. The existing rank-weighted mean, covariance, and step-size equations automatically use the smaller generation. The lineage currently contains only its evaluated root, so batch-aligned adaptation has no earlier sibling experiment. The hypothesis is that more opportunities to redirect search within the same evaluation allowance can outweigh the noisier selection statistics of smaller generations.

nodes.hypothesis: Reduce the scored CMA generation target to the smallest whole number of evaluator-announced batches containing at least two offspring, so accepted feedback updates the inherited Gaussian after each complete protocol batch whenever that batch already contains at least two members.

finding_summary.headline: Immediate feedback updates activated, but the mean score fell by 0.0224
finding_summary.insights: Removing the measured feedback wait did not solve the score limitation in this replica. More updates also meant smaller selected populations: effective selection mass fell from 5.94 to 3.17, and average covariance movement per update decreased on every task. Thus update count is insufficient evidence of stronger or more useful adaptation. The docking trajectory makes the distinction concrete: 25 of its 29 generations contained tied scores, and one update had weighted score enrichment of only about 2.6 × 10⁻¹³ despite moving the Gaussian. The molecular assessment still finds oversized hydrocarbons, repeated imine or sulfur linkers, and elaborate carbonyl-bearing rings, with limited controlled variation of conventional scaffolds. Faster reaction to the available scores did not resolve those generator limitations. This supports investigating the representation and the informativeness of sampled regions alongside adaptation cadence. It does not establish which caused the score loss, whether the smaller selection mass increased harmful noise, or whether the result generalizes beyond the single paired seed.
finding_summary.results: Every completed batch immediately updated the Gaussian, and the next batch used that updated distribution. For each of the five tasks, accepted offspring waited through zero further batch emissions before their update, versus a mean of 0.5 emissions among updated Parent offspring. The Parent also left 10 accepted offspring per task in an unfinished terminal generation; the Child left none. Feedback changed the distribution used for the next proposals after 28 of 28 nonterminal batches, up from 14 of 28. Each task completed 29 updates, including one terminal update with no later proposals. The frozen representation and update equations were preserved, and all rank, covariance, path, step-size and sampling checks passed. Nevertheless, the seed-0 mean of final best scores fell from 0.302617 to 0.280194, a change of −0.022423 rather than the predicted gain of at least 0.002. zaleplon_mpo fell from 0.443203 to 0.363235, deco_hop from 0.610746 to 0.603856, drd2_docking from 0.063511 to 0.029010, and median_2 from 0.208415 to 0.198819. sitagliptin_mpo improved from 0.187211 to 0.206051. Both runs used all 300 evaluations per task. Raw Gaussian decodes rose from 4,800 to 9,280 across the suite; recorded suite time rose from 43.68 to 97.64 seconds, including oracle and runtime variation.

molecular.headline: Rings are abundant, but polyenes, oversized hydrocarbons and repeated imine/sulfur chains crowd out coherent medicinal scaffolds.
molecular.overall_character: This report describes n-47deaf126449 against Parent n-bd0cbfe35fa3 using the supplied seed 0 trajectories. Each task contains 300 unique evaluated molecules, of which 290 were proposed by the optimizer; the common initial structures are distinguished from generated output below. The generated structures cover many ring topologies and functional groups, so the problem is not absence of rings or complete structural collapse. However, high-scoring subsets repeatedly occupy chemically restricted families: unsaturated nitrogen rings, imine/sulfur networks, very long hydrocarbon chains, or an aromatic methylenedioxy motif attached to complicated carbonyl-bearing rings. Ring closure is ubiquitous in the digest, whereas aromatic character varies substantially across tasks. These are SMILES-text occurrence rates, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring-quality measurements. A closure digit can represent an ordinary phenyl ring, a highly strained unsaturated small ring, or an enormous macrocycle. Synthetic plausibility is questionable overall: recognizable aryl, ether, amide and cyclic-carbonyl fragments coexist with repetitive conjugation, unusual closures, reactive carbonyl arrangements and polysulfides. Some isolated structures and supplied initial molecules look substantially more conventional. Drug likeness is weak overall, while structural diversity is broad across the observed output and more restricted within recurring high-score motifs. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0: no explicit tetrahedral stereochemical annotation was emitted, even in structures that could have multiple stereogenic centers. This does not mean all structures are achiral. Score associations below describe the supplied observations; they do not establish a receptor interaction, a synthetic route, or a unique missing objective feature.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, strongly unsaturated structures combine phenyl or pyridyl rings with imines, enamines, ethers and assorted nonaromatic nitrogen rings. The optimizer SMILES have mean length 36.1 and maximum length 74, ring_closure_rate 0.9897 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8069. The best molecule, evaluation 281, connects a methoxyvinyl-substituted imine and pyridyl group to a phenyl-bearing unsaturated N-N ring. Evaluation 151 instead joins pyridyl and aryl-sulfoxide groups through a cyclobutadiene-like ring; evaluation 118 contains a cyclopropene and an unsaturated lactam. These are chemically very different arrangements despite neighboring high scores. The later trajectory favors carbonyl-poor imine/enamine and N-N ring structures, whereas the Parent retains more carbonyl-containing chains and rings. The common initial molecule at evaluation 9 is a much more conventional trimethoxyindole carboxamide with a fluorophenyl substituent; it was supplied, not generated.
liabilities: The cyclobutadiene-like ring at evaluation 151 and cyclopropene at evaluation 118 raise substantial ring-strain and synthesis concerns; ring-rich strings are not evidence of comfortable ring geometry.
Extended polyenes, enol ethers and imine/N-N arrangements create stability and isomerism questions. Alkene geometry and any tetrahedral stereochemistry are unspecified.
Large aromatic or unsaturated assemblies also appear among the lowest scores, so aromaticity alone is not a useful chemical quality argument.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of conventional aryl/heterocyclic frameworks with stable, deliberately placed polar functions is missing from the high-score series. The supplied indole carboxamide and the Parent best demonstrate relevant combinations, while the Child frequently substitutes imine/enamine networks and unusual ring closures.

There is no clear series that preserves a useful ring framework while separately exploring ordinary amide, ether and ring-nitrogen placement. The examples do not identify an additional unique objective-required substructure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best generated score is 0.36323515471605416 at evaluation 281; evaluation 151 scores 0.3558775619487993 and the supplied indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the extended acyclic carbonate/amide polyene at evaluation 52 scores 7.550462063881703e-14, and the simple methoxypyridine carboxylic acid at evaluation 100 scores 2.188179510572902e-09. Thus neither making molecules smaller nor merely adding an aromatic nitrogen or carbonyl is sufficient. The higher examples support an association with a bounded aryl/heterocycle framework carrying distributed nitrogen and oxygen functions, but do not isolate a necessary group. The Parent maximum, 0.44320263021395917, belongs to an aryl nitrogen-ring structure that also retains a carboxamide and methoxyvinyl substituent. The Child does not reproduce that exact combination among its best examples. Its final hydrocarbon ring structure at evaluation 299 scores only 0.009441452624714554 despite retaining ring and aromatic syntax. The observed differences do not show that the unusual small rings themselves are beneficial.

per_task.generated_character: The output is large, heavily unsaturated and usually aromatic, with nitrogen-rich heterocycles and increasingly repetitive imine, hydrazone, thioether and polysulfide connections. Mean SMILES length is 58.7, maximum length 98, ring_closure_rate 1.0 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9103. Evaluation 233, the best example, has a brominated conjugated ring framework, an enal substituent and an extended aza/sulfur ring network. Evaluation 146 expands a polyaza aromatic/imine framework around an enal. Evaluation 283 and the final evaluation 299 combine aza-aromatic and phenyl or thienyl rings with conspicuous sulfur chains and imine linkers. The whole trajectory confirms a shift from carbonyl-rich sulfone/lactam structures toward these repetitive nitrogen/sulfur arrangements. The Parent has more recognizable aryl amide, ester and ketone connections, although it too produces oversized and unusual conjugated structures.
liabilities: Repeated imines and hydrazones raise hydrolytic stability and configurational ambiguity concerns, and multiple sulfur-sulfur bonds introduce redox-sensitive connections.
Conjugated aldehydes occur in several best molecules, adding electrophilic functionality rather than demonstrating a benign medicinal series.
Extended aza/sulfur annulations and chains have questionable synthetic accessibility and substantial uncertainty in their preferred geometry and chemical stability.
missing_features: A comparably effective high-score family with bounded heterocycle/linker size and predominantly ordinary stable connections is not established in the Child. The Parent provides a more recognizable aryl-amide/ester counterexample to the apparent need for repeat expansion.

The output does not cleanly separate useful nitrogen-rich ring connectivity from redundant imine or sulfur repetition. The observed scores alone do not reveal a unique required decoration or scaffold arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 233 scores 0.6038558964255558 and evaluation 146 scores 0.5954516704042321. The sulfone-containing lactam/polyene at evaluation 64 scores 0.27028397565922924, and the aryl sulfone/amide/ester at evaluation 61 scores 0.27106627775076975. Within this output, aza-aromatic/imine connectivity, often accompanied by an enal and reduced sulfur linkers, occurs in the higher-score region; ordinary carbonyl or sulfone groups are not sufficient. Those features co-vary, so their individual contributions cannot be separated. The final polysulfide-rich evaluation 299 still scores 0.5919117647058824. The Parent best scores 0.6107459743674006 and combines a halogenated aryl amide, an alpha-keto ester and an aza-aromatic ring system without the Child high examples' extensive sulfur chains. This is evidence that the repetitive sulfur chemistry is not necessary to reach the observed score region, not proof that any particular replacement improves the score.

per_task.generated_character: This trajectory is dominated by very large aliphatic structures: long methylene chains, huge carbocyclic or heterocyclic loops, and occasional phenyl rings, ethers, acetals, alcohols, esters and lactones. Mean SMILES length is 78.4 and maximum length 147; ring_closure_rate is 0.9655, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.5. The best molecule at evaluation 210 combines a ring lactone and biaryl framework with extensive carbon chains and an aryl hydroxyethyl branch; it has no nitrogen. Evaluation 264 similarly retains a long aliphatic bridge inside an aromatic nitrogen/oxygen ring assembly. Evaluation 126 has long alkyl chains, aromatic rings and ester connections. By the final evaluations, 299 and 300 are almost entirely hydrocarbon, with a cyclohexyl ring and very long branched chains. The Parent also explores this large-chain chemistry, but its later output includes substantially more discrete aryl, ether, carbonyl and cyclic-amine arrangements.
liabilities: Very long, mostly nonpolar chains imply extreme flexibility and likely difficult aqueous handling; the final pure hydrocarbons offer almost no polar interaction diversity.
Precisely assembling enormous macrocycles and long chains with scattered acetals, alkenes or esters would be demanding, without evidence here of a useful defined conformation.
The repeated near-identical scores do not distinguish these liabilities or justify interpreting continued molecular growth as improved chemistry.
missing_features: The higher Child examples lack a comparably differentiated arrangement of discrete rings, polar functions and a cyclic amine like that observed in the Parent high-score region; alkyl repetition dominates instead. This is a missing combination, not evidence that any single nitrogen group is required.

Bounded hydrophobic substituents and controlled polar spacing are poorly represented in the late output. A unique missing receptor-interaction feature cannot be inferred from the nearly flat score regime, especially because the supplied cyclic-amine molecule scores poorly.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Many chemically different large structures share the recorded score 0.02885837683273086, including final evaluation 300; the digest median is 0.028858. The best molecule reaches only 0.029009639868631948. The polar chlorinated amino/amide/polyol at evaluation 21 scores 0.006307806495142862, and the supplied methylpiperidine-containing aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. Thus the local observations favor the large-chain region over these examples, but then provide very little discrimination among its structures. They do not show that basic amines or additional polarity alone help. The Parent maximum is 0.06351092410835005 for a large but more structured molecule containing an aryl-substituted cyclic amine, a spiro ring junction, ether, alcohol, ketone and fluorinated aromatic substituents. The Child best and final molecules fail to recover that coordinated chemistry. The plateau cannot be interpreted as evidence of successful binding or assigned a physical cause from the molecular trajectories alone.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-score molecules repeatedly carry a benzodioxole, an aromatic ring bearing a cyclic methylenedioxy group, attached to saturated or partly unsaturated carbonyl-rich rings. The optimizer mean SMILES length is 52.8 and maximum length 123, with ring_closure_rate 0.9862 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8276. Evaluation 135, the best, attaches this aromatic acetal to a complicated bridged/fused polyketone core with an alkyl substituent. Evaluation 123 uses an expanded lactone/diketone ring, while evaluation 104 has a smaller bridged carbonyl-bearing carbocycle. Other high examples preserve the aromatic acetal while changing ring closures, unsaturation and ketone or lactam positions. The structures have a natural-product-like mixture of aromatic and saturated carbon frameworks, but their arbitrary ring complexity and absent stereochemical assignments make actual preparation questionable. They are more than simple aromatic chains, yet they do not form a clearly controlled stereochemical series.
liabilities: Multiple ring junctions and saturated substituted centers would make stereoisomer control and synthesis demanding, but explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is absent.
Closely spaced ketones and repeated enolizable carbonyl patterns add tautomeric and reactivity questions.
Convergence of the high-score excerpt on a common aromatic motif limits useful scaffold diversity despite many distinct molecular identities.
missing_features: The high-score Child excerpt lacks the Parent's simple, readily interpretable biaryl/ether alternatives around the recurring aromatic acetal. It does not show that complex bridged polyketones are necessary.

Controlled exploration of modest substituent and linker changes around the shared aromatic motif is limited relative to wholesale changes in the surrounding ring skeleton. No further unique objective-required motif can be recovered confidently from these examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best score is 0.19881918238645052 at evaluation 135; evaluations 123 and 104 score 0.19224322082161796 and 0.1896283315055771. The acyclic branched hydroxy-polyene at evaluation 290 scores 0.01355192713636236, and the small branched aldehyde at evaluation 115 scores 0.031250953717974365. The recurring aromatic methylenedioxy group with an attached ring framework is the clearest positive structural association. Ring complexity alone is not sufficient: the final dense polycycle at evaluation 299 lacks that recognizable aromatic motif and scores 0.10541990435198914, while evaluation 300 retains it and scores 0.17581973378636775. The Parent best is a much simpler ethoxy-substituted biaryl benzodioxole at 0.2084153270620087. The Child preserves the same useful aromatic motif but surrounds it with more elaborate carbonyl-bearing rings. These observations do not establish a reward for the added cage complexity or a requirement for its exact ketone pattern.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, partially unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen rings carry ketones, amides, lactones, aldehydes, phenols or enols; aromatic rings are less prevalent than in most other task outputs. Mean SMILES length is 36.9 and maximum length 84, ring_closure_rate 0.9138 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.3517. Evaluation 280, the best, combines a phenolic aromatic ring, an unsaturated nitrogen ring framework and an amino-ketone side chain. Evaluation 88 combines an unsaturated nitrogen ring with a brominated formylphenyl group and a conjugated N-formyl amide. Evaluation 213 is an unsaturated nitrogen-containing macrocyclic lactone with formyl and enolic functions. Formal charge syntax is relatively frequent: charged_rate 0.2276, with cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.1103. Evaluation 83 illustrates a formally charged cumulated nitrogen/oxygen arrangement alongside an amide and brominated unsaturated nitrogen ring. These counters do not establish the physical protonation or stability of those species.
liabilities: Several high examples contain aldehydes, conjugated carbonyls or enol/imine arrangements that raise stability and reactivity concerns.

Formally charged cumulated nitrogen/oxygen groups and other unusual nitrogen bonding appear among usable-score molecules, so the observed score does not itself screen out chemically questionable functionality.

Unsaturated macrocycles, uncommon fused ring closures and unspecified stereochemistry make the apparent molecular graphs more definite than their real chemical identities and accessible conformations.
missing_features: A stable, systematically varied family that retains the favorable size and nitrogen/oxygen balance is not established. Amino-carbonyl, hydroxylated imine and lactone arrangements appear as disparate examples rather than an interpretable series of conventional heterocycles.

Defined saturation and stereochemical arrangements around the substituted ring systems are absent. Their potential usefulness is a chemistry capability gap; these trajectories do not demonstrate a stereochemical score preference or justify prescribing a specific target-like motif.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best scores are 0.20605067334417151 at evaluation 280, 0.20209403173605398 at evaluation 88 and 0.1982617738654109 at evaluation 213, while the digest median is 0.000488. The larger aromatic amide/nitro/polyene assembly at evaluation 11 scores 1.0124110977439176e-51. Moderate size and a mixed nitrogen/oxygen cyclic framework recur among the higher examples, but they are not sufficient: the compact nitrogen/carbonyl polycycle at evaluation 261 scores 2.319795379947775e-43. Nor is avoiding formal charge a universal separator, because evaluation 83 scores 0.1775105772728547. The Parent best at 0.18721053870914972 instead combines a hydroxylated cyclic imine, primary amine and cyanophenyl substituent. The Child best changes the functional-group combination while retaining a bounded nitrogen/oxygen framework. The score differences do not identify one necessary halogen, amine type, carbonyl arrangement or hidden reference scaffold. The final molecules remain chemically mixed, with evaluation 300 at 0.07900628938932339.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring_closure_rate reaches 1.0, yet the cited high-score molecules include cyclobutadiene-like and cyclopropene rings, extended unsaturated macrocycles and complicated bridged polyketones. The Parent also supplies a simpler aromatic ether/acetal framework at 0.2084153270620087, so elaborate closures are not a demonstrated prerequisite for useful scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Abundant ring closure does not translate into reliable conventional ring geometry or controlled unsaturation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs support for ordinary aromatic, saturated and partly saturated ring frameworks with chemically sensible closure geometry, while allowing controlled substitution and fusion. Ring presence and parsable valence alone do not establish that capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One full trajectory repeatedly emits very long hydrocarbon chains at the identical recorded score 0.02885837683273086 and ends with almost pure hydrocarbons. Another high-score excerpt contains long alternating imine sequences and sulfur chains, including a final polysulfide-rich molecule at 0.5919117647058824. These are repeated structural patterns, not merely long SMILES caused by ordinary ring notation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably bound molecular extent or repeated backbone and linker units.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded, diverse chain and linker architectures and distinct functional-group placements without requiring extension of the same carbon, imine or sulfur unit. Preserve access to shorter alternatives so observed feedback can distinguish chemistry beyond repeat length.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, and a Parent high example combines a cyclic amine, ether, alcohol and ketone at 0.06351092410835005. Generated high-score excerpts instead often emphasize carbonyl-poor imine/N-N rings, sulfur networks or almost entirely hydrocarbon structures. The poor score of a supplied methylpiperidine-containing molecule also shows that simply inserting an amine is not sufficient.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary polar functions are available but are not reliably retained together in balanced ring-based structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to varied amide, ether, alcohol and amine contexts with controlled hydrophobic and polar spacing. The needed capability is coherent combinations and independent variation of those functions, rather than a mandatory group for any hidden objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited aromatic methylenedioxy examples retain the same local motif while cycling through bridged polyketones, expanded lactones and unsaturated fused systems. Elsewhere related aza-aromatic fragments are embedded in progressively different imine and sulfur networks. The digest reports 300 unique molecules per task, but distinct identities do not establish broad exploration of simple alternatives around a useful motif.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful motif diversity is often expressed through large changes in surrounding topology instead of modest, interpretable chemical variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support families that preserve a coherent ring framework while varying attachment position, linker size, saturation and ordinary polar substituents. This would expose more interpretable chemical alternatives without encoding the identity of the objective or asserting that one recurring motif is universally useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied optimizer digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited bridged carbonyl-rich structures, substituted lactones and partially saturated ring junctions nevertheless contain potential stereogenic arrangements. Their written molecular identities therefore leave chemically relevant configurations unresolved.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit tetrahedral stereochemistry is absent even where the generated ring frameworks could require it.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator would need to represent and preserve defined stereoisomers of substituted saturated and fused ring frameworks to explore that chemistry. This capability should be available independently of objective identity; the present trajectories do not establish that a particular stereoisomer would score better.

nodes.method_name: CMA-ES: covariance adaptation through a frozen molecular decoder
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the optimizer in CMA-ES: sample a multivariate Gaussian, rank evaluated samples, move its mean by weighted recombination, and adapt covariance and step size using selected displacements and cumulative evolution paths. [Hansen, Sections 1-4](https://arxiv.org/html/1604.00772v2) describes this mechanism. For the molecular transfer, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus and freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder. Each objective starts with fresh Gaussian and path state. Encodings of high-scoring supplied molecules may initialize geometric search locations, but their scores must not be assigned to nonidentical reconstructions. Generate latent samples, decode them into new molecules, and attach accepted oracle feedback to the exact latent sample that produced each submitted structure. Assemble scored generations while respecting the evaluator-announced batching, then update the Gaussian from descending observed-score ranks. Reject invalid or duplicate structures locally and continue de novo decoding. The corpus trains a generator and never supplies a ranked molecular library. The hypothesis is that learning correlated latent displacements directly from successful generations can uncover improving combinations without first estimating an objective surrogate, increasing the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Useful decoder support and covariance adaptation within scarce feedback are empirical prerequisites; continuous-domain performance is not evidence that decoded molecular landscapes will behave similarly.
