approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language prior from an unlabeled molecular corpus, then starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. After each accepted batch, it trains on the best-scoring half of the current molecules and the highest-scoring eligible historical elites. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest accepted elite identities with their original strings and scores. Every selected sequence receives equal loss weight and a target equal to its frozen-prior log probability plus sixty times its accepted score. Bounded clipped Adam steps fit those targets, and the updated policy directly samples complete molecules with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection. Stronger-history selection is already part of this Parent; its passive uniform replay comparison only measures that selection.
approach.novelty: Add conditional joint target normalization. Treat the unchanged selected current and historical sequences as distinct outcomes of one probability model. If their proposed probability masses sum above one, subtract the log of that sum from every selected log-likelihood target; otherwise leave every target unchanged. This removes a shared impossible probability demand while preserving all pairwise target differences, including the inherited reward and prior preference. It differs from the lineage siblings that changed prior learning, replay membership, memory retention or equivalent strings. An earlier experiment in another lineage removed common policy credit and performed worse; this experiment instead changes fixed likelihood targets only when their joint mass is impossible. A same-state comparison against the raw Parent targets will measure the resulting learning change. Better probability accounting may help subsequent search, but it does not guarantee broader chemistry or a score gain.

nodes.hypothesis: Conditionally normalize the unchanged selected current-and-historical augmented likelihood targets by a single shared offset: for a_i = frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, fit t_i = a_i - max(0, logsumexp_j(a_j)) over the actual selected training union, preserving equal row weights, pairwise target differences and every target when its joint probability mass is already at most one.

finding_summary.headline: Target normalization changed learning and reduced fit error; two docking replicas failed to finish
finding_summary.insights:
Removing impossible selected-target demands is sufficient to change the learner, but insufficient to preserve useful generation. Across the same 415 successful suggestion positions, the child used 73,384 raw draws versus 35,144 for the parent. Its duplicate fraction fell from 38.92% to 10.33%, while its unterminated fraction rose from 0.003% to 44.21%; the two failed requests add a further 131,112 draws. Lower duplication therefore did not mean a more productive sampler. Both updates immediately before those failures reduced projected fitting error and had measurable gradient changes, so successful normalization and fitting do not rule out loss of sequence completion. The evidence identifies a failure in the resulting proposal distribution, but does not isolate which token changes caused it.

The condition itself has strong controls: all three median-similarity sessions and two sitagliptin sessions never needed normalization and reproduced their parent molecule-and-score trajectories exactly. Every trajectory that changed first diverged after a positive-offset update. In the useful history-bearing opportunities, the common shift reversed 722 selected rows from upward likelihood pressure to downward pressure, even though their relative target preferences were preserved. This narrows the unresolved question to what the shifted regression does to shared sequence-model support, including termination and molecules outside the fitted union. The supplied chemistry assessment finds recognizable compact aromatic and basic-amine families among the leaders alongside attachment drift, excessive chain or ring growth, and absent stereochemical specification. A necessary probability bound on selected strings does not resolve those chemical limitations. The completed-task gains justify studying the conditional target effect further only with generation reliability and useful chemical transfer measured alongside fitting.
finding_summary.results:
The intended target and learning changes occurred. Of 430 recorded updates, 232 needed normalization. All 232 removed excess joint target probability mass, eliminated all 1,252 individually positive log-probability targets, preserved the differences between selected targets within the registered tolerance, and changed the combined learning gradient. The other 198 updates retained their targets exactly and had identical projected-target and raw-target gradients. Among the 219 history-bearing positive-offset updates followed by a successful proposal batch, pooled projected mean squared error fell from 164.659 to 9.544 and decreased in every update. Current-example error fell from 311.898 to 13.978 and historical-example error from 17.421 to 5.110. Individual historical errors still worsened in 288 of 1,095 exposures. The raw-target error, measured at those same before/after policy states, rose from 263.347 to 286.769; the optimizer was fitting the changed objective.

Search reliability deteriorated despite those fitting gains. Thirteen of fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations. Docking seeds 0 and 2 stopped at 260 and 140 evaluations because the policy could not refill a valid novel batch. In their final failed requests, 60,076 of 65,544 draws and 65,553 of 65,568 draws did not terminate. The child therefore has no complete three-seed macro mean. The sole complete seed scored 0.527720 versus its parent’s 0.514385, a paired gain of 0.013335. Among tasks completed in all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.459183 to 0.471568 for zaleplon and from 0.601097 to 0.718554 for scaffold hopping, stayed at 0.218884 for median similarity, and fell from 0.288538 to 0.286001 for sitagliptin. These completed-task results cannot establish the proposed three-seed macro improvement.

Search reliability deteriorated despite those fitting gains. Thirteen of fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations. Docking seeds 0 and 2 stopped at 260 and 140 evaluations because the policy could not refill a valid novel batch. In their final failed requests, 60,076 of 65,544 draws and 65,553 of 65,568 draws did not terminate. The child therefore has no complete three-seed macro mean. The sole complete seed scored 0.527720 versus its parent’s 0.514385, a paired gain of 0.013335. Among tasks completed in all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.459183 to 0.471568 for zaleplon and from 0.601097 to 0.718554 for scaffold hopping, stayed at 0.218884 for median similarity, and fell from 0.288538 to 0.286001 for sitagliptin. These completed-task results cannot establish the proposed three-seed macro improvement.

Removing impossible selected-target demands is sufficient to change the learner, but insufficient to preserve useful generation. Across the same 415 successful suggestion positions, the child used 73,384 raw draws versus 35,144 for the parent. Its duplicate fraction fell from 38.92% to 10.33%, while its unterminated fraction rose from 0.003% to 44.21%; the two failed requests add a further 131,112 draws. Lower duplication therefore did not mean a more productive sampler. Both updates immediately before those failures reduced projected fitting error and had measurable gradient changes, so successful normalization and fitting do not rule out loss of sequence completion. The evidence identifies a failure in the resulting proposal distribution, but does not isolate which token changes caused it.

The condition itself has strong controls: all three median-similarity sessions and two sitagliptin sessions never needed normalization and reproduced their parent molecule-and-score trajectories exactly. Every trajectory that changed first diverged after a positive-offset update. In the useful history-bearing opportunities, the common shift reversed 722 selected rows from upward likelihood pressure to downward pressure, even though their relative target preferences were preserved. This narrows the unresolved question to what the shifted regression does to shared sequence-model support, including termination and molecules outside the fitted union. The supplied chemistry assessment finds recognizable compact aromatic and basic-amine families among the leaders alongside attachment drift, excessive chain or ring growth, and absent stereochemical specification. A necessary probability bound on selected strings does not resolve those chemical limitations. The completed-task gains justify studying the conditional target effect further only with generation reliability and useful chemical transfer measured alongside fitting.

molecular.headline: Aromatic medicinal scaffolds and basic cyclic amines are present; attachment drift, oversized tails and unspecified stereochemistry remain.
molecular.overall_character: The output contains recognizable hydroxybenzamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, anilinoquinazolines, arylsulfonyl piperazines, tricyclic arylamines and acylhydrazones. Ring chemistry is abundant: the taskwise ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9716 to 0.9977, and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.906 to 0.9954. These are fractions of proposed SMILES containing the corresponding textual features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 38.8 to 45.5; they are string lengths, not molecular weights. Ordinary medicinal-sized structures coexist with much larger polyaryl, oligomeric and polymethylene outliers. The strongest families often look synthetically plausible by inspection, but unusual connectivity and extreme ring or chain growth make the complete output questionable as a ready-to-make collection. Structural diversity is moderate across trajectories and seeds, with much narrower high-score families. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0: potential stereocentres exist, but tetrahedral configuration is not encoded. All requested tasks have trajectories. The docking record is partial in two seeds, so its final excerpt must not be read as the endpoint of three completed runs. These are chemical readings of supplied structures and scores, not measured synthesis, stability, pharmacology or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring molecules are compact aromatic amides: phenolic benzamides bearing pyridylmethyl groups on the amide nitrogen, and hydroxy dimethylquinoline carboxamides bearing benzyl substituents. They combine aromatic or fused heteroaromatic rings with carbonyl acceptors, phenolic donors and ring nitrogens; some close analogues add halogen or nitrile substitution. These are recognizable, apparently makeable medicinal scaffolds. The amide nitrogen itself is not an ordinary basic amine. The low-score tail instead includes much larger polyaryl, repeatedly amidated structures and heavily substituted flexible assemblies. Compared with parent n-06c043e9d303, whose high scorers included azaindole ester amides, pyrazole carboxamides and heteroarylmethyl ureas, the child emphasizes different compact amide families; neither output lacks rings.
liabilities: Repeated aryl-amide growth produces very large, flexible, highly substituted structures with poor visible scores and a much less convincing medicinal size envelope.

The bis(pyridylmethyl) amides retain flexible benzylic links, while late catechol-like and N-hydroxy variants introduce additional chemical liabilities without reliable score improvement; stability was not measured.
missing_features: Many weak and final proposals fail to preserve the compact amide plus appropriately positioned aromatic nitrogen and hydroxyl arrangement seen in the better families.

Controlled alternative linkages that retain that donor/acceptor arrangement while changing flexibility are not demonstrated among the cited leaders. Any benefit from an unobserved scaffold remains unknown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamide reaches 0.48839749189747395, whereas the cited long polyaryl polyamide scores 8.44294806417311e-77. Within the benzamide family, a para-hydroxy analogue scores 0.46499055497527714, while replacing the hydroxyphenyl acyl group with a small oxygen/nitrogen heteroaryl group gives 0.13118230142245307. A final N-hydroxy amide that also loses a pyridylmethyl substituent scores 0.0053395148832984345; those simultaneous changes cannot be assigned separate effects. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The visible gradient therefore favors compact, specifically connected aromatic amide/heteroatom combinations, and sharply rejects excessive elaboration; it does not establish a missing reference pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of relatively compact, predominantly planar anilinoquinazolines: a fused nitrogen heteroaromatic core linked through NH to a fluorinated phenyl ring. The best examples add a phenol, with either fluorine or an amidine elsewhere on the fused core. Other high examples carry nitro, halogen, ester, or methoxy-substituted alkynyl side chains. This is an intelligible medicinal series with plausible conventional members, rather than a shortage of aromatic complexity. The halogen_rate is 0.8356 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.9954. Parent high scorers instead included fluorinated hydrazone, aminomethyl aryl and imine/thiourea assemblies; the child high-score family changes the core connections as well as its decorations.
liabilities: Dense aromatic and halogen substitution concentrates the leading series in a narrow chemical family; solubility and other physical properties have not been measured.

Nitro substituents, an unusual charge-separated sulfur group and a strained ring-contracted final structure merit chemical scrutiny. Their accepted scores do not establish stability or synthetic accessibility.
The methoxy-substituted alkynyl side-chain examples contain potentially stereogenic carbon without encoded configuration.
missing_features: Most weaker members lack the phenolic decoration in the same retained anilinoquinazoline context; functional-group identity and attachment location are not consistently maintained.

Broader high-scoring scaffold alternatives with comparably organized donors and ring-nitrogen acceptors are not demonstrated. The record does not show that added saturation or a basic aliphatic amine would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic anilinoquinazoline scores 0.8885781306387586 and its phenol/amidine relative 0.8845962113659023. Retaining the anilinoquinazoline but using the cited nitro decoration gives 0.6807958477508651, and the fluorine/chlorine analogue gives 0.6652249134948097. The low-score sulfone-containing fused heterocycle gives 0.2852486355366889. A tiny initial alkyl bromide already scores 0.5, so a value near that level is not evidence of useful chemical similarity by itself. The contrast supports the specific heteroaromatic/anilino arrangement and phenolic decoration more strongly than simply increasing fluorination or ring count. The amidine is optional in the best examples, not an established requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The supplied trajectories contain 260, 300 and 140 evaluations in seeds 0, 1 and 2 respectively, totaling the digest's 700 molecules. The highest-scoring excerpt is dominated by seed 1: N-alkyl or N-alkynyl piperazines and expanded diazacycles attached to a tricyclic diarylamine framework with saturated carbon bridges. They carry a credible protonatable aliphatic nitrogen beside substantial hydrophobic ring surfaces; basic cyclic amines are clearly present. Other seeds show tricyclic piperidine and flexible diamine families. Parent trajectories also contain high-scoring basic cyclic amines and flexible diamines, although their aromatic frameworks differ. Many of these ordinary-sized amine scaffolds are apparently makeable. At the opposite extreme, the final seed-2 excerpt includes immense polymethylene cyclic amidine and lactam structures that are chemically remote from the leading ligands.
liabilities: Extreme polymethylene ring growth, reaching the digest's maximum SMILES length of 154, creates obvious size and conformational liabilities; a ring-closure digit alone does not imply useful ring chemistry.
Long alkyl or alkynyl tails and expanded diazacycles add flexibility and hydrophobic burden to otherwise recognizable scaffolds. Those properties and biological selectivity were not measured.
The final excerpt belongs to the shortened seed-2 trajectory and must not be presented as the final chemical state of every seed.
missing_features: Many weak proposals lack the successful combination of an accessible basic aliphatic nitrogen, bounded linker length and organized aromatic surface, even when they contain numerous nitrogen atoms.

The record does not demonstrate stereochemically specified alternatives around the successful amine/ring arrangements. It provides no evidence that a particular unobserved stereoisomer would score better.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The alkynyl piperazine/tricyclic diarylamine reaches 0.9999940500545967; its shorter bridged analogue scores 0.9999908104453891 and an N-butyl analogue 0.9999903297149165. The cited nitro heteroaryl acid scores 1.8588450134335675e-05, and the sulfonamide containing a sulfonylated piperidine scores 1.9828327575562915e-05. This contrast is consistent with a properly presented protonatable amine and hydrophobic framework being useful; amide or sulfonamide nitrogen is not an equivalent substitute. The huge final cyclic amidine and lactam both receive 0.02885837683273086, which does not make their structures credible leads. The digest median is 0.007175, so the excellent leading family is not representative of most evaluated structures. These observations do not establish binding poses or why the shorter trajectories stopped.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules are arylsulfonyl piperazines joined to fused heteroaromatic lactam or cyclic ether/ketone frameworks, together with biaryl and alkoxy analogues bearing N-methylpiperazine. They have substantial aromatic surfaces, saturated diazacycles, sulfonyl acceptors and, in the leading fused series, a carbonyl and additional nitrogen functionality. These are recognizable, mostly plausible medicinal structures of moderate to relatively large size. The sulfonylated nitrogen is not basic; some N-methylpiperazine examples retain another protonatable nitrogen. The wider set also includes carbamates, imides, hydrazones and sulfur-rich heterocycles, as well as tiny fragments. Molecular identities and scores match parent n-06c043e9d303 in evaluation order across every supplied seed; the chemistry has not changed in these trajectories.
liabilities: Tiny reactive or unusual fragments, including an organic azide and N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide, coexist with the plausible medicinal families.
Some larger sulfur-rich and hydrazone-containing proposals have complicated connectivity or unspecified imine geometry without a clear benefit in the supplied scores.
missing_features: The weak tail lacks the integrated arylsulfonyl/cyclic-diazamine arrangement, and often the fused carbonyl-bearing ring, that co-occur in the leading examples.

Consistent exploration of alternative attachments while retaining that complete polar/aromatic combination is limited. The trajectories do not establish a specific additional functional group that would resolve the remaining score gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused nitrogen-heterocycle lactam/arylsulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2354681799202668; the cyclic ether/ketone relative scores 0.22956832167184824, and the methoxy biaryl N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide scores 0.22220352400833604. Carbon disulfide and the allyl azide each score 0.0, while the small hydroxylated ring acid scores 0.01347175576035981. The initial fused heterocyclic ester already reaches 0.1678386594791329. The observed gradient rewards combining several aromatic and polar structural elements over undersized fragments or a highly hydroxylated ring alone. The final seed-2 molecules spread those elements among other linkages and remain below the leading family; no unseen target structure can be reconstructed from these scores.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules occupy distinct compact families: an N-methyl benzamide linked to a hydroxylated, methyl-substituted fused nitrogen heterocycle; an aryl secondary alcohol connected through an amide to pyrazole; and aryl acylhydrazones bearing a pyridyl carbonyl end. The hydrazone series varies methoxy, methyl, dimethylamino and nitrile substitution while retaining aromatic rings and a carbonyl/N-N/imine connector. Conventional amides and the hydrazones look synthetically approachable by inspection, but makeability does not settle hydrazone stability or geometry. The low-score end contains highly extended polyaryl molecules, a peptide-like macrocycle, long alkyl appendages and complex polycycles. Seeds 0 and 1 reproduce the parent molecular/score sequences; seed 2 remains in the parent's aryl acylhydrazone family with changed substitutions rather than a new chemical class.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones carry possible hydrolysis, isomerization and tautomerism liabilities; the strings specify no imine geometry and supply no stability measurements.
Long-chain and highly elaborated polyaryl or peptide-like products greatly exceed the chemical size of the successful families and have extremely low visible scores.
The chemically distinct benzamide and secondary-alcohol families are not accompanied by a comparably developed set of improved analogues in their respective supplied trajectories.
missing_features: Many weak proposals fail to preserve the compact carbonyl plus nitrogen/oxygen pattern of the better examples, substituting excessive growth, different connections or strongly altered polarity.

The recurring hydrazone series lacks specified imine geometry and demonstrated stable alternative connectors at comparable size; the secondary-alcohol example lacks tetrahedral stereochemical specification. Their contribution to the score is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused heterocycle benzamide scores 0.30950439639437716, the aryl secondary-alcohol amide 0.27475852727088185, and the dimethylamino/nitrile hydrazone 0.27374106639693657. The methoxy hydrazone scores 0.23389266666198422, whereas a final phenolic relative scores 0.07524300360256067 and a bulky sulfamate-bearing relative 0.0002262008859360815. The cited peptide-like macrocycle scores 0.0 and the long-alkyl polyaryl structure 2.103895097704417e-113. The record supports a restricted size and polar/aromatic balance, with strong sensitivity to connections and substitutions, rather than adding heteroatoms or rings indiscriminately. The digest reports a median of 0.0 at its displayed precision; this is not a count of literally zero-valued molecules. These examples do not identify a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamide scores 0.48839749189747395, while replacing its hydroxyphenyl acyl group with the cited small oxygen/nitrogen heteroaryl group gives 0.13118230142245307. In another observed series, phenolic anilinoquinazoline reaches 0.8885781306387586 while the related nitro-decorated structure gives 0.6807958477508651. Abundant rings and heteroatoms alone do not preserve the favorable chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve useful functional-group connections when extending or decorating a scaffold.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded changes to attachment positions, ring heteroatoms and substituents while retaining accepted favorable combinations as alternatives within each isolated scoring history. Learn which combinations matter from that history's existing scores; no fixed pharmacophore or objective identity is justified.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest maximum SMILES length is 154 in a trajectory whose final excerpt contains enormous polymethylene cyclic amidine and lactam structures, both scored 0.02885837683273086. A repeatedly amidated polyaryl molecule scores 8.44294806417311e-77, and a long-alkyl polyaryl structure scores 2.103895097704417e-113. These are real accepted structures despite their unhelpful size and connectivity.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular size and ring closure are not reliably controlled during scaffold elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bounded chain extension, chemically reasonable ring closure and compact scaffold alternatives reliable capabilities. Let observed scores determine useful size regimes, without assuming every macrocycle or large molecule must be excluded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task's stereocentre_rate is 0.0. C=C(C)c1ccccc1C(O)CNC(=O)c1cc[nH]n1 contains an asymmetric alcohol-bearing carbon but no configuration marker; C#CC(OC)c1cc2c(Nc3ccc(F)c(F)c3)ncnc2cc1F likewise leaves its substituted carbon unspecified. The repeatedly emitted aryl acylhydrazones have no specified imine geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not specify tetrahedral stereochemistry and leave recurring imine geometry unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and validate stereochemical alternatives when the molecular graph supports them, while preserving their connection to accepted identities. Treat any score benefit from configuration as an open question; the present labels do not establish stereoselectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The top excerpts repeatedly reuse anilinoquinazoline decorations, tricyclic arylamine/diazacycle combinations, pyridyl acylhydrazones and phenolic bis(pyridylmethyl) benzamides. Other seeds contain distinct plausible amide, lactam and sulfonamide families, so the output is not globally collapsed; the limitation is sustained alternatives around the useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemical diversity across the whole output is not consistently retained among its useful scaffold families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain opportunities to extend chemically distinct accepted families within the current scoring history, alongside local analogue exploration. Evaluate scaffold and attachment diversity separately from changes that only move a halogen or lengthen an alkyl tail.

transferable_gaps.evidence: COc1ccc(C=NNC(=O)c2ccncc2)cc1OC scores 0.23389266666198422 and seeds a visible substitution family, but its imine geometry is unspecified. Conventional amide families also occur among the better molecules. The record shows neither stability measurements nor a controlled comparison of equally compact alternative linkers.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable and geometrically defined alternatives to recurrent hydrazone or imine linkages remain underdemonstrated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable linkage changes that preserve approximate size and donor/acceptor placement, allowing conventional amide and other chemically credible alternatives to be tested through the same task-local labels. Do not infer stability from SMILES validity or assume a linkage replacement will improve reward.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

retained_mechanisms: Unlabeled-corpus next-token training of a recurrent autoregressive SMILES prior with fixed-holdout checkpoint selection
Independent objective-local policy initialization from a verified frozen prior
Current scored-batch top-half elite admission and unchanged frozen-prior plus sixty-times-accepted-reward base targets

Complete autoregressive token sampling from the updated policy

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES prior on the supplied unlabeled strings, then chooses a checkpoint with a fixed holdout. Each objective receives a fresh policy copy and a frozen reference prior. Its best current observations train together with a uniform sample from the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted scores. A fixed prior-likelihood-plus-reward target drives bounded policy updates, and ancestral sampling generates complete new molecules that pass chemical and duplicate checks. Every unlabeled molecule is always presented in the same supplied traversal, so alternative starts and attachment contexts of that molecule receive no direct training exposure.
approach.novelty: Add equivalent rooted-SMILES views only during unlabeled prior training. For each selected training molecule, choose between its original string and one cached alternate traversal rooted at a reproducibly selected atom. Verify that the alternate has exactly the same canonical molecular identity and fits the existing token interface before using it. This lets the same molecular connections appear in different sequence contexts while preserving the original fixed holdout and all online learning rules. The earlier sibling grouped bracket characters into atom units; this experiment retains the Parent tokenizer and instead tests invariance to molecular traversal. Any improved language coverage must still transfer to valid novel chemistry to count as useful search.

nodes.hypothesis: During unlabeled prior training, mix each selected molecule's supplied SMILES with one cached, deterministic atom-rooted SMILES view whose canonical/isomeric molecular identity is verified, exposing the unchanged recurrent model to equivalent attachment contexts while keeping online learning and sampling unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Rooted views learned equivalent traversals, but validity fell and one replica stopped early
finding_summary.insights: Equivalent traversal exposure reached the training loss and transferred to held-out alternative strings. The smaller serialization preference is supported by improved alternate likelihood, while the loss on the supplied strings makes the tradeoff visible. This narrows the bottleneck: adding sequence contexts can improve traversal coverage without delivering reliable chemical search improvement. Lower duplicate rates did not translate into broader accepted scaffold coverage; invalid draws increased and late chemical families became more concentrated. The chemistry still favors conventional aromatic amine and carbonyl families, with unresolved attachment placement, extreme-size tails and reactive outliers. No missing stereochemical information was recovered. The available score changes are mixed and the completed-seed mean gain is below the registered 0.002 effect; the failed third task prevents the full intended score comparison. The specific canonicalization key mismatch identifies a separate robustness gap in the inherited feedback interface. Preparation stayed within the existing deadline and retained the same number of training batches, so lost training steps do not explain this outcome. Whether improved equivalent-string likelihood can preserve original-string quality and improve useful chemical coverage remains open.
finding_summary.results: Across three preparations, changed equivalent views appeared 10,938,511 times and contributed 553,572,420 target tokens to real training batches. Reconstructing all 3,629,346 cached row/view pairs and every training tensor receipt found no identity, token round-trip, length, or holdout-membership violation. The fixed panels contained 11,774 changed views. Their alternate NLL fell from 4.5739 to 0.7043 nats per alternate token. Under the same independent checkpoint comparison, alternate NLL improved from the parent's 1.6256 to 0.7043, while original-string NLL worsened from 0.5638 to 0.6004. The alternate-minus-original full-sequence NLL gap narrowed from 55.16 to 6.61 nats per changed molecule. Each preparation finished 29,742 training batches; mean preparation time rose from 243.5 to 902.0 seconds, with a 401.8 MiB temporary cache. On the same 14 completed tasks, raw validity fell from 90.24% to 86.55%, duplicates fell from 29.22% to 23.47%, and novel draws rose from 61.01% to 63.08%. Mean accepted scaffold counts stayed similar (218.4 to 217.2), while late scaffold concentration increased. The two completed paired seeds scored 0.51444 versus 0.51394, a mean change of +0.00050; their individual changes were -0.00199 and +0.00300. The third DRD2 run stopped at 170 evaluations because an emitted aromatic string changed canonical form when reparsed, activating the unchanged feedback-provenance guard. Its incomplete task leaves the three-seed macro score unavailable. All logged online updates preserve the frozen prior and original accepted replay strings.

Reconstructing all 3,629,346 cached row/view pairs and every training tensor receipt found no identity, token round-trip, length, or holdout-membership violation. The fixed panels contained 11,774 changed views. Their alternate NLL fell from 4.5739 to 0.7043 nats per alternate token. Under the same independent checkpoint comparison, alternate NLL improved from the parent's 1.6256 to 0.7043, while original-string NLL worsened from 0.5638 to 0.6004. The alternate-minus-original full-sequence NLL gap narrowed from 55.16 to 6.61 nats per changed molecule. Each preparation finished 29,742 training batches; mean preparation time rose from 243.5 to 902.0 seconds, with a 401.8 MiB temporary cache. On the same 14 completed tasks, raw validity fell from 90.24% to 86.55%, duplicates fell from 29.22% to 23.47%, and novel draws rose from 61.01% to 63.08%. Mean accepted scaffold counts stayed similar (218.4 to 217.2), while late scaffold concentration increased. The two completed paired seeds scored 0.51444 versus 0.51394, a mean change of +0.00050; their individual changes were -0.00199 and +0.00300. The third DRD2 run stopped at 170 evaluations because an emitted aromatic string changed canonical form when reparsed, activating the unchanged feedback-provenance guard. Its incomplete task leaves the three-seed macro score unavailable. All logged online updates preserve the frozen prior and original accepted replay strings.

Equivalent traversal exposure reached the training loss and transferred to held-out alternative strings. The smaller serialization preference is supported by improved alternate likelihood, while the loss on the supplied strings makes the tradeoff visible. This narrows the bottleneck: adding sequence contexts can improve traversal coverage without delivering reliable chemical search improvement. Lower duplicate rates did not translate into broader accepted scaffold coverage; invalid draws increased and late chemical families became more concentrated. The chemistry still favors conventional aromatic amine and carbonyl families, with unresolved attachment placement, extreme-size tails and reactive outliers. No missing stereochemical information was recovered. The available score changes are mixed and the completed-seed mean gain is below the registered 0.002 effect; the failed third task prevents the full intended score comparison. The specific canonicalization key mismatch identifies a separate robustness gap in the inherited feedback interface. Preparation stayed within the existing deadline and retained the same number of training batches, so lost training steps do not explain this outcome. Whether improved equivalent-string likelihood can preserve original-string quality and improve useful chemical coverage remains open.

molecular.headline: Conventional aromatic amines and carbonyl heterocycles dominate, with size extremes and an anomalous oxygen cation
molecular.overall_character: The output spans many recognizable medicinal-chemistry families: diarylamino heteroarenes, substituted quinazolines and pyrimidinones, indole-linked piperazines, sulfonamides, hydantoins, ureas and small saturated rings. Most leading molecules are medium-sized and have conventional bonds, with plausible synthetic entry points through amide formation, amine substitution or aromatic coupling. The full trajectories are structurally broad, although individual late families become much narrower. The supplied digest contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task except drd2_docking, which has 770 molecules and 740 proposals; that task's seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 170, so no later molecules are inferred. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9816 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9483 to 0.9966. Mean SMILES lengths range from 39.2 to 50.1, but long polyaryl assemblies, lipids, peptides and highly polar nucleotide-like structures create an extreme-size tail. Charged-token rates range from 0.023 to 0.1207; many charges belong to recognizable nitro or N-oxide groups, while a leading molecule contains a chemically anomalous terminal positive oxygen. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the supplied parent strings. The overall chemistry is mostly plausible and moderately drug-like, with isolated severe exceptions and no evidence that all stereogenic products represent defined stereoisomers.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leading family consists of fairly compact diarylamino pyrimidines or a related pyridine, decorated with methoxy, ethoxy, methyl, phenol and aryl halogen groups. These are aromatic, largely flat molecules with exocyclic NH connections and heteroaromatic acceptors. Most of this family has ordinary, synthetically plausible bonding. The best-scoring entry is an exception: its terminal positive oxygen is singly attached to an aryl carbon and has an open-shell valence representation, rather than an ordinary phenol or ether. Other seeds contain acylurea and hydrazone-related aromatic families. The lowest examples are much larger polyaryl assemblies, elaborate fused polycycles or long unsaturated chains with multiple carbonyl groups.
liabilities: The singly bound terminal positive oxygen in the nominal best entry is an unusual open-shell species and cannot be treated as an ordinary stable medicinal substituent.
Multiple aromatic rings and aryl NH links yield predominantly flat structures, while the extreme tail adds excessive ring and linker complexity.
Hydrazone-related and heavily elaborated low-scoring molecules introduce additional configurational or chemical ambiguity without resolving the observed structural fit.
missing_features: The large low-scoring structures lack the compact aromatic and polar-group arrangement retained by the neutral diarylamino heteroarene leaders.
Matched neutral, closed-shell alternatives around the best oxygen-cation entry are not fully established by the displayed examples, although closely scoring ordinary phenolic relatives already exist.

The current leading set does not recover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule; this is a missing well-performing chemical family among the displayed leaders, not proof that a particular group is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The unusual oxygen-cation structure scores 0.42762099872850584, while ordinary phenol/methoxy/methyl diarylamino pyrimidines with either meta aryl chlorine or fluorine score 0.42408253349563446. Ethoxy analogues score 0.42036761694214836 for either halogen, so the chemical family is supported without relying on the anomalous oxygen. Moving chlorine from the meta to para position in the displayed phenol-containing series gives 0.3925552460025089; the para-hydroxy relative scores 0.342125381162771. The largest multiaryl example scores 8.434866188027838e-50. This favors a compact arrangement of aromatic rings, amino links and selected substituent positions, rather than indiscriminate aromatic growth. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a compact substituted indole carboxamide; current seed 0 reaches 0.40822403535979507 with an acylurea-like family. Current seed 2 instead reaches 0.42762099872850584 versus the parent's 0.3900700429110833 with an aryl sulfonamide family. These different frameworks leave no unique missing pharmacophore established.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are moderately sized to bulky, aromatic and heteroaromatic structures with methoxy-rich phenyl or fused aza-aromatic systems. Quinazoline-like cores carry amidine, amide or aryl connections; another strong family consists of amino pyrimidinones connecting a methoxylated aryl group to a fluorinated aryl or pyridyl group. The amide, amidine, amino and ether functionality is mostly conventional and synthetically plausible. Some other high examples link several nitrogen-rich heterocycles, increasing aromatic density. The lows include a small acyclic polyether, simple dimethoxybenzene, a small bicyclic lactam and sulfur-oxidized aromatic compounds.
liabilities: Repeated aromatic and methoxy-rich substitution creates fairly flat, heavily decorated structures with limited saturated shape diversity in the leading series.
Amidine protonation and the ionization of nitrogen-rich heterocycles are not characterized by their mostly neutral drawn forms.
Large multiheteroaryl extensions and occasional reactive or charged structures in the wider trajectory add chemistry outside the relatively conventional leading families.
missing_features: Small fragment-like products lack the connected multi-ring heteroaromatic and polar-linker organization present in the leading molecules.

The low-scoring sulfone relatives show that adding an acceptor-rich substituent does not preserve the needed arrangement. More matched changes in linker position, heteroaromatic nitrogen placement and substitution are needed to distinguish useful geometry from mere group presence.

The displayed high-scoring series offers relatively little saturated-ring shape variation while retaining its useful aromatic and polar fragments; these data do not establish whether that missing shape diversity would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amidine-bearing methoxy-rich aza-aromatic molecule scores 0.6070600130851127, versus 0.601092340050207 for its amide relative. A trifluoroanilide aza-aromatic compound scores 0.6051953628166595 and an amino pyrimidinone with a fluoropyridyl group reaches 0.6038062283737025. per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are conventional indoles joined through short alkyl chains to an aryl-substituted piperazine. Their substituents include aryl chlorine or nitrile, alkoxy, alkyl, alkenyl, alkynyl and ordinary thioether groups. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve feasible absolute and relative configurations where stereochemistry exists, and generate matched stereoisomers when relevant. nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches a tree of partial SMILES strings. It initializes each objective's tree from the supplied scored molecules, chooses token branches using their average accepted return and an upper confidence exploration bonus, and expands branches supported by a corpus-trained language model. That model remains frozen and completes selected prefixes into whole molecules. Accepted scores update the generating paths. To fill a proposal batch, the Parent selects a block of rollout paths before generating their completions, using the same completed-observation counts for every selection in that block.
approach.novelty: Add pending-path counts to UCT so each selected rollout reserves its path before the next path is chosen. The exploration bonus then accounts for both completed and outstanding work, while average rewards continue to use accepted observations. Reservations disappear when a rollout is discarded or its feedback arrives. This tests whether acknowledging work already assigned reduces repeated sampling from one prefix during a batch. This lineage currently contains only the Parent; no sibling has tested pending-aware selection.

nodes.hypothesis: Reserve each selected rollout along its prefix path and include completed plus pending counts in UCT's exploration term, while retaining accepted-only empirical reward means; release each reservation when the rollout is discarded or its observation resolves.

finding_summary.headline: Reservations spread evaluated rollouts across prefixes; the screening score falls
finding_summary.insights: Delayed-feedback concentration is controllable with the existing frozen generator and accepted-only reward estimates. The controlled replay establishes that outstanding work changes actual choices, and the emitted-molecule analysis establishes that the added branch coverage survives invalid, duplicate and surplus filtering. However, almost complete dispersion across ten starting prefixes did not produce a better overall best molecule within the screening budget. This leaves the useful balance between branch reuse and wider allocation open; the score losses do not establish that reservations are generally harmful. The molecular assessment found broadly diverse ring chemistry comparable to the Parent, with useful amine and heteroaromatic motifs already reachable but inconsistent control of their arrangement and whole-molecule growth. That narrows the unresolved problem to obtaining and refining useful chemical combinations: a larger count of distinct SMILES prefixes alone does not establish better chemical coverage. These structural observations suggest an explanation to investigate, not a demonstrated cause of the score decrease. One seed supports activation and a mixed score outcome, without establishing reproducibility or which degree of allocation spread would improve final Top-1.
finding_summary.results: On the single paired screening seed, pending work changed 4,361 of 5,834 branch decisions with a choice between eligible children (74.75%). Of these changes, 3,961 came from altered UCT rankings among completed children; another 400 involved priority for children without completed observations. All 2,900 reservations resolved exactly once, without negative counts, leaks or changes to completed reward statistics. Mean concentration of evaluated rollout-start prefixes fell from 0.809379 to 0.117517 across 145 batches, and distinct prefixes per ten-molecule batch rose from 1.73 to 9.54. Single-prefix batches fell from 76 of 145 to zero, with lower concentration on all five objectives and every paired batch. Both runs delivered all 1,450 valid, unique optimizer proposals within the same oracle budget and retained identical frozen prior weights. The macro final Top-1 score nevertheless fell from 0.479189 to 0.473468, a decrease of 0.005720. Final scores rose for zaleplon_mpo (0.394920 to 0.409811), drd2_docking (0.977922 to 0.999998), and median_2 (0.179942 to 0.180094), while deco_hop fell from 0.606003 to 0.580076 and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.237157 to 0.197364. The proposed allocation mechanism is confirmed; its expected positive score effect was not observed.

molecular.headline: Diverse aromatic and saturated ring chemistry; missing stereochemical specification and consistent control of useful motif arrangements.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied seed-0 trajectories and their Parent counterparts were read; no task lacks a trajectory. Each current trajectory contains 300 unique molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Evaluation numbers below refer to these current trajectories unless explicitly marked Parent. The proposals are predominantly ring-containing medicinal-chemistry-like structures: linked phenyl and aza-aromatic rings, fused heterocycles, piperidines, piperazines, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, phenols and occasional highly elaborate polycycles. The digest ring-closure occurrence rates are 0.9897 to 1.0 and aromatic-token occurrence rates are 0.9517 to 0.9862; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths are 37.6 to 39.8 characters, with task maxima from 70 to 87 characters; these are size proxies, not molecular weights. Structural breadth is real and comparable to the Parent, including both aromatic and saturated ring families. Basic cyclic amines are clearly present and must not be called globally missing. Every task has stereocentre_rate 0.0, even though some structures contain potentially stereogenic saturated frameworks. The major deficits are unassigned stereochemistry, inconsistent arrangement of already available polar and aromatic motifs, and excursions into oversized or chemically awkward assemblies. Common scaffolds look makeable in principle, but the peroxyester, unusual imine/imidic-acid representations, densely substituted fused systems and very large appendages justify a questionable overall synthesis reading. This is a structural assessment of the supplied seed, not a synthetic-route validation or an activation judgement.

per_task.generated_character: Ring-rich aromatic and heteroaromatic molecules dominate: ring_closure_rate 0.9966, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9586 and mean SMILES length 39.3. Evaluation 64 is a fused sulfur/nitrogen heterocycle with an oxo group, hydroxymethyl substituent and aminomethyl-linked biphenyl; evaluation 89 is an aminomethyl biphenyl bearing a fluorobenzamide; evaluation 264 is an N-acylated, partly saturated fused nitrogen ring system. The initial indole carboxamide at evaluation 9 already combines a compact aromatic framework with amide and methoxy groups. These are recognisable small-molecule scaffold combinations, although fused-core preparation and substitution selectivity would need examination. The low end includes a long-chain phosphorus-acid/thioether assembly, a large polyaryl polyamine and a tiny nitrotriazole. Rings and functional-group variety are abundant; stereochemical assignments are absent.
liabilities: Evaluation 15 couples extensive hydrocarbon growth to multiple phosphorus-acid oxygens, while evaluation 183 combines large aromatic bulk with several amine-containing appendages; both illustrate poor control of whole-molecule size and polarity.

The dibrominated, multiply substituted cyclopentene at evaluation 38 and the elaborate fused systems raise substitution-selectivity and stereochemical preparation questions even though their graphs were accepted.
missing_features: Most weak examples lack the balanced, intermediate-sized aromatic-plus-polar arrangement visible in the stronger examples: some are too small and sparsely decorated, while others carry long chains or excessive appended ring systems.

A controlled set of close variants preserving a promising ring arrangement while adjusting heteroatom position, linker length or polar substituents is not demonstrated by the cited high and final examples. Their diversity does not identify one additional mandatory functional group.

Explicit stereochemical specification is missing from the substituted saturated frameworks, including evaluation 38. The supplied scores do not establish whether specifying it would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 64 scores 0.409810651230724, evaluation 89 scores 0.4020361505269851 and the initial indole amide scores 0.3051048083696145. In contrast, the long-chain phosphorus-containing evaluation 15 scores 0.0, the bulky polyamine at evaluation 183 scores 2.20671388958451e-47, and the small nitrotriazole at evaluation 77 scores 9.100886676973802e-15. The visible association is with an intermediate-sized aromatic framework carrying a restrained arrangement of polar substituents, rather than with simply adding rings, nitrogen or charge. It is not a universal amide requirement: some other high scorers lack an amide. The late piperazine/sulfonamide/piperidine assembly at evaluation 299 scores only 1.7564413240447329e-06, despite having familiar medicinal groups; the digest median is 0.007587. Parent evaluation 272 reached 0.3949199041196016 with an aryl nitrile/pyridyl/furyl thiourea assembly. The current best changes the particular scaffold while retaining the broad combination of aromatic bulk and short polar functions; it does not reveal a new globally absent ring class.

per_task.generated_character: The output consists mostly of linked or fused aromatic systems with diazines and other nitrogen heterocycles, exocyclic amino groups, ethers, thioethers and sulfonamides. Mean SMILES length is 37.6, ring_closure_rate is 0.9931 and aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9517. Evaluation 133 joins an amino-substituted diazine to a substituted phenyl and an ether-linked diazine; evaluation 130 is an anilino aza-aromatic fused system carrying another fused sulfur/nitrogen heteroaryl unit. Evaluation 126 is an aryl sulfonamide linking nitrogen-rich aromatic regions. Much of this resembles synthetically plausible heteroaryl coupling and substitution chemistry. The breadth also reaches a heavily halogenated fused system at evaluation 192 and a very large planar fused aza-aromatic assembly at evaluation 206, whose preparation and physical properties are less reassuring.
liabilities: The bromine/iodine-substituted fused aromatic at evaluation 192 and the extensive planar ring assembly at evaluation 206 carry substantial aromatic bulk and potential solubility and synthesis liabilities. Their relatively high recorded scores do not remove those structural concerns.

The cyclic and flexible carbon-linked sulfone examples score poorly despite ordinary-looking component groups, illustrating that functional-group inventory alone misses a consequential connectivity difference.
missing_features: The lower-scoring saturated sulfone and simple aminoether examples lack the connected aza-aromatic and exocyclic amino arrangement common among the stronger molecules.

The top excerpt does not demonstrate close substitution variants around its useful amino-heteroaromatic cores. Exact attachment positions and polar-group context remain unresolved; merely increasing fused-ring extent is not supported as an answer.

The exocyclic imino heterocycle at evaluation 291, the aryl imine at evaluation 55 and the imidic-acid representation at evaluation 300 raise tautomer, hydrolysis or configurational questions that are not resolved by the recorded score.

The stronger compact heterocyclic combinations are not accompanied in the digest by a coherent series that preserves their arrangement while varying one substituent. The missing capability is precise co-arrangement, not globally absent fluorine, amines or heterocycles.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0 on every supplied task, as in the Parent. The emitted aminocyclopentyl structure NC1CCC(c2c[nH]c3ccc(-n4cnnc4)cc23)C1 and substituted cyclopentene OCC1CC(n2cncn2)=C(c2cc(Br)cc(O)c2Br)C1c1ccccc1 contain saturated substitution patterns whose stereochemical alternatives are not specified. This establishes an output representation gap, not a measured score gain from stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not emit explicit stereochemical identities for its saturated and potentially stereogenic structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stereochemical specification available in de novo generation and preserve it through identity handling. Let accepted observations from the current session determine whether particular configurations are useful; do not assume every objective distinguishes them.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The structure c1ccc2c(c1)CCCN2CCCN1CCC(c2noc3ccccc23)CC1 scores 0.999998249672007, while the later amine-containing c1ccc(N2CCN(C(Cn3cccn3)c3ccncc3)CC2)cc1 scores 0.19802005266210823. In another supplied trajectory, O=S(=O)(Nc1ccc(-n2ccnc2)cc1)c1cccc2cnccc12 scores 0.5732259891576988 but O=S(=O)(CCNCCOc1ccc(Br)cc1)c1ccc(F)cc1 scores 0.2715410107705054. Both comparisons retain broad functional-group categories while changing connectivity and environment; they are observational contrasts, not matched molecular pairs. The output already contains cyclic amines and sulfur chemistry, so adding those categories alone would not address the gap.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not demonstrate controlled variation of linker geometry and nitrogen environment while preserving a promising ring arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo conditional variations that can retain a locally promising ring framework while changing linker length, attachment position or a nitrogen functional state separately. Derive any retained arrangement only from accepted observations within the current session, without a task-specific motif library.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Task mean SMILES lengths stay between 37.6 and 39.8 characters, but long and elaborate tails remain. The long-chain phosphorus-acid structure O=P(O)(O)OP(=O)(O)c1cncc(CCCC#CCCCCCCC(O)CSCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCO)c1 scores 0.0, as do the bulky oxime-ether ester and glycoside cited above. A large polar guanidine/sulfonamide assembly and a large hydrophobic polyaryl amine score 2.1621778663534096e-63 and 4.5515839886258796e-63 in the same trajectory, while its compact heterocyclic examples reach 0.19736413136179395 and 0.18901307662677713. Conversely, a tiny nitrotriazole in another trajectory also scores poorly, so indiscriminate shortening is unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control whole-molecule size and polar appendage growth around useful chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Allow de novo generation to adjust scaffold extent, branch growth and polar substitution separately, preserving enough context to learn which combinations the current accepted observations favor. Use adaptive chemical size control rather than treating SMILES length as molecular weight or imposing a universal small-molecule cutoff.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The emitted chlorinated peroxyester C=C(Cl)C(Cl)C(Cl)CCOOC(C)=O scores 0.02101192765437668 and the activated nitroalkene/sulfone C=C([N+](=O)[O-])S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1 scores 9.203194082858293e-05. Other cited structures contain imidic-acid representations, dense halogen substitution and elaborate unassigned polycycles. In contrast, some common amide, ether and cyclic-amine combinations score well. The high-scoring imino heterocycle also shows why an unfamiliar functional group cannot be discarded solely because it looks unusual.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a valid molecular graph from a chemically ordinary, plausibly preparable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemical-stability, tautomer and synthetic-complexity context during generation or candidate review, so accepted feedback can distinguish useful diversity from awkward assemblies. Prefer coherent chemistry learned from the permitted unlabeled corpus; avoid blanket bans on heteroatoms, formal charge or all uncommon groups.

nodes.method_name: ChemTS: UCT-guided SMILES prefix search with a frozen rollout prior
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in [ChemTS](https://arxiv.org/html/1710.00616v1): train a compact autoregressive SMILES model solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze it. For each independent objective, maintain a fresh prefix tree whose nodes hold visit counts and observed returns. Initialize its statistics from the supplied observations. Select prefixes through upper-confidence tree search, expand them using the frozen model's next-token distribution, and generate complete molecules by stochastic continuation. Backpropagate accepted oracle scores through the corresponding paths after feedback. Generate further continuations until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. This is an expanding generative tree, with no corpus ranking or fixed molecular candidate set. The hypothesis is that sharing each scarce reward across its visited prefixes directs subsequent continuations toward promising molecular families quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. The root adapts tree statistics; it does not update neural parameters with rewards. The paper supports this search mechanism, but its larger, time-limited experiments do not establish performance under this benchmark's scarce feedback. Learning a useful rollout prior within permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.

approach.method_basis: A genetic algorithm run directly on molecular graphs. It keeps a population of molecules that have already been scored by the objective, samples breeding parents from the high-scoring end of that population, and builds new candidates by cutting two parents apart and recombining connected fragments, and by making small local edits to atoms and bonds. Everything generated is sanitised, canonicalised and sent straight to the oracle; whatever comes back with a good score is merged into the population and the weakest members are dropped. There is no surrogate model, no pretrained network, no library of catalogue molecules to rank, and no cross-task memory: the only thing that steers the search is the scores of the molecules this run has itself already paid for.
approach.novelty: The method statement leaves the selection pressure, the population bookkeeping and the failure handling open, and this implementation fixes all three. Parents are drawn from three declared high-ranked score bands rather than from a single elite cut, so breeding stays broad while still being score-directed. Survival is greedy on a bounded population of sixty-four, seeded only from the ten scored molecules supplied at the start, with accepted offspring merged the moment their scores arrive so the very next batch already breeds from them. Proposals that come back invalid or already-seen are replaced by generating more molecules from the same operators, never by falling back to a fixed reserve list. Seven distinct atom and bond mutation operators sit alongside fragment crossover, and every breeding event logs its parent ranks, operator provenance and parent-beating outcome so the selection pressure can be checked after the fact rather than assumed.

nodes.hypothesis: Evolve a task-local population of scored molecular graphs by sampling breeding parents across high-ranked score quantiles, generating de novo offspring with graph crossover and atom/bond mutation, and greedily retaining the highest-scoring observed survivors after each feedback batch.

finding_summary.headline: Plain graph evolution with no learned model ranks third of thirteen Discovery roots, and every intended behaviour activated
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a strong, cheap baseline. Against the thirteen Discovery roots on this seed, which span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root sits third at 0.4917, within 0.019 of the best method in the round, and it did that with no pretraining, no corpus-trained generator, no surrogate and no learned policy. That reframes what the more elaborate lineages have to justify: any learned component now has to earn its place against direct selection on task-local scores, not against a naive baseline. The interesting tension is that activation was clean while efficiency was not. Roughly six in seven oracle calls went to molecules that did not beat the parent that made them, and the mean offspring was worse than its parent, so the strong result comes from occasionally getting lucky at scale rather than from reliably climbing. That is precisely the bottleneck a proposal-filtering mechanism would attack, and it is the most concrete Development target this root produces. What is still open: one seed only, so no reliability claim and no anchor decision; no paired comparison against any other algorithm; and the retry machinery was never stressed, since the longest rejection streak was two, so behaviour on an exhausted or hostile neighbourhood is untested.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.4917 on the single screening seed, with per-task finals of 0.5989 on deco_hop, 0.9051 on drd2_docking, 0.2083 on median_2, 0.3315 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.4145 on zaleplon_mpo. All four pre-registered observables moved in the intended direction and the falsifier was not triggered. Parent selection was strongly score-directed: across 2225 breeding selections the mean topness percentile was 0.883 against a uniform baseline of 0.5, an enrichment of +0.383, and all three declared quantile bands were used on every task. Both operator families produced offspring on every task, with crossover behind 0.439 and atom/bond mutation behind 0.743 of the 1450 emitted molecules; 74 outer retries were needed for 1524 attempts. Feedback demonstrably changed the search: 1025 offspring were admitted to the population immediately, 432 distinct admitted offspring were later chosen as parents 2084 times, and reuse began in batch 2 on every task. Final population best rose above initialization everywhere, most sharply on drd2_docking (0.0190 to 0.9051) and sitagliptin_mpo (0.0021 to 0.3315). The one weak number is local improvement: only 201 of 1450 offspring, or 13.9 percent, strictly beat their best breeding parent, and the mean child-minus-best-parent difference was -0.084.
