transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring digest molecules contain N-chloroamides, N-brominated heterocycles, N-F groups, multiply bonded sulfur with explicit sulfur hydrogens, and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Recognizable aromatic, carbonyl and amine fragments coexist with these liabilities. Some chemically more conventional analogues score well, so none of these liabilities is demonstrated to be universally necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local chemical environments while varying favorable ring and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could expose alternatives with conventional bond environments while preserving the surrounding attachments, using local chemical context rather than atom valence alone. Evaluate such alternatives through the existing score interface; a plausibility preference is a hypothesis to test, not an assumed score improvement or a blanket exclusion of sulfur.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading examples concentrate on close analogues of fused heteroaryl carbonyls, N-O bridged azaaryl lactams, aminoalkyl sulfur polycycles and dense fluorinated cages. Low-scoring counterparts often disrupt an aromatic ring, carbonyl linkage or aminoalkyl spacer; the output does not establish that elaborate bridges are required to retain the favorable arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks demonstrated simple scaffold and linker alternatives that retain favorable functional-group placement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically coherent ring/linker replacements or simplifications that retain attachment points and recognizable donor, acceptor and aromatic arrangements. Such proposals would test whether the same useful local features can be expressed in more conventional frameworks, using only the current molecule and observed feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the quoted molecules contain crowded substituted aza rings, fluorinated saturated carbons and bridged cages. The observed structural diversity therefore leaves configuration unresolved; the supplied scores do not establish whether assigning configuration would be recognized or rewarded.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate stereochemically specified alternatives for its asymmetric ring and substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where a generated graph permits stereoisomers, expose chemically consistent stereochemical alternatives and determine through the existing identity and evaluation interfaces whether they remain distinct and score-sensitive. Treat this as missing representation coverage, not evidence that one particular configuration is favorable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports charged_rate 0.0, yet higher-scoring molecules include unacylated cyclic amines and aminomethyl branches. Formal charge is unspecified or neutral in these strings; this observation neither removes their potential basicity nor establishes their state under any experimental condition.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate charge-state coverage for the free amines it already emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic representation could consider chemically appropriate ionization alternatives where the protocol permits them, while checking whether normalization and scoring distinguish those states. No objective identity or presumed assay condition should be used to choose a charge state.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several leading large heterocyclic molecules share the recorded score 0.6155070237050044 despite changes in alkyl length, sulfur substitution and N-bromination. Long ether/thioether appendages and crowded substitutions persist, while other leading families similarly contain many close variants of elaborate ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not establish which bulky peripheral decorations are dispensable within a high-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer controlled peripheral shortening or branch replacement that keeps the central attachment framework intact. Observed ties can motivate testing simpler molecules, but do not prove that an unevaluated deletion will preserve the score; retain ordinary feedback-based comparison.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It uses score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations, including its retained formula-preserving aromatic nitrogen-position exchange. Stable identity admission checks each fresh candidate before a surplus pool is formed. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses binary local-environment fingerprints to predict that pool, and correlated posterior draws choose the molecules submitted for evaluation. Accepted feedback updates both the breeding population and the full prediction archive.
approach.novelty: Make the posterior sensitive to how many times each local molecular environment occurs. Replace binary fingerprint presence with integer environment counts and the corresponding generalized Tanimoto covariance. Repeated ring or substituent environments can then change similarity even when their presence is already recorded. Earlier siblings changed survivor or parent allocation, graph edits and identity admission; they have not changed the posterior to retain environment multiplicity. This mechanism supplies quantitative representation to the existing learned selector. Its usefulness must be established through prospective prediction and the paired search results.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace binary Morgan-presence covariance with generalized Tanimoto covariance on integer counts of the same hashed local molecular environments, so the accepted-feedback Gaussian process conditions on environment multiplicity.

finding_summary.headline: Environment counts change selection and lift mean score by 0.0226, but uncertainty coverage worsens
finding_summary.insights:
The useful change comes from reweighting ordinary similarity relationships, not from splitting exact fingerprint ties: the only binary-equivalent pair in the Child pools remained count-equivalent. Counts usually increased archive-to-pool similarity and reduced posterior uncertainty, but neither direction was universal. Their prediction advantage was much larger when passively applied to the Parent's selected stream than on their own selected stream, showing why historical prediction gains need to be checked after selection adapts. Sitagliptin supplies the largest score gain even though its paired MSE worsens and its latent intervals cover only one third of scored emissions. Improved mean prediction therefore does not fully explain the whole-search gain; the contribution of changed uncertainty to allocation remains open. Uncertainty calibration is now a concrete issue to probe separately.

The molecular assessment finds smaller families in several streams, yet oversized assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds, constrained rings and unspecified stereochemistry remain. Counts preserve the same local environment vocabulary and many hashing collisions; they supply neither a demonstrated size penalty nor evidence of synthetic or geometric feasibility. These results establish count-sensitive posterior execution and utility on the supplied panel, while leaving broader chemical usefulness and transfer to other search distributions unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
Environment multiplicity changed the similarity matrices and posterior distribution in all 435 fits. On identical archives and pools, 69,570 of 69,600 predicted means changed; replaying the same random draws changed 434 of 435 selected batches. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.55177 to 0.57434, a gain of 0.02257 above the registered 0.002 minimum. Two seed means improved and one fell. Mean final scores rose for sitagliptin by 0.06213, median similarity by 0.02333, DRD2 by 0.02056 and decoration hopping by 0.00911, while zaleplon fell by 0.00228. All evaluations completed; strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350 offspring.

On the Child's identical scored molecules, the count model reduced prediction MSE from a passive binary model's 0.011797 to 0.011269, about 4.5%, and raised mean within-batch rank correlation from 0.469 to 0.550. The archive-mean baseline MSE was 0.042504. However, mean latent interval width shrank from 0.263 to 0.168, and nominal 95% coverage fell from 85.6% to 76.9%; including observation noise only raised count-model coverage to 77.2%. This is evidence for better average prediction and search outcomes on this panel, alongside worse uncertainty coverage.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich families become smaller in several streams, but unusual heteroatom bonds and unspecified ring stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks and their Parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure text presence ranges from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The products include indole carboxamides, linked nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatics, aryl-bearing cyclic amines, medium-ring aza-dicarbonyl assemblies, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Distinct families occur across seeds, while leading excerpts concentrate on related members within a family. Several streams are smaller on average than Parent n-9edaa26007c3, but small size does not remove N-F, N-S, unusual sulfur bonding, unsaturated small rings or difficult polycyclic connectivity. Every task has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral strings still contain potentially basic amines; the strings do not establish solution or evaluator protonation states. Structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of the supplied trajectories, recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-02-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. Parsing establishes connectivity, without establishing a feasible conformation, stability or synthetic route.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family comprises medium-sized, heavily substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Methoxy or vinyl-ether groups, methyl/vinyl substituents, an indole NH and an amide carbonyl recur; many leading amides carry N-F or N-Cl. A conventional secondary-amide member has 24 heavy atoms and three rings. The highest observed molecule instead has a compact bridged nitrogen-containing core, a phenyl carboxamide with an N-S bond, and 24 heavy atoms. The indole/aryl amide components are familiar synthetic building blocks, whereas the N-halogen, N-sulfanyl and bridged variants are less routine endpoints. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.2 versus Parent 44.7; halogen presence falls from the Parent digest 0.9609 to 0.623. The Parent highest observed record was an N-fluoro indole/pyridyl carboxamide at 0.46092619585962435. The current chemistry retains that broad family while increasing vinyl substitution and changing the leading bridged core.
liabilities: The leading N-F and N-Cl bonds are on amide nitrogen, rather than carbon-bound aromatic halogens; the highest molecule also has an N-S bond. These require separate chemical scrutiny from ordinary aryl carboxamides.
Vinyl ethers and the compact bridged nitrogen-containing core add reactivity or geometric questions. The bridged product has a potential stereochemical choice that its string does not specify.
missing_features: The low-end fragments lack the integrated fused-aromatic, carbonyl and aryl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the stronger molecules; some late substitutions also fail to retain its favorable balance.

Conventional amide substitution is demonstrated near the leading scores, but an equally strong family with both ordinary bond chemistry and straightforward alternative core connectivity is not established. The observations do not identify an unseen target-specific group that must be added.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The cited divinyl/methoxy pyridyl secondary amide scores 0.4330127018922193; replacing its amide hydrogen with either Cl or F gives 0.4423126980074005 in both cases. The N-fluoro phenyl/vinyl-ether congener reaches 0.4484138510190879, and the bridged N-S-containing product reaches 0.45766047024715. Methane scores 0.0. A late amino-substituted indole congener scores 0.2859212949869023 despite retaining the amide and aromatic rings. The visible gradient favors a particular combined aromatic/carbonyl/substituent arrangement over fragments, and tolerates unusual amide substitution; it does not show a general benefit from adding nitrogen or halogen.

per_task.generated_character: The leading excerpt contains a fused nitrogen/oxygen carbonyl heteroaromatic core connected through an aryl ether to pyridyl rings, including a nitrile-bearing terminal ring. Methoxy and methyl groups accompany branched polyenes bearing carbon-bound F, Cl and Br. The first cited product has 43 heavy atoms and four perceived rings; a longer equally scoring congener has 50 heavy atoms with the same ring count. The digest final seed-2 tail belongs to a different, smaller family of partially saturated fused diaza rings, arylamino methoxy-bearing carbon centres and substituted pyridines. Seed 0 still explores much larger repeated heteroaromatic assemblies. Mean proposal SMILES length is 94.6 versus Parent 125.3, but the maximum is 266 versus Parent 237. Ring and aromatic text presence are both 0.9713. Familiar heteroaryl and ether components coexist with dense substitution, unsaturated chains and difficult complete structures.
liabilities: Long branched polyenes with several carbon-bound halogens add synthetic and geometric complexity without a corresponding score separation in the cited plateau.

The smaller final family contains N,O-acetal-like carbon centres and, in the cited strong final product, an N-O linkage. Its alternative bond chemistry is not automatically resolved by its smaller size.
The multiple substituted alkenes and saturated stereogenic centres have no specified configurations in the emitted strings.
missing_features: The small fragments and truncated bis-pyridyl product lack the richer connected core/substituent arrangement visible in the stronger products.

The leading excerpt underrepresents compact, conventionally substituted alternatives that retain the useful connected heteroaromatic pattern without polyene extension. Near-equal scores for expanded appendages do not identify a missing decoration or support unlimited growth.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Chloroacetylene and other small fragments sit at 0.5, while the initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. The late bis-pyridyl hydrazine scores 0.5557275541795665, compared with 0.6109149100540779 for a larger connected diaza/aryl-amino-ether product. The leading polyene/heteroaromatic structure and its longer brominated congeners all receive 0.6199818405862896; duplicating more of the unsaturated appendage gives 0.619706525936414. Thus connected aromatic and heteroatom patterns distinguish the stronger molecules, but substantial peripheral growth is nearly score-neutral here. A carbonyl is present in the leading family and absent from a strong late family, so no mandatory carbonyl requirement follows. The Parent highest observed record was a much larger repeated assembly at 0.6114128757484105; the current higher observed maximum is associated with a smaller core assembly, without eliminating the oversized tail.

per_task.generated_character: The highest product is a medium-sized N-propyl pyrrolidine joined through a fluorinated carbon to a rigid oxygen-containing polycycle bearing aromatic and pyridyl surfaces. It has 26 heavy atoms and several substituted saturated centres. Other leaders combine an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine with a biaryl/oxygen-ring framework. A separate high-scoring family is more flexible: a tertiary aminoalkyl chain connects substituted aromatic rings through a sulfur centre drawn with simultaneous S=C and S=O bonds; aryl halogens and thioether or O-S appendages occur. The final seed-2 family includes aryl-linked saturated diaza rings and phenolic/cyclic ether functionality. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.2 versus Parent 65.1; ring presence is 0.9736, aromatic presence 0.9655 and halogen presence 0.9885. Recognizable aryl/basic-amine chemistry is abundant, alongside more questionable sulfur, peroxide and polycyclic endpoints.
liabilities: The S=C/S=O centre, O-S substituents and the final O-O bridge are unusual chemical contexts whose accepted scores do not establish stability or a practical synthetic route.
Substituted pyrrolidine, fluorinated connector and polycyclic centres create stereochemical and conformational choices left unresolved by the submitted connectivity.
Almost all proposals contain halogens by the digest text counter. This includes conventional carbon-halogen bonds and does not by itself establish useful physical properties.
missing_features: The weak sulfonylated and truncated examples do not retain the same accessible amine character and connected aromatic arrangement as the leaders. This is a functional-context gap, not a shortage of nitrogen atoms.

The strongest saturated and polycyclic products leave their stereochemical alternatives unspecified. Explicit charge-state alternatives are also absent from the strings, although evaluator protonation handling and any benefit from alternative states are not established here.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves the molecular formula. After graph checks, identity normalization and duplicate rejection, it evaluates the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next state even after a worsening move, and an independent archive keeps the best observation. Each selected transition installs a small, sign-balanced set of changed local motifs, ranked by whole-molecule count change and canonical description. A later neighbor is blocked when opposite inverse signs match the same stored transition.
approach.novelty: Prioritize memory for motifs rooted at the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by the selected transition. A local motif can change merely because an adjacent atom's environment changed; the current count-based ranking can give that surrounding motif a scarce slot while omitting a motif at the actual edit site. The new ranking puts changes supported at those sites first, then uses the Parent's existing ordering. Earlier siblings changed count turnover, occurrence boundaries, ring annotations, score-based credit, matching coverage or overlap retention. None used the concrete edit's atom correspondence to allocate the existing memory slots.

nodes.hypothesis: Prioritize a selected transition's globally changed motifs whose signed occurrence changes are supported among the atoms and bond endpoints directly edited by that transition, using this binary site-support priority ahead of the Parent's existing rank within its unchanged bounded sign-balanced inverse-motif installation.

finding_summary.headline: Direct-site credit redirected 80 evaluations but slightly reduced the panel score
finding_summary.insights: Direct edit provenance can redirect scarce memory slots and real evaluations. The unresolved issue is whether the resulting motif restrictions protect useful search behavior. Of the 373 keys added by site priority, 230 later matched a fresh molecule and 60 participated in a bidirectional veto; 105 of the 314 that expired had never matched. Full-stream source improvements increased from 468 to 475 and archive improvements from 238 to 254, while their mean positive gains fell from 0.024350 to 0.022872 and from 0.019744 to 0.018437, respectively. More locally supported credit and more small improvements therefore did not establish the registered panel benefit. A newly admitted sulfur-free aryl-amine molecule reached the DRD2 maximum of 0.949238, showing that useful conventional chemistry was accessible. The molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur, dense ring systems and undefined stereochemistry elsewhere, especially in the weaker sitagliptin outcome. Root provenance is not a chemical-quality test, and a later shared motif does not demonstrate reversal of the same physical site. The records identify 590 later scored descendants of the 11 changed selected states, but they cannot assign those descendant scores to one credited motif or supply the missing scores and proposals of an alternative walk.
finding_summary.results: On the same 435 selected transitions, the number of installed memory slots supported by a same-sign change at directly edited roots rose from 884 to 1,257 of 1,708 slots, or 51.76% to 73.59%. Retained keys changed at 236 installations; another 64 changed order only. Separate memory histories on the recorded Child walk produced 184 vetoes with the inherited ranking and 117 with site priority: 74 decisions became admissions and seven became additional vetoes. These changes reached 80 actually evaluated molecules across 67 batches, comprising 74 new admissions and six replacement evaluations. Twelve of those molecules improved their source, 68 worsened it, 11 became selected walk states and five improved the archive. All 435 selected-edit replays verified, with no runtime fallback. The three-seed macro mean was 0.520690, compared with 0.521759 for the Parent; the paired change was -0.001069, missing the required +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Mean endpoints improved on four tasks, but the sitagliptin decrease of 0.022009 outweighed those gains, including the DRD2 increase of 0.011290.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich molecules retain aromatic and polar frameworks, but unusual sulfur, reactive bonds and undefined stereochemistry persist
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks have trajectories. Each digest covers 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0; aromatic-token occurrence rates, in the supplied task order, are 0.9609, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7747. These are fractions of SMILES containing those tokens, not fractions of aromatic atoms or proof of feasible ring geometry. The molecules span compact fused aromatic carboxamides, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked amines, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. There is real variation across replicas and tasks, but many high-scoring examples are close relatives within these families; molecular uniqueness does not establish broad scaffold exploration. Ordinary amides, ethers, aromatic heterocycles and amines coexist with heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and highly constrained ring networks. No task has explicit charge or stereocentre tokens in optimizer proposals. Neutral SMILES can still contain basic amines; absent charge notation does not mean absent ionizability. The Parent comparison shows changes within these families and a notable sulfur-free aryl-amine maximum, without a general resolution of synthetic plausibility. Sizes and structural descriptions below come from passive parsing of the supplied trajectories; scores are recorded observations, not new calculations. The supporting audit, including input hashes and perceived structural descriptors, is .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-07-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json. Parsing and ring perception do not establish synthesis, stability, binding or realizable stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals have 21-29 heavy atoms and mean SMILES length 46.4. Much of the chemistry retains an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene-like framework connected through a carbonyl to a second aromatic ring, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, hydroxymethyl, thiol and halogen substituents. The ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide at 0.39905049777278273 has a recognizable synthetic framework. The maximum at 0.41003927643747895 is instead a benzofuran carboxamide carrying an N-chloro amide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and an amino/chloro carbon. Other high observations and the final digest include bridged, partly unsaturated ring systems. The Parent has the same maxima in seeds 1 and 2; seed 0 changes from an aromatic sulfur-ring ketone at 0.393567030299894 to the bridged sulfur-containing ketone at 0.40196779766986834. The chemistry remains aromatic/carbonyl-centered, with substantial variation in ring feasibility and substituent reactivity.
liabilities: N-chloro amides, N-fluoro groups in low-scoring descendants, thiols and benzylic halides introduce reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aromatic/carbonyl framework.
Dense closures and partially dearomatized enlarged rings create uncertain geometry and demanding synthesis; successful parsing is insufficient evidence of accessibility.
missing_features: Coverage of conventional matched carbonyl linkers and substituent patterns remains incomplete around the retained aromatic frameworks; the strong ordinary amide shows that reactive amide chlorination is not required for a high observation.
The bridged and amino/halogen-substituted products lack specified stereochemical identities. The trajectories do not show which configurations, if any, preserve the favorable arrangement.
No unseen optimal scaffold or exact missing target feature can be inferred from these comparisons alone.

Together these observations support preserving a compact aromatic-carbonyl arrangement while varying substituent placement; they do not isolate any one substituent as causal. The conventional amide already approaches the N-chloro maximum, so these observations do not establish a need for the reactive N-Cl bond. Late bridged molecules can still score poorly, including the enlarged nitrogen-ring final example at 0.04763525265209; ring closure alone does not preserve the useful arrangement.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The reference is MolDQN, published by Zhou and colleagues, which applies value-based reinforcement learning directly to molecular graphs, with no generative model in between. It starts from a molecule that already has a real score and then runs a short episode of single edits: add or remove an atom, add or remove a bond, change a bond order, always within what valence allows. At each step it draws a bounded set of legal successor molecules and asks a small neural network which one is worth taking, where the network is given fingerprints of the current molecule and the candidate, how many edits are left in the episode, and the best score the episode has seen so far. Selection is epsilon-greedy, so most of the time it takes the network's favourite and occasionally it takes a random legal edit. The reward is not the new molecule's score but the amount by which that score raises the episode's running best, so an edit that makes things worse earns nothing and is still taken as the next state to build from. That is the point of the method: a molecule can be walked downhill deliberately if the network expects a payoff a few edits later. Because there is no discounting and rewards are increments of a running maximum, an episode's total return is exactly the improvement it achieved. The network learns by double Q-learning from a replay buffer of edits that actually received oracle scores: an online network picks the best continuation from the successor state, a lagged copy of that network supplies its value, and the difference between that target and the online prediction drives the update.
approach.novelty: The commitments this root makes go well beyond the method statement. The reward definition is the largest: rewarding the increment to the episode's running best, undiscounted, is an adaptation chosen so that the quantity the agent maximises telescopes into exactly the best-score improvement the benchmark cares about, rather than the original formulation's terminal-property reward. Episodes are deliberately short, six edits, with ten independent lanes interleaved so that each ten-proposal batch contains exactly one pending action per lane and no lane ever influences another mid-batch. Candidate actions are drawn fresh every time, forty at each decision and eight for each replay continuation, and crucially the continuations used to form learning targets are re-sampled at training time rather than stored, so the action set is never allowed to harden into a fixed candidate library. Value predictions for candidates that were not selected stay predictions: only edits the oracle actually scored enter replay, and a rejected action leaves the lane's state and remaining depth untouched. The root uses one Q-head with a declared epsilon schedule falling from 0.4 toward roughly 0.16, explicitly no ensemble and no episode-fixed randomised value function, so that any exploration benefit later observed can be attributed. Each objective restarts weights, target copy, optimizer, replay and archive from nothing, and preparation stores no learned artifact and no molecule pool at all.

nodes.hypothesis: Select fresh molecular graph edits with a single epsilon-greedy continuation-value network, advance persistent finite-horizon episodes through every matched accepted successor, and learn from accepted transitions using undiscounted episode-best improvement rewards and double-Q Bellman backups through a lagged target network.

finding_summary.headline: Graph-edit Q-learning activated in full but scored 0.4067, eighth of thirteen Discovery roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean answer to a question it could not previously separate: correct temporal-credit machinery is not by itself worth a score. Every part of the Bellman construction was audited and held, including the exact double-Q target, the detached lagged network, reward telescoping, and the use of updated weights in subsequent decisions, and the result still lands in the lower half of the roots and below the frozen-latent swarm root that carries no learning at all. Two mechanisms explain that. The learning signal is thin, because four fifths of transitions carry zero reward under a running-best definition, so most gradient comes from the zero mass and the mean continuation term of 0.014 sits at the same scale as the residual error the network still has, which is also why nearly three thousand continuation values came out negative when the true quantity cannot be. And the search collapses: the molecules produced show that exploitation, once it finds a good core, spends its remaining budget swapping single atoms on that core, which is precisely the behaviour a value function would need a long-horizon reason to escape. For method choice this argues that direct graph editing is the right way to stay in makeable chemistry, but that pairing it with a value-learning controller adds machinery whose payoff is not visible at this feedback scale; the effort is better spent on the exploration and diversity side than on the credit-assignment side. Still open: this is a single seed with no parent and no paired comparison, so the ranking is indicative; the 216 recovered-loss links and 123 later episode-best gains after temporary losses are descriptive and do not isolate learned lookahead from ordinary hill-climbing; and whether episode-consistent randomised exploration would change the picture was deliberately left untested here.
finding_summary.results: One screening seed, macro mean 0.406692671573943, eighth among the campaign's thirteen Discovery roots on a spread running 0.2331 to 0.5103. Per objective the means were 0.7536466193285815 on the docking task, 0.6145349727054742 on the decoration-hop task, 0.33218372414937963 on the zaleplon task, 0.19512536527753646 on the median task and 0.13797267640874414 on the sitagliptin task. Every registered observable moved as intended. The graph sampler filled all 1450 acting neighbourhoods with 40 valid novel candidates each and all 20215 replay continuation neighbourhoods with eight, emitting exactly 29 batches of ten unique molecules per objective with zero invalid, duplicate or rejected proposals; an independent re-execution of 17026 distinct edit receipts reproduced every one. The temporal machinery worked: 250 episode starts, 1200 multistep continuations, and 800 accepted transitions that strictly lowered the score yet still advanced their lane, of which 666 went on to be the source of a later edit. Reward telescoping held to a maximum residual of 5.551115123125783e-17 with gamma exactly one. Of 22900 replay targets, 2685 were horizon terminals equal to reward and all 20215 nonterminal continuation terms were nonzero, mean 0.013847408184662015, so the targets genuinely differed from reward-only regression. Learning registered: mean paired Huber loss fell from 6.10635587187527e-05 to 5.3964929417511364e-05 and mean absolute temporal-difference error from 0.004401601105964189 to 0.004148056249060887, decreasing on every objective, with 1242 of 1450 individual steps improving. The learned values then drove behaviour: 1095 exploitation choices against 355 random ones, every neighbourhood showing nonconstant values, and a fixed sixteen-candidate diagnostic probe changing its preferred molecule 30 times over training. The counterweight is the sparsity of signal: 1179 of 1450 accepted transitions carried zero reward, only 271 were positive, and 2880 of the sampled continuations were predicted negative even though a true remaining episode-best gain can never be below zero.

molecular.headline: Drug-like fused aromatic scaffolds inherited from the seeds, decorated with impossible bonds and collapsed onto one core per objective
molecular.overall_character: Because every molecule is one legal edit away from a molecule that was already there, this node's output looks far more like real medicinal chemistry than a decoder's would. Ring closures appear in 99 to 100 percent of emitted molecules and aromatic atoms in 94 to 100 percent; the sets are full of genuine fused heterocycles, indoles, coumarins, xanthines, benzodioxoles and aminopyridines, carrying amides, sulfonamides and basic amines at sensible positions. The two problems are structural rather than cosmetic. First, the edit operators are constrained only by valence and connectivity, so they cheerfully form bonds that no chemist would draw: oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine hypohalites, nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, peroxides, hemiaminals, and three-membered oxygen rings fused straight onto an arene. Second, the search converges hard: within any objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- and two-atom variants of a single core, several sharing scores to four decimal places, so what reads as optimisation is largely relabelling. Stereochemistry is absent everywhere and no molecule carries a formal charge.

per_task.generated_character: Two families only. One is a methoxy- or ethoxy-substituted fused indole bearing a carbinolamine and an N-linked fluorinated bicycle, repeated with single-atom substitutions across almost the entire best list. The other is the supplied dimethoxyindole carboxamide with one atom changed. Ring closure and aromatic rates are both at or near 1.0, and the halogen rate of 0.86 comes almost entirely from a single inherited aryl fluoride.
liabilities: carbinolamine and aminal centres of the C(O)N type, which are hydrolytically unstable
sulfur attached directly to an amide or ring nitrogen as a bare SH
a bridged bicyclic alkene written across ring-closure pairs that would be anti-Bredt
a cumulated allene fragment surviving in the low-scoring set
missing_features: no pyrazolopyrimidine or comparable fused bicyclic nitrogen core is ever constructed
no nitrile group appears despite it being a common feature of this chemotype
no N,N-dialkyl acetamide is built onto the aryl ring
no stereochemistry on the sp3 carbinolamine centre the scaffold creates
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top eleven molecules occupy a band from 0.317 to 0.332 and differ from each other by a methyl versus ethyl, a hydroxyl versus methoxy, or the position of one substituent, so score is essentially flat across the whole exploited core. The zero-scoring tail is composed entirely of the supplied starting molecules and their immediate first edits, which means the improvement came in one jump and was then elaborated rather than extended.

per_task.generated_character: A single scaffold, elaborated exhaustively: a methoxy-substituted coumarin or benzoxazinone fused to a three-membered oxygen ring, bearing an aminopyridine that in turn carries a second heteroaryl with sulfur and oxygen substituents. Aromatic atoms appear in 100 percent of molecules and rings in 100 percent, and the mean length of 56 characters is stable across the run, which is what a converged edit search looks like.
liabilities: sulfenic acid substituents written as SO and OS directly on an aromatic ring
a three-membered oxygen ring fused across two adjacent aromatic carbons, an arene oxide
an NON(O)O chain built onto a fused heteroaromatic
an O-bromo substituent on a lactone carbon, which is a hypobromite
missing_features: no sulfonamide is ever formed, only lower sulfur oxidation states
no saturated ring is added anywhere on the periphery
no basic amine or other solubilising handle is introduced
no stereochemistry, even where the fused three-membered ring creates defined faces
per_task.score_gradient_reading: All twelve best molecules fall between 0.594 and 0.615, separated only by whether a given position carries SO, OS, O, S, Br or SC, and by whether the fused ring is a five- or six-membered lactone. The worst molecules, at 0.52 to 0.53, are the supplied starting molecules with a single atom changed. The objective evidently rewards the scaffold much more than the decoration, and the search extracted that in the first few batches and then plateaued.

per_task.generated_character: The most convincing output of the run and the longest, averaging 72 SMILES characters. Almost every high scorer is a dichlorophenyl sulfur group on a methylated diazepane or piperazine, connected through a benzylic tertiary amine to a pyridine bearing a fluorophenol and an acetic acid arm. These are recognisable ligand-shaped molecules assembled by editing the supplied sulfonamide reference, with a halogen rate of 0.92.
liabilities: a sulfilimine-oxide written as C=S(=O)(N), which is not a preparable functional group

transferable_gaps.evidence: Emitted molecules carry oxygen-fluorine, oxygen-chlorine and oxygen-bromine bonds (OF, OCl, OBr substituents), nitrogen-sulfur and nitrogen-chlorine bonds on imide nitrogens, NON(O)O chains, and a sulfilimine-oxide written C=S(=O)(N). Every one of these passed sanitisation, reparsing and an independent structural re-execution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Edit operators form element pairings that valence permits but chemistry forbids
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Legality checks on valence and connectivity are not sufficient to keep a graph editor inside makeable chemistry. The proposal step needs an element-pair and functional-group context filter, so that a heteroatom-heteroatom bond is only formed where such a bond is actually known, applied before a molecule consumes an oracle call.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In every objective the twelve highest-scoring molecules are one- or two-atom variants of a single fused scaffold, with score bands as narrow as six thousandths across all twelve, and five molecules in one set sharing an identical score to six decimal places. Late-run output is indistinguishable from mid-run output apart from substituent position.
transferable_gaps.gap: The search collapses onto one core and then relabels single atoms
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Sampling a local neighbourhood and taking its best member cannot leave a basin once it is in one, no matter how good the value estimate is, because every legal move is one atom wide. A generator needs a scaffold-level move, an explicit novelty or diversity pressure across lanes, or forced restarts from unrelated regions, or it will spend the majority of its budget confirming a structure it already has.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Sulfonamides present in the starting molecules are degraded to sulfinamides and then to sulfilimine-oxide forms, and sulfur substituents appear across the range from thioether to sulfenic acid within a single best list, purely as the by-product of adding and deleting oxygen atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group oxidation state is edited as if it were a free variable
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Treating a functional group as an arbitrary collection of atoms lets the editor wander through oxidation states that are not isolable. Groups should be manipulated as units with a declared set of allowed states, so that an oxygen deletion either produces a real lower oxidation state or is not offered at all.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure rates of 0.99 to 1.00 sit alongside aromatic-atom rates of 0.94 to 1.00, and no emitted molecule introduces a new aliphatic ring: rings that appear are either inherited flat heteroaromatics or accidental three-membered oxygen rings fused onto an arene.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator builds no saturated or three-dimensional structure
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Atom and bond edits on an aromatic template can decorate but cannot saturate, so the whole sp3-rich half of drug-like space is unreachable. Ring-forming operators that close aliphatic rings, and operators that reduce aromatic systems, are needed for a generator to explore three-dimensional shape.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across every emitted molecule, including the many products bearing sp3 ring carbons with four distinct substituents and the benzylic amine centres the operators construct.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry is set even where the edits create defined centres
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: An edit vocabulary that changes atoms and bonds but never sets configuration cannot address any property that depends on it, and worse, it silently produces racemic answers to questions whose answer is a single enantiomer. Stereo-setting operators and stereo-aware features are a prerequisite, not a refinement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Inserting a single oxygen produced peroxides such as the CCOOC ether chain, inserting oxygen next to nitrogen produced carbinolamine and hemiaminal centres of the C(O)N type, and inserting carbon next to an aromatic oxygen produced an ynol ether. None of these were rejected.
transferable_gaps.gap: Atom insertion creates unstable linkages as an unnoticed by-product
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Single-atom insertion is the operator most likely to build a group nobody intended, because the atom lands between two existing heteroatoms. A proposal-time substructure blocklist covering peroxides, hemiaminals, strained fused small rings and heteroatom-heteroatom chains would remove most of this class at no cost to reach.

nodes.method_name: MolDQN: Bellman-guided de novo graph-edit episodes
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in MolDQN's value-based control of molecular edits: learn future action returns from scored transitions and choose subsequent graph modifications with a deep Q-network. [Zhou et al., Sections 2.1, 2.2 and 2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1810.08678v3) describe finite molecular edit episodes, fingerprint features and double Q-learning. Our adaptation starts short episodes from task-local scored molecules and samples fresh valence-aware atom and bond edits at each state. A compact Q-network takes current and successor fingerprints, remaining episode depth and the episode's best observed score. Use a single Q-function with epsilon-greedy action selection in the root. Evaluate only selected new whole molecules; values assigned to unselected successors are predictions. Advance each trajectory after its matched feedback, even when the new molecule scores worse. For Top-1 alignment, use reward max(previous_episode_best, new_score) minus previous_episode_best and undiscounted finite-horizon backups: accumulated reward equals improvement in that episode's best score. This reward adaptation is our inference, not the paper's original reward. Train immediately from accepted transition replay using double-Q target selection and a lagged target network, with zero continuation value at episode termination. Retain all accepted intermediate molecules in the task incumbent archive. Interleave episodes according to announced batches, and generate further edits to replace invalid or duplicate proposals. Each decision samples an evolving neighborhood; no corpus pool, complete-molecule retrieval or fixed candidate enumeration is involved. No pretrained generator or external labels are required, and every objective starts with clean learning state. The hypothesis is that learned lookahead identifies useful edit sequences, including temporary score losses, quickly enough to raise the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Learning useful continuation values from scarce transitions is unproven; the paper's much larger training regime does not establish this transfer.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a population of at most sixty-four accepted molecules, kept in descending score order. It chooses a high-ranking score band and then a molecule uniformly within that band, produces a fresh surplus of crossover and mutation offspring, and uses correlated draws from a fingerprint Gaussian process to choose which offspring to evaluate. Every accepted score trains the posterior, even if its molecule leaves the breeding population. This loop reliably learns and selects, but most evaluated offspring do not improve on their generating parents, and successful molecular cores accumulate many close relatives.
approach.novelty: Give each represented molecular core equal breeding probability within the already selected score band. A core with many surviving analogues will share its probability among those analogues, while a less represented accepted core gains an opportunity to breed. The existing preference for high-scoring bands remains intact. The lineage's earlier child changed how generated offspring are selected for evaluation; this child changes only which accepted parents produce those offspring. Neither recorded sibling nor a supplied mechanism cluster has tested this conditional correction for core multiplicity.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each inherited score quantile, sample accepted breeding parents with probability inversely proportional to the number of eligible survivors sharing their Murcko core, so every represented core has equal conditional mass.

finding_summary.headline: Core-balanced breeding broadened core use and raised parent-beating yield, but lowered final scores.
finding_summary.insights:
Equalizing core probability can reduce repeated use of abundant families without improving the best molecules found. The clearest coverage expansions were in decoration hopping and DRD2, yet their parent-beating counts and final-score means fell. Zaleplon breeding became more concentrated despite correct balancing within each selected band, showing that changing the conditional draw does not guarantee broader realized coverage once the evolving survivor population is considered.

The modest parent-beating gain also uses a weaker reference: mean best-generating-parent score fell from 0.419645 to 0.395720, while mean evaluated-offspring score fell from 0.319152 to 0.301731. This relative yield gain therefore does not establish stronger offspring production. The number of admitted offspring later reused for breeding stayed almost unchanged, at 2,163 versus 2,167, and incumbent gains did not increase. The evidence narrows the problem to allocating toward productive surviving families rather than simply reducing their multiplicity imbalance; discarded or ineligible cores still receive no opportunity. The molecular assessment also shows that broader structural coverage continues to include repeated heterocycle growth, tiny fragments, reactive nitrogen-halogen/peroxide groups and strained fused rings. Murcko-core coverage alone does not resolve those quality limitations. Passive comparisons supply probabilities and parent identities, with no scores for alternate offspring or an alternate search trajectory.
finding_summary.results:
The allocation change executed correctly in all three replicas. Of 111,246 parent draws, 86,634 had unequal core multiplicities; every logged probability vector and inverse-CDF choice matched the intended rule. On the same eligible states and logged uniform variates, 36,398 selected parent ranks and 29,554 selected cores differed from the passive uniform comparator. Mean represented cores used per breeding batch rose from 12.98 to 14.60, and mean concentration of breeding uses fell from 0.299 to 0.189, measured as the sum of squared core-use shares. Coverage rose in 10 of 15 task/seed sessions; the effect was not universal. All accepted-state, survivor and pending-provenance checks passed, and both panels completed all 4,500 oracle evaluations.

Strict best-parent beats increased from 565/4,350 (12.99%) to 600/4,350 (13.79%), and mean child-minus-best-parent score improved from -0.100493 to -0.093989. Incumbent improvements were nearly unchanged, at 216 versus 218. Mean final-best score across tasks and seeds fell from 0.544374 to 0.524118, a paired change of -0.020256. Seed changes were -0.052822, -0.023812 and +0.015865; all five task means declined. Thus the intended allocation mechanism is confirmed, while the intended score increase was not observed.

molecular.headline: Repeated heterocycle growth and tiny fragments coexist with reactive, highly fused leading molecules
molecular.overall_character: The current panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, with complete three-seed Parent n-fc2c108a5253 trajectories. Aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9425 to 0.9931 and ring-closure presence from 0.977 to 0.9931; charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These are string-presence measurements, not aromatic atom fractions, ionization measurements or evidence of feasible stereochemistry. The output is ring-rich and often extensively aromatic: fused nitrogen carbonyl systems, aromatic amine/aminal frameworks and halogenated unsaturated heterocycles dominate the leaders. Chemical scale varies from tiny fragments to large assemblies of repeated heterocycles. This is particularly pronounced in deco_hop, whose mean SMILES length is 115.4 and maximum is 235; its seed-2 final molecules visibly repeat nitrogen-dione units. The Parent also produced reactive and extensively connected structures. Current leaders retain N-halogen bonds, peroxide or hypohalite motifs, tight ring fusion and unspecified configurations. Overall synthetic plausibility is questionable, with strongly implausible individual small-ring or growth outliers, and drug-like quality remains weak. Across-seed diversity is moderate; many late streams mainly elaborate a common core.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 molecules are moderately sized fused unsaturated nitrogen heterocycles bearing fluoroaryl carboxamides, alkyl/alkoxy substituents and hydroxymethyl or aminomethyl groups. Amide N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and fused-ring N-F are frequent in the leaders. Seed 0 reaches pyrazole thioamides with phenolic, cyclopentadienyl and cyclobutenyl groups; seed 1 reaches an aryl ketone with N-O/N-N functionality. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9782 and halogen presence is 0.7149. Relative to the Parent aromatic ketone, amide and thioheterocyclic families, the compact aromatic/carbonyl theme persists, with reactive nitrogen substitution and unusual ring geometry.
liabilities: N-Br, N-Cl and N-F bonds add reactivity to amide and ring nitrogens; N-O/N-N variants add compatibility concerns.
Unusual unsaturated small rings, scaffold doubling and very small fragment products reduce the chemical coherence of the output.
missing_features: Stable nonhalogenated nitrogen alternatives preserving the successful aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are poorly represented among the leading amide series.

Accessible fused-ring alternatives and explicit configurations or alkene geometry are absent for many unusual partially saturated and bridged products; a unique target pharmacophore cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best N-bromoamide/N-fluoro heterocycle scores 0.4294168350924388 versus 0.4163503402962837 for the paired Parent seed 2; other paired seeds change in different directions. N-Cl, N-F and N-Br amide variants share 0.41885833432199493, so their reactivity is not distinguished. A halogen-free pyrazole thioamide reaches 0.4220190409118175, showing N-halogen chemistry is not universally required in this region. Tiny peroxide or halogen compounds score 0.0, and an isolated fluoro-carbamoyl fragment scores 9.818532642967522e-13. The complete ring/carbonyl arrangement matters more than a reactive group in a tiny fragment.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-1 family is a relatively compact fused aza-heteroaromatic carbonyl system joined to fluorinated nitrogen heteroaryl rings. It bears a cyclic peroxide bridge and alkyl, vinyl or ethynyl substituents. In contrast, seed 0 and especially seed 2 produce large structures with repeated nitrogen-dione/heteroaryl modules, ester/ketone connections and many aromatic rings; some final products also contain N-Br. Aromatic and ring-closure presence are 0.9931 and halogen presence is 0.8575. The Parent also favored reactive fused heterocycles and expanded dione assemblies. Here the highest score occurs in the more compact seed-1 family rather than the large repeated assemblies.
liabilities: Cyclic peroxide, N-halogen and reactive linker motifs complicate stability and synthesis.
Very large repeated heterocycle assemblies create substantial size, aromaticity, flexibility and synthetic-complexity liabilities.
missing_features: Compact stable alternatives preserving the favorable heteroaryl/carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to peroxide-bearing or repeatedly expanded structures.
The late growth families lack a demonstrated need for repeated dione units, extra aromatic attachments and ester-linked duplication.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: Simulated annealing keeps one current configuration, perturbs it randomly, and always accepts an improvement while accepting a deterioration with a probability that falls as a temperature parameter cools. Early on the walk can move downhill and escape a local optimum; late on it behaves almost greedily. Applied to molecules, the configuration is a graph, the perturbation is an atom or bond edit, and the acceptance test uses the observed score returned by the oracle.
approach.novelty: This root runs many independent walks in parallel rather than one, with at most one outstanding proposal per walk, so the oracle batch is filled by different points in the space instead of by one trajectory. It ties the cooling schedule to accumulated feedback rather than wall time, seeds the initial temperature from the spread of the initial scores, and keeps a separate best-observed archive so that accepting a downhill move never loses the incumbent.

nodes.hypothesis: Maintain independent task-local molecular graph walks, generate de novo atom or bond edits from each current working state, accept nondecreasing observed scores and accept decreases with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), and cool T as accepted feedback accumulates while preserving a separate best-observed archive.

finding_summary.headline: The annealing machinery was exact in every respect and produced the round's lowest score, 0.233
finding_summary.insights: This node isolates the round's most important lesson. The search algorithm is provably correct and the search still failed, so what separates the field is not the optimizer but the proposal distribution it draws from. Aromatic content here is 50 to 67 percent against 87 to 100 percent for every root above 0.4, and the graph edits repeatedly produce aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres that are not real chemistry. Any future work on this lineage belongs in the edit operator set, not in the acceptance rule or the cooling schedule. One seed only, and its deco_hop result shows the walk does work where the initial molecules are already close.
finding_summary.results: This is the weakest of the thirteen roots at 0.233. It reached 0.558 on deco_hop and 0.382 on zaleplon_mpo but collapsed to 0.045 on drd2_docking and 0.014 on sitagliptin_mpo, where the median score across all 290 proposals was zero. Every mechanism check was exact: the recomputed cooling schedule agreed with all 145 proposal temperatures and all 1,450 stored proposal temperatures, the Metropolis decision reproduced 1,450 times out of 1,450 including the logged uniform variates, 557 downhill moves were accepted and 546 of them were genuinely reused as the source of a later proposal, and the best archive matched an independent cumulative maximum at all 1,600 checkpoints.

molecular.headline: Aromatic phosphorus rings and hypervalent centres: a correct search over chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure is high at 97 percent on every objective, but only half to two thirds of proposals contain any ordinary aromatic atom, the lowest of any root that completed. The gap is filled by exotic ring systems the graph editor is willing to construct: phosphinine rings written with aromatic phosphorus, hypervalent phosphorus and sulfur centres, and nitrogen-halogen bonds. These appear not only in the failures but in the highest-scoring molecule on two objectives, which means the oracle is scoring structures that could not be made. Molecules average sixty to sixty-four characters throughout, with no size control varying by objective.

nodes.method_name: Simulated annealing through de novo molecular graph walks
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in simulated annealing: randomly perturb a current configuration, accept improvements, sometimes accept deterioration, and gradually cool the acceptance rule. [Kirkpatrick, Gelatt and Vecchi](https://hedibert.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/12/1983KirkpatrickGelattVecchi.pdf) describe this mechanism for combinatorial optimization. Our molecular transfer maintains independent graph walks initialized from the current objective's supplied scored molecules. Each walk generates a new neighbor through atom or bond edits. After real feedback, accept a higher-scoring neighbor as the next working state; accept a lower-scoring neighbor with probability exp((new_score-current_score)/T), otherwise retain the source state. Subsequent edits follow the accepted working state, while a separate archive preserves the best observed molecule. Cool as feedback accumulates and distribute the evaluator-announced batch across walks with explicit proposal-to-source provenance. Regenerate invalid or already evaluated structures through further edits. Every submitted molecule is generated de novo; no corpus pool, learned prior or labeled source task is required. The hypothesis is that temporary score losses permit useful structural transitions whose later gains increase the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. This finite-budget optimizer does not claim equilibrium sampling or asymptotic convergence under molecular validity and novelty filtering.

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates neural proposals with two graph refinement phases, learns from exact accepted molecular trajectories using rank-weighted trajectory balance and a joint normalizer, and regularizes the adapting policy toward a frozen corpus-trained prior. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior chooses graph offspring for evaluation while preserving the first fresh-policy handoff. The reusable prior is selected along unchanged unlabeled training by valid, connected, unique generation yield, with original holdout loss breaking ties. During a neural phase the current sampler uses only the adapted policy distribution; the frozen reference influences learning but does not directly participate in token selection.
approach.novelty: Anchor each neural token draw to the frozen reference by using the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and prior probabilities at the same generated prefix. This keeps both the learned score preference and the reference in the actual sampling distribution. The earlier children changed prior preparation, replay allocation, KL direction or trajectory-balance credit; this one preserves the Parent learning stack and changes only ancestral generation. Lower reference divergence is tested directly on the sampled prefixes, while novel molecular yield, graph-feedback transfer and endpoint score remain separate empirical questions.

nodes.hypothesis: Generate neural proposals ancestrally from the normalized geometric mean of the adapted-policy and frozen-prior next-token distributions at each shared generated prefix, with equal fixed exponents and unchanged accepted-score learning.

finding_summary.headline: Geometric anchoring improved valid-novel yield but weakened neural scores and missed the mean-score gain
finding_summary.insights: Direct reference anchoring can substantially improve syntactic and novelty yield at generated prefixes while attenuating useful accepted-score adaptation. The effect was strongest after the first adapted-policy batch: later valid-novel yield rose from 64.00% to 85.42%, while later accepted neural mean score fell from 0.211885 to 0.160124. Graph feedback continued to train the policy: all 6,480 nonterminal graph-bearing replay steps had nonzero graph-only gradients, and exact accepted graph log likelihood increased by 0.180643 on average per training exposure. The weaker downstream family overlap and scores therefore occurred despite active graph learning. Ring-core overlap is a descriptive connection, not proof of causal or functional transfer. The extra raw yield did not expand the evaluated neural stream under this sampler. Both runs emitted exactly 1,500 neural molecules from 150 calls and needed no additional sampling call. The valid surplus discarded after filling a batch increased from 6,491 to 8,819. Mean active sequence length shortened from 59.409 to 48.290 draws including EOS, but measured neural-phase generation time rose from 14.608 to 27.896 seconds across the runs, including diagnostic overhead. This narrows the result: improved parser/novelty yield alone was not a limiting resource for these full batches. The supplied chemistry assessment describes broad ring-rich output with ordinary medicinal motifs alongside reactive bonds, unusual heteroatom bonding, uncontrolled growth and absent stereochemical specification. Those combined neural/graph outputs do not establish that the extra unscored valid draws preserve useful functional context. The experiment supports the conditional distribution effect and higher raw yield, while leaving useful molecular transfer and search advantage unsupported. It does not show that the adapted weights stayed closer to the prior; the KL comparison holds the generated prefix fixed and compares two sampling distributions at that prefix.
finding_summary.results: The intended sampling mechanism activated. Across 12,000 raw neural sequences and 579,478 active token prefixes, the recorded behavior distribution differed from the adapted policy. On those same prefixes, mean KL divergence to the frozen prior fell from 0.182477 for the adapted-policy endpoint to 0.040980 for behavior; mean behavior/policy L1 distance was 0.144892. Every raw sequence had lower average behavior-to-prior divergence. All 150 saved audit prefixes reconstruct the registered geometric midpoint. Valid-novel raw yield rose from 7,991/12,000 (66.59%) to 10,319/12,000 (85.99%), improving in all three seeds and all five tasks. Invalid draws fell from 3,807 to 1,680, unterminated draws from 37 to zero and duplicates from 165 to one. However, mean accepted neural score fell from 0.204941 to 0.158382. Among 1,350 later neural emissions, exact ring-core overlap with previously trained graph molecules fell from 53 to 39. The three-seed mean final-best score was 0.542371 versus the parent's 0.550198, a paired change of -0.007826; population standard deviations were 0.030347 and 0.021738. Paired macro changes were +0.009185, -0.078386 and +0.045722. Task-mean changes were -0.020870 for zaleplon, -0.052561 for scaffold hopping, -0.012984 for DRD2, -0.004175 for median similarity and +0.051459 for sitagliptin. Every task completed all 300 evaluations.
