molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal motifs coexist with reactive bonds, difficult polycycles and absent stereochemical specification.
molecular.overall_character: The evaluated proposals cover aromatic ethers, azaheterocycles, amines, amides, sulfones, fluorinated heterocycles and densely fused or bridged rings. Each task digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Across the task digests, ring-closure rates run from 0.9747 to 0.9966 and aromatic-presence rates from 0.9448 to 0.9839; these are fractions of proposal SMILES containing the relevant text, not ring counts or aromatic atom fractions. Mean SMILES lengths range from 43.7 to 65.4, with some much larger assemblies. Every stereocentre_rate is 0.0, despite structures with stereogenic ring junctions and substituted saturated atoms. The overall chemical vocabulary is broad, while the digest high-scoring sets repeatedly concentrate in particular scaffold families and seeds. Ordinary medicinal functional groups coexist with peroxides, terminal imines, unusual sulfur bonding, phosphines, N-fluorinated rings and small strained heterocycles. Compared with Parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the prominent families change, but neither chemical plausibility nor stereochemical completeness is consistently established. These are assessments of the evaluated molecular outputs; their trajectory source labels do not separate neural proposals from graph descendants, and they do not establish raw-generation validity or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest digest family consists of moderately sized pyridine/phenyl aromatic assemblies joined by a biaryl bond and a benzyl ether, with ethoxy or methoxy substituents and frequent halogens. CCOc1ccc(-c2ccccc2COc2cc(Cl)ccn2)cn1 has recognizable aryl-ether chemistry, aromatic nitrogen acceptors and no strongly basic aliphatic amine or carbonyl. Some close relatives add an amino group or close additional rings. Other seeds also explore substituted indole carboxamides and more elaborate fused heterocycles. The low end includes very large polyamide/polyamine assemblies, polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like structures and a long-chain phosphorus/quaternary-ammonium/silicon compound. The optimizer ring-closure rate is 0.9885, aromatic-presence rate 0.9759 and mean SMILES length 43.7. The leading ether structures appear substantially more synthetically conventional than the oversized and unusually fused excursions.
liabilities: Aromatic-heavy structures and peripheral halogen/linker edits dominate the leading family; the output does not establish solubility, conformational preference or a synthesis route.
Large fragment combinations add long chains, numerous polar groups or unusual phosphorus/silicon/charge combinations while losing the favorable score range.
missing_features: The low-scoring large structures fail to retain the economical aromatic/acceptor arrangement and limited side-chain size seen in the stronger ether family.
The leading family shows little saturated stereodefined shape variation; whether such alternatives would improve this objective is unmeasured, rather than an established requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest spans 0.0 to 0.475614712250357, with median 0.151051. The leading aromatic ether scores 0.475614712250357, whereas the long-chain charged phosphorus/silicon structure scores 0.0 and the large polyamine/amide assembly scores 2.5085649778800826e-59. A close local comparison changes only ethoxy to propoxy on the chlorinated biaryl ether: 0.46457806514522626 becomes 0.3189563030428961. This supports a preference for a specific modest-size substitution pattern rather than indiscriminate chain growth. In the matched Parent seed-2 trajectory, the best molecule was a carbonyl- and nitrile-bearing bicyclic nitrogen scaffold at 0.46457806514522626; the Child seed-2 ether family reaches 0.475614712250357. Different functional-group families can therefore occupy a similar score range, and these data do not establish an obligatory missing amide, nitrile or particular unseen pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The leading digest family is a medium-to-large aromatic anilino-thienopyrimidine series, bearing phenyl or heteroaryl substituents, methoxy, methyl and halogens. Its ring nitrogens and anilino NH provide an organized acceptor/donor pattern, but many leading members also contain a terminal methylene imine or an aryl methyl peroxide. The simpler aryloxy members have familiar medicinal-chemistry connectivity. Other seeds develop much larger fused azaaromatic, urea/formamide and repeated polycyclic assemblies, including the long final seed-2 molecule cited here. The low end instead includes cyclic sulfones, sulfonamides, acids and flexible sulfone-linked aromatic structures. Ring-closure rate is 0.9908, aromatic-presence rate 0.9839 and mean SMILES length 65.4; the maximum is 187 characters. The scaffold vocabulary is plausible, but the peroxide/imine substitutions and complex final assemblies make overall synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: The terminal methylene imines and explicit O-O bonds deserve chemical stability and synthetic scrutiny; no such verification accompanies their scores.
Large fused and repeated azaaromatic assemblies accumulate difficult ring connections and densely substituted nitrogen chemistry without a correspondingly decisive score advantage.
missing_features: The weaker cyclic-sulfone and flexible-chain proposals lack the organized fused azaaromatic/anilino donor-acceptor context shared by the stronger Child family.

Chemically conventional substituent alternatives are not comparably developed across the leading family: high-scoring termini often become imines or peroxides. Their chemical replacement is a quality gap; an objective-score benefit is not established.

The leading Child digest does not reproduce the Parent high-scoring quinazoline/piperazinone arrangement, so the observed family coverage is incomplete rather than demonstrably missing one required atom or group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading imine-bearing anilino-thienopyrimidine scores 0.6720445459737293; its otherwise matching pendant phenyl analogue without fluorine scores 0.6441828361070634. The peroxide analogue scores 0.629303689979929, and a conventional phenoxy analogue scores 0.6254953764861295. Thus high scores coexist with both conventional and chemically concerning substituents; the small numerical differences do not prove the concerning groups are necessary. The cyclic sulfone/carboxylic acid at the low end scores 0.2596495291029798, whereas a very large final azaaromatic assembly still scores 0.594488188976378. The observed gradient emphasizes the particular aromatic nitrogen-rich context more clearly than it enforces simplicity or ordinary peripheral chemistry. Parent seed-1 reached 0.8301591128254581 in a quinazoline/piperazinone-rich family, while Child seed-1 reaches 0.6720445459737293 in the thienopyrimidine series. This is a change in explored high-scoring chemistry, not evidence that adding a particular parent fragment would reproduce its score.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest molecules combine hydrophobic chlorinated aromatic groups with accessible aliphatic amines. They include a flexible aminated tertiary organophosphine, dichlorophenylpiperazines with alkyl chains and unusual C=S(=O) sulfur centers, and larger fused heteroaromatic/aryl amine structures. The seed-2 family combines an arylpiperazine, a secondary amine linker, an aminophenol ring and a halogenated fused heterocycle. These are recognizably amine-rich rather than nitrogen-deficient outputs. The low end instead contains acylated/sulfonylated nitrogens, nitro hydrazones and neutral carbonyl-rich aromatics without the same exposed aliphatic amine context. Ring-closure rate is 0.9747, aromatic-presence rate 0.9448, halogen rate 0.7241 and mean SMILES length 47.9. The charged rate of 0.0126 concerns written formal charges and does not measure how often the neutral amines could protonate.
liabilities: The aminophosphines and C=S(=O)-bearing sulfur structures require more chemical justification than an accepted score provides. Long flexible alkyl branches and alkyl chlorides add further chemical liabilities.
Small N-N ring closures can radically change strain, basicity and geometry. A formal parser-accepted ring does not establish that the intended cyclic-amine chemistry has been preserved.
missing_features: The low-scoring carbonyl/sulfonyl-rich structures lack the exposed non-amide aliphatic amine context present in the strongest molecules; the generator as a whole clearly can produce that context.

Reliable preservation of favorable cyclic-amine topology is missing: the close piperazine-to-small-N-N-ring comparison loses the stronger score despite retaining the surrounding aryl and linker features.
Explicit configurations are absent at substituted saturated centers and ring junctions; no stereochemical preference can be inferred from these unassigned SMILES.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aminophosphine scores 0.9957613133842727 and the sulfur-bearing arylpiperazine 0.9941946146870084, while the acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05. This supports accessible aliphatic amine plus hydrophobic aromatic context within the sampled structures, without identifying a binding pose or proving a contribution from phosphorus or unusual sulfur. A particularly informative pair preserves the rest of the seed-2 scaffold: its piperazine-containing molecule scores 0.9889622948332054, but contraction to the small N-N-containing ring in the final digest scores 0.4586415097801264. Correct local ring connectivity and amine spacing matter more than merely retaining nitrogen atoms. The Parent also produced arylpiperazines and bridged basic amines; its seed-2 arylpiperazine reached 0.9999999657062248 without the Child seed-0 phosphine or unusual sulfur motif. Those motifs are therefore not established as missing requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains fairly large but compact multicyclic indole-containing scaffolds with fused/bridged saturated or unsaturated ketone rings and an aryl sulfone or sulfonamide linked to benzodioxole. This provides aromatic surface, an indole NH, carbonyl and sulfonyl acceptors, and substantial rigid three-dimensional connectivity, but the saturated stereogenic centers are unspecified. Other seeds explore nitrogen-rich fused systems with piperazine and xanthone-like aromatic carbonyl/ether frameworks carrying amines or amides. The final xanthone-like examples are more conventional than the most elaborate bridged indole structures. The low end ranges from ethane and butane to small imine/guanidine-like compounds and a sulfur-rich heterocycle. Ring-closure rate is 0.9966, aromatic-presence rate 0.9747 and mean SMILES length 56.0. Ring chemistry is abundant; the principal limitation is the plausibility and specification of the particular connectivity.
liabilities: Dense ring fusion and substituted ring junctions impose substantial synthetic and stereochemical demands that the SMILES and scores do not resolve.
Some nearby variants introduce N-N or N-O linkages, while a final example duplicates a large aromatic carbonyl framework. These changes add chemical complexity without establishing a stronger score.
missing_features: The low-end small compounds lack the connected aromatic and carbonyl-containing ring framework seen in the stronger examples; simply supplying nitrogen or a heterocycle does not reproduce that context.
The leading bridged structures lack explicit relative and absolute stereochemistry, leaving their chemically realizable three-dimensional form underspecified.
The data do not identify a further obligatory functional group: different Parent and Child ring/carbonyl arrangements reach similar score ranges.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading saturated ketone/indole/aryl-sulfone molecule scores 0.26804278537408394, compared with 0.25552813151632275 for its close unsaturated ketone counterpart and 0.24018374019946398 for the corresponding unsaturated sulfonamide connection. These comparisons favor particular local saturation and linkage choices within an already rich ring scaffold, rather than ring count alone. Ethane scores 0.012461119656980673 and the small acyclic imine-rich compound 0.014440527314146958; neither carries the aromatic-carbonyl spatial context of the stronger families. A final aminomethylpiperazine/xanthone-like molecule scores 0.21967074064860953. Parent seed-1 reached 0.26493557493264663 with a different benzofused diazepinone/benzodioxole/sulfonylpiperazine arrangement. The Child dense indole polycycle is consequently one observed solution family, not an established necessary scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is moderately sized and fluorinated, combining an aromatic oxadiazole, an unsaturated ring containing adjacent nitrogens, a partly unsaturated nitrogen- or sulfur-containing ring and a short alcohol side chain. The top nitrogen-ring structures include N-F bonds as well as carbon-bound fluorine/fluoromethyl substituents. Several sulfur analogues instead have the unusual explicit C=[SH] connectivity. A different high-scoring seed-0 structure combines a fluorinated unsaturated chain, pyridyl sulfonamide and small fused N/O rings. Low-scoring structures include long-chain cations, polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like molecules, peptide-like expansions and repeated copies of the leading scaffold. Ring-closure rate is 0.9943, aromatic-presence rate 0.9644 and mean SMILES length 45.1. The proposal charged rate is 0.2264, although the leading fluorinated family is formally neutral. The structures show chemical variety but weak assurance that their unusual heteroatom bonds and ring geometry correspond to tractable, stable compounds.
liabilities: N-F bonds, adjacent nitrogen connectivity, unusual C=[SH] centers and the small fused N/O ring example require direct chemical scrutiny. Their scores alone provide no stability or synthetic evidence.
Repeated-scaffold growth and long-chain/polyfunctional excursions can destroy the observed favorable size/composition balance even while retaining recognizable substructures.
missing_features: Oversized and heavily hydroxylated proposals fail to preserve the modest-size fluorinated heterocycle/alcohol arrangement associated with the stronger Child structures.

Chemically conventional counterparts that retain the leading family's size, atom spacing and heteroaromatic context are not well established; the strongest examples instead contain N-fluorinated or unusual sulfur-containing rings. This is a plausibility gap, with any score benefit of replacement unproven.
Explicit stereochemical definition is absent despite substituted saturated ring atoms and multiple possible configurations.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading N-fluorinated compound scores 0.5728383251386864, with the closely related direct ring-fluorine analogue at 0.5544223426906131. A matched change shortens the latter molecule's hydroxyethyl substituent to hydroxymethyl, giving the final molecule at 0.25315061544485684. The local placement of fluorinated groups and alcohol-bearing carbon spacing therefore matters in this family. A much enlarged repeated-family molecule scores 1.5864369562081132e-30, and the cited polyhydroxylated carbohydrate-like structure scores 0.0. This is a strong observed size/composition constraint, not a general reward for accumulating heteroatoms. Parent seed-2 reached 0.3246833344580741 with a fluorovinyl-urea and indole-containing nitrogen heterocycle; the Child reaches its different fluorinated-ring family at 0.5728383251386864. The observed chemical change does not establish that N-F or unusual sulfur bonding is needed, and the trajectories do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring digest molecules contain aryl methyl peroxides, terminal methylene imines, aminophosphines, C=S(=O) sulfur centers and N-fluorinated rings. Conventional aryl ethers and cyclic amines also occur among strong molecules, so unusual bonding is not the only observed route to useful chemical context.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish a chemically credible functional group from a locally acceptable heteroatom or bond replacement.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent or validate complete bonded functional-group neighborhoods during generation and edits. Support chemically credible alternatives that retain local size, donor/acceptor arrangement and attachment geometry; do not use a high score as evidence that an unusual bond pattern is chemically sound.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A digest pair keeps the same surrounding aromatic scaffold and linker but changes a piperazine into a small N-N-containing ring, with observed scores 0.9889622948332054 and 0.4586415097801264. Another close pair changes hydroxyethyl to hydroxymethyl and has scores 0.5544223426906131 and 0.25315061544485684. Atom inventory alone misses these differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful cyclic-amine topology and local atom spacing are not reliably retained when related molecules are generated.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemically meaningful ring neighborhoods and attachment distances when varying peripheral groups, and explore ring-size or linker changes as explicit coherent alternatives. The generator should be able to vary substituents without inadvertently reconstructing the central functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chlorinated aromatic ether scores 0.46457806514522626 with ethoxy but 0.3189563030428961 with propoxy. A fluorinated heterocycle at 0.5728383251386864 contrasts with an enlarged repeated-family structure at 1.5864369562081132e-30. Large nitrogen-rich aromatic assemblies also remain visible among final proposals; the longest proposal SMILES in the digest is 187 characters.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain compact molecular context when combining or extending existing structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support bounded growth, deletion and fragment replacement that preserve useful neighborhoods and permit exploration at comparable molecular size. Avoid treating fragment duplication or appended chemical content as a substitute for a coherent new scaffold; accepted scores should determine which size regime remains useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited molecules nevertheless contain substituted saturated amine rings, fluorinated ring carbons and dense bridged or fused ring junctions. The output therefore describes connectivity families without resolving their stereochemical molecular identities.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generated structures do not specify stereochemistry even when the depicted topology creates stereogenic centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve existing stereochemical information and provide chemically consistent stereoisomer generation for newly created centers and ring junctions. Treat the absence of stereochemical testing as uncertainty; these trajectories do not establish which configuration, if any, would receive a stronger score.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent searches from one scored current molecule. It samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first complete batch allowed by its short-term memory of inverse local structural changes. After receiving real scores, it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that move is worse than the current state. Exact score ties currently go to the lexically first canonical identity. A separate best-observed archive keeps its own score and canonical tie rule.
approach.novelty: Choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms when several accepted neighbors share the exact maximum score, then use the existing canonical ordering if sizes also tie. This lets the walk avoid some neutral graph growth without surrendering the best score available in that accepted batch. Earlier siblings changed edit generation or structural memory; the whole-branch deletion child exposed smaller proposals but often lost score and later regrew. This mechanism instead acts on an already scored tie set. It adds no deletion operator, chemistry filter or size preference outside exact maximum ties.

nodes.hypothesis: Resolve exact ties at the maximum accepted batch score by choosing the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms, then the lexicographically smallest canonical identity, while leaving every non-tied accepted maximum and the independent best archive unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Six compact tie choices preserved immediate scores, but the panel mean fell
finding_summary.insights: Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.
finding_summary.results: Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

nodes.finding:
Six of 28 exact maximum-score ties selected a different molecule, all on deco_hop plateaus in two seeds. Every changed choice preserved the accepted maximum score and used one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical winner, saving ten atoms across those decisions. Three choices kept the source size and three reduced it by one atom. All 407 unique maxima retained the same choice on the same accepted batch, and the identity, archive and transition audits passed. Descendants exceeded the compact selected size after five of the six changes; the remaining case finished at that size after five further steps. Later archive improvements occurred, but the complete three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655, a paired loss of 0.001104 against the required gain of 0.002. Both affected seeds declined; all four other tasks and the third seed retained exactly the parent's molecule/score sequences.

Equal immediate scores do not make tied molecules equivalent starting points for the remaining search. The rule reached smaller real states and preserved the independent archive, so the missing score benefit cannot be explained by a tie implementation failure or an immediate sacrifice in accepted score. The two affected walks ended smaller than their parents yet found lower best scores, narrowing the claim: this size preference controls some neutral growth, but has not identified better future neighborhoods. The chemistry assessment reinforces the distinction between atom count and useful simplification: deco_hop proposals had slightly fewer atoms on average but greater molecular mass and more nitrogen-halogen bonds, while unusual sulfur chemistry persisted. A compact winner can also be a bond change or element substitution. Local chemical organization or neighborhood quality therefore remains a more informative open question than size alone. Six interventions in two overlapping walks do not isolate the contribution of each choice, and the sparse activation does not establish how the rule would behave on other tasks.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often aromatic molecules with recurrent unusual sulfur, reactive halogen bonds and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-770a3cefca6a covers every task in the supplied digest; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The digest contains 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. Its proposal ring_closure_rate is 1.0 throughout; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0 and describes the presence of aromatic SMILES tokens, not the fraction of atoms that are aromatic. These are substantial heterocyclic and polycyclic graphs, not small acyclic fragments. Passive RDKit 2023.09.6 parsing of all 4350 proposals succeeds: they contain 21-49 heavy atoms, with median 33, and 2-10 perceived rings, with median 4. Graph parsing does not establish energetic stability or a synthesis. Relatively conventional indole carboxamides coexist with heavily decorated nitrogen heterocycles, sulfur-rich cages, medium-ring bridges, heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual neutral sulfur multiple bonding. Some individual structures are plausible, but repeated problematic chemistry among the reported high scorers and late proposals supports the overall implausible/weak reading. Diversity is moderate at the graph level across the panel; high scorers within a task frequently remain closely related members of a local family. All proposal charged_rate and stereocentre_rate counters are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or stereochemical labels, not an absence of ionizable atoms or stereogenic graphs: 3432 proposals have potential unassigned stereocentres in the passive audit. Against Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, all molecule/score sequences match exactly on four tasks; only deco_hop seeds 0 and 2 differ. The chemistry comparison below concerns those observed outputs and makes no activation finding. All descriptor counts and parent comparisons are reproducible in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0012-03-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json; they describe proposal occurrences, and perceived ring counts can include overlapping rings in bridged systems. The digest final_molecules are the last proposal records from seed 2, not a selected endpoint or the best archive.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25. Their characteristic chemistry is an indole, benzofuran or benzothiophene joined through an amide or ketone to an aryl group, with alkoxy, methyl, amino, thiol and halogen substituents. The cited 0.39905049777278273 indole carboxamide is a relatively conventional 23-heavy-atom, three-aromatic-ring molecule bearing ethoxy, methyl and thiol groups. The 0.41003927643747895 best example has 26 heavy atoms and the same perceived aromatic ring count, but is a benzofuran with an N-chloroamide, an amino/chloro-substituted benzylic carbon, an aniline and a thiol. The 0.393567030299894 example is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with an aminomethoxy arm and chloromethyl group. Late seed-2 proposals instead include bridged unsaturated sulfur heterocycles with an amino-ketone linker; the last proposal scores 0.3852230774700024. All supplied molecule/score sequences are identical to the parent.
liabilities: The best benzofuran combines an N-chloroamide and an amino-bearing benzylic chloride; these create chemical-reactivity concerns beyond the ordinary aryl substitution pattern.

Thiol, chloromethyl and N-fluoro/N-hydroxy functionality occurs in the cited series; the last sulfur-bridged proposal additionally contains an N-N linkage. These motifs need individual chemical scrutiny rather than treating sanitized graphs as equally makeable.
missing_features: Sustained coverage of chemically conventional variants of the observed compact carbonyl-linked aromatic motif is incomplete: it appears among the stronger examples, but later proposals often deform the rings and linker or introduce unusual sulfur chemistry.

The best example lacks a defined configuration at its amino/chloro-substituted benzylic centre. A score benefit from resolving that configuration is untested; the records do not identify an additional required target-specific group.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. The stronger cited molecules retain a carbonyl-linked aromatic framework while changing its substituents. At 0.021532846118034143, the cited low example retains an aryl ketone but replaces the compact fused aromatic core with a partly saturated, enlarged ring system; it has only one perceived aromatic ring. At 0.03343008011310944, another low example retains three aromatic rings but replaces the amide carbonyl with a substituted saturated carbon. Together these observations associate higher scores with both carbonyl linkage and compact conjugated-ring organization, rather than aromaticity alone. The strongest example still contains reactive-looking groups, so the gradient does not demonstrate a preference for synthetic plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: These are large decorated heteroaromatics: 30-49 heavy atoms, median 38, with aromatic tokens in every proposal. The 0.6145389662714401 best family carries a fused nitrogen heterocycle with carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, a densely substituted benzylamino aryl group, imines, fluorinated arms and a sulfur-containing ester side chain. The first cited best molecule has 46 heavy atoms and calculated molecular weight 800.601. One equally scoring variant contains sulfur triple-bonded to carbon on both sides. Late seed-2 molecules retain carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycles but add polyunsaturated ether arms, N-bromination and sulfur-oxygen linkers; the cited hydroperoxide-bearing proposal scores 0.5518599963349826. This is the only task whose sequences differ from the parent, in seeds 0 and 2. Across its proposals, mean heavy atoms change from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207, while calculated mean molecular weight changes from 597.9077586206896 to 618.5739229885057. N-halogen occurrences change from 33 to 161 and S-halogen occurrences from 180 to 217. The atom-count change therefore does not describe a general improvement in the observed chemical quality.
liabilities: The cited best molecules contain unusual neutral carbon-sulfur triple-bond environments, a sulfenyl chloride, imines and extensive mixed halogenation. A molecular graph of this form is not a demonstrated stable synthetic product.

N-brominated heterocycles, a hydroperoxide, long polyunsaturated arms and sulfur-oxygen linkers occur in the late digest. Large molecular weight and flexible decoration remain substantial liabilities even when heavy-atom count is slightly lower than the parent mean.
missing_features: Chemically conventional, lower-mass decoration alternatives that retain the recurring carbonyl/heteroaromatic framework are poorly represented among the best examples; added branch length, sulfur and halogens dominate instead.

The strongest recorded plateau supplies no evidence for which missing decoration would improve the objective. What is missing chemically is stable bonding and controlled side-chain complexity within that scaffold family, not demonstrated access to a specific unseen target structure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic ester/phenol and fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. The cited low ring-rewired example scores 0.526081691583997. Higher-scoring examples preserve a related heterocyclic framework while extensively modifying and enlarging the decorations. The best score 0.6145389662714401 is shared by the cited single- and double-carbon-triple-bonded sulfur variants, so this observed plateau does not distinguish sharply different sulfur bonding. It supports tolerance of these decoration changes, not evidence that sulfur hypervalence is chemically beneficial. Within the late seed-2 series, the more aromatic carbonyl-bearing 0.5942930760374979 example exceeds the hydroperoxide/carbonyl-disrupted 0.5518599963349826 example, although their side chains also differ. Parent versus child observed maxima are 0.6161710037174721 versus 0.6145389662714401 for seed 0 and 0.6092182584436399 versus 0.5942930760374979 for seed 2; the smaller mean graph size did not accompany better maxima in these observed outputs.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms, median 36, and typically combine halogenated aryl groups, phenols, amine-bearing rings and sulfur-rich linkers or bridges. Every proposal has aromatic tokens; halogen_rate is 0.9966. The 0.9148143511682032 best example has 32 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including two aromatic rings, a tertiary aliphatic ring nitrogen, an aminomethyl substituent and an aryl-bound ring nitrogen. Its scaffold also contains unusual sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding. The 0.8856242185485628 example has an aziridine, an amino-substituted saturated nitrogen ring, a sulfur-sulfur double-bond unit and halogenated phenol/aryl groups. These are substantial amine-bearing frameworks, not a generator lacking ring amines. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding, hydrogen-bearing sulfur in unusual multiple-bond environments and a strained aziridine make the high-scoring series chemically questionable.

Heavy halogenation and complex ring topology accompany undefined configurations. Every proposal has at least one potential unassigned stereocentre in the passive audit, despite stereocentre_rate 0.0 in the digest.
missing_features: Conventional, less reactive realizations of the observed aryl-plus-nonacylated-amine arrangement are missing from the cited best family: the aromatic and amine motifs are entangled with unusual sulfur bonds and, in another high example, an aziridine.

Explicit molecular-state definition is missing despite the amines and stereogenic rings. The best example has four potential unassigned stereocentres; the neutral SMILES do not establish protonation at an assay condition, and no score benefit from state enumeration is shown.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited 0.007468397818197266 low example is a large aromatic carboxylic acid bearing amide and N-sulfonyl nitrogen functionality, with no conventional nonacylated aliphatic amine by the passive structural heuristic. Stronger cited molecules instead contain free aliphatic amine centres and retain aryl/phenolic surfaces. A closer comparison is the 0.8663008496126992 example and the 0.04252669549740123 late proposal: replacing the attached carbon of its chlorophenyl ring with sulfur destroys that ring aromaticity while retaining the surrounding amine-rich scaffold, and accompanies a large score decrease. Removing the methylene between a tertiary nitrogen and its sulfur-containing ring produces the cited 0.3331237338421948 proposal. Thus the observed gradient is sensitive to ring identity and connection geometry, not simply nitrogen count. The sulfur liabilities persist at high scores; these trajectories alone establish neither binding contacts nor measured affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms, median 35, and aromatic tokens throughout. The best family is a bridged azaaromatic/aryl framework with alkyl substituents, an N-methyl lactam and a cyclic N-O linkage. The 0.21196904390980506 example has 31 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and a dense network with seven overlapping perceived rings, including medium-sized loops; it has three potential unassigned stereocentres. Other seeds produce much heavier brominated aryl/sulfur/amine derivatives or sulfur-bridged lactam/polyether frameworks. The last seed-2 proposal is a 40-heavy-atom sulfur-rich, carbonyl-bearing polycycle with alcohol/ether/thiol substituents and score 0.18220097615153677. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Multiple overlapping medium-sized rings and a cyclic N-O bond complicate plausible synthesis and stereochemical control; the perceived ring count should not be mistaken for seven independent ordinary rings.

The cited low brominated molecule includes an O-Br bond, bromomethyl thioether and crowded sulfur environment. Late proposals include hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur and sulfur-carbon multiple bonds. These are chemically distinct liabilities despite retaining aromatic and carbonyl groups.
missing_features: The stronger aromatic/carbonyl arrangement is not represented by a broad set of simpler, synthetically interpretable scaffold alternatives. The top family achieves it through a complicated bridged N-O/lactam network.

Defined configurations and matched alternatives with simpler bridge connectivity are absent from the cited top series. The records do not demonstrate that adding more amines, halogens or ring closures would fill an objective-specific gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heteroaromatic scores 0.1678386594791329. The cited open-chain urea-related derivatives score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while the bridged azaaromatic/lactam family reaches 0.21196904390980506. The shorter alkyl-substituent analogue at 0.2087472610464947 and the best example at 0.21196904390980506 differ by a local alkyl extension, consistent with small substituent effects within that family. A much heavier brominated sulfur derivative scores only 0.12870267321446027. The observed association favors this particular connected aromatic/carbonyl arrangement over the shown opened analogues or indiscriminate heavy decoration. It does not establish that arbitrary extra rings are rewarded, or reveal the exact feature needed beyond the best observed score.

per_task.generated_character: These are relatively compact by atom count but highly interconnected sulfur-rich graphs: 25-33 heavy atoms, median 29, and median six perceived rings. The aromatic-token rate is 0.7184; late seed-2 proposals are entirely nonaromatic, so abundant ring closures do not imply abundant aromaticity here. The 0.5903526424693334 best molecule has 30 heavy atoms, five sulfur atoms, three fluorines, six perceived rings and seven potential unassigned stereocentres. It contains a carbonyl-rich nitrogen heterocycle, a fluorohydrin thioether substituent and a heavily bridged sulfur framework. The 0.5527071687189122 analogue has a related four-sulfur cage and eight potential unassigned stereocentres. The last seed-2 proposal instead has an aldehyde, ketone and N-fluoro amidine-like group in a nonaromatic sulfur cage with nine perceived rings. All supplied molecule/score sequences match the parent.
liabilities: Sulfur-carbon multiple bonding at multiply connected neutral sulfur atoms, sulfur-sulfur links, hydrogen-bearing sulfur centres, and small rings embedded in dense cages make the representative best structures synthetically implausible without much stronger chemical evidence.

The late proposals add an aldehyde, N-F bonding and, in the 0.004199910554494925 example, an S-Cl bond. The final graph has eleven potential unassigned stereocentres, so low heavy-atom count does not mean low chemical complexity.
missing_features: Chemically conventional ways of combining the observed fluorinated, carbonyl-rich heteroatom pattern with compact size are missing from the best family. Compactness is realized through densely bridged sulfur chemistry rather than a clearly tractable scaffold.

Stereochemical definition is absent precisely where the graphs are most stereochemically complex. The best and late examples have multiple potential configurations, but the supplied records do not show a score benefit from any particular stereoisomer or an absent free amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited early aromatic ester/dicarbonyl molecule scores 7.590554525032884e-10, while the fluorinated carbonyl/sulfur-cage family reaches 0.5903526424693334. However, an already sulfur-rich, fluorinated, six-perceived-ring example still scores 1.0546805269255595e-09. Sulfur abundance and ring count alone therefore do not explain the gradient. In the final seed-2 batch, the cited 26-heavy-atom cage scores 0.4484554129767839; an expanded lactone-containing neighbour scores 0.2536619453071564, and the sulfenyl-chloride-containing carbonyl derivative scores 0.004199910554494925. The shown scores are sensitive to precise connectivity and atom/functional-group balance. They provide no evidence that these unusual sulfur environments are makeable or that a specific absent medicinal motif would improve the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high-score molecules include carbon-sulfur-carbon connectivity with sulfur triple-bonded on both sides, neutral sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and hydrogen-bearing sulfur in multiply connected ring systems. These occur in graphs that parse successfully, including a recorded 0.6145389662714401 plateau that does not distinguish markedly different sulfur bond orders. The issue is the local bonding environment, not every sulfur-containing group.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control of chemically conventional sulfur bonding while exploring otherwise useful heteroatom patterns.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand access to conventional heteroatom and linker alternatives while retaining the surrounding scaffold, and distinguish unusual sulfur environments from ordinary thioethers, thiocarbonyls and oxidized sulfur groups. Chemical validity needs information beyond successful graph sanitization; the same chemical criterion must apply to every supplied objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Passive graph reading finds N-halogen bonds in 628 proposals, O-halogen bonds in 301 and S-halogen bonds in 333 out of 4350 proposals; these categories can overlap. Digest exemplars show N-chloroamides, N-brominated carbonyl heterocycles, O-brominated aryl substituents and sulfenyl chlorides. Some of these liabilities coexist with the highest recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Halogen placement is insufficiently selective for stable medicinal substituents rather than reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent halogen edits with their attachment chemistry intact, and offer matched conventional carbon-bound substitutions or replacements for reactive heteroatom attachments. Use the observed local scores to explore those alternatives without assuming that generic halogen presence is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In the changed proposal family, parent-to-child mean heavy atoms decrease from 38.90344827586207 to 38.60344827586207 while calculated mean molecular weight increases from 597.9077586206896 to 618.5739229885057. Elsewhere, a cited 30-heavy-atom high scorer carries five sulfur atoms and six perceived rings, and a 31-heavy-atom high scorer has a network of seven overlapping perceived rings. The recorded chemistry decouples small atom count from tractability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Compact graph size does not reliably produce lower molecular mass, simpler ring topology or easier synthesis.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically complete simplifications and scaffold alternatives that can reduce heavy-element burden, bridge congestion or flexible decoration while retaining observed aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships. Evaluate chemical simplicity independently of heavy-atom count; no supplied comparison establishes a score gain from a blanket size preference.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive perception nevertheless identifies potential unassigned stereocentres in 3432 of 4350 proposals. Cited high-score molecules include graphs with four and seven potential unassigned centres, and a cited final cage has eleven. Thus the missing labels are a molecular-definition gap, not evidence that the search only makes achiral molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemistry for many graphs with potential stereogenic centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly represent stereochemical choices when edits create, retain or remove stereogenic centres, using only task-independent molecular information and the permitted identity rules. This would improve the specificity of the output; the observed trajectories do not establish a score advantage for stereoisomer enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited comparisons include a compact carbonyl-linked fused aromatic family above enlarged or carbonyl-disrupted variants, and an amine-rich aryl framework whose ring-dearomatized sulfur analogue scores much lower. The top exemplars repeatedly remain within one local structural family, often adding unusual sulfur bonds or bridge congestion. Rings and aliphatic amine centres are already present; their stable arrangement in alternative scaffolds is the incomplete capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships are insufficiently explored through diverse conventional scaffold alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer scaffold and linker changes that preserve chemically interpretable arrangements of aromatic surfaces, carbonyls and nonacylated amines while changing ring topology or attachment geometry. Let real feedback determine where those arrangements matter; the evidence supports richer conventional alternatives, not a universal pharmacophore or a task-specific motif prescription.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: NF-BO does Bayesian optimization in a latent space that is exactly invertible. A normalizing flow maps molecular sequences to continuous latents and back with no reconstruction error, so a point chosen in latent space decodes to a definite molecule rather than an approximation. A Gaussian process is fitted over the scored latents, Thompson sampling picks promising directions, and proposals are made by perturbing selected token blocks within a trust region before decoding back through the inverse flow.
approach.novelty: This root commits to choosing which token blocks to perturb by an estimated sequence-level pointwise mutual information rather than uniformly, so the perturbation concentrates on positions the flow considers informative. It also adapts the flow to high-scoring task-local sequences mid-session and re-encodes every observation after each adaptation, which keeps the latent geometry aligned with the current objective instead of frozen at corpus statistics.

nodes.hypothesis: Search around scored task-local molecules in an injective SELFIES SeqFlow latent space, adapt the flow to high-scoring observations, and use a latent GP with Thompson sampling to select fresh trust-region proposals whose perturbed token blocks are chosen from estimated sequence-level PMI before exact inverse-flow decoding.

finding_summary.headline: The only root to fail: the flow adaptation aborted mid-run and two objectives never finished
finding_summary.insights: The failure is not in the idea but in adapting the flow while a session is live. Re-encoding every observation after each adaptation is what makes the latent geometry stay useful, and it is also what puts a failure-prone training step inside the oracle loop, where an abort costs the remaining budget on that objective. The partial results that did land are suggestive, with 0.652 on drd2_docking from only 140 calls, so the approach is not obviously weak. The molecules also show a distinct problem: perturbing token blocks in a SELFIES-based latent produces boron, phosphorus and cumulated-double-bond structures at very high rates. A repair should move adaptation to a batch boundary with a guarded fallback before this lineage is judged on score.

molecular.headline: Boron, phosphorus and cumulated double bonds: latent perturbation decodes to chemistry that does not exist
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically implausible output in the round. Cumulated double bonds, essentially absent from every other root, appear in 42 percent of proposals on one objective and 95 percent on another. Boron appears as a terminal double-bonded atom, phosphorus appears as cationic chains, and charged species reach 88 percent on one objective. Aromatic content runs 31 to 66 percent, and one proposal reaches 239 characters. The exact-inverse property the method depends on is working correctly; the problem is that the latent neighbourhood being searched decodes to sequences that are valid SELFIES and impossible molecules.

nodes.method_name: NF-BO: invertible sequence-flow search with token-adaptive latent proposals
nodes.method_thesis: Use NF-BO's SeqFlow mapping, exact left-inverse decoding, and token-adaptive trust-region search. Train a compact SELFIES flow on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Within each fresh objective session, adapt it using highly scored task-local sequences, re-encode all observations after updates, and fit a latent-space GP. Generate new latent proposals around scored observations by perturbing token blocks according to their estimated pointwise mutual information with the decoded sequence. Thompson sampling selects proposals for inverse-flow decoding. These mechanisms follow [NF-BO, Sections 4 and 5.3](https://arxiv.org/html/2504.14889v1). Regenerate as needed to fill the evaluator-announced batch with distinct canonical molecules; no corpus molecules are ranked or retrieved. The hypothesis is that score-directed local search around exactly reconstructable observations finds improving structures efficiently enough to raise the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Exact reconstruction alone is not the objective. Useful flow training and surrogate prediction under the permitted preparation and feedback remain empirical prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from unlabeled molecules and chooses its checkpoint by the yield of valid, connected, distinct ancestral samples, with heldout likelihood breaking ties. Each objective receives a fresh adaptable copy and a frozen reference. Accepted molecular trajectories train the adaptable policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and prior regularization. The online cycle emits one neural batch followed by two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh the scored breeding population and supply a protected first graph descendant. The graph operator independently cuts the two selected parents, usually retains the larger first fragment and smaller second fragment, and joins their exposed atoms with a single bond. Atom and bond mutations may follow. An accepted-score fingerprint posterior chooses the remaining evaluations from a temporary offspring pool, and accepted graph descendants return to neural replay. The join currently requires molecular validity but does not check whether either attachment resembles the bond environment it replaces.
approach.novelty: Add reciprocal cut-endpoint context matching to crossover: a retained endpoint may replace the opposite parent's discarded endpoint only when their local typed neighborhoods agree. This makes the actual attachment sites, rather than whole-molecule resemblance or complete-ring retention, the unit of compatibility. The lineage's previous siblings changed prior preparation or accepted-score neural behavior; related campaign experiments favored similar parents or preserved complete ring cores while leaving attachment compatibility unresolved. This experiment changes only the admissibility of the already sampled two-cut graft. A mismatch returns to the Parent's existing mutation path, and crossover involving its whole-fragment hydrogen-attachment fallback remains explicitly outside the gate.

nodes.hypothesis: Gate two-cut graph crossover by reciprocal equality of the retained and opposite discarded endpoint contexts, preserving the Parent fragment draws and routing mismatches through its existing mutation fallback.

finding_summary.headline: Attachment matching worked, but crossover nearly vanished and one replica failed
finding_summary.insights: Exact local attachment matching can suppress genuinely available mismatched grafts while preserving a small usable crossover channel. Its dominant effect here was to replace crossover with first-parent mutation: 23 of the 27 later-mutated crossover emissions had reproduced a parent before mutation, and only six evaluated emissions had a changed immediate recombination product. Better overall graph yield therefore does not establish better recombination. Mutation work rose from about 149 to 192 attempts per graph request, and scaffold variety within individual task/seed pools narrowed even though every pool filled. The rule also preserves unusual chemistry already accepted in a source: both pure crossover emissions retained N–F bonds, and the broader output still contained N–O and N–N environments and unspecified stereochemistry. The strong sitagliptin score increase cannot be read as improved synthetic quality. The completion failure is separately explained by an inherited molecule reader alternating between two aromatic SMILES representations after a protected ring-closing mutation; it does not erase the measured gate activation. Full three-seed utility and a useful contribution from compatible recombination remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejected 18,963 otherwise valid joins, including 18,158 that were also novel and encodable. Every one of the 847 surviving applicable joins satisfied both independently reconstructed endpoint matches. The channel remained usable, but barely: only two changed pure crossovers reached evaluation, alongside 27 crossovers followed by mutation. Crossover evaluations fell from 1,133 to 29, and their best-parent beats fell from 121 to two. Overall graph yield improved from 452/2,850 to 541/2,710 best-parent beats; on the same observed batch prefixes, the Parent had 437/2,710. All 271 reached graph batches were full, and all 143 reserved first descendants had real current policy ancestry. However, a feedback identity error stopped one task at 90 of 300 evaluations, so the panel used 4,290 of 4,500 calls and has no complete three-seed score. The two completed seed macro scores rose from 0.542383 to 0.565620 and from 0.579854 to 0.586448. Across complete three-seed task endpoints, sitagliptin rose by 0.163068 and deco_hop by 0.010448, while median_2 fell by 0.020074 and drd2 by 0.002229. Zaleplon fell by 0.006004 over the two completed seeds.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich ureas, azaarenes and cyclic amines coexist with unusual N–O, N–N and N–F chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied output of n-7ba291681388 spans recognizable medicinal scaffolds and chemically questionable derivatives. Aromatic and saturated heterocycles are abundant; ring supply is not the missing capability. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9851 to 0.9977 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.8379 to 0.9818. These are fractions of SMILES containing the respective notation, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has a stereocentre-notation rate of 0.0. Overall exploration includes several scaffold families, but the highest-scoring excerpts mostly contain close relatives within seed-specific families. Compared with parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the observed chemistry changes substantially without eliminating unusual heteroatom connections: compact ureas replace some exotic fused aromatic derivatives, smaller azaaryl assemblies retain N–O chemistry, and other trajectories concentrate on nitrogen chains or covalent N–F bonds. No synthesis, stability, protonation or biological mechanism is established by these scores. All listed tasks have trajectories. The supplied zaleplon_mpo seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 90, with 80 optimizer proposals; its digest contains 660 optimizer proposals across seeds. The other supplied task/seed trajectories reach evaluation 300, giving 870 optimizer proposals per task. That first comparison therefore describes the supplied prefix, not an equally complete endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of moderately sized N-benzyl/N-aryl ureas with hydroxylated phenyl or pyridyl groups and aryl halogens. These have familiar carbonyl and aromatic substitution chemistry and look more straightforward to synthesize than many surrounding proposals. The other prominent digest family combines a biphenyl nitrile with an ether-linked unsaturated imine/thioamide appendage. Low-scoring proposals include very large polyaromatic structures, extended polyenes, highly decorated amides and a polysulfide linker. Rings and aromatics are pervasive, with digest rates of 0.9924 and 0.9818; mean SMILES length is 46.4, a text-length measure rather than a molecular-size descriptor.
liabilities: The imine/thioamide side chains and long unsaturated tails introduce stability and geometric-isomer questions that the recorded scores do not resolve.
Polysulfide and unusually connected nitrogen-containing alternatives require separate chemical scrutiny; the makeability of the urea family does not generalize to the entire output.
The large low-scoring polyaromatic derivatives combine substantial size with complex substitution, increasing apparent synthetic burden.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the moderate aromatic size and restrained polar substitution seen in the leading ureas is missing from the oversized low-scoring proposals.

Distinct compact scaffolds that reproduce the leading polar-group arrangement through ordinary functional groups are weakly represented among the digest leaders. No particular absent target ring can be inferred from this sample.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The hydroxypyridyl urea scores 0.48211544265448975, versus 0.3051048083696145 for the initial trimethoxyindole amide. Replacing its aryl chlorine with bromine retains the same recorded score, while adding another phenolic hydroxyl gives 0.4588223100704468. The much larger polyene/amide structure scores 2.6967182149798692e-39. This supports a bounded aromatic framework with a particular polar-group arrangement, not unlimited aromatic or heteroatom addition. The imine/thioamide alternative still reaches 0.4711064141789182, so conventional urea chemistry is not uniquely rewarded. The parent seed-0 best was a more unusual fused aromatic N–O/sulfur-containing structure at 0.49151859442707624; the current urea family is chemically more conventional without a higher observed seed-0 maximum.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpt is a closely related family of alkoxy-substituted quinazolines connected to fluorinated azaaryl groups through tertiary nitrogen linkers. Every listed leader retains an N–O bond; several contain an electron-rich amino-substituted alkyne, hydroxymethylated nitrogen or an oxime ether. The final seed-2 excerpt instead contains densely fused nitrogen heterocycles and chloromethyl/bromomethyl substituents. Worst examples include nonaromatic, carbonyl-rich bicyclic or peptide-like structures and a smaller fused aromatic sulfone. Familiar heteroaromatic cores give these compounds medicinal-chemistry character, but their peripheral bond chemistry makes synthetic plausibility uneven. Ring-closure and aromatic-presence rates are 0.9977 and 0.9782.
liabilities: N–O attachments, amino-substituted alkynes and N-hydroxymethyl groups warrant stability and synthetic-route scrutiny even when they receive high scores.
Some final heteroaryl derivatives carry potentially reactive chloromethyl or bromomethyl groups, and their dense fused-ring topology increases synthetic complexity.
The scores provide no evidence that replacing these questionable connections with more conventional ones would automatically improve the objective.
missing_features: Equally successful alternative azaaryl arrangements joined entirely through conventional functional-group environments are not demonstrated in the bounded best set; it is dominated by one N–O-containing architecture.

The lower-scoring ring systems lack the leading combination and placement of heteroaromatic nitrogen and peripheral N/O groups. These observations do not identify a uniquely required absent heterocycle.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-alkyne-linked quinazoline reaches 0.8552185580114399; an ethylene-linked, hydroxymethylated analogue reaches 0.8437682003494467. The nonaromatic bicyclic sulfone/lactam gives 0.2596515290053845, while the small aromatic fused sulfone gives 0.26031991744066046. Thus the specific azaaryl and surrounding N/O arrangement matters more than ring presence alone; the comparison does not establish that the unusual alkyne itself is necessary. The parent seed-1 maximum of 0.8301591128254581 used a larger linked quinazoline assembly with problematic sulfur/nitrogen substituents. The current leaders retain the azaaryl pattern in a smaller assembly while still using unconventional connections.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring excerpt contains moderately sized diaryl compounds bearing saturated diaza rings and an aryl-ethyl-pyrrolidine substituent. Methoxy, phenolic and aryl-halogen substitutions surround accessible aliphatic amine centres. Both aromatic surface and saturated ring volume are substantial. Other seeds explore fused aryl amines and furan-containing cyclic amines with fluorinated unsaturated substituents. Much of the main polyamine family looks synthetically interpretable, although some bridged, aminal-like or highly fluorinated variants are less straightforward. The digest ring-closure rate is 0.9897 and aromatic-presence rate is 0.9759. The charged-notation rate of 0.0069 does not mean that the numerous neutral-written amines cannot protonate.
liabilities: Substituted saturated rings contain unassigned stereogenic centres, so the reported SMILES do not identify individual stereoisomers.
Several amine centres combined with sizeable aromatic surface raise protonation and solubility questions that the score does not measure here.

The final seed-2 family includes an N-hydroxylated enamine and a hydroxy-substituted alkyne alongside fluorinated enol ethers; these peripheral groups are less conventional than the leading polyamine core.
missing_features: No missing score-driving aromatic or basic-amine feature is supported for the near-ceiling leaders; both are already present.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and walks through batches of fresh local graph edits, including direct formula-preserving exchanges of aromatic nitrogen and carbon positions. It sanitizes each graph, repairs its canonical identity before duplicate checks, and submits the first full batch allowed by short-term inverse-motif memory. A selected transition installs at most four signed local attributes for four completed steps, with overlapping attributes refreshed to the latest transition. The current veto needs only one positive and one negative inverse match from the same transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current state even after a worsening move; equal maxima use the canonical lexical order, and an independent archive retains the best observed molecule.
approach.novelty: Require a candidate to match every currently live inverse attribute belonging to one selected transition before that transition can veto it, while still requiring both inverse signs. This makes the veto respond to a complete retained signature instead of any two opposite-sign fragments. Earlier memory siblings changed single-attribute matching to a two-sign rule or withheld memory credit from nonimproving moves. This experiment keeps credit for every selected move and changes only how completely a candidate must match the stored signature; the neighborhood extensions already present in the Parent remain in place.

nodes.hypothesis: Veto a valid novel neighbor only when its signed motif changes match every currently live inverse restriction of at least one selected-transition provenance group and that complete group contains both inverse signs, replacing the Parent's one-match-per-sign criterion without changing memory credit or lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Complete-signature memory admitted 113 scored neighbors, but lowered every seed's macro score
finding_summary.insights: Incomplete motif matches do exclude some useful variations: newly admitted methyl addition, ring opening and aryl substitution produced real archive gains. A newly admitted phenol-oxygen deletion was selected despite a score loss, then a newly admitted hydroxymethyl addition in the next batch produced the strongest observed DRD2 molecule. Those concrete successes did not rescue the overall score claim. The checks rule out an unexercised predicate, missing feedback, loss of unconditional memory credit, altered expiry or restored historical signatures as explanations for the negative panel result. Requiring full motif coverage reduces exclusions as intended, but this panel shows that greater matching specificity is not sufficient to identify restrictions that can be removed beneficially. Whether the partial-signature vetoes help diversification remains open: once batch membership changes, later source graphs and random-stream consumption change, and ancestry alone cannot assign the final score difference to one admitted edit. The chemistry assessment also finds persistent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur environments, difficult ring geometry and absent stereochemical assignments alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families. The stronger individual molecules therefore do not establish improved chemical feasibility or broader useful scaffold coverage.
finding_summary.results: On the Child's actual source states and live memory tables, the inherited rule would veto 178 fresh draws; the complete-signature rule vetoed 65 and admitted the other 113. Every new admission was evaluated, affecting 96 batches across all fifteen task sessions, and twenty became next states. Fifteen improved on their source, five tied and 93 worsened it; five produced immediate archive gains. Complete signatures still vetoed 63 distinct fresh molecular identities, including a two-attribute group left after overlap replacement. Memory credit, four-step tenure and overlap handling were preserved. All budgets and batches completed, using 5209 generation attempts versus the Parent's 5303. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.482572, a paired change of -0.039187 against the required +0.002. All three seed means declined. Four task means fell; median_2 rose by 0.002696. The largest task-mean losses were sitagliptin (-0.104268) and DRD2 (-0.075446). Across all accepted proposals, source improvements fell from 468 to 436, and strict archive improvements changed from 238 to 237 while their total magnitude fell from 4.699005 to 4.111202.
