molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal chemistry with concentrated leading families, uneven control of polar-group placement, and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives and all supplied parent trajectories were read. Each current objective contains 900 evaluated rows, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposals are predominantly recognizable aromatic medicinal chemistry: linked and fused heterocycles, aryl amides and ureas, sulfonylated nitrogen rings, ethers, and accessible aliphatic amines. Digest ring-closure rates span 0.9885-0.9943 and aromatic-token rates 0.9494-0.9851; these are fractions of strings containing the feature, not fractions of atoms. Descriptive RDKit calculations from the full trajectories, using the benchmark evaluator environment, give median heavy-atom counts of 24, 30, 25, 23 and 24 in the supplied objective order, with median ring count three throughout. All 4,350 proposals parse in that environment. Nonchiral Murcko framework counts range from 397 to 793 per objective, supporting broad overall structural diversity, while the displayed leaders often form close analogue families. Conventional connectivity supports a plausible overall synthetic reading, but unusual nitrogen connections, strained rings, dense fluorination and oversized outliers keep the medicinal-chemistry assessment moderate. Parsing does not establish a synthesis or measured physical properties. All digest stereocentre-token rates are zero; actual stereogenic molecules are present but unspecified. The final digest entries are individual late proposals, not final best-so-far molecules or a representative sample of every seed.

per_task.generated_character: Typical proposals are medium-sized and aromatic, with median 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. The leading structures are linked phenyl/pyridyl or diazine systems bearing an acetamide and a small methyl or amino substituent. The two highest entries each have 23 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-membered rings. A separate leader is an ethoxy/methyl-substituted anilide of a fused aza-aromatic carboxylic acid. These are plausible aryl-coupling and amide chemotypes. Compared with parent n-06c043e9d303, whose leaders included halogenated pyrazole carboxamides and pyrrolylmethyl diaryl ureas, the leading current chemistry shifts toward relatively simple linked aza-aromatic acetamides. Late examples also include diaryl ureas, N-amino ureas and aryl sulfonamides.
liabilities: Multiple linked aromatic rings can give a flat, hydrophobic framework; no solubility or conformational measurements establish its practical behavior.
Oversized polyaryl and peptide-like growth produces extreme low-score outliers. N-amino urea and hydrazone connections also require stability and tautomeric scrutiny beyond a valid graph.
missing_features: The high-score repertoire shows limited alternatives to linked aromatic acetamides and related carbonyl arrangements; the trajectories do not establish a specific absent target ring or functional group.
Precise arrangement of useful aromatic and polar regions is often missing from the low-score elaborations even when their component groups are present. Rings and aromaticity themselves are abundant.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The linked pyridyl acetamides reach 0.523043, compared with the parent pooled leader at 0.469707. Within a current diazine/acetamide series, changing the middle phenyl connection from para to meta accompanies scores of 0.478654 and 0.489798, respectively: topology matters even with the same inventory of groups. More nitrogen or more rings is not uniformly beneficial. A large polyaryl hydrazone/polyamide scores about 4.57e-62 and the peptide-like polyamide extension scores zero. A late N-amino diaryl urea is only 0.006962, whereas larger related urea examples reach appreciable scores. The observed association is controlled size plus an organized aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, not a universal rule that smaller or more nitrogen-rich is better.

per_task.generated_character: This proposal set is typically larger, with median 30 heavy atoms, and has a digest halogen rate of 0.7655. The leading family combines a substituted pyrimidine or pyridine, an aryl group, and an ether-linked oxazole or thiazole carrying another aryl group. The best example has four aromatic rings and eight fluorines. These are recognizable, synthetically plausible heteroaryl/ether structures with substantial aromatic surface and mass. Other seeds contain hydrazone-rich aryl systems and fluorinated tetrahydrofuran-linked fused azaheterocycles; the digest terminal examples also include an amidoxime-ether-like structure. Parent leaders were likewise highly fluorinated but emphasized pyridyl amines/amides and aryl acylhydrazones rather than this ether-linked heteroaryl family.
liabilities: Dense aryl fluorination increases mass while largely preserving a flat aromatic architecture; useful scores do not establish solubility or other physical properties.

Hydrazone and amidoxime-ether chemistry raises configuration and tautomer questions. The low-scoring carbonyl directly attached to sulfonyl sulfur is a less conventional connection whose chemical behavior needs separate scrutiny.
missing_features: The leading excerpt is dominated by a closely related fluorinated aromatic family; similarly productive alternatives in core and linker topology are less evident than substitutions around that family.

The tetrahydrofuran-containing terminal molecules have unspecified stereogenic positions, and the open-chain imino chemistry lacks explicit bond geometry. No score evidence identifies a preferred stereoisomer or mandates additional fluorines.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The highest current ether-linked structure scores 0.605991; the parent pooled leader scores 0.603953. A close series with six, seven and eight fluorines scores 0.605415, 0.604650 and 0.605991, so extra fluorination is not monotonically rewarded even in this neighborhood. Corresponding oxazole/thiazole examples also share a score of 0.594222. A simpler fluorinated diaryl ether still reaches 0.599851. At the low end, a cyanophenyl sulfone is 0.257003 and a much larger aryl/heteroaryl sulfone is 0.266174, while trifluoroethanol is about 0.500438. Size and halogen count alone do not explain the gradient; the visible advantage is associated with the assembled aromatic and linker context.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules are accessible tertiary amines attached to aromatic hydrophobic regions. The highest entry is a compact N-propyl arylpiperidine bearing a benzocyclobutene ring system: 17 heavy atoms, one aromatic ring, a piperidine, and a fused four-membered carbocycle. Other near-ceiling molecules retain the N-alkyl arylpiperidine but replace that fused carbocycle with a larger dibenzoazepine-like imine system. The full trajectories also contain longer arylalkyl piperidines and flexible diamines. Typical proposal size falls from the parent median 28 heavy atoms to 25. The parent likewise produced high-scoring arylpiperidines and flexible diamines, so accessible amine chemistry persists across the change in leading topology. Most bonding is conventional, although the strained small ring and larger imine-containing ring closures complicate an otherwise plausible synthetic reading.
liabilities: The compact leader contains a strained benzocyclobutene ring; larger leaders introduce imine-containing fused systems. These are concrete chemical features, not evidence of failed synthesis or instability under unspecified conditions.

Longer arylalkyl and diamine variants increase conformational freedom. The near-ceiling scores do not establish which protonation state, conformation or stereoisomer provides the implied interactions.
missing_features: Near-ceiling recorded scores do not support inventing an additional mandatory pharmacophore. The remaining observable coverage gap is economical access to alternative amine/aromatic geometries without assuming that ring-bound nitrogen is always necessary.

The leading substituted piperidine carbon is stereogenic but unspecified. Descriptive perception of the full proposals finds 583 molecules with unassigned stereocentres and no assigned stereocentre tokens.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact benzocyclobutene/piperidine is 0.999999980 and the larger fluorinated or chlorinated imine analogues are approximately 0.999999971. Thus added halogens, another aromatic ring or an extra amino group are not demonstrated requirements for the high scores. Low examples include an aromatic amide with an N-sulfonyl piperidine at about 1.98e-05 and an extensively sulfonylated/acylated aniline at about 3.80e-05. Their nitrogens do not provide the same accessible basic environment as an N-alkyl piperidine. However, a late benzylaminocyclohexane scores only 0.002584 despite retaining an aliphatic amine, while a more extended aryl diamine reaches 0.957115. These nonmatched examples support context-dependent amine/aromatic placement, not an amine-presence rule or a measured binding mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: Typical proposals have 23 heavy atoms and three rings. Leaders concentrate on arylsulfonyl nitrogen rings, often combined with a benzodioxole and a carbonyl. The highest molecule is a benzodioxole sulfonyl derivative of a seven-membered N-N-containing lactam, not an ordinary piperazine. Closely following structures are conventional piperazines bearing a phenylsulfonyl group on one nitrogen and a benzodioxole-derived acyl, carbamate or urea group on the other. These are plausible medicinal-chemistry frameworks, although the N-N-containing lactam is less routine. The parent also favored arylsulfonyl piperazines, with fused aza-lactam, chromanone and biphenyl surroundings. Current chemistry changes the surrounding ring/carbonyl arrangement while preserving that broad polar-linker family.
liabilities: The highest seven-membered ring contains an N-N bond, which is chemically different from an ordinary diamine ring and should not be conflated with the simpler piperazine leaders.

Allyl azide, carbon tetrachloride and long lipid-like ester excursions offer poor medicinal-chemistry continuity with the leading structures. Sulfonamide and amide nitrogens must not be counted as interchangeable basic amines.
missing_features: Precise alternative arrangements of the favorable aromatic, sulfonyl and cyclic carbonyl regions are less developed than overall scaffold diversity. The full proposals contain 738 nonchiral Murcko frameworks, so a general inability to make different rings is not supported.

Neither additional nitrogen nor a universally basic ring nitrogen is established as the missing ingredient; electronic character and connection positions distinguish the observed useful polar frameworks.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-N lactam reaches 0.240464, versus the parent pooled leader at 0.235468. The related acylated, carbamate-bearing and urea-bearing piperazines score 0.231809, 0.230331 and 0.226378. A smaller N-methyl phenylsulfonylpiperazine still scores 0.207187. These examples associate the gradient with aromatic and cyclic polar-group arrangement rather than an obligatory free basic piperazine nitrogen: both nitrogens are deactivated by carbonyl/sulfonyl substitution in several leaders. Carbon tetrachloride and allyl azide score zero, aminocyclopropane is 0.020675, and a long-chain ester is 0.027513. Late polyaromatic oxygen/sulfur heterocycles can remain near 0.10-0.13 despite substantial ring content.

per_task.generated_character: This is a chemically broad but mostly very low-score set, with median 24 heavy atoms, three rings and 793 nonchiral Murcko frameworks. The best structure combines a fluoroindole, an N-linked methanesulfonic acid group and a partly saturated fused oxygen/nitrogen bicyclic substituent. The next combines a heteroaryl carboxamide with fused aza rings and a cyclic imine/amidine region. Other leaders include a benzyl-substituted fused N-N/aza-aromatic system bearing hydroxyl groups, a carbonyl-rich cyclic imide-like structure, and a thioether-linked heteroaryl morpholine amide. These are medium-sized polar heterocyclic molecules; synthetic plausibility is mixed, with familiar fragments but more demanding ring connectivity in the leaders. The parent leaders instead included a compact aza-aromatic benzamide, an aryl hydroxyethyl amide and pyridyl acylhydrazones.
liabilities: The leading sulfonic acid and amine combination is strongly ionizable in chemical terms; its neutral drawing does not determine solution-state microspecies or permeability. Cyclic amidine/imine and hydroxylated aza-ring examples also raise tautomer questions.

N-N connectivity and a conjugated carbonyl-rich cyclic structure warrant stability/reactivity scrutiny. Large polyol, peptide, lipid-like and macrocyclic excursions add substantial synthetic and stereochemical complexity while having vanishing recorded scores.
missing_features: The missing capability is consistent coverage of compact, productively arranged polar heterocycles. The output already contains aromatic nitrogen, saturated amines, oxygen rings, sulfur groups and carbonyls, but their presence rarely reproduces the favorable combinations.
The fused oxygen/nitrogen bicycle in the best molecule has unspecified stereogenic ring junctions. No stereochemical alternative or preferred configuration is identified by the supplied scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The current sulfonic-acid/fused-ring leader scores 0.235168, followed by the heteroaryl amide at 0.206946 and the hydroxylated N-N heterocycle at 0.166538. The parent pooled leader was 0.309504. Large lipid-like, polyene macrocyclic and peptide-like examples score zero or extremely close to it; an oxygen-rich glycoside/nucleoside-like structure is about 6.22e-87. Yet a small propyl diazine is only about 1.31e-09, and a phenoxy triazine bearing hydroxyl groups is about 0.000129. Thus compactness and heteroatoms are insufficient without the right local arrangement. The digest median of 0.0 is rounded: the full 900-row median is about 7.96e-08 and three rows are exactly zero. The scattered leaders do not establish a unique required acid, amine, carbonyl or target scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A positional change within a linked aromatic acetamide series accompanies 0.478654 versus 0.489798 despite retaining the group inventory. Another high-score family contains accessible N-alkyl piperidines, whereas its low-score examples include N-sulfonyl piperidines and other deactivated nitrogen environments. Elsewhere, doubly carbonyl/sulfonyl-substituted piperazines are useful despite lacking an ordinary free basic ring nitrogen. These are context-dependent molecular associations, not a universal preference for more nitrogen or a particular charge.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies diverse functional groups but does not consistently retain their useful attachment geometry and electronic character.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically valid changes in attachment position, ring connectivity and local nitrogen environment while preserving recognizable productive arrangements. Use only the current session's observed feedback to distinguish their value; a global preference for basic amines, heteroatom count or one linker type would misread the output.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Full proposal sets contain 397-793 nonchiral Murcko frameworks, yet leading excerpts concentrate on linked aza-aromatic acetamides, polyfluorinated heteroaryl ethers, and N-alkyl arylpiperidines. A fluorinated analogue series scores 0.605415, 0.604650 and 0.605991 with six, seven and eight fluorines; peripheral atom additions give little consistent separation. Another session has 793 frameworks but a full-trajectory median near 7.96e-08.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad framework diversity coexists with narrow families among the strongest observed molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate alternative cores and linkers around arrangements already supported by local feedback, alongside peripheral substitutions. The needed chemical breadth concerns productive structural neighborhoods, not merely more distinct strings, unrelated frameworks or fluorinated variants.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. Descriptive perception under the benchmark environment finds 143, 154, 583, 218 and 299 proposals with unassigned stereocentres in the supplied session order. Cited structures include a substituted piperidine, fluorinated tetrahydrofuran-containing molecules and a fused oxygen/nitrogen bicycle. No proposal string specifies double-bond geometry either. This is incomplete molecular specification, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would score better.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify stereochemistry for molecules that possess stereogenic centers or configurable imino groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent chemically supported stereocentres and bond geometry and make consistent stereochemical alternatives accessible to de novo generation. Preserve achiral structures and let observed feedback determine whether this additional specificity is useful, without assuming an unobserved preferred configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Typical proposal sizes are moderate, but cited low-score outliers include polyaryl polyamides, long-chain esters, glycoside/nucleoside-like polyols and large polyene macrocycles. Several of these reach zero or vanishing scores. Conversely, a compact 17-heavy-atom arylpiperidine reaches 0.999999980, while a small propyl diazine in another session is about 1.31e-09. Both uncontrolled elaboration and severe simplification can leave the useful chemical region.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has uneven control of molecular growth and the placement of polar groups within a bounded structure.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide context-sensitive control over appendage size, linker length and polar-group arrangement, including chemically coherent contraction and growth. Infer useful scale from local structural neighborhoods and feedback rather than imposing universal smallness, maximal ring count or greater polarity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited output includes an organic azide, N-amino ureas, hydrazones, an N-N-containing cyclic lactam, amidoxime-ether-like chemistry, a strained fused carbocycle and a sulfonic-acid/amine combination. These motifs have distinct chemical implications even though their strings are evaluable, and several also occur among relatively strong examples. Charged-token counts therefore neither describe all ionizable centers nor establish a preferred solution form.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces chemically interpretable graphs without consistently resolving their stability, ionization and synthetic liabilities.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Keep functional-group reactivity, plausible ring construction, tautomerism and ionization context visible when generating alternative structures. Treat these as conditional chemical properties rather than equating validation with makeability or excluding every occurrence of a motif that also appears in productive molecules.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts at the best supplied scored molecule and repeatedly samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits from that one current graph. It sanitizes and normalizes each edited molecular identity, rejects previously proposed molecules, and submits the first full batch admitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. Memory vetoes a neighbor only when both inverse signs match the same earlier selected transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph even when its score worsens, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Bounded inverse restrictions, four-step aging, overlap refresh and obstruction release remain part of that Parent, as does the repaired proposal-to-feedback identity join.
approach.novelty: Add one local sulfur-valence introduction gate. A generated neighbor may retain or remove a sulfur environment already present in its source, but it may not introduce or multiply a sulfur environment outside an explicit small envelope of ordinary valence patterns. This redirects eligible graph edits toward alternative neighbors before they reach the unchanged memory gate. It preserves thiol and sulfide valence, aromatic sulfur, terminal carbon-sulfur double bonds, and the usual neutral sulfur-oxide patterns. Earlier siblings changed memory matching and repaired identity bookkeeping; they did not constrain sulfur chemistry. The related corpus-support experiment in another walk admitted chemistry merely because it occurred locally in a corpus. This proposal instead tests a fixed, narrow sulfur rule without learning a vocabulary or changing preparation.

nodes.hypothesis: Reject an otherwise valid canonically novel graph neighbor before tabu testing exactly when it introduces or increases the multiplicity of a sulfur local-environment signature outside a fixed neutral sulfur-valence envelope relative to the same scored source graph, then continue the inherited graph-edit sampling loop from that unchanged source.

finding_summary.headline: The sulfur gate eliminated targeted violations, with higher sampling cost and uneven score gains.
finding_summary.insights:
The targeted sulfur channel was largely independent of the existing tabu veto: 760 of 766 rejected draws would otherwise have reached allocation. Ordinary sulfur alternatives remain abundant enough to fill every batch and retain the panel's average score, despite the extra sampling work. All selected initial sources were already clean under the envelope, so the experiment demonstrates prevention of new violations; it does not exercise recovery from an inherited violating source. Most rejected opportunities come from atom replacement, which accounts for 734 of the 766 rejections.

The small favorable mean score is accompanied by a substantial loss in one seed and lower mean scores on two tasks. It supports the stated mean non-inferiority direction on this panel without establishing a consistent improvement. The molecular assessment also shows where the chemical benefit stops: more ordinary sulfur and recognizable aromatic polyamines coexist with nitrogen/oxygen-halogen bonds, constrained unsaturation, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry. Sulfur valence is one separable source of implausible chemistry; whole-molecule stability, accessible ring geometry and stereochemistry remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The gate rejected 766 of 5,307 otherwise valid novel neighbors across all fifteen task sessions. Of those rejections, 760 would have passed the unchanged tabu rule, and every rejection was followed by a different permitted neighbor from the same scored source. None of the 4,350 emitted molecules contains sulfur outside the declared envelope, compared with 2,398 of 4,350 Parent emissions. Sulfur remains in 2,821 emitted molecules, including thiols, sulfides, aromatic sulfur, thiones, sulfoxides and sulfones.

All three seeds complete all five 300-evaluation tasks and all 435 ten-member batches. The sampling cost rises from 5,285 to 6,234 raw attempts, or 12.15 to 14.33 attempts per batch. Emission yield falls from 82.31% to 69.78% of raw attempts. Recorded edits, normalized identities, accepted-score joins and downstream memory/winner rules pass the independent audit.

molecular.headline: More conventional sulfur and amine skeletons coexist with N-halogen bonds, hypobromites and severely strained cages
molecular.overall_character: The current three-seed panel contains 900 recorded entries and 870 optimizer proposals per task, compared with the supplied three-seed Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 trajectories. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9379 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence remain 0.0. These are string-presence counters, not atom fractions or measurements of ionization and stereochemical feasibility. The prominent high-scoring sulfur motifs now include thiols, sulfides, thiones, sulfoxides and aromatic sulfur, rather than the Parent's frequently multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur cages. Some aromatic amine leaders are entirely sulfur-free and have substantially more recognizable medicinal skeletons. This is a real difference in the observed chemistry, but the output still includes reactive N-Br/N-Cl/N-F and O-Br bonds, N-N/N-O networks, highly constrained small rings and dense carbon/nitrogen cages. Aromatic ring/carbonyl families, large decorated diones and polycyclic amines give moderate diversity across tasks and seeds; local families dominate each late trajectory. Overall synthetic plausibility remains poor because several of the leading complete structures are severely strained or reactive, despite more plausible subseries. No activation or causal attribution is inferred from these molecular observations.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic/fused-ring carbonyl compounds remain prominent. Seed 2 reaches a methoxy- and methyl-substituted indene linked to pyridine through a carbonyl-S-N unit carrying N-Br. Seed 1 contains more conventional indene aryl ketones with ethylthio, methylamino and methoxy substituents; other high examples carry hydrazine, bromomethoxy or sulfenamide groups. Seed 0 reaches an N-bromothioamide on an oxygen-containing unsaturated fused framework. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9977 and halogen presence is 0.8402. These replace the Parent's unusual-sulfur ketones or N-chloroamides with different sulfur chemistry, but several leaders still combine reactive functionalities. The aryl ketone subseries is comparatively plausible.

N-N/N-O networks and constrained unsaturated ring closures remain chemically or geometrically questionable.
missing_features: Broader stable realizations of the compact aryl-carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented relative to N-halogen, sulfenamide and hydrazine substitutions.

Accessible alternatives to the late bridged N-O frameworks and explicit configurations for products that acquire stereocentres are absent from the shown high/final series; no unique target-specific group is established.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its best-scoring half. A memory retains the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and the strongest eligible historical records join the current examples with their original strings and scores. Within history, an example's weight decreases with the number of earlier fitting batches that used it. The total current and historical loss shares remain proportional to their row counts. The policy fits weighted squared errors toward frozen-prior log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, takes up to twelve clipped Adam steps, and retains the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add gradient-norm balancing between the current and historical learning groups. At the start of each history-bearing update, measure the current mean-loss gradient and the historical gradient after the Parent's exposure weighting. Set the two loss shares inversely to those gradient norms, then hold the shares fixed for the update. Each group therefore starts with the same gradient contribution magnitude, while history keeps its existing relative weights. The measured Parent usually lets the current group dominate despite stronger historical rewards. Earlier siblings changed which histories train, their within-group exposure weights, residual penalties, target ceilings, checkpoint retention or historical displacement protection. This mechanism changes the balance between the two group gradients before the unchanged optimizer acts. Equal contribution does not guarantee useful historical information: it can greatly reduce learning from fresh molecules or reinforce repetition. Actual gradient and proposal evidence will determine whether that tradeoff helps.

nodes.hypothesis: At each history-bearing adaptation update, set fixed current and historical loss shares inversely to the norms of their respective starting mean-loss gradients, with the historical gradient retaining the Parent's normalized inverse-exposure weights, so the two groups have equal starting contribution magnitudes; preserve selected members, augmented targets and the inherited optimizer.

finding_summary.headline: Balancing changed learning, but group-gradient reconstruction failed and every seed lost final score.
finding_summary.insights:
The first historical intervention isolates a useful tradeoff before the sampled trajectories diverge. On identical starting examples and likelihoods, average final current-group error was 41.85 with balancing versus 29.32 with the Parent, while historical error was 18.88 versus 23.33. Current fitting was worse in thirteen of fifteen matched sessions. More historical influence can therefore buy better average historical fitting while weakening learning from the fresh batch; it is not a general protection guarantee. Across the later child stream, historical group error still rose in 71 updates and 817 individual historical exposures worsened. History received more than 99% of the loss in 21 nonterminal updates, and the effective selected batch shrank from 9.19 to 5.82 rows on the same selected inputs.

The score loss is not explained by a universal absence of chemical variety. Accepted core counts fell for three objectives but rose slightly for median-2 and sitagliptin. The molecular assessment finds that sitagliptin remains broadly diverse while failing to reproduce useful compact polar arrangements consistently; its largest score loss occurs despite 783 distinct cores versus 775 before. Docking already reaches coherent cyclic-amine chemistry near the numerical ceiling. Familiar rings, higher validity and improved replay fitting do not by themselves produce useful new molecular combinations. The same recurrent representation still generates oversized tails, questionable linkages and unspecified stereochemistry. Positive, unattainable historical targets also remain common: 627 exposures versus 489 in the Parent, on their different sampled streams.

This rules out failure to change coefficients or gradient direction as the explanation for lost utility. It also shows that scalar balance is an insufficient success criterion. Exact group-vector reconstruction remains open: real backward agreement establishes which objective executed, but cannot explain the systematic disagreement with the separately summed gradients. The saved evidence cannot determine whether that numerical discrepancy contributed to the score loss. Any interpretation that stronger historical influence is beneficial must now account for both the observed loss of fresh-batch fitting and increased repetition, as well as this unresolved numerical behavior.
finding_summary.results:
The fixed-share mechanism reached the real optimizer. In all 420 history updates followed by proposals, the measured starting contribution imbalance fell from 0.7012 on average to at most 4.59e-8. History received 84.54% of the loss mass on average. Every update changed the direct gradient direction even after clipping, and all 450 real first backward passes matched the direct actual objective exactly. Original accepted targets, selected-member rules, within-history exposure ratios and the fifteen history-free first-proposal controls remained intact.

One registered numerical check failed systematically: the direct balanced gradient did not reconstruct from the separately measured group gradients within the stated tolerance in any of the 435 history updates. Relative discrepancies reached 0.283% in nonterminal updates and 0.413% in terminal updates, compared with the approximately 0.001% registered tolerance. This limits the claim of exact vector reconstruction; it does not erase the observed scalar balance, changed direct gradient or real optimizer execution.

After history fitting, raw duplicate draws increased from 37.38% to 57.67%, canonical-novel yield fell from 54.80% to 37.62%, and batches needing further sampling increased from 29 to 90. All fifteen evaluations nevertheless completed their 300-call budgets. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.517655 to 0.493672, a paired change of -0.023983. Seed changes were -0.004895, -0.009276 and -0.057779. The largest task loss was sitagliptin, whose mean endpoint fell from 0.287161 to 0.169219. Mean recorded AUC rose from 0.406769 to 0.423980, mainly alongside faster docking progress, so better average early discovery did not deliver the predicted final-score gain.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic chemistry reaches coherent cyclic amines, but retains narrow analogue families, oversized tails and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: This assessment reads every supplied trajectory for node n-95c3f5710341 and Parent n-3462511d7ff0: all five objectives and seeds 0, 1 and 2, with 900 recorded molecules and 870 accepted optimizer proposals per objective in each panel. No objective lacks trajectories. The counters describe accepted optimizer strings, not rejected raw generations or experimentally isolated compounds. In the fixed task order, ring-closure presence rates are 0.9977, 0.9966, 0.9954, 0.9908 and 0.9839; aromatic-atom presence rates are 0.9885, 0.9943, 0.9885, 0.9575 and 0.9425. These are molecule-level text-presence rates, not fractions of atoms that are aromatic. A passive RDKit reading gives median heavy-atom counts of 24, 32, 27, 23 and 24 and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 3 and 3. Phenyl and heteroaromatic rings, amides, sulfonamides, ethers, nitriles and saturated nitrogen heterocycles are all represented. Distinct atom/bond-specific Bemis-Murcko core counts are 425, 315, 506, 735 and 783, versus Parent counts 472, 372, 537, 733 and 775. Thus the complete output is structurally broad, while several high-scoring seed streams concentrate on close analogues. Core counts do not measure usefulness. Many leading structures use conventional medicinal-chemistry bonds, but imidates, activated alkenes, acylhydrazones, unusual sulfur connectivity, overgrown peptide-like structures and long alkyl appendages make the whole set only questionably plausible. All accepted structures parse in the matching RDKit environment; that establishes representation validity, not synthesis, stability, exposure or biological activity. Explicit tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemical notation is absent throughout both panels despite potentially stereogenic structures. Passive descriptor methods, source hashes and all seed comparisons are retained in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-09-improve-L03-molecular-audit/audit.json and stereo.json. Score interpretations below are associations within the supplied molecules; they do not infer an unseen target structure or mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The accepted set is dominated by compact aromatic amides: median 24 heavy atoms, with nitriles in 255 of 870 proposals versus 7 in the Parent. Seed 1 develops diaryl cyanoacrylamides with acetanilide or imidate substituents. Its cited maximum has 24 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, two carbonyls and a nitrile. Seed 0 instead reaches an N-ethyl methylpyrazole carboxamide attached to fluorobiphenyl, also with 24 heavy atoms, and related heteroaromatic lactam/carboxamides. Seed 2 keeps methoxy-substituted indole and benzimidazole families carrying an aryl amide or benzyl nitrile. These are recognizable small-molecule frameworks, although the imidates and activated alkene require more chemical scrutiny than ordinary aryl amides. The Parent maxima were predominantly three-ring pyrrole, aryl-ether and diarylamine carboxamides. Current versus Parent recorded maxima by seed are 0.492632 versus 0.490235, 0.495261 versus 0.447421, and 0.447848 versus 0.476731. The chemistry changes differently in each seed rather than uniformly acquiring a missing ring class.
liabilities: The cyanoacrylamide is an electrophilic conjugated alkene, and aryl imidates introduce hydrolytic and tautomeric questions. These are structural concerns, not measured reactivity or stability.
Repeated amide-rich growth, a permanently charged bulky peptide-like molecule and densely functionalized polycycles create large synthetic and physicochemical burdens.
There are 108 accepted proposals with RDKit-perceived unassigned tetrahedral centres, while the digest stereocentre-notation rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the compact aromatic, nitrogen-containing envelope is missing from the low-scoring tail; both excessive growth and nitrogen-free fragments occur. The data do not establish an obligatory unseen fused-ring scaffold.

Productive variation beyond the repeated diaryl activated-alkene core is limited within seed 1: 53 of its 58 highest-scoring accepted proposals share one atom/bond-specific Murcko core. Ring chemistry is available, but useful alternative attachment arrangements are unevenly explored.

Defined alkene geometry is missing from the cyanoacrylamides; defined tetrahedral stereochemistry is missing from more complex off-family products. The score evidence does not establish a benefit from specifying either.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited 24-heavy-atom acetanilide/cyanoacrylamide reaches 0.4952605565, whereas a 50-heavy-atom quaternary-ammonium peptide-like proposal scores 0 and the 59-heavy-atom repeated indole-amide/guanidine structure scores 2.7846374431e-48. Compactness is associated with the better observations, but is not sufficient: the nitrogen-free, 16-heavy-atom cyclic alcohol scores only 0.0107671849. Seven digest maxima score identically despite aryl positional changes and replacement of an acetanilide linkage by an imidate. This suggests limited discrimination among those compositionally similar arrangements, not evidence that the imidate has equal chemical quality. The initial trimethoxyindole carboxamide scores 0.3051048084; late seed-2 benzimidazole/benzyl-nitrile and related indole-amide examples score 0.4355405789 and 0.3410994870. A ring-rich but enlarged 33-heavy-atom late product drops to 5.3229519627e-06. The observed gradient favors a compact aromatic heteroatom/carbonyl arrangement over indiscriminate ring or chain growth.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest typical proposals in the panel: median 32 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings, with halogen text in 0.7138 of accepted strings. Seed 0 builds four-ring amino-azine/heteroaryl systems with benzylamine links, aryl nitriles and sometimes trifluoromethyl groups. The maximum is a 33-heavy-atom triazine-bearing structure with nine nitrogen atoms, including three nitriles, and no oxygen. Seed 1 develops extensively substituted quinoline/oxazole/aryl ethers. Seed 2 instead concentrates on methoxy/hydroxy aza-aromatic acylhydrazones carrying fluorinated or brominated benzoyl groups. The final cited examples in that seed have three aromatic rings and 32-38 heavy atoms. The azine, ether and amide linkages are conventionally accessible in principle; multiple regioselective substitutions and acylhydrazone geometry complicate that general plausibility. Compared with the Parent, nitrile-bearing proposals rise from 31 to 214 and sulfonamides fall from 160 to 19. The Parent seed-0 high end included extended alternating nitrogen linkages; its seed-1 high end was also an amino-azine family, and seed 2 used aryl sulfonamides with imine-bearing extensions. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.615587 versus 0.589985, 0.607304 versus 0.618622, and 0.605208 versus 0.608588.
liabilities: Large aromatic surfaces, multiple halogens and closely related nitrile-rich substituent patterns can create solubility and selectivity concerns; neither property was measured here.
Acylhydrazones bring possible E/Z mixtures and hydrolytic sensitivity, and some products repeat that linkage rather than introducing a distinct stable framework.
The low-scoring thiocarbonyl-to-sulfone linkage and isolated silicon-oxygen fragment illustrate that a valid representation can still be chemically unusual for this molecular context.
missing_features: The most productive amino-azine and aryl-nitrile arrangement is absent from the lower-scoring sulfone-rich examples, despite similar aromatic ring content. Ring count alone misses the relevant attachment chemistry.

Alternative coherent linkers and ring connectivities are poorly represented within the late acylhydrazone family: 57 of the 58 highest-scoring seed-2 proposals share one Murcko core. The unseen feature needed to exceed the observed range cannot be identified from these examples.
Defined hydrazone geometry and a consistent choice among the hydroxy-aza-aromatic tautomeric possibilities are not established by the strings. No stereoisomer or tautomer comparison was supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-azine/nitrile maximum scores 0.6155870909 and the related butylamino heteroaryl analogue 0.6150075415. Four aromatic rings alone do not explain these values: the cited four-ring sulfone/sulfonamide assembly scores 0.3001508296, and an azine-family aryl methylsulfone variant scores 0.3476272862. Even the four-heavy-atom silicon-oxygen species receives 0.5004396377, so the numerical baseline is not a measure of medicinal-chemistry adequacy. Within late seed 2, a compact acylhydrazone scores 0.6018420613 while the extended repeated acylhydrazone scores 0.5758791436. The visible association is with particular aromatic attachment and heteroatom patterns; neither adding aromatic rings, nitriles, halogens nor molecular size is a universal rule.

per_task.generated_character: The high end contains recognizable amine-bearing medicinal chemistry, with more saturated carbon than the aromatic-amide and azine panels. Median size is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 produces aryl-oxypropyl piperidines and arylpiperazines with a second aromatic group, propyl substituents and halogens. The cited maximum has 28 heavy atoms, two benzene rings and a saturated piperazine ring, with an unacylated aliphatic nitrogen. Seed 1 uses alkyl-substituted indole arylpiperazines with N-benzyl substitution. Seed 2 develops hydroxyindolyl/aryl branched primary amines with ether-linked azetidine, pyrrolidine or piperidine groups; its cited leading late compounds have 29 heavy atoms and four rings. Ordinary ether formation and amine substitution make the main linkage patterns plausible, while branched stereogenic products need stereochemical control. The Parent also reached aryl-bearing cyclic amines, but had 357 amide-containing proposals versus 141 here and 153 piperazine-containing proposals versus 228 here. Its seed-2 maxima included N-hydroxyaminal-like connectivity; the current cited seed-2 maxima use primary amines instead. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.9999999801 versus 0.9961294199, 0.9999999417 versus 0.9999855105, and 0.9999998288 versus 0.9999832445.
liabilities: Alkylated, often halogenated aromatic groups linked by flexible chains to basic nitrogens raise lipophilicity, protonation and off-target questions. The neutral SMILES and low charged-text rate do not mean that the amines would remain neutral in solution.
Some late proposals grow additional aryl/amine appendages; size alone does not guarantee the same useful arrangement.
RDKit identifies unassigned tetrahedral centres in 362 of 870 accepted proposals versus 225 in the Parent. Neither panel provides explicit stereochemical notation.
missing_features: No necessary binding motif absent from the recorded maxima can be inferred: hydrophobic aromatic groups and unacylated cyclic amines are already present. Many low-scoring amide/sulfonamide structures lack that same nitrogen environment and spatial arrangement.

Defined stereochemistry is missing in the branched primary-amine family. The cited seed-2 maximum has an unassigned tetrahedral centre; the trajectories do not show which stereochemical form was intended.

The strongest seed-0 and seed-1 families offer limited alternative attachment geometries: their 58 highest-scoring proposals contain only 6 and 5 distinct Murcko cores respectively. Any chemical benefit from new geometries remains unmeasured at the observed score ceiling.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-oxypropyl piperazine reaches 0.9999999801. A similarly sized 25-heavy-atom, three-ring aryl-amide/thiadiazole molecule with a sulfonylated piperidine nitrogen scores 1.9828327576e-05. The nitro acylhydrazone scores 4.1105044112e-05. The association is with accessible unacylated amine centres and their spacing between aromatic groups, not nitrogen or ring count alone. An amine by itself is also insufficient: the late hydroxyphenethylamine scores 0.4396341729, below the branched indolyl/aryl amines near the reported ceiling. Numerous aryl F/Cl/I and substitution-position changes have essentially indistinguishable high scores. These saturated numerical values do not establish comparative binding affinity, selectivity or pharmacokinetic quality.

per_task.generated_character: The full output is broad: 735 distinct Murcko cores among 870 proposals, compared with 733 in the Parent, and a median of 23 heavy atoms and three rings. The seed-0 high end nevertheless repeatedly combines piperazine, aryl sulfonyl groups and a benzodioxole ring system, varying the second connection among sulfonamide, amide, carbamate, urea and amidine. Its cited maximum is a 27-heavy-atom bis(arylsulfonyl)piperazine with four rings, two aromatic. Both piperazine nitrogens are sulfonylated, so counting a piperazine here must not be confused with the unacylated basic-amine environment seen elsewhere. Another high example joins a fused nitrogen-containing lactam ring system to a sulfonylpiperazine and benzodioxole, with 35 heavy atoms and six rings. Seed 1 remains dispersed around benzodioxole/indole and sulfonylpiperazine chemistry; seed 2 includes aryl sulfonamides with methylpiperazine and fused lactams. Most leading amide and sulfonamide connections look synthetically conventional. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.241016 versus 0.212512, 0.192772 versus 0.204283, and 0.199800 versus 0.258869. The stronger Parent seed-2 molecule combined a benzodioxole sulfonylpiperazine with a fused aza-aromatic sulfonyl partner. The current seed-2 high end does not maintain that same assembled combination.
liabilities: Multiple sulfonyl groups and carbonyls create a substantial polar burden, while capping both piperazine nitrogens changes ionization relative to a free diamine. These consequences should not be inferred from nitrogen count alone.

One high digest member includes an unusual explicitly hydrogen-bearing sulfur centre bonded to oxo, aryl and nitrogen groups; its score of 0.2218238064 does not establish that connectivity as a stable synthetic product.
Simple acids, long-chain acyclic amines and unrelated polycyclic structures occupy the low-scoring tail despite the broad aggregate core count.
missing_features: The combined benzodioxole, aryl-sulfonyl and diamine-ring arrangement seen in the strongest examples is not consistently carried into the broad remaining output. Generating more unrelated rings has not supplied that missing co-occurrence.

Alternative fused heteroaromatic partners and polar-linker arrangements that retain the useful assembled context remain uneven across seeds. The Parent comparison shows that this chemistry was reachable, but does not establish a required target fragment.
Defined stereochemistry is absent from the saturated and bridged-ring excursions; the cited late bicyclic diketone has five unassigned tetrahedral centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonylpiperazine scores 0.2410164257, the aromatic amide/sulfonamide 0.2318094739, and the urea/sulfonamide 0.2263778191. Glycolic acid and phosphoric acid score 0.0116405049 and 0.0082655920, and the acyclic aminonitrile scores 0.0134271539. The data favor organized aromatic and polar-linker combinations over small acids or isolated amines. Ring presence is still insufficient: the final saturated bicyclic diketone scores 0.0841158231 and a methoxyphenyl bridged amine 0.1174440439, whereas the fused aryl-sulfonamide lactam scores 0.1815338686. A 35-heavy-atom fused heteroaromatic example reaches 0.2402649305, so a simple smaller-is-better reading would also be wrong. The observed gradient depends on combining aromatic decoration with the appropriate polar connections.

per_task.generated_character: The output is chemically diverse rather than a single collapsed family: 783 distinct Murcko cores among 870 accepted proposals, versus 775 in the Parent. Median size is 24 heavy atoms with three rings. Seed 1 supplies the highest cited product, a 23-heavy-atom aryl sulfonamide on a benzo-fused O,N lactam, and a similarly compact aza/thio heteroaromatic ester. Seed 0 reaches a 23-heavy-atom tertiary aniline bearing benzyl nitrile, methoxyethyl and carboxamide substituents, as well as a spiro cyclic sulfonamide carboxylic acid and a trifluoromethyl alcohol/hydroxamate. Seed 2 reaches a 21-heavy-atom brominated quinolone-like nucleoside and an amide-linked piperidine/azine structure. These differ substantially in basicity and polarity; a common target-like scaffold is not visible. Conventional functional groups coexist with demanding spiro, glycosidic and stereogenic structures. Current versus Parent maxima are 0.186297 versus 0.271145, 0.192839 versus 0.264242, and 0.128520 versus 0.326097. The Parent high end included compact guanidine-bearing, thiourea/carbonyl and fluoro/trifluoromethyl sulfonyl-amide structures; the current high end does not reproduce that exact chemistry. The Parent and current better examples nevertheless occupy broadly similar compact size ranges, so broad scaffold availability alone does not explain the difference.
liabilities: Long alkyl chains, repeated peptide-like connections and oversized densely oxygenated polycycles consume substantial chemical complexity while scoring at or near zero.

Hydroxamates, sulfoxide representations, glycosidic linkages and stereogenic spiro or branched products require individual stability, speciation and synthesis assessment; their presence alone does not make them unsuitable.
There are 332 accepted proposals with unassigned tetrahedral centres, versus 274 in the Parent, with no explicit stereochemical notation in either panel.
missing_features: A reproducible compact polar arrangement is missing from most later products: isolated successful amide, sulfonamide, ether and amine combinations are followed by oversized or differently connected products. Size control alone would not repair the equally compact low-scoring examples.

The output lacks consistent stereochemical identity where it matters structurally: the cited glycosidic compound has three unassigned tetrahedral centres, and the spiro acid and alcohol/hydroxamate each have one. No stereochemical score preference can be inferred.

The molecules do not reveal a single absent target motif. The defensible gap is context-sensitive assembly of size, ring content and polar groups, not a task-named template or indiscriminate addition of fluorine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact aryl sulfonamide/lactam scores 0.1928392260 and the tertiary-aniline carboxamide 0.1862969146. A 44-heavy-atom long-alkyl aryl hydroxamate and a 55-heavy-atom peptide-like structure score exactly 0. Across seeds, the 58 highest-scoring proposals have median heavy-atom counts 23, 22 and 22; the corresponding lowest-scoring groups have medians 38, 30 and 31. The size association is strong, but appropriate polar connectivity is also needed: the final 23-heavy-atom indolyl thioimidic structure scores 6.3468645426e-08, while a different 23-heavy-atom amino-azine scores 0.0468234245. The digest median of 0.0 is rounded; the exact median over all supplied records is 3.8150477172e-08, and only three accepted optimizer proposals score exactly zero. The late seed-2 set therefore represents continued chemically varied low-scoring output, not convergence onto the isolated compact maxima. No uniquely required fluorination pattern or basic amine can be inferred, since the leading cited sulfonamide/lactam is unfluorinated and lacks an unacylated aliphatic amine.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited compact aryl sulfonamide/lactam and tertiary-aniline carboxamide each have 23 heavy atoms and observed scores 0.1928392260 and 0.1862969146, while the 44-heavy-atom long-alkyl hydroxamate and 55-heavy-atom peptide-like product score 0. Elsewhere, a 24-heavy-atom diaryl cyanoacrylamide reaches 0.4952605565 while a 59-heavy-atom repeated indole-amide product falls to 2.7846374431e-48. Yet the compact 23-heavy-atom indolyl thioimidic example also scores only 6.3468645426e-08. Both scale and the way polar groups are connected matter.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve a useful molecular size and polar-group context while constructing new structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is to vary scaffold and attachment patterns while retaining the useful size, heteroatom environment and degree of substitution evidenced by accepted feedback. This calls for composition-sensitive growth and termination without imposing a universal desired size, fixed scaffold or objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The complete output contains hundreds of distinct Murcko cores in each panel, yet 53 of 58 high-scoring proposals in one diaryl activated-alkene seed and 57 of 58 in one acylhydrazone seed share a single core. Seven cited activated-alkene maxima retain exactly the same score after positional or amide-to-imidate changes. In contrast, broad low-scoring streams repeatedly lose the combined aromatic and polar-linker arrangement of their stronger examples.
transferable_gaps.gap: Broad ring availability does not translate into consistent exploration of alternative structures around productive chemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A transferable generator should be able both to preserve meaningful relationships between rings, linkers and polar groups and to change their topology beyond terminal substitution. The needed capability is context-preserving structural variation; core diversity or canonical novelty alone should not stand in for useful chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A cited 28-heavy-atom aryl-oxypropyl piperazine with an unacylated nitrogen scores 0.9999999801, while a 25-heavy-atom three-ring structure with sulfonylated piperidine nitrogen scores 1.9828327576e-05. Elsewhere, a bis-sulfonylpiperazine is itself a leading observed structure. Thus free amines, aromatic nitrogens, amides and sulfonamides are available, but their chemical roles are not interchangeable and there is no universal rule to add or unmask an amine.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks reliable control over the functional role of nitrogen when it changes linkages and ring attachments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: New structures need to preserve or deliberately vary nitrogen hybridization, adjacent electron-withdrawing groups and spacing from aromatic surfaces as distinct chemical features. Use each independent stream of accepted feedback to learn which arrangement transfers; do not infer ionization from formal charge notation or nitrogen count.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes aryl imidates, electrophilic cyanoacrylamides, acylhydrazones and repeated acylhydrazone extensions, plus an explicitly hydrogen-bearing hypervalent sulfur centre. Some have high observed scores, and the imidate even ties ordinary amide analogues. Their scores and successful RDKit parsing supply no synthesis or stability evidence.
transferable_gaps.gap: Valence-valid generation does not consistently distinguish conventional stable linkage patterns from reactive or unusual alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing chemical capability is to produce sensible functional-group connectivity and plausible alternative linkages while preserving useful surrounding context. Chemical feasibility should be distinguished from representation validity and high accepted score, without treating every occurrence of a legitimate reactive functional group as automatically unacceptable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre-notation rate is 0.0. Passive inspection also finds no slash/backslash double-bond geometry notation anywhere in either complete panel. The current accepted sets contain 108, 75, 362, 217 and 332 molecules with unassigned tetrahedral centres in the fixed panel order. Cited examples include a branched primary amine with one centre, a glycosidic structure with three and a bicyclic diketone with five; the activated alkenes and hydrazones also leave geometry unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator emits potentially stereogenic structures without specifying their stereochemical identity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The absent capability is to represent and preserve intentional tetrahedral and double-bond stereochemistry when generating such structures. This enables chemically defined alternatives from ordinary feedback; it does not justify assuming that a particular stereoisomer would improve an unmeasured score.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It retains a direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchange and checks stable canonical identities before admitting fresh candidates. A greedy survivor population supplies breeding parents, while all accepted observations train a fingerprint Gaussian process. The process builds a surplus pool and chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its molecular fingerprints record whether each local environment occurs, discarding how many times it occurs.
approach.novelty: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in that same posterior: use Morgan occurrence counts with count Tanimoto covariance. Repeated aromatic, carbonyl and other environments will then contribute their counts to molecular similarity instead of a single presence flag. This tests whether occurrence weighting improves prediction on the Parent's actual repeat-rich molecules. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation, molecular edits or identity admission; this changes the representation used to transfer accepted scores across their unchanged candidate pools. It does not assume that larger molecules are better or that the existing exact fingerprint ties will separate.

nodes.hypothesis: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in the inherited Gaussian-process posterior by replacing binary Morgan features with radius-two 2048-bin Morgan occurrence counts and their dot-product Tanimoto covariance.

finding_summary.headline: Occurrence counts improved prediction and mean best score, while uncertainty coverage deteriorated.
finding_summary.insights:
Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.
finding_summary.results:
Occurrence weighting changed every one of the 435 fitted pool distributions across all five tasks and three seeds. On identical accepted data, 69,570 of 69,600 pool means and marginal standard deviations differed from the binary comparator. The logged count predictions, feedback updates and correlated selections reconstructed without mismatch. Reusing the same normal draws with the binary comparator changed 2,768 of 4,350 choice positions in 434 pools; those alternative choices were not scored.

On the 4,350 molecules actually evaluated, count-posterior MSE was 0.011269 versus 0.011797 for the matched binary posterior and 0.042504 for the archive-mean baseline. Mean within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.4694 to 0.5498. Coverage deteriorated: 60.90% versus 71.36% within one latent standard deviation, and 76.92% versus 85.63% within 1.96. All 4,200 eligible next-fit probes changed; standardized uncertainty fell on every probe, while score-unit uncertainty rose on 20 because the archive scale changed. All training and pool factorizations succeeded at the first jitter in both panels.

Recorded final-best macro score rose from 0.551771 to 0.574344, a paired mean gain of 0.022573 against the declared 0.002 criterion. Child and Parent population standard deviations across seeds were 0.012317 and 0.008223; paired-delta standard deviation was 0.020520. Seed gains were +0.044871, -0.004661 and +0.027509. Mean task changes were +0.062135 for sitagliptin_mpo, +0.023333 for median_2, +0.020559 for drd2_docking, +0.009115 for deco_hop and -0.002276 for zaleplon_mpo. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. Strict improvements over each offspring’s best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350. These search outcomes include the ensuing changes in generation and feedback.
