molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold families retain amides and amines, but unusual heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven growth persist.
molecular.overall_character: Read the complete child and parent panels: every supplied task at seeds 0, 1 and 2, including all 300 trajectory records per seed. Each child task contains 870 optimizer proposals; all parse in the supplied RDKit environment. This is graph validity, not evidence of a synthetic route or useful biological activity. Passive descriptor and feature counts are derived directly from those SMILES and recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-05-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. These are predominantly branched, multi-ring molecules with abundant aromatic atoms, carbonyls, ethers, nitrogen heterocycles and halogens. Digest ring-closure hit rates range from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text hit rates from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings with a feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Ring topology is genuinely varied across the panel, but the higher-scoring portions of individual seed trajectories repeatedly elaborate a few scaffold families. Some families occupy a conventional medicinal-chemistry size range; another includes very large, repetitive heteroaromatic assemblies. Ordinary amides and basic amine centres are present, so neither rings nor basic nitrogen is globally missing. The main chemistry deficiencies are unreliable preservation of conventional heteroatom bonding, absent stereochemical specification despite newly created stereocentres, limited alternative scaffold coverage around successful motifs, and uncontrolled growth or collapse to tiny fragments. Every task has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0; neutral SMILES do not imply that its amines cannot protonate. Parent comparisons below describe recorded chemistry and scores only, without attributing changes to algorithm activation. The excerpts of best molecules and final molecules are pooled across seeds; they are not three independent endpoint summaries.

per_task.generated_character: Seeds 1 and 2 mainly produce methyl-, methoxy- and vinyl-substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 0 also reaches a compact bridged nitrogen-containing framework bearing an aryl carboxamide and an N-S substituent. The seed winners have 24, 25 and 24 heavy atoms respectively. Thus this is compact aromatic scaffold elaboration, not a search confined to fragments or lacking ring nitrogen. The ordinary aryl amides look synthetically approachable in principle; the highest-scoring N-S and N-halogen congeners are less conventional. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9644/0.9621.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-chloro amides, plus the terminal N-S attachment in the maximum, raise chemical stability and preparation questions that SMILES sanitization does not answer.
Vinyl ethers, multiple vinyl substituents and complicated bridging add potential reactivity or synthetic burden; late single-heavy-atom proposals also lose essentially all useful molecular context.
missing_features: A consistently conventional realization of the top-scoring aromatic/carboxamide envelope is not demonstrated: ordinary amides occur, but the seed maxima use N-S or N-halogen substitution. The data do not establish that any absent named pharmacophore is required.
The new stereocentre perceived in the seed-0 best graph is unspecified; comparable stereodefined alternatives are absent from the supplied proposals, and their score value is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole fluorophenyl amide scores 0.3051048083696145; the ordinary divinyl, methoxy, pyridyl amide in the digest reaches 0.4330127018922193. Its N-chloro and N-fluoro versions both score 0.4423126980074005, showing that the recorded score does not distinguish those two substitutions here. The seed-0 bridged N-S compound reaches 0.45766047024715. Tiny outputs such as C and F score 0.0, while the final carbonyl-linker-expanded amide scores 0.3057223329855419. The observed gradient favours a specific compact aromatic/carboxamide arrangement over loss of that context, without a general reward for larger size or any evidence that chemical stability improved. Recorded parent-to-child best scores, in seed order, are 0.442313 to 0.457660, 0.460926 to 0.442313, and 0.451975 to 0.448414. Parent and child remain in closely related aromatic amide or carbonyl families, with the child seed-0 maximum using a different bridged N-S structure.

per_task.generated_character: The seed panel contains distinct size regimes. Seed 0 grows repeated azaaromatic, carbonyl-containing and imine-bearing assemblies; seed 1 concentrates on an azaheteroaromatic carbonyl/O-ring core with heteroaryl ether, nitrile and heavily halogenated polyene substituents. Seed 2 instead retains a more compact benzo-fused nitrogen ring, alkoxy groups and an alkoxy-bearing aminomethyl connection to a fluorinated pyridyl ring. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 91, 46 and 31, compared with parent medians 79, 83 and 39. Growth therefore changes in different directions across seeds. Digest mean SMILES length is 94.6, maximum 266, with ring/aromatic hit rates both 0.9713. Conventional aromatic ethers and azaheterocycles coexist with crowded unsaturated appendages and unusual oxygen connectivity.
liabilities: Very large repeated aromatic assemblies and highly substituted polyenes create substantial synthetic and conformational burdens without a demonstrated reward for each extra fragment.
Halogenated alkenes lack geometric specification; seed-0 cumulated double bonds and the seed-2 O-O/O-halogen variants add chemical liabilities beyond the conventional heterocyclic cores.
missing_features: The leading seed-1 series lacks well-covered compact, ordinary substituent alternatives that preserve its useful heteroaromatic attachment context without repeated halogenated polyene growth; the smaller seed-2 family shows that extreme bulk is not universal to the higher scores.

Consistent preservation of ordinary ether connectivity is missing in part of the proposal stream: passive reading finds O-O bonds in 162 of 290 seed-2 proposals, compared with only 4 in its upper recorded-score quartile and 48 in its lower quartile. These quartiles contain 73 rows each; this is association, not an isolated peroxide effect.
The alkoxy-bearing carbon stereocentre in the compact seed-2 family is not assigned. No additional objective-required motif can be inferred from the visible score gradient alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small molecules such as C#CCl and ClCCl remain at the observed 0.5 floor; the initial cyclic dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.548381482770623. The digest seed-1 leader and its much more heavily extended brominated/chlorinated polyene congener both score exactly 0.6199818405862896, although their passive molecular weights are 624.431 and 868.744. These examples show tolerance of added bulk, not a demonstrated score benefit from that addition. Seed 2 has a substantially smaller final nitrogen-ring/aryl-ether compound at 0.6109149100540779, whereas the truncated diaryl hydrazine scores 0.5557275541795665. The apparent reward is for retaining favourable heteroaromatic connectivity and substitution context; sheer size is not consistently needed. Parent-to-child seed best scores are 0.609808 to 0.609280, 0.611413 to 0.619982, and 0.597688 to 0.616992. The first pair retains oversized heteroaromatic chemistry, while the latter pairs accompany smaller scaffold families than their parents.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules combine substituted aromatic surfaces with non-amide aliphatic amines. Seed 1 has N-propyl pyrrolidine attached to compact bridged ether/aryl or azaaryl systems; seed 2 uses saturated nitrogen rings linked to fluorinated biaryl and oxygen-containing rings. Seed 0 keeps a flexible tertiary amine between halogenated aryl regions and reaches unusual sulfur chemistry, including sulfur double-bonded to both carbon and oxygen. Seed winners contain 30, 26 and 31 heavy atoms. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9736/0.9655 and halogen hit rate is 0.9885. Basic amine centres and nonplanar saturated rings are clearly present; their exact ionization and configurations are not supplied. Some ring-amine/aryl combinations are medicinally recognizable, while the bridged structures and sulfur endpoints need much stronger synthetic justification.
liabilities: The carbon=sulfur=oxygen motif, extensive halogenation and some N-S/O-halogen edits are unconventional for routine medicinal chemistry; their high recorded scores do not establish stability or accessibility.
Crowded bridged rings and the peroxide-containing final example add stereochemical, conformational and synthetic uncertainty that graph validity does not settle.
missing_features: Stereodefined versions of the favourable ring-amine/aryl geometries are absent: the overall best graph has three perceived but unassigned tetrahedral centres. The supplied scores do not resolve which configurations or protonation states were responsible.

The seed-0 maximum does not demonstrate an ordinary, stable sulfur-linkage realization of its favourable amine/aryl context. Other seeds already show that basic nitrogen on rings can be generated, so a global lack of ring amines would be an incorrect diagnosis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact pyrrolidine/bridged-ether leader scores 0.9964552366323939; the acyclic tertiary-amine, sulfur-rich leader scores 0.9959491085611949. In contrast, the sulfonylated pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197 and simple aryl sulfonyl derivatives score 0.00024675866379847753. This associates a suitable amine/aryl arrangement with higher scores, but does not prove that an amine alone is sufficient: the initial amine-bearing hydroxamate is also low at 0.0003786988088202195. Upper versus lower score-quartile median heavy-atom counts are 31 versus 41, 30 versus 39, and 31 versus 39 across seeds, so these trajectories do not support a blanket size reward. A final peroxide-containing, heavily bridged seed-2 molecule scores 0.6566255585773542 despite retaining amines. Parent-to-child best scores are 0.979377 to 0.995949, 0.951235 to 0.996455, and 0.991404 to 0.991289. The similar third endpoint accompanies a changed nitrogen-ring/aryl topology; none of these numbers establishes experimental binding or a particular pose.

per_task.generated_character: These are mixed aromatic/aliphatic nitrogen polycycles with recurring N-methyl cyclic amide or dicarbonyl fragments, propyl substituents and aryl groups. Seed 0 forms more densely connected nitrogen/carbonyl rings, seed 1 joins two aryl regions through ether-containing and nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and seed 2 joins a quinoline region to an unsaturated nitrogen-ring/dicarbonyl system. The seed winners have 37, 33 and 30 heavy atoms. The overall best is perceived as four rings, including rings of size ten and seven, with two aromatic rings and two carbonyls; it is not a flat aromatic-only molecule. These are plausible bond patterns for specialized synthetic targets, but ring closure and stereochemical control are substantial unresolved requirements. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9851/0.9747 and halogen hit rate is only 0.1356.
liabilities: Medium-sized ring closures, linked ring junctions and N-N connectivity in leading structures complicate route design even when the individual amide and ether groups are familiar.
Some late variants introduce N-S, N-O or O-O connectivity; a dense ring system alone does not make those edits chemically equivalent to the more conventional neighbours.
missing_features: Alternative, less synthetically demanding connections of the favourable aromatic and nitrogen/dicarbonyl fragments are not well represented at the maximum: the pooled best excerpt is concentrated in close variants of the seed-1 family. This is limited chemical coverage, not proof that any particular unseen scaffold would score better.
Defined configurations for the new saturated ring junctions and substituent-bearing centres are absent. The overall leader has an unassigned tetrahedral centre, and the seed-2 endpoint has two.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic cyclic-dicarbonyl example scores 0.1678386594791329, while the connected diaryl-ether/nitrogen-dicarbonyl leader reaches 0.24321515648721753. A different connection of the same formula in the digest scores 0.23979854715495866; retaining component types does not make topology irrelevant. The seed-2 final quinoline/dicarbonyl molecule scores 0.23035161967494103, compared with 0.21717071756426068 for more decorated neighbours and 0.21094823834331713 for the sulfur-containing neighbour. Tiny C, C#C and OO proposals score 0.0. The observed high-score envelope therefore retains both aromatic regions and nitrogen/carbonyl connectivity rather than favouring isolated fragments; it does not imply that adding rings or decorations indefinitely is useful. Parent-to-child seed best scores are 0.204784 to 0.222706, 0.213610 to 0.243215, and 0.207878 to 0.230352. Both panels retain nitrogen/dicarbonyl scaffolds, while the child changes their connections and saturated ring geometry.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 supplies the whole pooled best excerpt: anisyl or related aryl groups attached to a fused nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino heterocycle, with fluorinated small nitrogen rings and frequent N-F attachments. The overall leader has 27 heavy atoms, a carbonyl and an exocyclic imino group, and includes a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 1 instead develops phenolic aryl/dicarbonyl heterocycles with fluorinated unsaturated side chains; seed 2 develops more compact phenolic aryl/carbonyl-imino analogues with fluoroalkyl substitution. These are medium-sized, aromatic and heteroatom-rich rather than large repeated assemblies. Ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9575/0.9517 and halogen hit rate is 0.8954. Passive inspection finds N-halogen bonds in 254, 155 and 125 of the 290 proposals in the respective seeds; fluorination is often directly on nitrogen, not solely on carbon.
liabilities: Repeated N-fluorination is a major distinction from ordinary carbon fluorination and raises questions of reactivity and synthetic handling. Passing SMILES perception is insufficient to establish medicinal suitability.
The four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring, nearby imino functionality and unspecified stereochemistry make the overall leader a more demanding chemical target than its moderate size suggests.
Late emissions still include very small species such as OBr, showing loss of the useful molecular context even after complex higher-scoring structures have been found.
missing_features: The maximum is not demonstrated using a fully conventional set of carbon-bound fluorine and ordinary nitrogen substituents: leading analogues repeatedly retain N-F. It remains unknown whether more ordinary bonding could preserve the observed compact fluorinated carbonyl/imino pattern at comparable scores.

The small-ring substitution creates an unassigned stereocentre in the overall leader. Stereodefined alternatives and a demonstrated less strained realization of the same spatial arrangement are missing; their score benefit cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl cyclic-dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.0020944534688323298. Compact fluorinated carbonyl/imino analogues reach 0.6510211907030741 and 0.6492585029324071 in seed 0. Neither fragmentation nor repetition helps these particular examples: F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26 and the duplicated, heavily linked heterocycle in the worst excerpt scores 5.038398954372863e-25. A final seed-2 phenolic aryl analogue scores 0.5136226132583438, whereas a different final compound with an unsaturated aliphatic ring replacing the aryl region scores 0.056329114721316687. This supports a compact fluorinated aryl/heterocycle envelope in the observed stream, without identifying which objective components or individual substitutions cause the reward. Parent-to-child best scores are 0.475978 to 0.651021, 0.575091 to 0.487006, and 0.503080 to 0.602525. The child shifts seed 0 toward the fused imino/N-F family, loses score in the distinct seed-1 family, and simplifies the highly fused parent seed-2 chemistry. The seed-0 excerpt must not be read as a uniform result across seeds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes aryl amides bearing N-F or N-Cl, nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino rings repeatedly bearing N-F, a high-scoring sulfur centre double-bonded to carbon and oxygen, and peroxide-containing ring systems. Passive full-trajectory inspection also finds 162 O-O-containing proposals in one 290-proposal stream, with fewer of those in its upper score quartile. These are observed bond patterns, not inferred synthetic failures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional functional-group bonding while it modifies otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically ordinary linkage alternatives and preserve functional-group context during edits, so accepted feedback can compare such alternatives with unusual bond arrangements. Valence checking alone cannot supply this capability, and an unusual motif should not be assumed beneficial or worthless merely because it is unusual.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive parsing confirms unassigned tetrahedral centres in compact bridged amine/aryl leaders, medium-ring carbonyl systems and fluorinated small rings; the bridged amine leader at 0.9964552366323939 has three. No optimizer trajectory uses alkene stereobond markers either.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates stereogenic graphs but does not emit defined stereochemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore valid configurations when graph edits create stereogenic atoms or geometrically distinguishable double bonds. The missing capability is configuration coverage; these trajectories do not establish a universal score benefit from adding stereochemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal stream has a median of 91 heavy atoms versus 79 in its parent, while another contracts substantially. The cited halogenated heteroaromatic leader and an extended polyene congener have molecular weights 624.431 and 868.744 but share score 0.6199818405862896. Other high-scoring streams favour smaller molecules than their own lower-scoring groups. Thus growth is chemically uneven and its benefit cannot be assumed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful scaffold retention is not coupled to reliable exploration of compact alternatives to repeated fragment growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose contractions and compact replacements that preserve successful attachment context alongside growth proposals, allowing the local accepted scores to reveal where size or repeated environments matter. A universal growth preference or universal size penalty is not supported by this panel.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring excerpts repeatedly elaborate substituted indole carboxamides, a narrow fused carbonyl/imino heterocycle family, or one connected diaryl/nitrogen-dicarbonyl family. Different seeds do discover different topologies, and topology variants sometimes differ in score, so this is limited local coverage rather than absence of ring-building capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich output does not provide broad alternative scaffold coverage around each locally successful chemical motif.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically comparable reconnections and scaffold replacements available while retaining the useful aryl, amine or carbonyl context learned from accepted molecules. Seek broader connectivity coverage without embedding a named objective or a presumed target scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest worst and final examples include single-heavy-atom C and F, tiny C#C and OO, and terminal OBr. They lie at or near the bottom of their own recorded score spans even though the same streams already contain complex higher-scoring ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still loses nearly all molecular context in a minority of late proposals.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support context-preserving repair or resampling of destructive edits, informed by the accepted molecular history. The observed gap concerns loss of useful structure, not a benchmark-specific minimum size or a claim that all small molecules are undesirable.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent performs molecular search directly in fixed-width SELFIES token frames. It keeps one real score and the original construction frame for each canonical molecule, ranks observations into a small positive group and lower-scoring negatives, and selects a positive exemplar uniformly. A fresh random coordinate order fixes values from that exemplar until every retained negative frame is excluded, then continues until at most four coordinates remain free. Uniform token draws in the resulting region supply most proposals; a broad uniform component supplies the rest. Molecular validation and novelty filtering precede evaluation, and complete-batch feedback updates the ranked records. Its observed negative exclusions were correct, but the four-coordinate limit determined every final mask, leaving the molecular neighborhoods strongly dependent on each molecule's single retained serialization.
approach.novelty: Add verified equivalent serialization views to the labeled molecular records. Each molecule receives a small, bounded bank of alternative SELFIES frames obtained through graph-preserving atom reorderings and exact molecular identity checks. Each regional classifier selects one view per labeled molecule, so the same real observations can define different token neighborhoods without receiving extra weight. Original sampled frames remain immutable score receipts. This is the lineage's first Child: its only existing implementation always classifies and samples using the one retained original frame. The new causal claim is that changing an equivalent coordinate representation changes decoded regional proposals; a paired diagnostic using the original frames will measure that effect before considering whether scores improve.

nodes.hypothesis: For each regional RACOS classifier, uniformly select one identity-verified equivalent SELFIES serialization view per scored molecular record from a bounded task-local view bank, and apply the inherited negative-exclusion, uncertainty-shrinking and uniform-sampling rules to those selected views while preserving one observation weight and the immutable original sampled-frame score receipt per molecule.

finding_summary.headline: Equivalent views changed 782 evaluated proposals; the screening mean fell
finding_summary.insights:
Equivalent construction representatives can change the molecules reached by a local token sampler. The effect comes from different fixed token values: all 1,341 paired regions fixed the same 75 coordinate locations and left four free. Alternative negative views changed when exclusion finished in 652 regions, but never added a final restriction beyond the uncertainty limit. This narrows the demonstrated contribution to the selected exemplar representation under the observed masks. Eleven alternative-view pairs still decoded to the same molecule, so token differences alone would have overstated the effect.

More novel support did not establish better search. Only 36 of 792 accepted children from alternative exemplar views beat their source, compared with 42 of 517 from original views; these conditional groups have different molecule and task support and do not isolate a score effect. The alternatives for generated records also remove an average of 17.58 non-PAD tokens, so this experiment combines atom traversal with normalization of redundant construction tokens. Coverage is uneven: 325 generated records have no admitted alternative, including 137/290 in drd2_docking and 119/290 in sitagliptin_mpo. The paired shadows have no scores, leaving both the contribution to later optimization and reliability across seeds open.

The supplied molecular assessment still finds frequent radicals, unusual charges and reactive or strained connectivity among generated molecules, including high scorers. Exact identity verification protects the already scored bank entries; it does not make their sampled offspring chemically credible or preserve useful scaffold relationships. Useful, chemically ordinary molecular neighborhoods remain unresolved despite the demonstrated representation effect.
finding_summary.results:
The equivalent views produced a measurable molecular effect. Verified alternatives were available for 1,175 of 1,500 scored records, and an alternative exemplar was selected in 808 of 1,341 regional constructions. Holding the molecular observations and sampling randomness fixed, 797 paired proposals decoded to different molecules; 782 of those changes survived filtering and received real evaluator scores. All identity, one-observation, score-attachment and batch checks passed.

Regional novelty acceptance rose from 96.24% to 97.61%, and decoded overlaps across regions fell from 48 of 1,355 raw draws to 31 of 1,341. The fraction of accepted regional children beating their exemplar rose slightly, from 67/1,304 (5.14%) to 78/1,309 (5.96%). The five-task final Top-1 mean nevertheless fell from 0.315539 to 0.289335. Parent-to-current maxima were 0.345581 to 0.366339 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.579123 to 0.571504 for deco_hop, 0.120104 to 0.028849 for drd2_docking, 0.167839 to 0.168550 for median_2, and 0.365051 to 0.311434 for sitagliptin_mpo. Both runs completed all five tasks with 300 evaluations each. This is one screening seed.

molecular.headline: Frequent rings conceal radical-rich chemistry: recognizable aryl/carbonyl scaffolds coexist with highly charged polyenes and strained rings.
molecular.overall_character: The digest and all supplied current and Parent seed-0 trajectories were read. Each covered task contains 300 observations, including 290 optimizer proposals; no tasks lack trajectories. The output ranges from tiny fragments to medium and larger multiring frameworks. Ring_closure_rate spans 0.6966 to 0.8172, but aromatic_atom_rate spans 0.0207 to 0.6: ring construction is common while intact aromatic chemistry is very uneven. These digest rates measure the presence of SMILES text features in proposed molecules, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. The recognizable families include haloaryl indole carboxamides, methoxy chromenone/pyridyl assemblies, and aryl ester/dicarbonyl frameworks. Other high-scoring families are almost entirely nonaromatic polyenes, cumulenes and unusual heteroatom rings. Charged_rate spans 0.6897 to 0.9448. Read-only RDKit reparsing of the supplied graphs confirms frequent radical centres, including in leading molecules and in some structures without formal charge. Low-coordinate boron, carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and silicon environments coexist with oxonium, unusual sulfur bonding, peroxide-like chains and strained unsaturation. Synthetic plausibility is poor overall; neutral carbonyl-rich examples and some conventional aromatic fragments provide a more credible subset. Formal graph diversity is substantial, but stronger proposals within a task repeatedly revisit related families, giving moderate useful structural diversity. Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0, establishing absent stereochemical specification rather than absence of potentially stereogenic atoms. Parent comparisons below describe observed chemistry and supplied scores; neither those comparisons nor local score associations identify an unseen target pharmacophore or establish a causal score contribution from a particular chemical feature.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly medium-sized, branched, unsaturated frameworks with haloaryl carboxamides, alongside small fragments. Mean SMILES length is 42.9 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8172, aromatic_atom_rate 0.5655 and halogen_rate 0.7552. Evaluation 30 retains a methoxyindole carboxamide linked to fluorophenyl, but carries a radical-bearing boron anion. Evaluation 268 instead combines a bromophenyl aminoacetamide with an unsaturated oxygen-containing bicyclic core and low-coordinate boron/nitrogen substituents. The intact amide and aromatic fragments are recognizable synthetic chemistry; the electronic states and reorganized unsaturated rings make the leading complete structures implausible ordinary synthetic targets. Charged_rate is 0.831.
liabilities: Low-coordinate boron anions and additional radical nitrogen/phosphorus centres. Evaluation 189 has compensating formal charges while retaining radical centres, so net neutrality does not establish credible electronic structure.
Extensively rearranged unsaturated rings, atypical sulfur substitution and unspecified stereochemistry make scaffold geometry and synthesis uncertain.
missing_features: Reliable coverage of chemically ordinary variants retaining the haloaryl-carbonyl/nitrogen architecture visible in the stronger molecules. The supplied neutral indole carboxamide shows a credible version, but the leading generated variants add radical-bearing atoms.

Controlled variation of intact heteroaromatic and amide arrangements beyond repeated ring expansion and heteroatom insertion. The equal scores of the aromatic and partly nonaromatic relatives prevent inferring a universal requirement for additional aromatic rings.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial neutral methoxyindole carboxamide at evaluation 9 scores 0.3051048083696145; the boron-anion indole at evaluation 30 scores 0.354481213984869, and its ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic relative at evaluation 174 has exactly the same score. The aminoacetamide/bromophenyl framework at evaluation 268 reaches 0.36633919598396925. Thus the visible upper tail preserves assembled aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships, while strict aromaticity alone does not explain the score. The tiny epoxide at evaluation 298 scores 0.0; the final sulfur-containing ring-reorganized aminoacetamide at evaluation 300 scores 0.2966478915460209. Parent n-e8acbddfa050 reached 0.3455806835841063 with a nitrogen/thione-rich multiring framework carrying oxonium and low-coordinate charged atoms. The current upper tail shifts toward haloaryl carboxamides and boron-bearing unsaturated cores, while unusual electronic states persist.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aromatic assemblies containing methoxy-substituted chromenone-like carbonyl heterocycles, phenyl/pyridyl regions and often nitriles. Mean SMILES length is 46.9 and maximum length 86; ring_closure_rate is 0.7793 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.5828. Hydrazinium substituents recur. Evaluation 237 incorporates an extended unsaturated ring bridge, imidate-like connectivity and an O-N substituent. Evaluation 199 combines a reorganized lactone/oxonium ring system with a charged O-O-O chain. The aromatic and carbonyl components are recognizable, but the elaborate cyclizations and reactive decorations make the overall synthetic plausibility questionable to poor. Charged_rate is 0.8276.
liabilities: Peroxide-like O-O chains, multiply charged oxygen environments and the O-Br bond in the final small acyl hypobromite at evaluation 299.

Ring-contracted lactone connectivity, extended unsaturated bridges and recurrent N-N/N-O functionality require specific stability and synthetic justification. The leading evaluation 237 is closed-shell on reparsing, but that does not establish an accessible synthetic route.
missing_features: Broader stable decoration chemistry around the aromatic/polar frameworks. The current upper tail repeatedly uses hydrazinium, aminooxy or oxonium/oxygen-chain functionality, while the Parent contained a relatively strong neutral aryl-aminal example.

Coherent alternatives that retain useful aryl/carbonyl relationships without requiring highly rearranged lactone rings or long unsaturated cyclization bridges. Exact hidden decoration requirements cannot be inferred from these trajectories.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy chromenone/biaryl nitrile at evaluation 8 scores 0.5418375031378128; the pyridyl-nitrile/hydrazinium derivative at evaluation 37 scores 0.5643691820162409. The oxonium/methylthio-containing evaluation 249 receives the same 0.5643691820162409, despite its additional oxonium centre and altered substituents. The ring-bridged evaluation 237 scores 0.5715043852298755 and the charged oxygen-chain relative at evaluation 199 scores 0.5684258279147134. Acetylene at evaluation 246 scores 0.5. The final extensively rearranged, nonaromatic polycycle at evaluation 300 scores 0.507630410654828. The observed preference is for assembled aromatic/polar architectures over tiny or strongly disrupted structures; the score does not show that reactive oxygen or hydrazine functionality is necessary. The Parent upper tail instead emphasized indole amidine/carboxamide and diaryl cyclic-aminal families: its maximum was 0.5791225581141548 and a neutral diaryl hydroxyaminal scored 0.5766980825479363. The current maximum is associated with a different, still chemically problematic aromatic family.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists of relatively large nonaromatic polyenes/cumulenes, branched chains and large unsaturated rings. Mean SMILES length is 60.7 and maximum length 109. Ring_closure_rate is 0.6966, but aromatic_atom_rate is only 0.0207; charged_rate is 0.9448 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.6207. The best molecule, evaluation 277, is acyclic. Evaluation 293 closes a long heteroatom-bearing unsaturated chain into a large ring. Both contain repeated carbon cations, boron anions, low-coordinate phosphorus, unusual sulfur multiple bonds and oxonium environments. Reparsing confirms multiple radical centres in these leading graphs. They express extensive formal unsaturation and heteroatom diversity with very little conventional medicinal scaffold chemistry, making them implausible ordinary isolable compounds.
liabilities: Numerous radical centres and low-coordinate charged atoms, including repeated carbon cations, boron anions and atypical sulfur/phosphorus multiple bonds within individual molecules.

Long cumulated/conjugated sequences and highly unsaturated macrocyclic or bridged connectivity with unspecified geometry. A ring-closure digit here supplies little evidence for a stable, useful three-dimensional scaffold.
missing_features: Chemically credible closed-shell realizations of the larger carbon frameworks and polar functionality represented in the current upper tail. Its apparent size/architecture preference is realized through highly unusual electronic states.

Coverage of intact aryl-containing, constrained polar architectures is greatly reduced relative to the Parent upper tail. The low-scoring aromatic and tertiary-amine examples show that neither adding a generic aromatic ring nor adding an amine is an evidence-backed solution by itself.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The long acyclic evaluation 277 scores 0.028848761971118526 and the large-ring relative at evaluation 293 scores 0.02884865939301175. The similarly elaborate final evaluation 296 scores 0.02884463593273818. A much shorter boron/nitrogen/oxygen ionic fragment at evaluation 212 scores 0.0020518739328129186; the final short brominated oxonium ether at evaluation 295 scores 0.004062928989281451. Within this trajectory, fuller nonaromatic carbon/heteroatom frameworks generally occupy the upper tail, with little separation among the largest relatives. Simple aromatic presence is insufficient: the biphenyl nitrile/alkoxide at evaluation 16 scores 0.0013501216598358666, and the initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate with a saturated tertiary amine at evaluation 6 scores 0.0003786988088202195. The Parent maximum, 0.12010438063540518, came from a halogenated aryl-containing polycycle with its own unusual sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. The current maximum accompanies near-loss of aromatic frameworks and growth of nonaromatic chains/large rings; this comparison does not isolate why the scores differ.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules are medium-to-large aryl ethyl-ester/dicarbonyl frameworks with N-methyl carbonyl or urea-like regions, phenol/ether substituents and substantial ring rearrangement. Mean SMILES length is 48.7 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.8034 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6. Evaluation 243 is a neutral aryl-ester macrocycle joining the carbonyl/nitrogen region through an N-O-methylene-O linkage. Evaluations 282 and 298 are also neutral and closed-shell, retaining aryl and dicarbonyl motifs in cross-conjugated or ring-expanded arrangements. These are more recognizable synthetic targets than much of the remaining output, although their cyclizations and reactive linkages remain demanding. Charged_rate is 0.6897; uncharged phosphorus-containing relatives also carry radicals on reparsing.
liabilities: N-O/acetal-like linkage in the leading macrocycle and extensive cross-conjugation or ring expansion in nearby neutral structures; chemical stability and synthetic accessibility are unestablished.

Phosphorus/silicon insertions, radicals and charged replacements elsewhere in the same families. Evaluation 53 lacks formal charge but contains a radical-bearing phosphorus environment, illustrating an electronic-state problem that charge counting alone misses.
missing_features: More controlled, stable variations of the aromatic/ester/carbonyl arrangement supported by the stronger molecules. Current high-scoring neutral examples exist, but often reach new topology through extended cyclization or N-O connectivity.

Broader development of distinct intact aromatic amide-rich families, exemplified by the relatively strong initial amide/hydroxamate, alongside the dominant ester/dicarbonyl family. The observations do not reveal an unseen reference structure.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/fused dicarbonyl at evaluation 7 scores 0.1678386594791329. The generated macrocycle at evaluation 243 scores 0.16854996561581048; evaluations 282 and 298 score 0.16695175953014704 and 0.1651413292730383. Adding the sulfur-oxygen substituent in the related evaluation 271 gives 0.160745220268056. The late short brominated ether at evaluation 299 scores 0.020160580116942894, while the small imidate-like anion at evaluation 292 scores 0.0. The gradient supports retention of assembled aromatic/ester/carbonyl relationships over fragments; substantial rearrangements within that family remain close in score. The chemically distinct initial aromatic amide/hydroxamate at evaluation 6 also scores 0.1569767171139282. The Parent retained the same initial maximum of 0.1678386594791329, with its best generated annulated dicarbonyl relative at 0.16526725762745997. The current leading chemistry remains centered on the same ester/dicarbonyl family while exploring new neutral ring topologies.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger output comprises medium-sized, mostly nonaromatic fluorinated amino/polyene frameworks, unusual boron/phosphorus rings, and imine-containing polycycles with silicon or selenium. Mean SMILES length is 44.4 and maximum length 84; ring_closure_rate is 0.7828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.2138, charged_rate 0.9241 and cumulated_double_bond_rate 0.4483. Evaluation 298 links an amino-substituted unsaturated ring to a methoxy-substituted small cyclic alkyne bearing adjacent carbon anions, and adds a boron/sulfur/iodine appendage. Evaluation 210 combines fluorophosphorus and boron/oxygen ring chemistry with carbon anions; evaluation 223 is a long acyclic unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen/sulfur chain. These upper-tail structures contain radicals and unusual ionic states. The cyclic alkyne geometry and heteroatom connectivity make their synthetic plausibility especially poor.
liabilities: Adjacent radical-bearing carbon anions, nitrogen anions, unusual boron/sulfur/iodine connectivity and low-coordinate phosphorus, silicon or selenium environments in stronger molecules.
A highly strained small cyclic alkyne in the leading family, extended cumulenes/polyenes in other strong members, and absent stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Stable closed-shell versions of the medium-sized fluorinated, nitrogen-bearing chain/ring architectures represented in the upper tail, with controlled ionization and feasible bond geometry.

Chemically ordinary amine/ether and related polar substitutions that can vary those architectures without carbon-anion/radical arrays, cyclic alkynes or low-coordinate heteroatoms. Their score effect remains unmeasured; the data do not justify prescribing a missing aromatic pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Evaluation 298 scores 0.31143387897841074. Its hydroxyl-bearing relative at evaluation 187 scores 0.25352114095863515: replacing that oxygen substituent with the nitrogen-anion environment changes the score locally, while introducing additional electronic-state concerns. The distinct ring-containing evaluation 210 scores 0.30182012887455895; the acyclic evaluation 223 scores 0.28798101896372785 and its cyclized relative at evaluation 109 scores 0.26731656125719533. Rings and aromaticity therefore cannot be treated as universal requirements for the visible high-score region. The related final cyclic-alkyne framework at evaluation 296 scores only 3.830424901142501e-06, and the heteroatom-dense charged chain at evaluation 20 scores 4.0773933311719747e-53. The observed median is 6.8e-05. The score is sensitive to the particular assembled carbon/heteroatom arrangement; size and charge density alone do not explain it. The Parent maximum was 0.36505100258606615 in another radical-rich fluorinated unsaturated nitrogen/oxygen/phosphorus family. The current upper tail uses different ring and amino motifs without establishing more credible chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied proposal sets have charged_rate from 0.6897 to 0.9448. Reparsing the trajectory graphs confirms radical centres in leading boron-substituted aryl carboxamides, carbon-anion amino frameworks and phosphorus/sulfur polyenes. Some formally uncharged phosphorus-containing dicarbonyl relatives also contain radicals. Neutral closed-shell aryl/carbonyl examples are present in strong score regions, demonstrating useful conventional electronic-state coverage that is inconsistently maintained.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically credible electronic states when varying polar and ionizable functionality.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make closed-shell polar structures and chemically ordinary ionization states routinely accessible through joint control of bond patterns, valence, radical state and protonation. Account for compensating charges and neutral radicals as well as net charge. Let observed feedback determine which polar arrangements matter.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading digest molecules include small cyclic alkynes, charged oxygen chains, reorganized lactone rings and long cumulene-rich loops. A stronger neutral macrocycle retains an N-O-methylene-O linkage, while a methoxy-bearing aromatic molecule and its oxonium/methylthio variant have identical scores. Frequent ring closures therefore coexist with chemically strained or reactive architectures, and their presence does not show that those liabilities are needed for the score.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent functional-group stability and feasible ring geometry even when a graph parses successfully.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide stable, ordinary substitution and ring-construction options that maintain complete functional groups and feasible unsaturation. Represent ring strain and labile bond combinations alongside local valence so that changing a substituent need not create a cyclic alkyne, peroxide chain or unsupported heteroatom multiple bond.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring excerpts repeatedly retain assembled aryl/carboxamide or aryl/ester/dicarbonyl motifs, whereas low-score and final excerpts include tiny fragments or substantially disrupted variants. One current trajectory has aromatic_atom_rate 0.0207 despite ring_closure_rate 0.6966; its upper tail consists of nonaromatic chains and large loops, while the Parent upper tail retained aryl polycycles. A different high-score family includes strong acyclic members, showing that the gap concerns coherent arrangements supported by feedback rather than ring presence alone.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently preserves useful scaffold and linker relationships while exploring new molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support coherent substitution and attachment changes that preserve the ring edges and complete linker/functional-group patterns of useful observed structures. Keep distinct intact scaffold families accessible, with preservation and diversification guided by current molecular feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Stronger ring-containing examples are dominated by unsaturated, ring-expanded or unusually charged architectures. Ordinary saturated nitrogen rings occur in the supplied initial chemistry, but the leading generated structures often express nitrogen functionality through hydrazinium, imines, radical anions or heteroatom-rich unsaturated loops. This identifies a coverage gap; the visible scores do not establish a universal benefit from saturation, a basic amine or stereochemical specification.
transferable_gaps.gap: Conventional saturated heterocycle and stereochemically specified structure coverage is weak among the stronger generated molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible saturated and partly saturated heterocycles, controlled amine ionization and explicitly specified stereochemical alternatives available as general construction choices. Preserve their bond geometry and identity through variation, and use task-local feedback to determine where that chemistry is useful.

nodes.method_name: RACOS: negative-exclusion sampling of de novo SELFIES regions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is RACOS, selected before locating the primary source. Its categorical form chooses a positively labeled exemplar, randomly fixes coordinates to that exemplar until negative examples are excluded, further restricts the number of free coordinates, and samples the resulting region; a broader uniform component preserves exploration. Each proposal can use a newly randomized classifier. These are the mechanisms described by Yu, Qian and Hu in [Derivative-Free Optimization via Classification](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/10289/10148). My molecular adaptation applies this process directly to bounded categorical SELFIES frames, with removable padding that permits changes in molecular length. Preparation extracts only a construction-token alphabet from the permitted unlabeled corpus. There is no trained molecular encoder or decoder. Initial labeled molecules become exemplars only after encoding and decoding reproduce their canonical identity. For generated molecules, retain the actual sampled frame, its decoded canonical molecule, and the score actually returned for that molecule. Rank the current objective's observed molecules into a high-score positive group and a lower-score negative group; use these labels to construct exclusion regions. Free token positions are newly sampled and decoded into complete molecules, checked, canonicalized, and deduplicated. Rebuild a region or use the broad generation component when a region cannot provide a fresh molecule. These are online constructions from token primitives, not retrieval or enumeration of complete molecules. After each announced batch receives real feedback, refresh the labeled sets and incumbent; all pending proposals use only previously observed scores. Each objective starts with clean task-specific state and follows the protocol's supplied batch and resource limits. The hypothesis is that explicitly excluding observed poor token configurations will concentrate new molecular proposals around combinations that improve the incumbent with few labels. Success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Region exclusion, validity, or classification accuracy alone cannot establish that hypothesis. Positional token restrictions may have weak structural meaning, and multiple frames can decode to the same molecule; exact representation checks address score provenance but do not establish useful search geometry.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule, chooses a graph operator from fixed weights and makes one concrete local edit. It sanitizes and normalizes candidates, rejects duplicates, applies inverse-motif tabu memory and directly evaluates a full batch. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current state even after a worsening move, and a separate archive retains the best result. Accepted scores already identify each neighbor's generating operator and source, but none of that feedback changes future operator probabilities.
approach.novelty: Reweight the existing operators by their smoothed historical fraction of accepted neighbors that strictly beat their own source molecule. Each accepted neighbor credits exactly one generating operator. The first batch keeps the original mixture; later batches give relatively more probability to operators with higher observed success fractions while every operator keeps positive probability. Unlike the earlier breeding-parent experiment, credit belongs to a fixed set of edit types rather than changing molecular parents, and it compares with the actual source of each edit rather than a global incumbent. No graph edit, chemistry gate, tabu rule or winner rule is added.

nodes.hypothesis: Reweight the Parent's fixed graph-operator mixture at each suggestion boundary by each operator's smoothed accepted source-improvement fraction, using one generating operator per accepted neighbor and retaining positive probability for every unchanged operator.

finding_summary.headline: Operator feedback changed evaluated neighborhoods but produced smaller gains and a lower panel score
finding_summary.insights: Unique credit to a fixed edit operator did not remove the failure seen in the earlier breeding-parent experiment: historical success weighting increased progress-event frequency while reducing average gains and final archive value. The effect is especially clear for sitagliptin, where source improvements rose from 109 to 116 while their mean size fell from 0.044884 to 0.029538 and all three final scores declined. Credit conditions on accepted outputs also leave generation costs invisible: bond changes consumed 630 invalid attempts, and overall emission yield fell from 82.31% to 78.56%. Historical counts pool changing source graphs and tabu admission states, so their enrichment is an allocation result rather than a calibrated prediction of future improvement. Distinguishing improvement magnitude, archive progress and generation yield is now a concrete next question; this experiment does not establish which would fix the loss. The molecular assessment still finds sulfur-rich cages, reactive attachments and unresolved stereochemistry. Those persistent liabilities explain why more local-score successes cannot be read as better chemical feasibility.
finding_summary.results: The allocation change reached the evaluated search: 2,250 operator draws differed from the fixed mixture on the same random state, producing 1,594 accepted neighbors and 181 selected next states. All 435 batch allocations and 4,200 consumed feedback records matched the prescribed credit rule; first batches and all original graph, identity, winner and tabu rules were preserved. On each actual credit state, weighting raised the expected smoothed historical success fraction from an average 0.193425 to 0.231490. Accepted strict source improvements increased from 462 to 471 out of 4,350 neighbors, but their mean size fell from 0.024939 to 0.021552. Archive-improvement events fell from 238 to 230, and generation needed 5,537 attempts instead of 5,285. All sessions completed. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.520918 to 0.498734, a paired loss of 0.022184 against the required gain of 0.002. Seed deltas were +0.020623, -0.027981 and -0.059192. Zaleplon improved by 0.014340 in mean score; decoration hopping, DRD2, median similarity and sitagliptin fell by 0.000898, 0.014919, 0.001324 and 0.108118 respectively.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic scaffolds drift into sulfur cages, reactive halogen attachments, and undefined stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The optimizer produced medium to large, highly branched molecules with abundant aromatic, fused, bridged, and partially saturated rings. Every task has a ring_closure_rate of 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate ranges from 0.6115 to 1.0. These are incidences of SMILES text patterns across molecules, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 44.8 to 71.6 characters, which describes representation length rather than molecular weight. Amides, ketones, amines, phenols, ethers, and heteroaromatics coexist with chlorinated or brominated side chains, heteroatom-bound halogens, N-O/N-N linkages, and conspicuous multiply bonded sulfur. The most extreme products are densely cross-linked sulfur/nitrogen cages; some compact heteroaromatic amides remain much closer to ordinary medicinal chemistry. Structural diversity is moderate across the observed trajectories, but leading excerpts often consist of close variants of one seed-specific family. Both charged_rate and stereocentre_rate are 0.0 throughout; neutral notation does not imply that the amines cannot protonate. Parent n-9f7c7ec50039 already produced anomalous sulfur bonding, reactive attachments, and unspecified ring-junction stereochemistry. The child retains these liabilities, with different families dominating different seeds. Synthetic plausibility is questionable overall and particularly poor for the sulfur cages. The supplied structures and scores do not establish isolability, conformational feasibility, or experimental biological activity. All supplied child and Parent trajectory files were read. All five tasks are covered. Digest final_molecules are the tail of seed 2, not the best-so-far structures or the endpoints of every seed; comparisons below distinguish those cases. Scores in the prose are rounded from the recorded values.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger seed-0 molecules are relatively compact aza-fused or bridged unsaturated ring systems bearing an N-methyl-N-phenyl carboxamide, with hydroxymethyl, hydroxymethylamino, thioether, or chlorohydrin-like substituents. The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide is recognizable medicinal chemistry. A hydroxymethyl aza-fused analogue also looks more synthetically credible than most of the later sulfur networks, although its fused unsaturation still needs structural assessment. The low-scoring excerpts instead include expanded unsaturated rings, imidate/oxime-ether-like linkages, thioethers, and lost or rearranged amide connectivity. The seed-2 tail is a multiply bridged sulfur/nitrogen framework attached through a ketone to an unsaturated carbocyclic group. The proposal aromatic_atom_rate is 0.8563 and halogen_rate is 0.6322; this is a ring-rich series with substantial aromatic retention, not a collection of simple chains.
liabilities: The high-scoring series includes carbon bearing both hydroxyl and chlorine, hydroxymethylamino substituents, and a small N-C-O ring; their stability and preparative accessibility are much less secure than those of the underlying amide and aromatic groups.

Later molecules accumulate unusual sulfur valence and constrained unsaturated ring junctions; their lower scores do not make these products chemically representative alternatives to the compact aza-anilides.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl/anilide arrangement seen in the stronger examples: many weaker and late structures no longer retain it. Chemically ordinary variants of that arrangement are underrepresented among the leading excerpts compared with chlorohydrin-like appendages and extra bridges.

Defined relative configurations at newly saturated fused or bridged junctions are absent. The records do not show whether stereochemical alternatives would improve the objective, and they do not identify a unique missing target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.305105, the relatively conventional hydroxymethyl aza-fused N-methylanilide 0.452052, and the bridged hydroxymethylamino variant 0.469707. The chlorohydrin-like thioether variant is almost tied at 0.469497. By comparison, the expanded-ring imidate/oxime-ether-like molecule scores 0.003733 and the sulfur-rich seed-2 final proposal 0.241011. Within these records, compact heteroaromatic/carbonyl-to-anilide organization is associated with better scores than disrupted, expanded heteroatom-rich linkages; neither chlorination nor extra sulfur is established as necessary. For seed 0, the Parent best was 0.396663 in a sulfur-containing partially unsaturated carbonyl-linked heterocycle, whereas the child best is the compact bridged aza-anilide. This is a change in the observed chemical family, not evidence that every seed became chemically cleaner.

per_task.generated_character: The products are large, heavily decorated heteroaromatic and partially saturated polycycles. Early molecules retain an aryl ester/phenol and an N-substituted fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. The leading seed-1 family contains carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, a fluorinated unsaturated amino connector, an N-O-containing ring, an aminal-like junction, and a lactone-containing ring system attached to a brominated aromatic ring. Chloromethyl groups and chloroalkyl substituents on an arylamine add potentially reactive side chains. The seed-2 tail instead carries an extended fused aza-aromatic framework and a chlorinated hydrazine-like N-N substituent. Aromatic and ring-closure text is present in every optimizer proposal, while halogen_rate is 0.7759. Familiar fragments are present, but the complete leading architectures have questionable synthetic plausibility.
liabilities: Chloromethyl and chloroalkyl arylamine substituents introduce reactive carbon-halogen sites; they should not be conflated with comparatively conventional aromatic carbon-halogen substitution.

The leading frameworks combine N-O bonding, crowded aminal-like centers, thiocarbonyl functionality, and unusual sulfur coordination. The tail additionally contains an N-Cl bond on an N-N chain. Neutral, parseable graph notation does not establish that these combinations are stable or makeable.
Saturated stereogenic junctions and unsaturated linker geometry are not explicitly resolved in the quoted structures.
missing_features: Leading examples offer little diversity of chemically ordinary alternative cores retaining the carbonyl/heteroatom and aryl-decoration arrangement. Most are close edits of the same unusual fused framework.

Clean analogues that separate decoration placement from reactive attachment chemistry are missing from the leading evidence. The tied sulfur/carbon pair shows that at least one unusual sulfur feature can vary without changing the observed score; it does not establish what an unseen ideal scaffold should be.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester/phenol fused dicarbonyl compound scores 0.548381, and an early ring-rearranged sulfur-containing analogue scores 0.525114. The best decorated seed-1 family reaches 0.613099. A matched pair that changes the exocyclic-methylene-bearing ring atom from sulfur to carbon has exactly the same recorded score, 0.61309945665013; the local sulfur feature therefore has no demonstrated advantage in that pair. The observations associate gains with a reorganized, elaborated heterocycle/aryl decoration pattern, but they do not isolate a necessary bond arrangement or show that reactive additions cause the gains. The Parent likewise produced elaborated carbonyl/thiocarbonyl heterocycles with unusual sulfur and halogen attachments; its seed-1 best was 0.590648, while the child seed-1 best is 0.613099. The higher observed score accompanies a different elaborate framework without resolving its chemical liabilities.

per_task.generated_character: The trajectories move from a large aryl-rich carboxylic-acid/carboxamide/sulfonamide molecule toward halogenated aromatic groups combined with nonacylated aliphatic amines and sulfur-rich linkers or polycycles. The leading seed-0 structures contain intertwined nitrogen rings, arylthio substituents, sulfur-oxygen or sulfur-imine groups, and an explicit sulfur-sulfur triple bond within a ring. A high-scoring seed-1 molecule is more extended: a tertiary amine connects a phenyl-substituted aza-aromatic group to a sulfur-containing ring and chlorinated/bromomethyl aromatic fragment. The seed-2 tail has aliphatic amines, halogenated aromatics, an N-N heteroaromatic unit, and multiply bonded sulfur. All proposals contain ring-closure, aromatic, and halogen text. Although the amine/aryl fragments are familiar, the leading complete structures have poor apparent synthetic plausibility because of the sulfur bonding and ring geometry.
liabilities: The explicit ring-embedded S#[SH] linkage and other multiply bonded, hydrogen-bearing sulfur centers are severe chemical plausibility problems that a large objective value does not resolve.

Other leading examples contain sulfur-bromine or sulfur-chlorine attachment, bromomethyl electrophiles, and lipophilic halogenated aromatic surfaces. These accompany, rather than validate, the amine-containing motifs.
Crowded polycycles with unspecified stereochemistry make the intended three-dimensional arrangement ambiguous; these scores alone are not evidence of affinity or a feasible binding conformation.
missing_features: A clean series combining nonacylated amines and aromatic surfaces through ordinary bonds and physically credible ring conformations is missing among the leading excerpts. Basic amines themselves are already present; their useful spatial arrangement remains entangled with abnormal sulfur chemistry.

Stereochemical resolution of the saturated ring junctions and substituted side chains is absent. Formal-charge variants are also absent from the emitted SMILES, but this does not reveal how the evaluator treats protonation and does not prove that charged candidates would score better.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial acid/carboxamide/sulfonamide compound scores 0.019041, and its quoted low-scoring aryl-dechlorinated analogue 0.007468. The amine-rich sulfur cage reaches 0.980666, and the extended tertiary-amine/aromatic example reaches 0.967103. The quoted seed-2 secondary-amine/sulfur-imine tail example scores 0.661635. Removal or rearrangement of the acid and acylated nitrogen region, together with accessible nonacylated amines and aromatic surfaces, accompanies the gains; these changes are confounded with sulfur and topology changes. An initial molecule already containing a tertiary cyclic amine scores only 0.000379, so the mere presence of a basic nitrogen is insufficient. The sulfur-sulfur triple bond has no demonstrated physical benefit from these records. Parent seed 0 also reached a high score, 0.885624, with amines and unusual sulfur linkages. The child seed-0 maximum is higher while introducing an even more conspicuous sulfur-triple-bond ring liability.

per_task.generated_character: These are medium to large aryl-rich heterocycles with alkyl substituents, tertiary amines, carbonyls, and progressively rearranged fused or bridged rings. The leading seed-2 family retains phenyl and N-aryl pyrrole-like surfaces attached to a cyclic amino-ketone and an N-N-O-containing ring tether. The strongest quoted members carry aryl O-Br or O-F groups; closely related phenols are also present. These oxygen-halogen bonds are hypohalite-type attachments, not aryl bromide or aryl fluoride substitution. Lower-scoring examples often open the cyclic polar region into amide/urea/hydrazide-containing appendages while retaining aromatic rings. Ring and aromatic text occur in every proposal, but halogen_rate is only 0.1828. This family has more familiar carbonyl/amine chemistry than the dense sulfur cages elsewhere, yet its N-N-O bridges and O-halogen functionality keep overall synthetic plausibility questionable.
liabilities: O-Br and O-F bonds are reactive attachment chemistry and are not interchangeable with conventional carbon-bound medicinal halogens.

N-N-O tethers, medium-ring amino-ketones, and additional fused junctions add stability, stereochemical, and synthetic-route questions. The seed-2 tail retains this unusual tether while some proposals disrupt an aromatic ring into an unsaturated nitrogen-containing ring.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary scaffold alternatives preserving the aryl surfaces and cyclic amine/carbonyl arrangement without the N-N-O tether are not established by the leading excerpts; the best molecules mostly revisit one decorated scaffold.

Independent variation of polar-group placement and ring topology in stable analogues is underrepresented. The phenol example is already encouraging as a comparatively ordinary oxygen substituent, but the records do not identify an exact missing reference scaffold or demonstrate a need for O-halogen bonds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl ester fused dicarbonyl compound scores 0.167839, compared with 0.124680 for the quoted opened polar-chain derivative and 0.211256 for the alkylated, cyclic amino-ketone O-Br lead. An otherwise matched phenol analogue scores 0.205785, so most of that observed score is retained without the O-Br bond. Another matched O-Br/O-F pair shares exactly the score 0.20974563597484144. These contrasts favor retention and placement of the aromatic surfaces and cyclic polar region over the opened-chain examples; they give little chemical justification for retaining reactive oxygen-halogen substituents. Parent seed 2 also favored an aryl-rich bridged carbonyl/amine framework, with a best score of 0.201856. The child reaches 0.211256 with a different N-N-O-tethered framework, while both Parent and child still show reactive or unusual heteroatom attachments.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules are highly cross-linked sulfur/nitrogen cages with little or no lowercase aromatic notation in the leading excerpts. They combine cyclic cumulated double bonds, numerous hydrogen-bearing multiply bonded sulfur centers, sulfur-imine and sulfur-oxygen groups, imines, and residual carbonyl functionality. The best seed-0 structure also carries a fluorinated small carbocyclic ring and a pendant thiol. The seed-2 final structure is another dense sulfur/nitrogen cage and contains no halogen. The full proposal set still has aromatic_atom_rate 0.6115, but cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.2931 and stereocentre_rate is 0.0. Thus the leading nonaromatic cages are part of a broader trajectory that began with ordinary aryl-rich dicarbonyl heterocycles. These are the least synthetically credible leading architectures in this report: high connectivity and unusual sulfur valence overwhelm the familiar individual carbonyl and nitrogen groups.
liabilities: Constrained cyclic cumulated double bonds, repeated multiply bonded sulfur bearing hydrogen, and densely fused small rings create serious geometric and chemical-stability concerns.
Sulfur-oxygen/nitrogen motifs are embedded in unusually coordinated cage frameworks, rather than appearing simply as isolated conventional sulfoxides or sulfonamides.

New stereogenic junctions remain unspecified. The top fluorinated structure and the halogen-free final cage should not be treated as ordinary makeable medicinal scaffolds solely because they received higher objective values.
missing_features: Conventional compact nitrogen-containing ring systems reproducing the broad polar-group arrangement without abnormal sulfur bonding are absent from the leading evidence. Because many features change together, these trajectories cannot identify a required unseen target scaffold.

Physically interpretable saturated ring junctions with defined stereochemistry are missing. The leading examples do not establish whether an ordinary saturated scaffold could supply the apparent compactness and heteroatom arrangement without cyclic cumulenes and densely cross-linked sulfur.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-rich fused dicarbonyl compound scores 0.002094; the quoted early expanded derivative scores 7.590555e-10. The fluorinated sulfur cage reaches 0.439823 and the halogen-free seed-2 final cage 0.399238. Gains therefore accompany major changes in aromaticity, compactness, heteroatom arrangement, and ring connectivity, rather than retention of the initial aryl ester topology. They do not prove that a particular sulfur valence, a fluorine atom, or a strained cyclic cumulene is independently beneficial. The quoted lower-scoring sulfur-rich structure at 1.633094e-08 also shows that sulfur enrichment alone is insufficient. Parent trajectories already culminated in dense sulfur cages. Its seed-0 best was 0.481186 versus 0.439823 here; the child shows the same central chemical liability without a new conventional scaffold family explaining the score behavior.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Leading cited molecules contain a ring-embedded sulfur-sulfur triple bond, repeated multiply bonded sulfur bearing hydrogen, and dense sulfur/nitrogen cages. Familiar thioethers and sulfur-oxygen groups also occur, so the defect is the bonding environment rather than the mere presence of sulfur. The Parent shows related liabilities.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably distinguish conventional sulfur chemistry from unusual multiply bonded, hydrogen-bearing sulfur networks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-independent chemical vocabulary or admissibility rule could distinguish ordinary sulfur environments from unsupported coordination and multiple-bond patterns. It should retain conventional sulfur chemistry and test the changed output through the same observed-score interface; these records do not establish that removing sulfur wholesale would help.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited leading and tail molecules include O-Br, O-F, N-Cl, S-Cl, and S-Br attachments as well as chloromethyl, bromomethyl, and chloroalkyl amines. Ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens are present too. A matched O-Br/O-F pair is tied, and a corresponding phenol retains a nearby score, so the reactive attachments are not chemically justified by a unique observed advantage.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically ordinary attachment sites when introducing halogens.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal rule could condition halogen placement on the attachment atom and its functional-group environment, distinguishing ordinary carbon substitution from reactive oxygen-, nitrogen-, or sulfur-halogen bonds and activated alkyl sites. This would test a chemical capability rather than encode an objective-specific answer.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task has ring_closure_rate 1.0, yet the cited products include a sulfur-triple-bond ring, cyclic cumulated unsaturation, an N-C-O small ring, and densely cross-linked unsaturated cages. In one proposal set cumulated_double_bond_rate reaches 0.2931. Ring abundance therefore coexists with conspicuous geometric liabilities.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring generation lacks evidence of control over strain and realizable three-dimensional geometry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-independent ring proposal or feasibility criterion could account for multiple-bond geometry, small-ring heteroatom environments, and bridge compatibility. Ordinary fused and saturated rings should remain accessible; ring count or text validity alone cannot establish physical plausibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading excerpts repeatedly revisit one aza-anilide, decorated carbonyl heterocycle, amino-aromatic framework, or bridged amino-ketone family. Lower-scoring cited molecules often disrupt an amide, aromatic surface, or cyclic polar region while acquiring unusual linkages. Some cleaner hydroxymethyl and phenol analogues already retain substantial scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically coherent alternative scaffolds are underrepresented relative to closely edited, increasingly unusual ring frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic chemical move vocabulary could preserve recognizable functional groups while exchanging complete substituents, linkers, or feasible ring units. The missing capability is access to ordinary scaffold alternatives with controlled polar-group placement, not addition of a fixed target pharmacophore or a guarantee that every scaffold change will improve the score.

transferable_gaps.evidence: stereocentre_rate is 0.0 in every task digest despite cited molecules containing saturated fused or bridged junctions, crowded aminal-like centers, substituted amine side chains, and fluorinated small rings. This is absence of explicit stereochemical representation, not evidence that the molecular graphs are all achiral.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not specify stereochemistry for newly formed saturated junctions and substituted centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator could retain or assign chemically feasible stereochemistry when creating stereogenic centers or ring junctions, using the same task-agnostic feedback channel. The current observations cannot measure a stereochemical score benefit because the corresponding alternatives were not emitted.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
