approach.method_basis: Particle swarm optimization runs a population of points that each remember where they have been. A particle keeps a position, a velocity, and the best position it has personally found, and each step its velocity is pulled by inertia toward its own past direction, by a stochastic attraction to its personal best, and by another to the best position the whole swarm has seen. Applied to molecules, the positions live in the continuous latent space of a molecular autoencoder, and every position is turned into a real molecule by a frozen decoder before being scored.
approach.novelty: This root commits to velocities that persist across the entire objective rather than being redrawn each round, so a particle carries momentum through many feedback batches. It attaches accepted scores to the exact latent position that generated the molecule, rather than to a re-encoding of it, which is what keeps the personal and social memories geometrically honest when the decoder is many-to-one.

nodes.hypothesis: Move persistent particles through a frozen deterministic SELFIES VAE latent space using inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward their own best observed position and the swarm best observed position, and attach accepted molecular scores to the exact generating positions before updating those task-local memories.

finding_summary.headline: Swarm dynamics reproduced across seeds as final scores fell
finding_summary.insights: The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. The initial identity gate prevented all supplied initial scores from becoming attractors in the new seeds; shared memory was then established from the first accepted batch and used normally thereafter. That separates safe score handling from the decoder's limited ability to recover the supplied molecules. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. The loss of the stronger aromatic/basic-amine family accompanies the largest score decline, but the data do not isolate its cause. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. Representation quality and motion scale remain separate questions for controlled follow-up. The execution finding is specific to the evaluated CUDA runtime: all runtime repeat-decodes matched, while independent CPU replay changed the decoded identity on 16 of 2,932 new motion attempts. Cross-backend decoder identity is therefore not established.
finding_summary.results: The two additional seeds reproduced the intended persistent motion, accepted-score memories and information transfer. All 2,932 motion equations and state transitions were verified, including 2,732 reuses of persistent velocity. Cognitive attraction was nonzero in all 1,896 eligible distinct-position opportunities, social attraction in all 2,801 eligible opportunities, and real shared memories influenced other particles 2,700 times. Accepted proposals established 200 personal bests and strictly improved them 658 times; every updated personal memory with a later opportunity was reused. All 2,900 proposals were accepted with no evaluator invalids or duplicates, and every generating position matched its runtime repeated decode. Mean final-best scores were 0.450789 in the original seed, 0.358719 in the first new seed and 0.288163 in the second. The three-seed mean is 0.365890 with a population standard deviation of 0.066585. Most of the variation comes from drd2_docking, whose final scores fell from 0.859171 to 0.476176 and 0.124923. The three-seed means for the other objectives are 0.345495 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.569962 for deco_hop, 0.174178 for median_2 and 0.253060 for sitagliptin_mpo. The decoder learned in each preparation: new-seed heldout reconstruction losses fell from 4.565228 to 0.629885 and from 4.534641 to 0.633075. Exact heldout molecular reconstruction remained only 6/480 and 7/480. None of the 100 initial encoding receipts in the new runs reconstructed its original identity, so all 200 particles correctly began without scored attractors.

None of the 100 initial encoding receipts in the new runs reconstructed its original identity, so all 200 particles correctly began without scored attractors.

The lower scores do not come from omitted inertia, unused personal memory, missing information transfer or score assignment to the wrong logged latent position. The initial identity gate prevented all supplied initial scores from becoming attractors in the new seeds; shared memory was then established from the first accepted batch and used normally thereafter. That separates safe score handling from the decoder's limited ability to recover the supplied molecules. Low token loss and abundant valid outputs coexist with weak exact reconstruction and large structural changes: emitted molecules average about 0.85 Morgan distance from both their decoded source and personal best. The molecular assessment is consistent with this coarse search behavior, finding many polyenes, irregular rings and reactive polar forms, with conventional aromatic/amine arrangements unevenly represented. The loss of the stronger aromatic/basic-amine family accompanies the largest score decline, but the data do not isolate its cause. These replicas vary both the prepared representation and the stochastic search, so they do not establish that encoder quality is the sole constraint or that any swarm component improves scores. Representation quality and motion scale remain separate questions for controlled follow-up. The execution finding is specific to the evaluated CUDA runtime: all runtime repeat-decodes matched, while independent CPU replay changed the decoded identity on 16 of 2,932 new motion attempts. Cross-backend decoder identity is therefore not established.

molecular.headline: Polyene-rich molecules with irregular ring systems and reactive polar groups; conventional aromatic–amine arrangements are unevenly represented
molecular.overall_character: This report covers the supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories, compared with seed 0 of the same Algorithm Node. All five tasks are represented, each by 600 evaluated records including 580 optimizer proposals. The output is structurally varied but dominated by alternating double bonds, enol ethers, aldehydes, conjugated carbonyls and irregular medium-sized or large ring closures. Phenyl, thiophene and occasional nitrogen heteroaromatic fragments are present, but many compounds combine them with nonaromatic polyenes or unusually connected rings rather than conventional medicinal scaffolds. Ring-closure indicator rates are 0.8897–0.9724, whereas aromatic-atom indicators are only 0.5517–0.8172. Rings are therefore abundant without being uniformly aromatic. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.5 to 62.5, with a maximum of 147 on one task. These text lengths are not molecular weights. The cumulated-double-bond counter ranges from 0.0 to 0.05; it does not count the many ordinary alternating polyenes visible throughout the trajectories. The compounds contain useful amide, sulfone, amine and aromatic elements, but synthetic plausibility is questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because long conjugated linkers, aldehydes, unusual sulfur/nitrogen valence patterns and complicated closures recur even among favorable examples. Some smaller conventional-looking compounds occur, so this is not a claim that every structure is unmakeable. Every stereocentre indicator is 0.0, and the cited polyenes also leave alkene geometry unspecified. Graph validity and a favorable scalar score do not establish an isolable chemical form, stability or a defined three-dimensional structure.

per_task.generated_character: The high group consists of moderately sized but unusual conjugated ring systems: an S-imino diene ring attached to an aminated unsaturated carbon ring with carboxamide and thienyl enone groups, a fused unsaturated lactam/thioether system bearing a fluoroaniline, and hydrazone-containing or charged nitrogen structures. Aldehydes, amides, nitro groups, thioethers and enamine-like connections recur. Ring_closure_rate is 0.9552, aromatic_atom_rate 0.631 and mean SMILES length 40.5. Ring perception of the best structure gives a nonaromatic medium carbon ring rather than an ordinary phenyl or azaaryl core. Synthetic routes and stereochemical forms would be materially less straightforward than those of the initial indole carboxamide.
liabilities: The highest-scoring structure combines an unusual S-imino ring with an enone, while another high scorer carries O=[N+]=N. Their chemical forms and reactivity require separate assessment.

Aldehydes, thioesters, conjugated enamines and multiple unspecified double-bond geometries complicate stability and synthesis. Cumulated_double_bond_rate is 0.05, in addition to the frequent alternating polyenes.
The worst proposals introduce substantial size, flexibility or tightly connected ring complexity without retaining favorable scores.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of compact, conventional aromatic and polar ring systems is missing from much of the output; ring closure is often achieved through extended unsaturated or irregular fused frameworks instead.

Stable and geometrically defined alternatives to the conjugated aldehyde/enamine and unusual S=N or O=[N+]=N motifs are insufficiently represented around otherwise favorable size and polar-group combinations.
No unique missing target motif follows from the chemically heterogeneous high group, and stereochemical sensitivity is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The S-imino/polyene/carboxamide structure scores 0.3565472174010858 and the fluoroaniline/lactam/thioether structure scores 0.34302515021197216. The initial conventional indole carboxamide already scores 0.3051048083696145. The seed-0 best at 0.37483330611175764 was also an unsaturated lactam bearing polar nitrogen functionality and an aromatic nitrile/carboxamide region, so the replication retains the same broad conjugated/polar character while changing connectivity. At the bottom, very large alkylated or ring-extended molecules score 1.1533920765551684e-30 and 8.812272454079934e-27; a long arylalkyl amine/polyene scores 3.8438521003485694e-25. The initial tiny alkyl bromide is also very low at 8.305895500294491e-10. The observable preference is a bounded size with aromatic/polar features, not unrestricted extension or truncation. The median is 0.042253, and late seed-2 oxygen/sulfur-rich polyenes remain modest, including 0.09723031993424279 and 0.03267406883416671. The high scores do not identify a uniquely required ring system or establish that the unusual functionalities are beneficial in isolation.

per_task.generated_character: The upper end is dominated by very elaborated polyaryl amides, ureas, nitroaryl groups and fluorinated phenyl rings, sometimes joined into large conjugated or cyclophane-like systems. The best structure encodes an unusually large conjugated nitrogen/carbonyl ring with fused aromatic portions and unsaturated side arms. Other high examples are long chains of phenyl rings connected to amides and nitrobenzophenone-like regions. Seed 2 includes additional irregular fused or bridged polar rings. Mean SMILES length is 62.5 and the maximum is 147; ring_closure_rate is 0.9655 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.7638. These are mostly large, synthetically demanding structures, with only a modest numerical separation from the initial screening-like molecules.
liabilities: Multiple nitroaryl groups and extensive conjugated or polyaryl surfaces introduce physicochemical and reactivity questions that the score does not answer.
A relatively high-scoring structure contains an acyl fluoride, which is chemically distinct from ordinary aryl fluorination.
Large irregular ring closures, unspecified polyene geometry, a late peroxide linkage and hydrogen-bearing sulfur functionality make many examples demanding synthetic or chemical-form targets.
missing_features: Compact, well-defined arrangements of aromatic nitrogen, donor/acceptor groups and linkers are unevenly represented; much of the output adds phenyl rings, polyenes and carbonyl groups instead.

Chemically comparable alternatives around the low-scoring nonaromatic sulfone systems are missing as an interpretable local series. The baseline shows that sulfone removal cannot be prescribed universally.
The high group does not reveal a unique missing decoration or geometry, and a small score difference from the initial molecules does not establish a need for its much greater structural complexity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The large conjugated polycarbonyl/N-containing ring system scores 0.5620451020164658, the polyaryl amide/urea with nitro groups scores 0.5619777544131481, and the extended oligophenyl amide scores 0.5607123583378306. The initial fused-dione ester already scores 0.548381482770623, compared with a reported median of 0.520067. The visible gradient therefore tolerates extensive aromatic and polar-group elaboration without demonstrating that such complexity is necessary. The seed-0 best scored 0.5927058823529412 and combined a nitrogen-rich aromatic ring, a sulfone and aryl imine/amine links; the new high group shifts toward larger carbon-rich aromatic/amide assemblies. All six digest worst proposals contain carbon-bonded sulfones in largely nonaromatic unsaturated surroundings, with the worst at 0.25506553536376875. The higher-scoring baseline sulfone prevents attributing this contrast to sulfone presence alone. Late seed-2 sulfone/polyene structures continue near 0.26–0.28, while a different fused aminal/heteroaryl structure reaches 0.5551363900174116. These are unpaired chemical contrasts, not proof of a required substituent or a forbidden functional group.

per_task.generated_character: The new high-scoring molecules are chiefly chlorinated arylalkyl hydrocarbons with long alkyl or conjugated links. The best contains chlorinated phenyl groups and a chlorinated diene, with no nitrogen or oxygen. Other upper examples add a phenol, aldehyde, ether or an enamine-like amino arm; a partially unsaturated aryl-substituted nitrogen ring appears below them. This is a largely lipophilic, halogen-rich population rather than a dense family of conventional basic cyclic amines. Mean SMILES length is 55.5, halogen_rate 0.8948, ring_closure_rate 0.9276 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.6724. The arylalkyl chemistry can be recognizable, but long links and unusual heteroatom-rich late structures weaken general drug-likeness.
liabilities: The high nitrogen-free arylalkyl molecules combine extensive halogenation and hydrophobic surface with few polar groups, raising solubility and nonspecific-partitioning questions without establishing either outcome.
Conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers and halogenated unsaturation recur. Late proposals add very unusual sulfur or organophosphorus forms, including a difluorophosphoryl group, without favorable scores.
Long chains and large irregular closures increase conformational ambiguity; the score alone does not supply a binding geometry.
missing_features: The combined exposed aliphatic amine and bounded aromatic/spacer arrangement seen in the favorable baseline is poorly represented in the new high group, even though the generator can make amines.
The new examples do not provide a controlled comparison of linker length, amine availability and aromatic substitution; adding nitrogen indiscriminately would not follow from the shown scores.
Defined configurations and alkene geometries are absent in molecules whose flexible or substituted links can change their spatial arrangement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl/diene scores 0.4761756997497859, and the more extended chlorinated arylalkyl structure scores 0.3966137972553488. An amino/phenol/aldehyde-containing relative scores 0.35740480261120694. The current high group therefore associates the visible signal with connected hydrophobic aromatic surfaces; it does not itself demonstrate a mandatory amine. The supplied seed-0 baseline is informative: its best at 0.8591709360377655 paired a free tertiary alkylamine with a brominated fused aromatic region, and another tertiary-amine-containing structure scored 0.7578688791540653. The new upper group largely lacks that combination. Current low examples include a small fluorinated enol-ether ester at 0.00010990702906285781, a conjugated aryl aldehyde at 0.00012492407267700092 and an amide-containing biphenyl at 0.00012620521493077546. Aromatic or halogen presence alone is insufficient. The median is 0.022728, and the final sulfonamide/polyene or oxygen-rich structures remain low. The baseline comparison supports exploring exposed amines in suitable aromatic surroundings, while remaining insufficient to claim a particular receptor interaction.

per_task.generated_character: The favorable seed-2 molecules are relatively compact combinations of aromatic rings and polar cyclic groups. The best joins benzodioxole through an amino link to a methoxy/methyl-substituted seven-membered N-containing carbonyl ring; the latter should not be called an ordinary six-membered pyridone. Other high examples include a diaryl sulfone with an oxygen-rich fused medium ring and a benzodioxole-containing cyclic hydrazone/lactam. Seed 1 more often emits enlarged fused carbonyl/imine systems with alkyl appendages. Mean SMILES length is 43.6, ring_closure_rate 0.9724 and aromatic_atom_rate 0.8172. The smaller upper examples have recognizable chemical components, but uncommon ring topology and more elaborate lower-scoring structures keep makeability uncertain.
liabilities: The unusual seven-membered aromatic carbonyl ring and cyclic hydrazone require attention to tautomeric form and geometry rather than treatment as routine six-membered heteroarenes.

Other proposals combine aldehydes, N–O connections, ester/acetal-rich medium rings and highly unsaturated small rings. These features create stability or synthetic questions even when ring and aromatic indicators are positive.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, chemically conventional versions of the favorable aromatic/polar arrangements is limited; many alternatives instead become long polyenes or irregular medium-ring systems.
A unique missing reference-like structure cannot be inferred from the narrow score separation and chemically different upper examples.
Stereochemical and double-bond geometry specification is absent in the substituted saturated and hydrazone/polyene structures.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The benzodioxole/amino/aza-carbonyl-ring compound scores 0.18685638443799904, the diaryl sulfone scores 0.17882042440964765 and the cyclic hydrazone/lactam scores 0.17816898171823184. The initial fused-dione ester scores 0.1678386594791329. That initial molecule was also the seed-0 overall best; the highest seed-0 optimizer proposal was an unsaturated macrocyclic lactam at 0.14023138978580565. Thus the favorable new chemistry is somewhat more compact and organized around aromatic/polar ring combinations than the baseline generated high end. The lowest current examples are a small dibromoalkane at 0.014314958357846713 and acyclic unsaturated acid, aldehyde and enol-ether structures around 0.018–0.021. This supports aromatic ring architecture with appropriately arranged polar functionality over simple polyene fragments or heteroatom count alone. The median is 0.111326. The last proposals range from a small oxygen heterocycle at 0.0464643845937283 to a complex amide/lactam at 0.17194608615974535, so favorable chemistry is not tied to a single ring family or monotonically increasing size.

per_task.generated_character: The output favors moderately sized but highly unsaturated carbonyl/N/O-rich structures: an N-methoxy nitrogen-rich cyclic amide with a benzoyl group and an aldehyde arm, aryl amides bearing imidates and explicit alkoxides, sulfonamide/enamide chains and unsaturated lactam-containing rings. Many structures have few or no aromatic rings; aromatic_atom_rate is 0.5517 and ring_closure_rate 0.8897. Mean SMILES length is 40.7 and halogen_rate only 0.069. The chemistry is therefore substantially different from a uniformly fluorinated aromatic library. Ordinary amide or phenyl fragments are embedded in numerous unusual, potentially labile molecular forms.
liabilities: The best molecule contains an N–O connection, an N–N connection and a conjugated aldehyde; these introduce stability, oxidation and isomeric-form questions.
Explicit benzyl alkoxide or deprotonated oxygen species occur among favorable examples. Their protonation state and isolable form cannot be inferred from their score.

Repeated enol ethers, imidates, alpha-dicarbonyls and enamine-like connections make the population chemically reactive or tautomerically ambiguous. The large polyene and polyacetal extremes additionally impose size or flexibility burdens.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently reproduce the particular bounded connectivity that separates the favorable cyclic compound from its closely related open-chain form.
Chemically stable, well-specified alternatives to the alkoxide, N–O/N–N, imidate and conjugated-aldehyde arrangements are insufficiently demonstrated around the favorable polar skeletons.

The trajectories do not justify a claim that a specific fluorinated fragment or basic amine is missing from an obligatory target motif. The larger limitation is control of topology, polarity and chemical form.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-methoxy cyclic amide with an N–N connection, benzoyl group and conjugated aldehyde scores 0.2687964912603012. A closely related open-chain compound evaluated last scores 0.040358516578188335, providing a useful contrast in connectivity with largely overlapping functional groups. The aryl amide/imidate/benzyl-alkoxide structure scores 0.23418129517000225, and a nonaromatic unsaturated bicyclic amide with a sulfonamide arm scores 0.23098874100279387. Neither aromaticity nor fluorination is a universal high-end feature here. The seed-0 best at 0.259395205519374 was another carbonyl-rich unsaturated amide chain attached to a brominated unsaturated carbocycle. Both baseline and replication favor particular moderately sized polar/unsaturated arrangements, without establishing that the reactive functionality itself is required. At the bottom, a much larger fluorinated polyene scores 5.931767096585795e-76 and an oxygen-rich polyacetal macrocycle scores 1.8652722566013391e-41. Adding unsaturation, fluorine or oxygen alone does not help. The median is 0.000248, and most final carbonyl-rich structures also remain very low, so even abundant amides and aldehydes do not reliably reproduce the favorable connectivity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Ring-closure indicators remain high at 0.8897–0.9724 while aromatic indicators range only from 0.5517 to 0.8172. The digest repeatedly shows nonaromatic polyene rings, long unsaturated chains and complicated closures. Several extended examples score near zero, whereas smaller aromatic/polar combinations score favorably. A cyclic nitrogen-rich compound scores 0.2687964912603012 and its closely related open-chain form 0.040358516578188335, showing that connectivity can matter beyond functional-group inventory.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator often substitutes long conjugated links and irregular large rings for bounded, chemically conventional scaffold architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable bounded ring sizes, controlled linker lengths and chemically conservative changes in ring connectivity around observed favorable structures. Preserve the ability to explore nonaromatic rings while distinguishing purposeful ring architecture from unchecked chain extension or closure complexity; let current task-local observations choose useful topology and size.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest high or late examples contain conjugated aldehydes, enol ethers, imidates, thioesters, an acyl fluoride, unusual S=N and O=[N+]=N functionality, N–O/N–N links and explicit alkoxides. These occur alongside useful amide, sulfone and aromatic features rather than only among the lowest-scoring molecules.
transferable_gaps.gap: Favorable polar-group combinations are not consistently supplied in stable, well-defined chemical forms.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer conservative functional-group and oxidation-state alternatives within related skeletons and preserve explicit, chemically coherent hydrogen and charge states. Use local observations to test alternatives instead of assuming that a favorable scalar objective establishes stability or that all ionizable, sulfur-containing or carbonyl groups should be removed.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied baseline includes a tertiary alkylamine attached to a halogenated fused aromatic region at 0.8591709360377655. The corresponding new high group is dominated by nitrogen-free chlorinated arylalkyl compounds, with a best of 0.4761756997497859. Amines are present elsewhere, and some favorable carbonyl-rich molecules do not need an exposed amine, so simple amine absence or universal amine addition would misread the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably combine exposed aliphatic amines with bounded aromatic and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support controlled placement of unacylated aliphatic nitrogens, together with variations in aromatic attachment and spacer length, while retaining other favorable scaffold features. Let current task-local feedback determine when exposed basicity is useful rather than prescribing it for every objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0 across 580 optimizer proposals. The cited structures include substituted saturated ring junctions, branched side chains, hydrazones and many polyenes whose SMILES do not specify the relevant configuration or alkene geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometrically complex saturated and unsaturated structures are emitted without configuration specification.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make configurationally defined variants accessible and preserve their identities through generation and canonicalization. Assess them only through the current task observations; the files establish missing specification, not which stereoisomer is preferable or whether a particular score is stereosensitive.

nodes.method_name: Molecule Swarm Optimization with persistent latent velocities
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Molecule Swarm Optimization: each particle keeps its latent position, velocity and best observed position, and moves through inertia plus independent stochastic attractions toward its personal best and the swarm's best. [Winter et al., Methods 2.2-2.4](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836962/) describe this molecular use of particle swarm optimization. For our adaptation, train a compact SELFIES VAE solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, freeze its encoder and deterministic decoder, and start each objective with clean swarm memories. Encodings of supplied molecules provide starting geometry; their scores initialize attractors only when decoding preserves canonical molecular identity. Otherwise establish scored attractors from actual generated evaluations, never from mislabeled reconstructions. Generate fresh latent positions through particle motion and decode new complete molecules. Locally retry stochastic motion for invalid or duplicate outcomes until the announced batch is filled. Match accepted feedback to the exact generating position before updating personal and shared bests; each batch uses only resolved memories. The corpus supplies a generator, never a molecule library for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that persistent individual trajectories explore alternatives while shared successful locations redirect them quickly enough to improve the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. This uses the provided scalar objective directly, without additional desirability terms. Useful latent geometry and rapid transfer of discoveries between particles remain empirical prerequisites. The published model and evaluation scale do not establish those prerequisites under the permitted preparation and scarce feedback.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecules from score-ranked accepted parents using fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It trains a Tanimoto fingerprint Gaussian process on all accepted observations and chooses a batch from each new offspring pool through correlated posterior function draws. Its atom-replacement move picks any source atom, then applies the inherited aromaticity and valence rules to choose a different element. That move can remove a carbonyl from an otherwise promising amide or carbonyl-containing ring.
approach.novelty: Preserve existing carbonyl groups during atom replacement by choosing the replacement site only among atoms outside C=O pairs. The remaining atom and element substitutions use the Parent's rules, allowing local variants around an intact carbonyl framework. This differs from the completed halogen-site experiment and earlier changes to parent memory or partner choice: it changes the support of one substitution operator, with intact C=O retention as the measurable intermediate effect.

nodes.hypothesis: Restrict atom-replacement targets to atoms outside existing carbonyl C=O pairs, preserving both carbonyl atoms and their double bond in that operator.

finding_summary.headline: Carbonyls survived replacement, but scores fell and neighboring functional groups still changed
finding_summary.insights: The intervention closes the intended destructive replacement channel, but that channel is not sufficient to explain useful graph evolution. Existing carbonyl atoms and their double bond can survive while adjacent amide-like or ester-like connections change, and subsequent operators still remove some carbonyls. Indeed, thirty-six protected replacements introduced an acyl-halide connection by changing an unprotected neighboring atom, and five of those paths reached evaluation. The sole all-protected case correctly retried through another operator rather than substituting a protected endpoint. The Parent also had five source-beating carbonyl-loss emissions, so motif removal was not uniformly harmful. The negative score result therefore narrows the useful question to which complete functional relationships deserve preservation, rather than carbonyl retention alone. The supplied chemistry reinforces that limit: useful aryl amine and indole-carbonyl families coexist with strained aromatic bridges, oversized repeated assemblies and reactive halogen or peroxide connections, with no specified stereochemistry. In particular, the large seed-0 DRD2 decline accompanies bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry; the experiment does not isolate one structural cause of that decline. The inherited representation issue also reached one evaluated pure-crossover product, outside the replacement channel. Neither unchosen sites nor unselected pool molecules have counterfactual scores, so the observed subgroups cannot establish that allowing a particular omitted replacement would have improved the endpoint.
finding_summary.results: All 12,104 successful replacements on carbonyl-bearing sources preserved every original C=O pair. The protected substitutions reached 11,191 pool descendants and 718 actual evaluated descendants. Among products made by a single replacement, carbonyl loss fell from 751 of 7,016 Parent pool products and sixty of 589 Parent emissions to zero of 7,100 pool products and zero of 526 emissions. This did not preserve the whole functional group: 93 evaluated descendants contain replacements that changed an original carbonyl’s neighboring atom class, including 41 that lost an adjacent nitrogen. Across the full emitted stream, acyl-halide-bearing molecules increased from seventeen to 272. All fifteen task/seed runs completed with 4,350 valid novel submitted offspring and no evaluator invalid or duplicate attempts. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.509621, a paired change of -0.034753. The seed changes were -0.089860, -0.027023 and +0.012624. The mean DRD2 change was -0.146641, while median_2 improved by 0.009198.

The mean DRD2 change was -0.146641, while median_2 improved by 0.009198.

The intervention closes the intended destructive replacement channel, but that channel is not sufficient to explain useful graph evolution. Existing carbonyl atoms and their double bond can survive while adjacent amide-like or ester-like connections change, and subsequent operators still remove some carbonyls. Indeed, thirty-six protected replacements introduced an acyl-halide connection by changing an unprotected neighboring atom, and five of those paths reached evaluation. The sole all-protected case correctly retried through another operator rather than substituting a protected endpoint. The Parent also had five source-beating carbonyl-loss emissions, so motif removal was not uniformly harmful. The negative score result therefore narrows the useful question to which complete functional relationships deserve preservation, rather than carbonyl retention alone. The supplied chemistry reinforces that limit: useful aryl amine and indole-carbonyl families coexist with strained aromatic bridges, oversized repeated assemblies and reactive halogen or peroxide connections, with no specified stereochemistry. In particular, the large seed-0 DRD2 decline accompanies bulkier hydroperoxide-containing chemistry; the experiment does not isolate one structural cause of that decline. The inherited representation issue also reached one evaluated pure-crossover product, outside the replacement channel. Neither unchosen sites nor unselected pool molecules have counterfactual scores, so the observed subgroups cannot establish that allowing a particular omitted replacement would have improved the endpoint.

molecular.headline: Aryl amines and indole carbonyl rings gain locally, but strained aromatic bridges and reactive halogen bonds persist
molecular.overall_character: The complete supplied current and parent trajectories cover every task and seed. Current outputs include compact bridged aryl amides, linked heteroaromatic diones, aryl/basic-amine assemblies, expanded indole-fused carbonyl rings, and fluorinated dione derivatives. Ring and aromatic content are rich: ring-closure presence rates range from 0.9759 to 0.9954, and aromatic-token presence from 0.9368 to 0.9908. These are molecule-level SMILES text readings, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of feasible geometry. Each task has 900 observations including 870 optimizer proposals. Substantial ring systems predominate, but occasional very small fragments and repeated oversized assemblies remain. The more conventional indole carbonyl family provides a plausible chemical direction, while other leaders retain direct N-F or N-Cl bonds, strained aromatic bridges, or reactive alkyl/oxygen-halogen functionality. High-scoring neutral aryl amines are present, so basic centres are not a general missing capability. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout, despite ionizable groups and potentially stereogenic connections. The seed families provide moderate structural diversity, with many variants still concentrated around their respective core arrangements. Relative to the parent, the chemical families change without consistently resolving synthetic plausibility, geometry, or stability.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact methoxy/methyl-substituted aromatic systems with fused or bridged nitrogen-containing rings, an alkene, and an N-fluoro phenylamide. Related molecules add fluorine, hydroxyl, amino, N-N, or oxygen-containing bridge connections. Other seeds produce sulfur-containing fused lactams and extensively annulated nitrogen/carbonyl systems, sometimes with small-ring or difficult bridge topology. Thus the generator already supplies aromatic bulk, heterocycles, and carbonyl functionality: aromatic and ring presence are 0.9621 and 0.9759, with mean SMILES length 45.5. The aryl/carbonyl components are recognizable, but direct fluorination of the amide nitrogen is a distinct stability concern, and the densely connected ring geometry is not validated by the SMILES.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonding on the amide nitrogen is not routine carbon-bound fluorination and raises chemical stability questions.
Several related structures add N-N or N-O connections without improving the leading supplied score.
Dense annulation and bridging complicate synthesis and conformational feasibility, while occasional small fragments discard the useful architecture.
missing_features: Matched ordinary amide-nitrogen alternatives retaining the leading aryl and bridged-ring arrangement are missing from the cited top series.
Less constrained ring connections preserving the productive carbonyl and aromatic relationships are insufficiently represented.
Stereochemically defined substituted bridge variants are absent despite their potentially stereogenic connectivity.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/methyl bridged N-fluoroamide reaches 0.457660. Adding a carbon-bound fluorine or a bridge amino group gives 0.431364; adding hydroxyl gives 0.426006, and replacing a bridge carbon with nitrogen gives 0.429932. These local examples favor the less decorated leading arrangement, rather than indiscriminate addition of polar or halogen groups. Small fragments such as ethene and methane score zero. Final complex annulated structures range from 0.111928 to 0.353532 among the cited examples, so ring complexity by itself is insufficient. The current seed-0 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.446352 while exchanging its bridged N/O-aromatic ketone connection for an N-fluoroamide family. The current seed-1 and seed-2 maxima, 0.403194 and 0.368052, are below their respective parent maxima of 0.412682 and 0.416350. The supplied chemistry therefore does not establish that the N-F bond is needed for the score increase.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family links an alkyl-substituted azaaromatic ring to an N-chlorinated fused dione and a substituted dimethylaminoaryl group. The aryl group contains a benzene-fused oxygen-containing small ring, so the apparent compactness still comes with geometric strain. Some near-leaders also carry an N-chloro-N-methyl arylamine or additional tightly fused ring connections. Elsewhere, particularly in seed-0, much larger assemblies accumulate azaaromatics, carbonyls, unsaturated side chains, and repeated connecting units. Mean SMILES length is 89.1 and maximum 244; aromatic and ring presence are both 0.9862. Final seed-2 molecules combine heteroaromatic diones, arylamides, chlorinated N-alkyl groups, and unusually constrained azaaromatic fragments. Apparent synthesis and stability remain questionable across these different size regimes.

The benzene-fused oxygen small ring and other constrained aromatic closures require geometric and synthetic scrutiny.
Large repeated unsaturated/carbonyl assemblies add substantial size and connecting-group complexity without a consistent supplied-score advantage.
Acid chlorides and chlorinated N-alkyl groups appear in late molecules and are not evidence of stable medicinal chemistry.

Ordinary ring replacements for the benzene-fused oxygen small ring and tightly constrained azaaromatic fragments are underrepresented.

Small fragments, including ethane and chlorodimethylamine, remain at the 0.5 floor. The seed-0 oversized, extensively unsaturated assembly peaks at 0.602368, below the compact seed-1 family, so more size or repeated functionality is not a general solution. The parent's best was 0.632470 in an oxygen-halogen/peroxide-containing polycycle. This is not simply an ordinary fused saturated ring: the short aromatic bridge imposes serious geometric questions. Neighboring leaders use azetidine, pyrrolidine, or more bridged amine connections; seed-1 instead yields a fused aryl/amine system with an exocyclic alkene and chlorinated saturated carbon. Aromatic and ring presence are 0.9874 and 0.9931, and halogen presence is 0.9954. transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable local replacements that preserve the surrounding aryl/carbonyl arrangement and approximately preserve size accessible throughout generation. transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring molecules include compressed carbon bridges across aromatic rings, benzene-fused oxygen small rings, and other highly constrained aromatic fragments. transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied proposals include very small zero-scoring fragments and large repeated assemblies. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles
De novo connected-fragment graph crossover
Local atom/bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph-based retries for complete novel pools; saturation-dependent retry branches retained but not exercised
Bounded greedy score-ranked survival and subsequent breeding from accepted offspring

Accepted-only task-local fingerprint Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior sampling over fresh offspring pools, masked batch selection, and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback retained but not exercised

Carbonyl-preserving atom-replacement target support: exclude exactly existing C=O endpoints, retain the inherited conditional element law, and expose fixed-source/inner-retry traces through pool and evaluated-descendant provenance

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules, using score-quantile parent sampling, connected-fragment crossover and local graph mutations. Its retained mutations include formula-preserving relocation of aromatic nitrogen, and stable identity checks admit a surplus pool of novel candidates. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses integer counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity to predict that pool jointly. The Parent chooses each evaluation by taking a fresh correlated posterior draw's highest available candidate, then admits accepted feedback to its prediction archive and breeding population.
approach.novelty: Add explicit batch-best allocation. Build one shared panel of posterior function draws and choose each next molecule by how much it raises the panel's average best score among the molecules already selected. This lets the remaining evaluations cover high-outcome possibilities that the current batch has not captured. Earlier siblings changed survival, parent allocation, graph production, identity admission or posterior features and noise; they have not optimized the utility of the selected batch as a set. The new rule retains the Parent's count posterior and tests a different use of its predictions, with a fixed 128-path numerical panel and separately measured real search outcomes.

nodes.hypothesis: Allocate the announced batch by greedy maximization of a shared Monte Carlo estimate of the posterior expected maximum over the selected pool members, so each added molecule is valued by its incremental contribution to the batch's predicted best outcome.

finding_summary.headline: Batch utility changes selection and raises offspring yield, but final mean score does not improve
finding_summary.insights:
The missing batch-set objective was a real decision difference, but correcting it did not supply the registered final-score benefit. This rules out lack of allocation opportunities or a nonexecuting selector as explanations for the result. It also shows why more parent-beating offspring and more incumbent updates are insufficient evidence of stronger final solutions: they can be more frequent increments along a weaker search history. Here the absolute batch-best scores declined even as those counts rose.

The higher internal objective describes the same finite posterior panel used to choose the batch. It does not reveal the real scores of the unevaluated alternatives. The posterior model itself is unchanged; the lower prediction MSE reflects a changed selected stream and feedback history, and does not establish repaired uncertainty. Coverage remains especially poor on sitagliptin, at 37.4%. Model error, limited tail sampling and the objective’s focus on the next batch rather than future breeding remain plausible limits. Those explanations need separate evidence; the current paired panel does not identify their individual contributions. Greedy maximization is also approximate: on the Parent’s original ten-path panels, its existing batches already captured every path maximum and a passive greedy replacement sometimes lost internal utility.

The molecular assessment finds recognizable ring-rich families alongside recurrent reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry. The slightly narrower core coverage and higher same-pool correlation show that batch-best complementarity need not mean broader or cleaner chemistry. Valid graphs and higher posterior batch utility therefore leave chemical feasibility unresolved. The supported finding is successful allocation activation with no demonstrated final-score gain on these three seeds; transfer to different posterior quality, chemical families or batch sizes remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The batch objective changed the selected set in 434 of 435 batches when compared with the Parent rule on the same candidate pools and posterior draws. Among 3,765 later positions with a distinct positive-gain winner, 3,440 choices differed from the corresponding raw-draw winner under the same mask. Every emitted choice matched the registered acquisition. The internal estimate of the batch maximum rose by 0.00597 on average against the Parent comparator: 418 batches improved, 17 tied and none declined. The finite panel still saturated: 150 later positions across 45 batches had exactly zero gain and followed the declared index tie rule.

On the actual scored searches, strict improvements over the best generating parent rose from 624 to 688 out of 4,350 offspring, and incumbent improvements rose from 241 to 298. Yet the average accepted batch-best score fell from 0.48731 to 0.46096. The three-seed final macro mean was 0.57398 versus 0.57434 for the Parent, a change of -0.00036, below the required +0.002 improvement. One seed improved and two fell; seven of fifteen task/seed endpoints improved. Mean endpoints rose for sitagliptin and median similarity, while decoration hopping, DRD2 and zaleplon declined. Every session completed with valid, novel emissions and no numerical fallback.

Selected-stream prediction MSE fell from 0.01127 to 0.00980, while mean within-batch rank correlation fell from 0.550 to 0.515. Nominal 95% latent intervals covered only 77.6% of outcomes, versus 76.9% for the Parent. On identical Child pools, the changed rule selected slightly more uncertainty than the Parent rule, but average conditional correlation increased slightly and distinct molecular cores fell from 7.17 to 7.06 per batch.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with cyclic amines and amides, but recurrent reactive bonds, unusual ring closures and unassigned stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories; the brief lists no tasks_without_trajectories. The output contains compact methoxyaryl heterocycles, extensively decorated nitrogen heterocycles, flexible diaryl cyclic amines, medium-ring polyamides, and fluorinated carbonyl-rich heterocycles. These are predominantly connected ring-containing molecules, with occasional tiny fragments. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9506 to 0.9793 and aromatic-token rates from 0.9333 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or evidence of conventional ring geometry. All 4350 optimizer occurrences parse as single connected molecules in passive RDKit 2023.09.6 checks. This establishes graph validity only. Many accepted graphs contain nitrogen-halogen or oxygen-halogen bonds, peroxide links, dense thione chemistry, or short bridges across aromatic systems. Useful ordinary medicinal-chemistry motifs are present, especially non-acylated cyclic amines, aryl ethers and amides, but their coexistence with these liabilities makes overall synthetic plausibility questionable and drug-likeness weak. Structural diversity is moderate across the supplied seeds and objectives, with recognizable families dominating the high-score excerpts; high string uniqueness does not establish broad chemically plausible scaffold coverage. Every task has a zero digest stereocentre rate, although passive perception finds unassigned tetrahedral centres in many proposed graphs. Compared with parent n-559d25e9c9c7, the families remain recognizable while ring topology and heteroatom attachments change; the task entries describe those chemical differences alongside existing recorded scores without attributing activation or assigning new scores. All passive sizes, bond counts and perceived ring sizes below come from the supplied trajectories and are recorded in the accompanying molecular.audit.json. Digest best examples are pooled across seeds, whereas its final examples are the last listed seed-2 evaluations; those final examples are proposals, not a claim that the incumbent was lost.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer mainly produces compact aromatic nitrogen compounds: median 25 heavy atoms, with a digest mean SMILES length of 41.5 and ring/aromatic-token rates of 0.9506/0.9437. The initial methoxyindole arylamide scores 0.3051048083696145. One high-score family retains indole-like rings and an arylamide but attaches fluorine to the amide nitrogen and halogen to the pyrrolic nitrogen. The pooled best molecule instead has 26 heavy atoms, two benzene rings, a benzene-fused four-member nitrogen ring, methoxy groups, a nitrile, a formamidine-like substituent and an N-chloro aryl enamine; its perceived ring sizes are 4, 6 and 6. This is ordinary fragment vocabulary assembled into a chemically unusual architecture. Relative to the parent, the median heavy-atom count remains 25, but nitrogen-halogen-containing proposals increase from 102/870 to 500/870. The parent endpoints are mainly indole/arylcarboxamide variants and a more extensively closed arylamide system; the child adds the nitrile-bearing small-ring family. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecule by sampling local graph edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon within the same six-member ring. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch permitted by short-term inverse-motif memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a loss, while keeping a separate best archive. Memory records signed changes in rooted one-bond environments, keeps up to four inverse attributes from each selected transition, and vetoes a proposal when both signs match one live transition. These environments record atom properties and bond order but omit whether a bond belongs to a ring.
approach.novelty: Make inverse memory distinguish cyclic and acyclic versions of the same local environment by adding a binary ring-membership flag to every bond in its rooted motif. Ring and chain occurrences will then receive separate signed counts and restriction keys. The original motif description remains the ordering prefix, so the addition preserves priority between existing motif families. Earlier memory siblings changed sign coverage, score-based credit, count-based ranking, overlap retention or occurrence boundaries; they retained the same pooled structural descriptions. This experiment changes the topological context of the remembered attribute. It keeps the Parent's graph generation and nitrogen relocation mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Refine each rooted radius-one motif with binary cycle membership of its root-to-neighbor bonds, so signed occurrence counts and inverse tabu restrictions distinguish cyclic from acyclic instances of an otherwise identical local environment.

finding_summary.headline: Separating ring and chain motifs changed 20 evaluated neighbors, but all three seeds lost score
finding_summary.insights: The result rules out lack of structural activation or lack of evaluated exposure as the explanation for the missing score benefit. The original labels really did pool ring and chain occurrences, and the refined labels still transferred restrictions between distinct molecules during a live memory window. That additional topological distinction alone did not improve this search. It also did more than remove vetoes: resolving opposite changes that previously canceled changed which motif families were retained in nine transitions and created one extra veto. The largely unfavorable outcomes of the newly allocated neighbors show why passive admissions cannot be treated as evidence of useful search. The full trajectories also change when a batch stops on a different draw, so the large final losses do not identify the causal score contribution of any single annotation or unscored alternative. The supplied molecular assessment still finds aromatic and carbonyl arrangements alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry. Binary cycle membership does not describe ring size, geometry, strain or chemical stability; those limitations remain open after this experiment.
finding_summary.results: The observed graphs contained 834 old motif families with multiple cycle contexts, and those distinctions reached live restrictions and scored proposals. A separate unannotated memory replay on the same sources and accepted history shows that 19 evaluated molecules were newly admitted and one evaluated molecule replaced a newly vetoed ring opening, changing 20 of 435 actual batches. Only one of these 20 molecules improved its source, by 0.001295; 19 worsened it and none tied. None immediately improved the best archive. One worsening ring closure became the next walk state, but its 20 later evaluated descendants added no archive gain. The three-seed mean final score fell from 0.521759 to 0.476854, a paired loss of 0.044906 instead of the required gain of 0.002. All three seeds declined. DRD2 and sitagliptin accounted for the largest task losses; zaleplon improved slightly on average.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl scaffolds persist, but high scores also accompany reactive decorations, sulfur cages and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-9dc03aaf234b produces medium-sized to large, heavily branched ring systems: recognizable indole/benzofuran/benzothiophene carbonyl compounds, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl-linked cyclic amines, bridged amides and sulfur-dense cages. All five tasks are covered. Each digest contains 900 evaluated molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals, across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9057, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7264 in the supplied task order; these are fractions of strings containing aromatic tokens, not aromatic-atom fractions or evidence that every leading molecule is aromatic. Every set has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Neutral SMILES can contain basic amines, and these records do not reveal protonation or stereochemical processing inside an evaluator. There is meaningful variation between seeds and tasks, but high-scoring excerpts commonly comprise close relatives of a few frameworks. An ordinary indole carboxamide is reasonably recognizable synthetic chemistry; many other leaders combine unusual sulfur coordination, heteroatom-halogen bonds or tightly connected bridges whose makeability is questionable. These coexist with useful-looking aromatic and carbonyl arrangements. The chemistry remains broadly similar to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc even where particular structures and recorded scores differ. All supplied child and parent trajectories were read passively. Structural sizes below are atom counts derived from their saved SMILES; scores are copied from those trajectories or the digest. The audit at .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-04-improve-L16.molecular-audit.json records input hashes, graph readings and exact digest-to-trajectory matches. The digest final_molecules entries are the last evaluated neighbors of seed 2, not the best archive or all seeds combined. Missing features below distinguish absent chemical quality from demonstrated score requirements: these data cannot identify an unseen target pharmacophore, prove synthesis or establish biological activity.

per_task.generated_character: The optimizer proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. Compact fused aromatic heterocycles linked through an amide or ketone to a phenyl ring are prominent: the 0.39905049777278273 indole carboxamide has ethoxy, methyl and thiol substituents, while the 0.41003927643747895 benzofuran relative carries an anilide, an aminochloromethyl group, an aniline nitrogen and an N-chloro amide. Other strong examples replace the heteroaromatic core with bridged unsaturated O/N/S rings. The 0.3984261621341843 ketone is a considerably more entangled sulfur-containing polycycle. Ordinary aryl amides are plausible starting chemistry; the chlorinated nitrogen and unusual bridged sulfur products are much less convincing synthetic endpoints. Ring-token presence is universal and aromatic-token presence is 0.9057; this is not a ring-poor search.
liabilities: The highest displayed benzofuran compound includes an N-chloro amide and an aminochloromethyl substituent; these are chemical reactivity concerns distinct from ordinary carbon-bound aryl chlorine.
Thiols, unusual multiply bonded sulfur, highly bridged unsaturated frameworks and the cyclic alkyne-containing low example raise stability or geometric concerns.
Potential configurations in the aminochloromethyl and bridged products are unspecified; the proposal stereocentre-token rate is 0.0.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the useful aromatic-carbonyl connection through late structural changes; some low neighbors lose it while retaining many rings and heteroatoms.

A wider set of stable matched versions of the compact heteroaromatic carbonyl framework without N-halogen substitution or unusual sulfur bridges. Conventional indole amides already occur, so the missing capability is sustained chemically coherent variation, not access to aromatic rings or amides.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial methoxy-rich indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. Its higher-scoring relatives retain a relatively compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement. Low examples with a tetrahedral aminoalkyl linkage instead of the intact amide carbonyl score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.04832573556546499. The 0.0083275363022723 low example combines disrupted fused-ring chemistry, a small nitrogen ring and a cyclic alkyne-containing sulfur appendage. These comparisons support preservation of carbonyl connectivity and a coherent aromatic framework, although several substitutions change together. They do not establish that N-chlorination, a thiol or a sulfur bridge is required. Parent and child share the displayed 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895 leaders. In seed 0 the recorded peak changes from the 0.393567030299894 benzothiophene ketone to the 0.3984261621341843 bridged ketone; that structural change does not itself demonstrate better makeability. The displayed final sulfur-cage neighbors still include a low 0.11267802872031613 example.

per_task.generated_character: These are the largest proposal families, with 30-47 heavy atoms, mean SMILES length 70.4 and maximum length 92. Every proposed string contains rings and aromatic atoms. Nitrogen-rich fused aromatic carbonyl/thione cores carry substituted azaaryl groups through amine-containing linkers, together with long branched ether, ester or sulfur-containing tails. The displayed seed-0 leaders combine a chlorinated azaaryl group, a methylidene imine, a fused carbonyl/thione system, N-bromination and a fluoromethyl substituent. Seed-2 leaders use a different azaaryl/dicarbonyl arrangement and cyclic O-S-O connectivity. Ordinary heteroaromatic and carbonyl fragments are present, but their heavily decorated combinations, reactive terminal groups and unspecified side-chain configurations make the complete molecules questionable synthetic targets.
liabilities: N-bromo and N-chloro heterocycles, terminal S-Cl bonds and an O-Cl terminus occur in displayed strong molecules. Their presence must not be conflated with ordinary aryl halogenation.
Unprotected imines, unusual sulfur-carbon double-bond substitution and long multiply substituted tails introduce stability and synthesis concerns.
The decorated tails contain potential stereogenic sites but all proposal strings have stereocentre-token rate 0.0.
missing_features: A simpler, stable realization of the favorable azaaryl/amine/carbonyl arrangement across the displayed leaders; the score plateau leaves substantial decoration chemically unmotivated.

Systematic variation of ordinary linker and side-chain chemistry that preserves the conjugated core without simultaneously introducing reactive terminal bonds. The trajectories do not identify a unique unseen scaffold required by this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.548381482770623. Lower optimizer examples at 0.526081691583997, 0.5286081645773063 and 0.5300762397705813 alter its fused-ring connectivity, carbonyl/imine pattern or conjugation. Higher molecules retain substantial nitrogen-containing aromatic and carbonyl/thione organization while adding different azaaryl decoration. The displayed leaders at evaluations 257, 269, 278, 279, 288, 294, 295 and 299 of seed 0 all score 0.6091282178833478 despite changes to sulfur substitution, branching, bromination or terminal heteroatom-halogen groups. This plateau gives no evidence that those extra decorations are individually needed. The final seed-2 example with disrupted azaaryl aromaticity scores 0.541787206685953, whereas the displayed nitrogen-linked aromatic relative reaches 0.6084360836298065; connectivity also differs, so aromaticity alone is not isolated. Relative to the parent, seed-0 peak structures remain decorated azaaryl fused heterocycles, but the recorded peak is 0.6091282178833478 versus 0.6161710037174721. per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 32-43 heavy atoms; all contain aromatic tokens, rings and halogens. Early molecules are biaryl carboxylic acid/amides with a sulfonylated pyrrolidine. Strong later molecules have substantially different nitrogen and sulfur connections: a 0.8500094650652374 family places an ordinary tertiary azetidine nitrogen between a substituted aryl-containing chain and a small sulfur/nitrogen ring bearing an aryl thioamide. A separate 0.868020189804352 family is a dense bridged aryl/N/S structure with brominated phenyl regions and a substituted sulfur ring. Basic carbon-bound amines therefore are present, although not every nitrogen is an ordinary basic amine. The aromatic portions are familiar, but strained small rings, unusual sulfur valence and the overall bridged architectures make many complete products difficult to regard as plausible medicinal compounds.
liabilities: Small saturated N/S rings, multiply connected bridges and sulfur centers with unusual multiple bonding raise geometric and stability concerns.

Displayed strong molecules combine thiols, thioamides and terminal sulfur-halogen bonding with highly halogenated aromatic regions; a high recorded score does not establish acceptable reactivity or solubility.
The displayed leaders contain potential stereogenic relationships but no proposal includes a stereocentre token. Their actual three-dimensional configurations are unresolved.

Defined stereochemical identities for constrained products. Emitted strings also show no charged forms, but these records cannot establish whether the evaluator considered protonation or whether an explicitly charged proposal would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The low displayed acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives score 0.007468397818197266 to 0.011875520467584314, far below the nitrogen-containing sulfur-rich leaders. This is consistent with a different arrangement of hydrophobic rings and nitrogen centers, together with loss or transformation of acidic/carbonyl functionality; it is not proof of a specific binding interaction. A basic center by itself is insufficient: the initial N-methylpiperidine/hydroxamate compound scores 0.0003786988088202195. The two displayed 0.8500094650652374 molecules replace an aryl-linked substituted sulfur center with the corresponding carbon center while preserving that recorded score. Several neighboring sulfur/carbon variants also share 0.8302140284961123. Thus the observed score does not require every unusual sulfur linkage. The 0.868020189804352 bridged leader is identical to the parent seed-1 leader. Seed 2 has a recorded peak of 0.47197342727666497 versus the parent 0.9148143511682032, yet its final molecules remain complex amine-bearing sulfur cages; the changed score accompanies a different arrangement within the same broad problematic chemistry, not loss of all rings or nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals range from 27 to 45 heavy atoms, with mean SMILES length 61.4. All contain rings and aromatic atoms. The highest displayed family combines an alkyl-substituted azaaryl ring and an aryl group with bridged unsaturated amide/urea-containing rings. The 0.20981104279018886 leader has an N-methyl carbonyl-containing ring and an N-N-O bridge; related entries vary a bridge methylene, alkyl branches or the N/O sequence. Other seeds retain aryl carbonyl families but add sulfur-containing bridges, hydrazine-like connections, alcohol/ether substituents and halogenation. N-N-O bridges and a displayed O-O linkage introduce potential chemical lability; lower examples also contain O-Br and unusual sulfur junctions.
The final sulfur-rich bridged products and the highest N/O-bridged family have no specified stereochemistry.

Ring-opened aromatic compounds with exposed carbonyl/urea chains score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515. The higher bridged azaaryl/aryl examples therefore suggest that the relative arrangement and constraint of aromatic and carbonyl groups matters more than simply adding aromatic atoms. Within that family, the methylene-containing leader scores 0.20981104279018886, the closely related urea/N-N-O bridge 0.20775769309691736, the shorter N-O bridge 0.2056349053193895 and the peroxide-containing bridge 0.20647766243219587. per_task.generated_character: These proposals are relatively compact in atom count, with 25-33 heavy atoms, but often extremely dense topologically. Aromatic-token presence is 0.7264 across all proposals; the leading 0.48118636011729826 molecule itself has no aromatic atoms on parsing. It is an unsaturated sulfur-rich cage with carbonyl groups, a fluoromethyl substituent, an acyl fluoride and a sulfinamide-type substituent. Other strong examples contain N-F bonds, imino nitrogen, sulfur-carbon multiple bonds and overlapping small heterocycles. The highest product has formula C14H15F2N3O3S8, illustrating that compactness here does not mean ordinary carbon-based drug chemistry. Its unusual sulfur coordination, interlocked rings and unspecified configurations make synthesis and physical realizability especially questionable.

Displayed leaders include reactive acyl fluoride, sulfinyl fluoride, N-F and N-S connections in complicated combinations.
Potential stereochemical relationships at saturated carbon and unusual sulfur centers are unassigned, despite the strong geometric constraints.

Chemically controlled alternatives to reactive acyl-fluoride, sulfinyl-fluoride and N-fluoro substitutions while preserving polar-group placement. Their benefit remains to be tested; the records do not support prescribing an unseen target-specific amine or aromatic fragment.

Higher structures are generally more compact heteroatom-rich cages with altered saturation, nitrogen/carbonyl connectivity and fluorine placement. However, sulfur-rich cages also occur among extremely low examples, including 3.046653569109811e-09, so neither sulfur loading nor ring density is sufficient. A particularly direct displayed comparison changes the acyl-fluoride carbonyl carbon of the 0.48118636011729826 leader to sulfur, giving the sulfinyl-fluoride relative at 0.43569274814003056. The observed score favors that carbonyl version over further sulfur substitution, without establishing that either reactive fluoride group is desirable medicinal chemistry. The parent contains the same 0.48118636011729826 leader and the 0.4413006791220245 seed-2 heterocycle. Its seed-1 peak is 0.5903526424693334 versus the child 0.4075035943835411, with dense sulfur ring chemistry persisting in both. transferable_gaps.evidence: Displayed strong products retain N-halogen, O-halogen or S-halogen bonds, unusual sulfur multiple bonding and densely connected heteroatom junctions. Yet a carbon-linked and a sulfur-linked aryl/cyclic-amine pair both score 0.8500094650652374, and replacing an acyl carbonyl carbon with sulfur changes 0.48118636011729826 to 0.43569274814003056. Thus unusual sulfur is not uniformly required by the observed feedback. Ordinary amides and carbon-bound amines are already accessible; their coherent combination with stable surrounding chemistry remains incomplete.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently turn favorable aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements into complete molecules with conventional bond chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched ordinary carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and conventional sulfur alternatives while preserving the useful attachment pattern. Distinguish heteroatom-halogen bonds and unusual sulfur coordination from ordinary aryl halides, sulfides, sulfoxides and sulfones. Assess the resulting complete structures through the same observed feedback; local element substitution alone does not establish chemical quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All proposal sets have ring_closure_rate 1.0. The output includes bridged N/O amides, small N/S rings, cyclic alkyne-containing appendages and sulfur cages. Carbonyl-disrupted aromatic relatives score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.04832573556546499, while ring-opened carbonyl-chain examples score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515 below related constrained aromatic/carbonyl families. Dense ring content is therefore neither the missing resource nor sufficient evidence of a useful arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator supplies abundant cycles but does not consistently preserve useful functional-group geometry in plausible ring and linker arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coherent variations in ring size, fusion, bridge connectivity and linker length that preserve promising carbonyl and heteroatom attachment relationships. Include ordinary less strained ring alternatives alongside constrained ones. Treat geometric feasibility and functional-group integrity as molecular properties to investigate, rather than equating any cycle with a satisfactory ring system.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Decorated nitrogen-heterocycle relatives share 0.6091282178833478 across changes to branching, sulfur centers and reactive terminal groups. A separate carbon/sulfur linker pair shares 0.8500094650652374. Bridged N/O carbonyl compounds remain close at 0.20775769309691736, 0.2056349053193895 and 0.20647766243219587 even when the bridge includes an extra nitrogen or peroxide linkage. These observations do not show that every appendage or labile bond contributes useful chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-tolerated local simplifications are not consistently combined into simpler, chemically coherent whole molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate matched simplifications that remove unnecessary branches and replace labile connections while holding the principal scaffold and polar-group positions fixed. Include complete combinations of locally tolerated ordinary replacements, using actual feedback to learn whether their combined simplification remains useful. Do not assume that a tie for one local change proves a benefit for an untested whole molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. Displayed examples include an aminochloromethyl substituent, substituted saturated amine rings, N/O bridges and interlocked sulfur cages. These graphs contain potential stereochemical relationships, but the saved identities specify no configurations. The same problem occurs in several structures shared with the parent; a changed graph or score has not resolved it.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted identities leave stereochemical and geometric relationships undefined in many constrained products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make feasible stereochemical identities accessible and preserve their definitions through structural edits, using only the candidate molecular graph and ordinary feedback. Pair configuration handling with alternatives whose bridge and ring geometry is credible; assigning tags to an implausible cage would not repair its chemistry. Any score sensitivity to configuration must be established empirically.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
