approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It builds a fresh surplus pool, then a fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted labels selects evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its retained identity-admission repair confirms stable canonical keys before pool insertion. Atom replacement currently changes one element at a time; occasional multistep walks can combine substitutions, but there is no direct move that relocates a ring nitrogen while preserving composition.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with one coordinated nitrogen positional exchange: swap a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring. This changes nitrogen placement while retaining formula, connectivity and substituent attachments. The earlier siblings protected carbonyl atoms or whole ring cores, redirected halogen growth, or changed parent allocation. This adds a local alternative without those restrictions. A different lineage exposed only ten such exchanges and missed its score target; here the larger fresh pool and inherited learned selector provide different conditions for testing the same chemical move.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the inherited per-site atom-replacement menu with a direct exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving molecular formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchanges reached 30 evaluations and one new task best; mean score rose 0.007397
finding_summary.insights: This establishes a useful local alternative under the existing pool generator and learned selector, including an observed incumbent gain, while narrowing the utility claim to particular molecular families. Pure exchanges were often neutral or harmful, and all eight evaluated descendants that also contained other edits lost to their best generating parent. Evaluated exposure was concentrated in zaleplon, decoration and median; neither DRD2 nor sitagliptin evaluated an exchange. The sitagliptin score gain therefore cannot be credited to a directly scored positional isomer, and the aggregate trajectory difference does not isolate the contribution of each swap. Three later reversals were correctly rejected as duplicates, demonstrating why operation counts alone overstate retained alternatives. Formula and connectivity preservation also leave the larger chemical limitations intact: the successful nitrogen relocation retained a reactive N-F substituent, the overall emitted stream grew in mean size, and explicit stereochemistry remained absent. The evidence supports testing nitrogen position as a local chemical variable; it does not establish broader ring-topology coverage, synthetic feasibility, or a uniformly favorable exchange neighborhood.
finding_summary.results: The intended positional edit executed correctly. All 536 sampled exchanges preserved formula and connectivity; 435 changed molecular identity and 101 were symmetry identities. Changed exchanges reached 404 pool entries and 30 evaluated molecules. Twenty-nine evaluations retained the exact immediate isomer; one also changed another atom later, while retaining the exchanged nitrogen placement and aromatic ring. The 22 evaluations containing only the exchange gave five source improvements, nine ties and eight losses. One pyridyl nitrogen relocation raised an accepted score from 0.438799 to 0.460926 and established a new final task best. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score increased from 0.544374 to 0.551771, a gain of 0.007397 above the registered 0.002 threshold; population standard deviation decreased from 0.013310 to 0.008223. Two seed macros improved and one declined. Zaleplon and sitagliptin task means rose, while decoration, DRD2 and median means fell. Every task completed its budget, all pools filled, and all admitted identities and feedback joins remained consistent. Recorded total wall time rose from 2,391 to 4,705 seconds, with both greater oracle time and substantially larger diagnostic logs.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and ring-rich products include oversized repeats, reactive substituents, short arene bridges and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied tasks were read, including their Parent trajectories. Each child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure presence ranges from 0.9805 to 0.9908 and aromatic-text presence from 0.9471 to 0.9874; these are fractions of SMILES containing the relevant syntax, not fractions of atoms. The output contains recognizable indole carboxamides, heteroaromatic carbonyl systems, aryl-substituted cyclic amines and complex aza/carbonyl ring assemblies. Across seeds these are distinct families, but leading excerpts repeatedly decorate a limited family within a session. Some products are compact and chemically recognizable; others have repeated aromatic assemblies, unusual heteroatom bonds or severe ring-geometry concerns. Every digest has charged_rate and stereocentre_rate 0.0. Read-only RDKit perception of the supplied SMILES supports the structural descriptions and atom counts below; no synthetic route or three-dimensional feasibility is established by that parsing. Relative to Parent n-213e85380e04, chemistry changes unevenly: one stream grows substantially, another gains cyclic cumulenes, and another contains fewer halogenated products. These are observations of output, not a judgment of mechanism activation.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of medium-sized, alkyl- and methoxy-substituted indole carboxamides connected to pyridyl rings. The first cited product has 25 heavy atoms and three rings, with an indole NH, an amide carbonyl, a pyridyl nitrogen and an N-F bond on the amide. Closely related products change aromatic halogens or nitrogen placement; another high-scoring cited product contains an N-O-Cl appendage on the indole nitrogen. Mean proposal SMILES length is 44.7, ring-closure presence 0.9805, aromatic presence 0.9782 and halogen presence 0.9609. Ordinary aryl carboxamide chemistry is recognizable, but its N-halogen and N-O-Cl variants are less routine synthetic endpoints. The Parent had similar mean length, 44.5, but lower halogen presence, 0.869, and its highest observed record was a bridged carbonyl/heteroaryl assembly at 0.4463521672202675. The child leading family is less topologically elaborate while retaining the same broad aromatic/carbonyl emphasis.
liabilities: N-F on an amide and N-O-Cl on a ring nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound halogens and raise reactivity and handling concerns.

Peripheral variation remains concentrated around one aromatic family; increased aromatic or halogen content alone does not preserve the favorable feature balance, as the duplicated late product shows.
missing_features: The tiny fragments and large repeated-core tail fail to retain the bounded fused-aromatic/carbonyl/heteroaryl arrangement expressed by the leaders.

The highest excerpt offers limited conventional amide N-substitution and alternative core chemistry at the same observed score. Whether removing the reactive substituents can retain that score is unresolved; the data do not identify an additional unseen target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the leading pyridyl N-fluoroamide scores 0.46092619585962435. Within the leading framework, the three cited aromatic F, Cl and Br congeners all receive 0.46092619585962435. The cited alternative pyridyl nitrogen position receives 0.4387992465191 with the rest of that F-bearing framework retained. Thus attachment-relative heteroaromatic nitrogen placement is distinguishable in these observed products, while the particular aromatic halogen is not distinguished in this comparison. Methane receives 0.0, and the late repeated indole/amide assembly receives 9.929836687250678e-11. The visible gradient favors a bounded combination of aromatic surface, carbonyl linkage and heteroaryl placement over fragmentation or wholesale duplication. It does not establish that the chemically unusual N-F bond is generally desirable.

per_task.generated_character: The highest child excerpt contains very large repeated assemblies of aryl and pyridyl rings and conjugated oxygen/nitrogen carbonyl heterocycles. Ethoxy groups, chloromethyl ethers, imine and alkene connectors, cyanates and, in some congeners, aryl nitriles decorate those assemblies. The first two cited products have 91 and 113 heavy atoms, respectively. The final seed-2 excerpt instead contains smaller linked or annulated N-methyl dicarbonyl heterocycles, often bearing N-F, N-Cl or O-Cl groups. Mean proposal SMILES length is 125.3, versus 94.4 in the Parent; child ring and aromatic presence are both 0.9874. This is abundant ring chemistry with substantial repeated-core growth, not broad evidence of ordinary medicinal scaffolds. The complete multi-ring products have difficult synthesis and geometry questions even where their component groups are familiar.
liabilities: Very large repeated aromatic systems create substantial size and synthetic-complexity liabilities; unique strings do not establish useful scaffold breadth.

The leading chloromethyl ethers contain carbon-bound chlorine, while the late O-Cl products contain oxygen-bound chlorine. The leading O-C#N groups are cyanates, distinct from the aryl nitriles present in other cited congeners.
Imine and highly unsaturated connectors, cyanates, chloromethyl ethers, and the late N/O-halogen groups require chemical scrutiny despite their accepted scores.
missing_features: Compact alternative cores retaining the linked heteroaromatic, carbonyl and substituent arrangement are underrepresented in the highest child excerpt, which concentrates on repeated large assemblies.

A chemically coherent version of the useful feature pattern without chloromethyl ethers, cyanates or heteroatom-halogen attachments is not demonstrated at the leading score. The trajectories do not reveal a unique missing decoration or justify a target-specific core.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Methane and the other cited low-end fragments have the observed 0.5 floor. The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle receives 0.548381482770623. A smaller late linked heterocycle receives 0.5775169069797117, and the more elaborate final annulated example receives 0.5974025974025974. The enormous leading assembly receives 0.6114128757484105; a related version without one repeated peripheral carbonyl heterocycle receives 0.6102549646056505. A still larger cited congener receives 0.6112056392805056. These observations favor connected aromatic/carbonyl/heteroatom patterns over tiny fragments but show little score separation among the very large examples. They do not demonstrate that repeated growth itself is useful. The Parent seed-1 peak was 0.6324703199409752 in a much smaller linked heterocyclic family, so the child size increase did not reproduce that observed endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products combine two substituted aromatic ends, an alkene-containing connector, and a saturated five-member diaza ring. Potentially basic amine centres occur in the ring and side chain; some analogues add an amino substituent to the carbon shared by both ring nitrogens. The leading cited molecule has 31 heavy atoms and three rings. Methoxy, methyl, aryl halogen, chloromethyl and sulfanylmethyl substituents recur. A separate high-scoring seed-0 family has a fused aza/sulfur ring framework with an exocyclic C=S bond to ring sulfur. Mean proposal SMILES length is 65.1, with ring presence 0.9851, aromatic presence 0.9782 and halogen presence 0.9874. The aryl/amine framework is recognizable medicinal chemistry; crowded aminal centres and unusual sulfur environments make the full products less routine. Child and Parent seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories are identical; the strongest diaza-ring family therefore persists unchanged, while seed 0 shifts from the Parent spiro-amine family to the sulfur-containing framework.
liabilities: Some diaza-ring carbons bear an additional amino substituent and are attached to both ring nitrogens, creating crowded aminal-like centres whose stability and accessibility need scrutiny.
Chloromethyl and sulfanylmethyl appendages and the ring-sulfur/exocyclic C=S environment are unusual additions to otherwise recognizable amine frameworks.
All digest charge and stereocentre text rates are zero. Neutral SMILES for potentially basic amines do not establish their actual protonation state during evaluation or in solution.
missing_features: The weak fragments and late truncated/dearomatized products lack the complete aromatic-end/amine/geometry combination that the stronger molecules retain.

The substituted diaza-ring and fused sulfur/amine products have no stereochemical specification. Their spatial alternatives and explicit protonation states are not represented in these emitted strings; a score benefit from representing them is not established.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading aminoalkyl/aryl/diaza-ring product receives 0.9914038363125457. In a close enamine-linked comparison, the N-methyl ring analogue receives 0.981088217863691 and the N-formyl analogue 0.48797702544581545, consistent with sensitivity to amine versus amide electronics in that arrangement. The N-sulfanylmethyl product with an aromatic N-aryl end receives 0.9831131294702842; its late analogue with that aromatic ring replaced by a larger nonaromatic unsaturated ring receives 0.08210159005746291. The final truncated product, losing the other aromatic appendage, receives 0.011495655106721757, and the small halogenated aryl fragment receives 0.001421581552029289. The visible gradient supports the combined aromatic appendages, amine character and connecting geometry. It does not say that every nitrogen or additional halogen independently improves the objective.

per_task.generated_character: Higher-scoring child products are medium-to-large fused and bridged aza/carbonyl assemblies containing ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings, phenyl appendages, N-methyl imide/urea-like carbonyl units, unsaturated connections and, in some congeners, an N,O-acetal centre. The first cited molecule has 33 heavy atoms and five perceived rings, including medium-sized nonaromatic rings. The final seed-2 excerpt contains quinoline-like aromatic groups joined to annulated nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl systems. Mean proposal SMILES length is 56.2, ring presence 0.9908 and aromatic presence 0.9828. Halogen presence is only 0.1379, down from the Parent 0.269. These products carry substantial ring chemistry without depending strongly on halogens, but assembling their connected medium rings and defining their stereochemistry would require deliberate synthetic planning.
liabilities: Fused or bridged medium rings, unsaturated ring junctions and N,O-acetal centres introduce geometry, stereochemical and synthetic-planning concerns.
Serial changes can interconvert amine, amide, imide and urea-like nitrogen environments; ring count alone does not describe those functional changes.
The late duplicated aza-dicarbonyl example adds considerable structural complexity without preserving the score of the better compact arrangement.
missing_features: The low-scoring fragments lack the coupled aromatic, cyclic nitrogen and carbonyl arrangement visible in the stronger products.

The leading excerpt gives limited straightforward alternative ring connections retaining that arrangement, and its stereochemical choices remain unspecified. The observed scores do not identify an unseen target scaffold that can be prescribed.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl dicarbonyl heterocycle receives 0.1678386594791329. The leading ethoxyaryl/phenyl/aza-dicarbonyl assembly receives 0.21361011906838706; its close carbon-for-nitrogen ring analogue receives 0.21301048592169716. That small separation supports neither an indiscriminate nitrogen requirement nor a unique missing atom. Ethane receives 0.012461119656980673. A late doubled aza-dicarbonyl assembly receives 0.16555828159251879, while a more compact bridged relative receives 0.20112987335919708. These are compatible with reward for an integrated aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement rather than fragments or unlimited repetition. The Parent highest observed record, an alkyl-pyridyl/large aza-carbonyl ring assembly, receives 0.22405709718343647. The child explores different complicated ring connections without showing a simpler leading chemotype.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family links an N-methyl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle to a halogenated arene with a short aliphatic bridge across nonadjacent aromatic positions. The bridge carries a primary amine and fluorinated carbon centres. The first cited product has 27 heavy atoms; its arene bridge contains three aliphatic carbons, while the second cited product has a shorter two-carbon bridge. These are geometrically constrained bridged arenes. Related products carry O-F, N-O-S or N-O-Cl appendages. The later seed-2 family replaces carbonyl functionality with imino and exocyclic fluoroalkene groups and includes N-fluoroaziridines and cyclic cumulenes. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.9, ring presence 0.9816 and aromatic presence 0.9471. Cumulated-double-bond text presence rises from the Parent 0.0483 to 0.2218. Size stays broadly similar, but unusual ring geometry and bond chemistry are more conspicuous.
liabilities: Very short bridges between nonadjacent aryl positions impose substantial geometric constraints; aromatic SMILES syntax and successful graph parsing do not establish a feasible three-dimensional arene.
O-F, N-O-S/N-O-Cl appendages and an N-fluoroaziridine are reactive or otherwise unusual functional contexts, even when the associated scores are relatively high.

The late examples put cumulated double bonds inside small or medium rings, including a four-member nitrogen-containing ring. This is a ring-geometry concern in addition to the increased cumulated-bond text rate.
The bridge amino/fluoro centres and aziridine substituents create stereochemical choices that the emitted strings leave unspecified.
missing_features: Tiny fragments and large repeated assemblies fail to retain the compact combination of amino functionality, halogenated aromatic surface and polar heterocyclic features visible in the stronger family.

The strongest bridged structures lack evidence of spatially credible, synthetically straightforward ring connections and have no stereochemical specification. Chemically conventional alternatives preserving their useful feature arrangement are underrepresented; no unseen pharmacophore or particular stereoisomer can be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact bridged primary-amine/fluorinated-arene/dicarbonyl product receives 0.5750908973498792, and the shorter bridged analogue with changed substituents receives 0.5321574883498289. Their simultaneous structural changes prevent assigning the difference to one feature. The cited O-F/N-O-S congener still receives 0.5220117218784629, showing that these liabilities are tolerated in that neighborhood. The very large repeated dicarbonyl/polyaryl product receives 1.6758614448245604e-53, and methanethiol receives 2.449867090426732e-23. A distinct compact imino/fluoroalkene product with an N-fluoroaziridine receives 0.5030795275617259, whereas the cited late cyclic-cumulene examples receive 0.21349359802594703 and 0.2408594025924811. The clearest high-scoring family combines bounded size, amino functionality, halogenated aromatic surface and carbonyls, but the alternative family shows that this is not a demonstrated mandatory group list. Parent seed 1 had a primary-aminomethyl/fluorinated-arene/dicarbonyl peak of 0.5845583988949146; the child moves the amine into a constrained bridge without demonstrating a chemical-quality improvement.

The observed chemistry can therefore retain unusual bond environments among its higher-scoring products; element presence alone cannot distinguish them from conventional carbon-bound substituents.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose chemically coherent local alternatives that retain functional-group roles while changing a substituent. Distinguish carbon-halogen chemistry from direct nitrogen/oxygen-halogen chemistry and from extended heteroatom chains; let the same available feedback compare these alternatives without a task-specific substituent list.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc4c(F)c(c3Cl)C(F)C4(C)N)cc2n(C)c1=O bridges nonadjacent aryl positions through two aliphatic carbons. Cn1c(=N)n(S)c(=CF)c2c(C3C(Cl)N3C3=C=CN3F)n3c4cc(CO)c(cc4O)c3c21 contains a cumulated double bond in a four-member nitrogen-containing ring. One proposal stream has cumulated-double-bond text presence 0.2218, compared with its Parent 0.0483. These are actual outputs despite abundant perceived aromatic and ring chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not reliably respect the geometric constraints of short aromatic bridges and cyclic multiple bonds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support ring construction and rearrangement that account for bridge length, attachment separation, ring size and multiple-bond placement. Retain the ability to explore new topology while making spatially credible alternatives available; canonical identity and aromaticity checks alone do not supply this chemical capability.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every supplied digest has stereocentre_rate 0.0. C=C(CNC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F has substituted side-chain and diaza-ring centres, and Cn1c(=O)c2cn(-c3cc4c(F)c(c3Cl)C(F)C(N)(F)C4)cc2n(C)c1=O has substituted amino/fluoro bridge centres. Their strings specify connectivity without choosing the corresponding stereochemical arrangements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not specify stereochemical alternatives for its substituted saturated and bridged structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information when present and support consistent stereochemical specification when graph changes introduce such choices, with identity handling that distinguishes the resulting isomers. The observed absence is a coverage gap; it does not establish that a particular isomer will improve an objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.981088217863691, whereas its N-formyl analogue C=C(NC(CC)c1ccc(OC)c(C)c1)C1(N)N(C=O)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.48797702544581545. The late truncated C=C(CNO)C1(N)N(C)CCN1c1cccc(F)c1F receives 0.011495655106721757. Nitrogen presence alone does not retain the favorable combined arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted chemistry does not consistently preserve a useful combination of aromatic appendages and amine electronics during structural variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make interpretable alternatives available that can vary core geometry while retaining amine class and connected aromatic appendages, and separately expose deliberate conversions between amines and amides. Use observed feedback to identify valuable combinations instead of assuming that all nitrogen-containing fragments are interchangeable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set has mean SMILES length 125.3, versus its Parent 94.4, and its leading repeated aromatic assemblies have very similar observed scores despite markedly different sizes. Elsewhere, CCc1c(C)cc2c(cc(C(=O)NCc3c(C)cc4c(cc(C(=O)Nc5ccc(F)cn5)n4Br)c3C)n2Cl)c1CO receives 9.929836687250678e-11 after repeating an aromatic/amide assembly. Methane, C, also occurs as a zero-score fragment. Neither unlimited growth nor severe fragmentation consistently retains the chemical combinations seen in stronger products.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably maintain coherent molecular size when modifying connected multi-feature structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide structural edits that retain a coherent connected set of functional features without automatically duplicating whole aromatic assemblies or stripping them to tiny fragments. Any size preference should come from general molecular structure and the available feedback, without a fixed formula or size target keyed to an objective.

nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: Recover n-d88727c16484 with its algorithm unchanged: a task-local walk makes the fixed random atom, bond and ring edits from one scored current graph, filters invalid and canonically previously proposed molecules, and evaluates the first announced full batch allowed by tabu memory. A candidate is vetoed only when its signed radius-one motif changes match both inverse signs from the same active source transition. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current graph, even on worsening moves, with the existing canonical tie rule. The independent best archive, bounded balanced inverse-attribute installation, four-step tenure, latest-transition overlap refresh, oldest-first obstruction releases and passive allocation diagnostics all remain in place.
approach.novelty: This is implementation recovery, not a new search mechanism. Normalize the graph-edit result through the existing canonical_molecule helper before it supplies the pending identity and emitted SMILES. The repaired identity reflects the RDKit parse/serialize round trip that the recorded accepted feedback used; this repairs proposal-to-feedback matching without changing the bound same-transition bidirectional tabu mechanism.

nodes.hypothesis: Repair accepted-feedback trace lookup by using the canonical SMILES obtained after reparsing each generated edit, so proposal bookkeeping and returned molecular structure share the same identity used by the recorded feedback.

finding_summary.headline: The repaired walk completes all three seeds while preserving the recorded search behavior.
finding_summary.insights:
The new evidence closes the specific uncertainty left by the recovery run: the identity fix supports the full previously failing seed, beyond the ten batches that could be replayed earlier. Exact preservation of all available successful histories narrows the earlier interruption to proposal-to-feedback identity bookkeeping. The original executable has no completed continuation for the failed task, so this establishes operational recovery and a complete score estimate without establishing a new search advantage. The seed-0 comparison supplied with this replication is the same repaired algorithm, not a separate intervention.

The small spread in macro score also hides task variation: sitagliptin final scores range from 0.4484554129767839 to 0.5903526424693334 across the three seeds. The molecular assessment finds different ring frameworks across the added seeds but persistent reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry, with late trajectories concentrated within related families. Successful identity handling and stable macro performance therefore leave chemical feasibility and useful scaffold coverage unresolved.
finding_summary.results:
The previously failing seed-2 feedback now reaches the correct pending proposal. The repaired walk processes all ten scores in that batch and continues to the full 300-evaluation task budget. Both added seeds complete all five tasks: 3,000 evaluations, 2,900 optimizer outcomes and 290 completed walk steps, with no invalid evaluations, duplicates or unresolved feedback. Replaying the original source still reproduces the exact identity-lookup exception, while the repaired replay matches the formal continuation.

The comparison preserves every one of the 4,310 previously recorded molecule/score entries in normalized order. All fourteen complete task logs are identical to the original runs; the failed prefix differs only in the spelling of one molecular identity, whose returned graph is unchanged. The inherited tabu behavior remains active in the two new seeds: 132 of 3,032 valid novel attempts are vetoed, while 1,577 partial inverse matches reach evaluation and supply 153 selected next states.

Macro final Top-1 is 0.518077929779343 for seed 0, 0.527798815337278 for seed 1 and 0.516876739241218 for seed 2. The complete three-seed mean is 0.5209178281192797, with population standard deviation 0.004890242222897396. The previously incomplete zaleplon task finishes at 0.41003927643747895. These are formal evaluation results; the diagnostic replay makes no oracle calls.

molecular.headline: Additional seeds vary the ring frameworks but retain reactive heteroatoms, dense cages and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: This report covers seeds 1 and 2 of n-9f7c7ec50039. The supplied parent comparison is the same node's existing seed-0 chemistry, not a new parent-to-child chemical intervention. All current tasks have 600 recorded entries and 580 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout; aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.719 to 1.0, and charge and stereocentre token presence are 0.0 throughout. These counters describe SMILES-token presence, not aromatic atom fractions, basicity or stereochemical feasibility. The added seeds span recognizable indole/benzofuran amides, large nitrogen-rich diones, halogenated aromatic amine assemblies, bridged lactams and sulfur-rich cages. This gives moderate diversity across seeds and tasks, although each late trajectory remains concentrated in a related family. Several conventional medicinal fragments are retained, but many high-scoring complete structures have unusual sulfur valence, N-halogen or O-halogen bonds, highly constrained ring junctions or extensive flexible substitution. Rings and aromatic content are abundant; reliable synthetic accessibility and explicit stereochemistry remain the clearer gaps. The more conventional members should not be conflated with the implausible sulfur-rich and densely bridged leaders.

per_task.generated_character: Moderately sized aromatic carboxamides are prominent: seed 1 has ethoxy-, methyl- and thiol-substituted indole anilides, while seed 2 reaches an amino/chloro-substituted benzofuran N-chloroanilide. Later seed-2 molecules replace the fused aromatic core by bridged unsaturated oxygen or sulfur frameworks, retaining an aryl carbonyl-containing linkage. Aromatic-token presence is 0.9569 and halogen presence is 0.6552. The indole anilide is a comparatively plausible synthetic scaffold; chlorinated nitrogen, an aminochloromethyl centre and constrained sulfur cages are less convincing. Relative to the seed-0 aryl-ketone family, these seeds more often retain an amide among their best molecules.
liabilities: N-chloroamide, thiol and aminochloromethyl functionality adds reactivity to an otherwise recognizable aromatic scaffold.
Late bridged unsaturated sulfur structures and N-N linkages have unresolved geometry and synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Broader accessible fused heteroaryl amides preserving the successful carbonyl and aromatic attachment pattern are poorly represented in the late output.
Defined stereochemical alternatives are absent for the aminochloromethyl centre and bridged ring junctions; the supplied molecules cannot establish a required stereoisomer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxamide scores 0.3051048083696145. A conventional substituted indole anilide reaches 0.39905049777278273, near the benzofuran N-chloroamide maximum of 0.41003927643747895. The latter exceeds the seed-0 maximum of 0.3966634883331815, but the visible chemistry does not show that its reactive groups are necessary. A distorted, partially saturated N-hydroxy heterocyclic amide scores only 0.030639811858172862. In a bridged family, chlorine and bromine analogues tie at 0.3900523103411983. Preserving a compact ring/carbonyl arrangement appears more consistently favorable than ring expansion or intricate heteroaryl replacement.

per_task.generated_character: The best seed-2 family consists of large fused nitrogen-rich diones joined to a pyridine-containing oxygen/nitrogen ring system and a branched polyene side chain. It carries a mixed ketal, a butyl group, N-fluoromethyl and N-methylthiomethyl substituents. The fluorine in N-fluoromethyl is carbon-bound, not an N-F bond. Seed 1 instead explores expanded nitrogen heterocycles with imine, ester, alkyne and alkene substituents. All proposals contain aromatic and ring-closure tokens; mean SMILES length is 67.6, reflecting extensive substitution rather than directly measuring molecular size. Compared with the seed-0 best containing N-Br and unusual sulfur, the seed-2 leaders use more conventional valences, although their size, flexibility and mixed functionality remain problematic.
liabilities: Long polyenes, alkynes and mixed acetal functionality introduce isomerism, oxidation or hydrolysis concerns and complicate synthesis.
Large flexible substitution patterns and unspecified stereochemistry reduce confidence in a single accessible molecular shape.
missing_features: Compact versions preserving the recurring fused-dione and heteroaryl attachment pattern are underrepresented among the late high-scoring molecules.
Stable alternatives to the long unsaturated chains and mixed ketal/thioacetal-like substitution are not broadly explored at comparable core geometry.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.548381482770623; a modified, strained fused imino/carbonyl structure scores 0.526081691583997. The expanded seed-2 dione family reaches 0.6092182584436399, below the seed-0 maximum of 0.6161710037174721. The best family tolerates different polyene termini, chlorine addition, and exchanging ketal oxygen substitution for sulfur at exactly 0.6092182584436399. Conversely, disrupting the fused dione with a sulfur-containing partially saturated ring gives 0.5548207448659938. The data favor retaining the heterocyclic arrangement while allowing substantial peripheral variation; they do not establish a single missing substituent.

per_task.generated_character: High-scoring seed-2 molecules combine a methylphenol ring and chlorophenyl group with cyclic tertiary nitrogen, aminomethyl substituents and fused unsaturated sulfur-containing rings. Seed 1 reaches a different rigid polyaryl framework with bromine, aniline, chloromethyl, a sulfur-bound hydroxyl group and a cumulated N=C=S linkage attached to a highly substituted sulfur centre. Aromatic presence is 1.0, halogen presence is 0.9948 and cumulated-double-bond token presence is 0.0879. These seeds replace the seed-0 aziridine-rich family by other aromatic/amine geometries, but retain unusual sulfur bonding and dense ring connectivity. Neutral SMILES do not establish the protonation state of the amines.
liabilities: Hydrogen-bearing multiply bonded sulfur, sulfur-sulfur multiple bonding and highly substituted cumulated systems raise strong stability and synthetic concerns.
Dense polycyclic geometry and heavily substituted aromatic surfaces combine with unspecified stereochemistry; a high score does not establish a feasible bound shape.
missing_features: Accessible cyclic-amine linkers preserving the favorable aromatic spacing without unusual multiply bonded sulfur remain underrepresented in the high-scoring output.
Defined configurations for substituted and fused saturated-ring centres are absent, and the trajectories do not compare chemically relevant protonation alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early acid/amide/sulfonamide derivative scores 0.007468397818197266; the late phenol/amine/sulfur-ring family reaches 0.9148143511682032, compared with 0.8856242185485628 in seed 0. A related family with carbon versus sulfur at a ring position ties at 0.8825461379136246, despite a substantial chemical change. Removing a methylene in the amine-to-sulfur-ring connection gives 0.3331237338421948, and replacing the chlorophenyl partner by a sulfur-containing nonaromatic ring gives 0.04252669549740123. Aromatic placement and amine/linker geometry matter in the shown series, while the score alone does not resolve sulfur plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces bulky bridged nitrogen heterocycles with aromatic ether rings, lactam and ketone groups, an aryl ester, methoxy and alkyl substituents, and an N-N bond. Seed 1 instead explores brominated aryl lactam/carbamate families carrying thioesters and aryl O-Br, followed by more sulfur-rich variants. All proposals contain aromatic and ring-closure tokens; halogen presence is 0.4069. Relative to the smaller seed-0 bridged N-O family, these seeds have more extensive carbonyl, side-chain and ring substitution. Familiar aryl/carbonyl fragments are present, but the full bridged connectivity and reactive O-Br or unusual sulfur groups make apparent synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Aryl O-Br is a reactive hypobromite motif; thioesters and unusual sulfur centres add further stability questions.
Large bridged frameworks with multiple carbonyls and N-N bonds present unresolved ring geometry and substantial synthetic complexity.
missing_features: Less extensively bridged, synthetically accessible frameworks preserving the recurring aromatic and carbonyl arrangement are underrepresented among late molecules.
Stable realizations without aryl O-Br, unusual sulfur or unnecessary N-N connectivity are missing from much of the expanded family; stereochemical specification is absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, an opened carbonyl-rich derivative scores 0.12467972074136988, and the best aryl-ether/bridged-dicarbonyl family reaches 0.20185639717998205. The seed-0 maximum was 0.2107445781802027. Retaining constrained aromatic/carbonyl geometry accompanies the higher scores; larger substitution alone gives no consistent gain. Replacing a bridge nitrogen by hydrogen-bearing sulfur leaves a matched pair at 0.1996542320706886. A late phenol-containing sulfur-rich analogue remains at 0.1881666776148033. The shallow gradient does not identify a unique missing target fragment or distinguish all chemically important heteroatom changes.

per_task.generated_character: Both seeds generate compact but densely interconnected sulfur/nitrogen cages. Seed-1 leaders retain a partially aromatic nitrogen-rich dione with NH, carbon-bound fluorine and a sulfur-linked fluorohydrin, surrounded by multiply bonded sulfur bridges. Seed-2 late products are nonaromatic cages containing ketone, aldehyde, N-fluoroamidine-like functionality and constrained sulfur/carbon unsaturation. Aromatic-token presence is 0.719 over both seeds, but the seed-2 final cages lack aromatic atoms in their displayed graphs. Compared with seed 0, the detailed functional groups and cage topology change substantially while unusual sulfur valence and unresolved stereochemistry persist. These are highly implausible complete synthetic targets despite recognizable carbonyl and nitrogen fragments.
liabilities: Multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and crowded ring junctions raise severe chemical-stability and geometric-feasibility concerns.
Fluorohydrin, aldehyde and N-F functionality introduce further reactivity, while the cage stereochemistry is left unspecified.
missing_features: The sampled high-scoring region lacks a demonstrated accessible framework retaining the favorable carbonyl/nitrogen/fluorinated arrangement without unusual sulfur cages.
Stable alternatives to N-F and sulfur-linked fluorohydrin motifs, together with explicit bridge stereochemistry, are poorly represented in the late output.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An early modified fused dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10 and an already sulfur-rich, N-fluorinated cage scores 1.0546805269255595e-09, so sulfur or fluorine presence alone is not predictive. The seed-1 dione/fluorohydrin cage reaches 0.5903526424693334 versus the seed-0 maximum of 0.48118636011729826. Seed 2 reaches 0.4484554129767839 in its final family. Related expanded ketone or lactone cage variants score 0.01685401516576383 and 0.2536619453071564, respectively. Scores are sensitive to detailed ring size, bond placement and carbonyl/nitrogen environment; the trajectories do not isolate a transferable target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest examples include N-chloroamides, N-F, aryl O-Br, multiply bonded hydrogen-bearing sulfur and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Carbon/sulfur ring variants tie at 0.8825461379136246, and nitrogen/sulfur bridge variants tie at 0.1996542320706886 despite their different chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain stable heteroatom chemistry within favorable molecular arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically conventional carbon, nitrogen, oxygen and ordinary sulfur alternatives while preserving attachment positions. General chemical feasibility must distinguish reactive or unusual bonding that the observed scalar feedback sometimes treats as equivalent.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest has ring-closure presence of 1.0 and stereocentre-token presence of 0.0. High-scoring structures include densely bridged sulfur cages, constrained lactams and substituted saturated ring junctions without explicit configurations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates elaborate ring closures without establishing accessible geometry or stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support accessible fused, spiro and less bridged alternatives, together with stereochemical assignment and variation where applicable. Preserve useful attachment geometry while distinguishing a valid molecular graph from a feasible stereochemical structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Large fused-dione products retain an identical score of 0.6092182584436399 after changing polyene termini, halogen substitution and ketal heteroatoms. Other late families retain bulky aryl/carbonyl frameworks while adding reactive sulfur or brominated substituents.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular growth and peripheral decoration dominate several late families without showing which additions are necessary.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make compact analogues and simpler linkers available alongside growth operations, preserving recurring aromatic, carbonyl and amine arrangements. Equivalent observed scores should permit exploration of structurally simpler and more conventional candidates.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied seeds reach different indole/benzofuran, fused-dione, aromatic-amine and cage structures, yet the high-scoring and final excerpts within each seed repeatedly vary one established framework. A conventional indole amide already reaches 0.39905049777278273, close to the more reactive neighboring family maximum of 0.41003927643747895.
transferable_gaps.gap: Diversity across seeds has not translated into broad accessible alternatives within each late chemical family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand scaffold and linker alternatives around chemically recognizable aromatic/carbonyl/amine patterns, including stable heterocycle replacements, rather than relying mainly on increasingly elaborate local heteroatom and ring changes.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: COWBOYS separates the generative model from the surrogate entirely. A variational autoencoder is trained on the unlabeled corpus and its decoder is frozen, giving a latent space with a known Gaussian prior. A Gaussian process is then fitted not in that latent space but directly on molecular fingerprints and their scores. Generation samples the latent prior tilted by the probability that the molecule it decodes to would beat the current incumbent, using a Markov chain that preserves the prior. The result is that the surrogate steers sampling without ever having to model the latent geometry.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a Tanimoto-kernel Gaussian process on fingerprints as the tilt, and to preconditioned Crank-Nicolson transitions, which is the specific choice that keeps the latent prior invariant no matter how strong the tilt becomes. It requires the same deterministically decoded molecule to be used both for the probability estimate and for submission, so the surrogate is never consulted about a molecule different from the one that gets scored.

nodes.hypothesis: A corpus-trained frozen SELFIES VAE generates de novo molecules through prior-preserving pCN MCMC whose latent target is the standard Gaussian prior multiplied by a task-local fingerprint Tanimoto GP's probability of exceeding the observed incumbent, with the same deterministic decoded molecule used for prediction and submission.

finding_summary.headline: Decoupling the surrogate from the latent space reached 0.433, sixth of thirteen
finding_summary.insights: The design goal is met: the surrogate genuinely steers sampling and the prediction-submission identity never breaks, which is a real integrity property that several latent methods in this round cannot claim. The acceptance rate near 54 percent indicates the chain is mixing rather than sticking. What limits it is that a fingerprint Gaussian process fitted to at most 290 points has to generalise across a space the decoder can reach, and its probability estimates flatten out where the incumbent is already high, which shows as a median score of exactly zero on the hardest objective. Whether a different kernel or an incumbent-relaxation would help is untested, on one seed.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.433 places this sixth. It reached 0.868 on drd2_docking, 0.573 on deco_hop and 0.341 on zaleplon_mpo, with 0.212 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.172 on median_2. Corpus pretraining cut held-out reconstruction loss from 4.225 to 0.161. Every session initialized a fresh Gaussian process on exactly ten scored structures and grew it in steps of ten to 290. Across the five sessions the sampler attempted 36,800 transitions and accepted 19,938, all 145 rounds had nonconstant posterior probabilities, and all 1,450 submitted molecules matched the recorded prediction identity exactly, so no molecule was ever scored that the surrogate had not itself evaluated.

molecular.headline: Sensible aromatic scaffolds with imine and azo linkers the decoder favours over stable bonds
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure is high and consistent at 98 to 99 percent on every objective, and aromatic content runs 67 to 91 percent, so the population sits in real chemical space more often than not. Molecules are moderate at forty-four to forty-seven characters and cumulated double bonds are near zero. The recurring weakness is linker chemistry: imines, amidines and azo groups appear throughout, including among the top scorers, where a stable amide or ether would be expected. That points at the corpus tokenization rather than the sampler, since the tilt has no preference over bond types.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Acyclic imines, amidines and N=N chains appear among the top-scoring molecules on three separate objectives, in positions where an amide or ether would be the ordinary choice.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator favours imine and azo linkers over stable equivalents
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The decoder learned these linkages from the corpus and no part of the pipeline penalises them, since the surrogate scores fingerprints and has no notion of stability. Down-weighting labile linker tokens at the corpus level would shift the whole population without changing the sampler.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On the two objectives where it scores worst, the median across all 290 proposals is zero or near zero while the best is far above it, meaning almost every sample fell in a region the surrogate could not distinguish.
transferable_gaps.gap: the surrogate's tilt flattens once the incumbent is high
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Probability of improving on the current incumbent goes to zero everywhere once the incumbent is strong, which leaves the tilt uninformative and the chain sampling near the raw prior. An acquisition that stays graded above the incumbent would keep the steering alive later in the budget.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly zero across all 290 proposals on every one of the five objectives, including molecules with substituted saturated rings where configuration is defined.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator produces no stereochemistry
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Stereochemical markers are absent from the sequence vocabulary, so this dimension of chemical space cannot be expressed regardless of how well the surrogate steers.

nodes.method_name: COWBOYS: GP-conditioned de novo latent sampling
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact SELFIES VAE from the permitted unlabeled corpus during preparation, then freeze its decoder. Within each independent objective session, fit a Tanimoto-kernel GP directly to the observed molecular fingerprints and scores. Generate new molecules through preconditioned Crank-Nicolson MCMC targeting the Gaussian latent prior multiplied by the GP probability that the deterministically decoded molecule exceeds the observed incumbent. The molecule assessed by the surrogate must be the molecule submitted. Fill the protocol-announced batch with distinct generated structures and update the GP after feedback. The corpus supplies a generative prior, never a ranked molecule library. This follows the decoupled mechanism in [COWBOYS](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v267/moss25a.html). Our hypothesis is that structure-level prediction and immediate Bayesian conditioning can direct scarce labels toward a higher final observed maximum without fitting a reward-dependent neural generator. Success is measured by the benchmark's mean of independent final Top-1 scores.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds fresh molecular graphs from a greedy population of accepted high-scoring molecules. Both mutation sources and crossover partners are drawn from preferred score bands, with uniform choice inside each band and exclusion of the first parent when choosing its partner. A fingerprint Gaussian process trained on every accepted label then selects which generated offspring are evaluated. The implementation already favors strong individual parents, but it does not use molecular similarity when deciding which two parents to recombine.
approach.novelty: Condition the crossover partner choice on similarity to the already selected first parent, using the same fingerprint definition that the Parent already declares. More similar eligible partners receive more of the chosen score band's probability, while the first-parent rule and score-band preference remain intact. This tests whether recombining related high-scoring molecules preserves useful local structure more often. The completed siblings altered core balance and survivor diversity; this experiment changes compatibility of a parent pair without replacing survivors or changing crossover chemistry.

nodes.hypothesis: Within the inherited selected score band, sample a crossover partner with probability proportional to its accepted-molecule fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the already selected first parent.

finding_summary.headline: More similar crossover partners produced more local gains, but lower final scores
finding_summary.insights: The experiment separates selecting related molecules from obtaining more productive chemistry. Similarity enrichment and changed pairings are established, but the smaller parent-relative deficit partly accompanies a weaker reference parent and does not demonstrate stronger absolute offspring. Crossover contributed more local incumbent gains while the inherited mutation stream contributed fewer; mutation is not an unaffected control because new pairings change the accepted population and subsequent random trajectory. Much of the final-score loss came from the second seed's sitagliptin run, so this panel supports negative mean transfer rather than a universal failure of related-parent crossover. Fingerprint relatedness also did not preserve a common core more often: the share of evaluated crossover offspring reusing a generating parent's core fell from 34.25% to 33.00%, while survivor core coverage broadened. The molecular assessment still found repeated large assemblies, reactive halogen connections and strained rings; larger repeated products often offered little score separation from smaller relatives. Thus shared fingerprint features alone did not ensure that the unchanged fragment crossover preserved useful attachment relationships or chemical scale. The conditional-law comparison establishes allocation, but supplies no score for an unchosen partner and no causal attribution for either member of a pair.
finding_summary.results: The intended pairing mechanism changed actual breeding. Of 34,123 partner draws, 33,350 had unequal similarities and used the registered weights; 7,967 choices (23.35%) differed from the passive uniform choice on the same eligible partners and random variate. On nondegenerate states, expected Tanimoto similarity rose from 0.48313 under uniform selection to 0.51979 under the applied law. Actual mean pair similarity rose from the Parent's 0.48309 to 0.51650. The first-parent rule, greedy survival, graph operators and posterior selection remained unchanged. Both runs evaluated 1,679 crossover and 2,671 mutation offspring. Crossover best-parent beats rose from 172 to 176 and sequential incumbent improvements from 75 to 84. Its mean parent-relative deficit narrowed from -0.15687 to -0.13737, but the mean best generating-parent score also fell from 0.43361 to 0.40325, and absolute crossover-offspring score fell from 0.27674 to 0.26587. Raw invalid crossover attempts increased from 123 to 326. Mutation incumbent improvements fell from 143 to 130, leaving fewer total improvements (214 versus 218). The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.54437 to 0.52840, a paired change of -0.01597; seed changes were -0.00054, -0.06139 and +0.01401. All five task means declined, with the largest mean loss on sitagliptin (-0.06334). Every formal task still completed its full evaluation budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic carbonyl and amine families carry reactive halogens, strained connections and repeated large assemblies
molecular.overall_character: All current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task has 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is predominantly aromatic and ring-bearing: aromatic-token rates range from 0.9701 to 0.9874 and ring-closure rates from 0.9805 to 0.9908. Compact fused heteroaromatic amides, aryl-linked saturated amines and quinoline/pyrrole/lactam combinations coexist with very large repeated dione, ester and carbonate assemblies. The most size-expanded task has mean SMILES length 108.2 and maximum 253, while tiny fragments also occur throughout the trajectories. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. This leaves potentially basic nitrogen centres drawn without a solution ionization state and stereogenic bridged or substituted rings without configurations. Diversity is moderate across seed families but often narrow within a leading series. Familiar medicinal fragments are present, yet overall synthetic plausibility is questionable because N-halogen and acyl-halide groups, N-N and N-O connections, strained small rings, peroxides and reactive unsaturation persist.

per_task.generated_character: The leaders are compact fused and bridged aza-aromatic systems with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. Alkyl and ether substitution decorate the ring framework; several leading amides are directly N-fluorinated. A related family contains a conventional N-H amide and a thiophenol substituent, while another has an ordinary sulfur bridge and aryl ketone. Other seeds produce N-chloro amides or cumulated unsaturation in larger heterocycles. The lowest proposals are tiny imine or halogen-containing fragments, and a late elaborated amide product adds another ring/carbonyl connection with a much lower score. Conventional carbonyl fragments are recognizable, but the bridged topology and reactive nitrogen substituents limit synthetic confidence.
liabilities: N-F and N-Cl amides are reactive functionality rather than ordinary aryl halogenation.
Some relatives add thiols, O-Br groups or unusual unsaturation, including a cumulated-double-bond string rate of 0.0816.
Bridged ring arrangements and appended carbonyl rings increase geometric and synthetic complexity.
missing_features: The lowest fragments and over-elaborated products lose the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.

Matched stable nitrogen substituents and ordinary ring connections around the leading framework are incomplete; the N-H amide and conventional sulfide/ketone relatives already show viable alternative chemistry.
Configurations at substituted bridge atoms are unspecified, and cumulated unsaturation in other relatives lacks a demonstrated feasible geometry.

Replacing a ring methyl by methylthio gives 0.4166419114047398 for the same halogen pair, so sulfur addition is not rewarded in that local comparison. A conventional N-H amide relative reaches 0.4254027310763201 and an aryl ketone/sulfide relative reaches 0.42570769607214154; N-fluorination is therefore not universal among the stronger outputs. The more elaborated final amide structure scores 0.015332630870835013, and tiny fragments score 0.0. These observations favor a compact aromatic carbonyl arrangement without isolating one universally required heteroatom bond.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 family contains N-methylated heteroaromatic diones, substituted aza-aromatic ester groups and imine-containing unsaturated side chains with oxygen-linked alkynes. Some members join multiple copies of these motifs through branched carbon or ether-containing connections. nodes.method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and samples local atom, bond, path and ring edits, including a direct exchange of aromatic nitrogen and carbon that preserves molecular formula. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and submits the first full batch admitted by its structural memory. The highest-scoring accepted neighbor becomes the next current molecule even after a tie or loss, while a separate archive keeps the best observation. Every selected transition currently installs short-lived inverse motif restrictions, regardless of whether that transition improved its source. A later neighbor is vetoed when opposite signed restrictions match the same earlier transition.
approach.novelty: Give new memory credit only to a selected transition that strictly improves its actual source score. Tied and worsening winners still become current and age existing memory, but install or refresh no restrictions. This tests whether protecting locally unsuccessful moves unnecessarily blocks fresh variations that reverse their motifs. Earlier siblings refined which motif matches cause a veto, repaired identity bookkeeping, changed local chemistry or reweighted edit operators; none conditioned restriction installation on the individual selected winner's observed gain. The Parent's aromatic nitrogen exchange remains part of the tested method.

nodes.hypothesis: Install and refresh inverse-motif restrictions only when the selected actually accepted neighbor has a strictly higher score than its recorded source; tied and worsening selected transitions still move and age the walk but receive no new memory credit.

finding_summary.headline: Selective memory credit admitted 74 scored neighbors, but lowered the panel mean
finding_summary.insights: The experiment establishes that protecting nonimproving moves can block useful fresh variations: newly admitted methyl removal and aryl-fluorine removal both produced immediate archive gains. It also rules out an unexercised gate, missing feedback or changed restriction tenure as explanations for the negative panel result. Those useful cases were sparse, and overall source-improvement frequency and positive-gain magnitude fell. The archive improved slightly more often, but its total improvement was smaller. This narrows the question to the search value of the restrictions: withholding credit based on one move's local gain does not reliably identify protection that is expendable on this panel. Whether protecting nonimproving moves helps diversification remains unresolved because the passive comparison cannot reproduce an alternative walk or score excluded candidates. Preserved overlap provenance matters in practice: an older improving pair survived a skipped refresh and blocked a candidate that unconditional credit would admit. Thus the gate does not create a universal admissibility superset. The supplied molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur connections and dense ring systems alongside recognizable aromatic/carbonyl and amine families; the changed allocation supplies no evidence that chemical feasibility improved.
finding_summary.results: All 184 tied or worsening selected moves skipped memory installation, omitting 719 attributes while retaining 984 attributes from improving moves. On the Child's recorded history, unconditional credit would veto 188 novel draws; the actual gate vetoed 115. This admitted 74 candidates across all fifteen task sessions, while preserved older provenance caused one additional veto in the opposite direction. Twenty newly admitted candidates became next states. Fourteen improved their source score, thirteen tied and forty-seven worsened it; only two immediately improved the archive. The three-seed macro mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.501486, a paired change of -0.020273, against the registered requirement of +0.002. Two seeds declined and one improved. Task means improved for zaleplon and median_2, but declined for deco_hop, DRD2 and sitagliptin, with the largest loss in DRD2. All runs completed their full budgets and batches.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyl and amine families persist, with small fused rings, reactive heteroatom bonds and sulfur-rich cages
molecular.overall_character: All supplied Child and Parent trajectory files were read; all five objectives are covered. Each Child task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. Ring-closure and branch-token rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token rates are 0.9793, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 and 0.7839 in the supplied task order; mean SMILES lengths are 45.9, 68.6, 68.6, 61.8 and 63.4. These are substantial connected ring-bearing compounds, ranging from comparatively compact indole/carbonyl derivatives to bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, aryl polyamines, expanded heterocycles and densely connected sulfur cages. The token rates describe strings containing those features, not aromatic atom fractions or chemically perceived ring counts. Diversity is moderate across seeds and frameworks, but many leading examples are close local analogues. The chemistry changes relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc without resolving its recurring feasibility problems. Ordinary amides, ethers, amines and aromatic rings coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, peroxide connections, unusual sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and demanding ring junctions. Every task has charge-token and stereocentre-token rates of 0.0; this leaves stereogenic relationships unspecified and does not imply that the amines cannot protonate. Apparent synthesis and medicinal quality are therefore questionable despite recognizable useful fragments. Score comparisons below are observations from the provided trajectories, not new scores, binding-mode assignments or claims about hidden objective requirements.

per_task.generated_character: The relatively compact leading molecules retain an aromatic core and a carbonyl connection to another aromatic ring. The strongest seed-2 example is a benzofuran-like system fused to a small saturated carbocycle bearing a primary amine, with a methyl group and an arylmethyl ketone whose terminal ring carries an N-chloro amino group. Seed 0 instead produces an ethoxy/methyl aromatic framework fused to small carbocycles, linked through an ordinary amide to an aminoaryl group; nearby variants contain benzothiophene or aza-aromatic rings and hydroxylamine functionality. Seed 1 retains an ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The latter has recognizable conventional synthetic connections, whereas the small fused rings and reactive substituents complicate other leaders. Lower examples replace the carbonyl connection with a saturated heteroatom-rich carbon, disrupt aromaticity or join a thioester to an expanded unsaturated sulfur ring. Late molecules retain the carbonyl families while adding further sulfur and N-O chemistry.
liabilities: N-Cl and N-O functionality introduces reactivity concerns distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogens.
Small fused carbocycles and later densely connected sulfur-containing rings make strain and practical synthesis uncertain.
Free thiol and hydroxylamine functionality adds potential oxidation or metabolic liabilities in some otherwise recognizable aromatic carbonyl compounds.
missing_features: The weak carbonyl-replaced and ring-expanded derivatives lack the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement present in the stronger families.
Stable matched analogues around the strongest small-ring and N-chloro structures remain incomplete, although a conventional indole amide already supports a nearby score.
Configurations at substituted saturated ring positions remain undefined; the strings do not establish feasible ring-junction geometry.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored current molecule by sampling local graph edits, sanitizing and normalizing their identities, rejecting duplicates and submitting the first full batch allowed by its inverse-motif memory. It chooses the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even after a worsening move and keeps a separate best archive. Element substitutions currently change only one atom, so exchanging the positions of an aromatic nitrogen and a carbon needs an intermediate graph and another round of feedback. The repaired identity join and the established memory lifecycle are part of this Parent.
approach.novelty: Add a direct aromatic nitrogen relocation: exchange a pyridine-like ring nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon within the same aromatic six-member ring. This changes where the nitrogen sits while retaining atom count, molecular formula, substituent attachment positions and the ring framework. The exchange becomes an additional option at either participating atom in the existing atom-change menu. Earlier siblings filtered sulfur or ring closures, removed whole branches, or assigned tetrahedral configurations; none directly moved a ring heteroatom while preserving composition. Their mechanisms are not combined with this one.

nodes.hypothesis: Extend the existing change_atom neighborhood with a direct two-site exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, producing formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers without an evaluated single-substitution intermediate.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen relocation reached ten scored positional isomers, but the panel gain missed its target
finding_summary.insights: The neighborhood extension is demonstrably usable: the ten evaluated products cannot be reached by any single legacy element substitution from their recorded sources. Unlike the earlier configuration-only experiment, nitrogen relocation changes both the motifs seen by tabu memory and the measured source scores. This rules out identity-only or score-invisible activation as the explanation for the limited panel benefit. Exposure is sparse and local outcomes are mixed: only ten of 4350 evaluated neighbors are exchanges, and most lose to their source. One selected deco_hop exchange leads into later archive improvements, but the whole walk and its random draws also change, so those later gains cannot be assigned to nitrogen placement alone. The evidence supports positional-isomer accessibility and score sensitivity, while the preregistered overall score benefit is refuted for this panel. The molecular assessment still finds the Parent-like aromatic/carbonyl families alongside reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual sulfur and dense cages; formula conservation by itself has not established better medicinal or synthetic quality.
finding_summary.results: Ten fresh formula-preserving nitrogen positional isomers reached evaluation from thirteen sampled exchanges. All ten changed local signed motifs; three improved their source score and seven worsened it, with no ties. Three became subsequent walk states and one immediately improved the best archive. Every sampled exchange preserved atom count, bonds, molecular formula and qualifying-ring aromaticity. The three-seed macro mean rose from 0.520918 to 0.521759, a paired gain of 0.000841, below the required 0.002. One seed improved, one declined slightly and one was unchanged. The largest task change was deco_hop in the improving seed; DRD2 and sitagliptin endpoints were unchanged in all seeds.
