molecular.headline: Parent-like aromatic carbonyl and amine families retain reactive heteroatoms, unusual sulfur bonding and dense cages
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. All current proposals carry ring-closure tokens; aromatic-token rates range from 0.7184 to 1.0 and mean SMILES lengths from 46.2 to 69.9. The output stays within substantial ring-bearing molecules, from relatively compact indole or benzofuran carbonyl compounds to bulky decorated heterocycles, aryl amines and highly bridged sulfur-rich cages. The main leading families largely recur in the parent. There is moderate diversity across seeds but strong local concentration among closely related ring frameworks. Ordinary amides, thioethers and amines coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O connections, peroxides and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional substituents. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. These strings therefore do not specify stereoisomers at possible stereogenic centres, and their neutral forms do not establish the solution ionization of basic amines. Chemical plausibility remains questionable primarily because of local bonding, ring geometry and reactivity, rather than an absence of ring or aromatic chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The leading benzofuran-like molecule has methyl groups, a thiol, an amino-chloromethyl substituent and an N-chloro aryl amide. Another strong family is a comparatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. A benzothiophene-like aryl ketone with an aminomethoxy group leads the current seed-0 molecules. More bridged relatives contain O/N connections and partially saturated carbon rings; later examples introduce unusually substituted sulfur or N-N functionality. The low molecules disrupt an aromatic ring, replace the carbonyl connection or add more flexible heteroatom-rich chains. The straightforward indole and benzothiophene families are plausible synthetic starting points, while the reactive and bridged relatives are less convincing as stable medicinal compounds.
liabilities: N-Cl amides and amino-chloromethyl groups introduce reactive bonds beyond ordinary aryl chlorination.
N-F/N-O groups, thiols, unusual sulfur coordination and N-N connections appear in other members.
Dense ring closures and altered aromaticity can make practical synthesis and geometry uncertain.
missing_features: Low ring-expanded or carbonyl-replaced structures lack the intact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement retained by the stronger molecules.
A systematic set of stable N-H amide and ordinary ring alternatives around the leading framework is incomplete, although several such relatives already score closely.
Substituted bridge atoms and partly saturated ring relationships remain stereochemically undefined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro benzofuran-like amide scores 0.41003927643747895 and the ordinary indole carboxanilide reaches 0.39905049777278273. A bridged N-chloro amide scores 0.3923638265355735, while its N-H amide relative scores 0.3816990444462938. Conventional amide chemistry is therefore compatible with a nearby score, without proving that chlorine removal is neutral in every local context. Another bridged N-H amide family scores 0.3900523103411983 with either carbon-bound chlorine or bromine and 0.385823971421255 without that halogen. Carbonyl-replaced or ring-disrupted low examples score 0.03343008011310944 and 0.021532846118034143. The higher scores associate with compact aromatic/carbonyl organization. Parent seed 1 and seed 2 retain the same best structures and scores. Current seed 0 reaches 0.393567030299894 with the benzothiophene-like ketone, versus parental 0.3966634883331815 with a more unusual sulfur-containing framework.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are bulky decorated aryl/aza-heterocyclic compounds bearing carbonyl and thiocarbonyl groups, imines, an amino-fluoroalkyl connection and a long mixed ether/thioether chain. A multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre connects another side chain; N-bromo and terminal sulfur-chlorine variants are present. The final seed-2 family instead combines a heteroaromatic dione with an unsaturated carbon chain and a fused aza/ether ring carrying acetal-like substitution. The changed seed-1 family contains a cyano-substituted amidine, heteroaromatic rings, a thioester and an O-F substituent. Recognizable fragments abound, but long flexible appendages and reactive heteroatom bonds weaken synthetic and stability plausibility.
liabilities: Multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur is not an ordinary thioether or sulfone linkage.
N-Br, S-Cl and O-F bonds introduce reactive chemistry in different families.
Long mixed ether/thioether chains, unsaturation and branching increase flexibility and synthesis complexity without a demonstrated local advantage for several extensions.
missing_features: The lower altered-ring molecules lack the same retained aromatic heterocyclic organization as the stronger decorated families.
Matched simpler relatives with conventional stable linkers are incomplete; equal scores across many peripheral changes do not show a need for N-bromination, long-chain extension or additional sulfur.
Side-chain configuration, imine geometry and acetal-like centres remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated structure scores 0.6161710037174721. Multiple relatives share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite extending alkyl groups, adding side-chain branching or replacing N-methyl with N-bromo. Two final aza/ether-ring variants retain 0.6092182584436399 despite different oxygen/sulfur substitution. Sulfur-rich rings and linkers recur, including sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds and multiply bonded sulfur carrying additional carbon or nitrogen connections. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent trains a recurrent SMILES language model on an unlabeled molecular corpus and starts each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch supplies its highest-scoring half, joined by the strongest eligible earlier elites from a memory of thirty-two accepted molecules. Historical examples keep their original strings and scores and receive diminishing weights according to earlier fitting exposure, with the total current and historical coefficient shares preserved. The policy fits squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, with each positive target independently capped at zero. It takes the inherited clipped Adam updates and retains the final policy. Complete SMILES are then sampled directly from that policy, and the first chemically valid, canonically novel draws fill the announced batch. Extra valid novel draws from those same calls are discarded.
approach.novelty: Add a quota of one emitted molecule per ring scaffold within each existing sampling call. The first eligible member of a scaffold is admitted in sample order; later members in that call are skipped. A refill starts a fresh allowance, so a productive scaffold can still contribute again without a global diversity ban. This moves core allocation to the point where freshly generated molecules actually reach evaluation. The earlier sibling diversified retained historical memory, where most protected alternatives never reached a later fitting update and the mean gain missed the meaningful threshold. Other siblings changed the prior or learning rule. None tested a quota on the direct emitted stream. This experiment keeps the current strong replay and target-ceiling stack and measures which sampled core alternatives gain emission. The Parent also improved through peripheral analogues, so losing productive local substitutions is a concrete risk; more core names alone will not establish useful search.

nodes.hypothesis: Within each existing direct-policy sampling call, admit at most the first valid canonically novel molecule for each successfully extracted nonempty atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko scaffold, resetting the scaffold allowance at the next refill call and leaving acyclic or extraction-fallback identities under inherited admission.

finding_summary.headline: The quota broadened evaluated scaffold coverage but lowered final scores despite earlier progress.
finding_summary.insights:
This resolves the earlier uncertainty about whether protected alternatives ever reach useful downstream opportunities. Here, all 264 locally added families were scored, and 111 of their molecules entered fitting, making 212 training appearances, including 101 historical replay appearances. Direct admission therefore carried diversification through evaluation and learning. That propagation was insufficient for a final-score benefit. The 337 calls without a quota opportunity reproduced their local no-quota choices exactly, and paired behavior agreed through the first intervention in every session, narrowing the change to admission and the subsequent feedback it altered.

The result supports a tradeoff between early progress and later refinement. The parent obtained fifteen actual incumbent gains from repeated-core analogues, while the child gained only six incumbents from its locally added families. These are observations from separate completed trajectories, so they cannot price the child’s unscored rejected molecules or establish that those particular rejections caused the endpoint loss. The chemical assessment helps explain why counting cores is insufficient: productive attachment positions and combinations of peripheral groups remained uneven despite broader ring coverage. The number of evaluated molecules with potential tetrahedral centres rose from 846 to 1,145, with no assigned configurations in either cohort; the quota supplied neither configuration control nor a guarantee of preserving useful functional roles.

The open question is whether broader early coverage can coexist with sufficient sampling of productive peripheral analogues to retain late improvements. The AUC gain makes that distinction worth testing, while the lower final score rules out treating increased family coverage alone as evidence of better search.
finding_summary.results:
The admission mechanism executed correctly in all 497 sampling calls. It rejected 459 otherwise novel repeat-core draws before capacity and produced no repeated ring core within a call; the parent emitted 460 such repetitions. Against equal-sized choices from the same actual draws, 154 calls gained a total of 264 family slots: 259 ring-core appearances and five acyclic singleton appearances. Every added family reached evaluation, and six of those molecules improved the incumbent. Across complete runs, distinct evaluated ring cores increased from 2,813 to 3,079, while the largest occupancy of one core in a session fell from 160 molecules to 44. Total strict incumbent improvements nevertheless fell from 149 to 120.

The three-seed mean final score decreased from 0.522705 to 0.508379, a paired change of −0.014326 against the required +0.002 benefit. Seed changes were +0.002392, −0.018880 and −0.026492. All five task means declined, although the DRD2 endpoint difference was only about two millionths near the score ceiling. Recorded mean AUC increased from 0.405593 to 0.427858; about 94% of that aggregate increase came from DRD2, mainly its much earlier progress in seed 2. All fifteen sessions completed their budgets. Batches needing refills increased from 16 to 33, and measured generation time increased from 24.75 to 37.02 seconds. The utility falsifier is triggered; the verified admission mechanism remains confirmed.

molecular.headline: Broad, ring-rich medicinal chemistry; productive attachment patterns and stereochemical definition remain uneven.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks and all three seeds were read, including the Parent trajectories. Each task contains 900 evaluated records, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. Passive RDKit inspection of the 4,350 Child proposals finds 4,350 parseable, single-component molecules, 4,303 containing rings and 4,199 containing aromatic rings. The typical proposal has 26 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The digest's ring-closure rates are 0.9828–0.9943 and aromatic-marker rates are 0.9391–0.992; these are fractions of SMILES containing markers, not fractions of atoms. Aromatic amides, sulfonamides, fused nitrogen heterocycles, arylpiperazines and arylpiperidines are well represented. Most recognizable small-molecule families are plausibly makeable, while the tails include simple inorganic species, oversized polyaromatics or peptides, and unusual nitrogen functionality. Drug-likeness is moderate because plausible medicinal frameworks coexist with substantial size, flexibility and substitution liabilities; no synthesis route or experimental property was established. Structural breadth is real: the evaluated proposals contain 3,079 distinct atom/bond-typed nonisomeric Murcko ring scaffolds versus 2,813 in the Parent. Functional roles and productive substitution patterns remain much more specific than these scaffold counts. RDKit identifies potential tetrahedral centres in 1,145 Child proposals, versus 846 Parent proposals, with zero assigned centres in either; all task digest stereocentre-marker rates are also zero. This is missing configuration coverage, not evidence that a particular stereoisomer would score better. Counts retain repeated identities across seeds. Reproducible passive descriptors, input hashes and recorded-score comparisons are saved in r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.py and r0012-05-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json beside this report.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have a median of 24 heavy atoms, three rings and three aromatic rings. They are chiefly aromatic amides: acetamido benzodiazines, benzimidazole-containing systems, lactams, benzylamides and diaryl ether carboxamides carrying amidines. The leading acetamido benzodiazine/phenethyl structures have 22 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, with ordinary amide and carbon–carbon attachment chemistry that looks synthetically plausible. Other proposals extend into large peptides and densely fused polycycles. Evaluated ring-core diversity is 604 versus the Parent's 539, while the recognizable high-scoring chemical vocabulary remains aromatic carbonyl/nitrogen chemistry.
liabilities: Large peptide extensions and highly substituted polyaromatics impose much greater size or conformational burden than the leading compact amides; extra amide or ring content alone does not retain the observed score.
Amidines change ionization and hydrogen-bonding character relative to neutral aromatic amides. Their presence is not equivalent to retaining the same nitrogen functionality.
The saturated and polycyclic tail includes unresolved tetrahedral configurations: 178 proposals contain potential tetrahedral centres and none are assigned.
missing_features: Consistent assembly of the compact aromatic amide environment is missing from many proposals: heteroarenes and carbonyls are available, but the useful combination of size, attachment position and nitrogen role is often lost during elaboration.

The leading benzodiazine positional variants do not reveal a productive direction beyond their shared score. The stronger pyridyl ether/carboxamide combinations observed in the Parent are absent from the Child's leading examples.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; four acetamido benzodiazine positional variants reach the same 0.4428306005333078. The upper recorded-score quartile occupies 20–29 heavy atoms, whereas the lower quartile spans 1–49. A fluorine-only molecule scores 0.0 and the cited 44-heavy-atom peptide extension scores 6.353312339014414e-28. Among final proposals, the amidinoaryl pyrrolidine amide scores 0.3173316605218366, but adding another aryl carboxamide gives 0.0004762091843102436. These observations favor a bounded combination of aromatic extent, nitrogen placement and carbonyl attachment, rather than monotonic elaboration. The Parent's seed-2 pyridyl ether carboxanilide at evaluation 271 scores 0.5, whereas the Child's amidine-bearing diaryl ether example reaches 0.42749549733373915; the Child seed-0 best improves on the Parent's 0.43351949803907636. The chemistry changes are uneven across seeds, and the examples do not identify a unique missing target structure.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals are especially aromatic and halogen-rich: medians are 31 heavy atoms, four rings and four aromatic rings, and the digest halogen-marker rate is 0.8747. The leading family is methoxy-substituted anilino quinazoline chemistry with a phenyl, furyl or thienyl appendage and fluorinated aniline. The best example has 27 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings; its exocyclic NH, ring nitrogen acceptors and ether are recognizable, synthetically plausible medicinal chemistry. The full trajectories also contain hydrazone-rich and other nitrogen-heteroaromatic families, polyaryl ethers and sulfones. Observed ring cores number 505 versus 355 in the Parent, but all twelve digest-best entries remain close relatives of the anilino fused-diazine family.
liabilities: Extensive aromatic surface and repeated halogenation create a plausible solubility burden; neither adding fluorine nor adding more aromatic rings consistently improves the recorded score.
The lower tail includes an activated alkene flanked by sulfonyl and ester functionality, which deserves a different reactivity reading from the stable aromatic ether examples.
Simple inorganic or very small nitrogen-containing proposals are chemically valid species but poor evidence of useful molecular construction for this observed family.
missing_features: The strongest Child family lacks the coordinated alkoxy decoration of the stronger Parent example. The missing evidence concerns successful combinations and positions of appendages, rather than access to aromatic rings, fluorine or ether groups individually.

The digest-best set contains no comparably successful alternative arrangement of the anilino donor and heteroaromatic acceptors outside this close fused-diazine family. The observed gradient provides no basis for prescribing extra saturation or basic amines.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The difluoroanilino phenylquinazoline scores 0.6460611381594701, and its trifluoro analogue scores 0.6456917428325912. Furyl and thienyl replacements each score 0.6439546794971287; these substitutions mostly preserve the local plateau. A four-aromatic-ring polyaryl ether/methylsulfone scores only 0.30122048819527814, showing that aromatic ring count alone does not explain the ordering. The vinylsulfone/unsaturated-ester example scores 0.2948214550303749, while even nitrate receives 0.5004402958788305, so a middle-range numerical value does not establish a coherent organic framework. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-273 best is a more extensively alkoxy-decorated anilino phenylquinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The Child preserves the general core but does not reproduce that higher-scoring peripheral arrangement among its best molecules.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals combine saturated amine rings with aromatic groups: median size is 27 heavy atoms, with four rings and two aromatic rings. The leading 24-heavy-atom arylalkyl piperidine and 29-heavy-atom arylpiperazine contain a neutral, structurally basic aliphatic nitrogen connected to hydrophobic aromatic regions. Other strong examples combine piperazines or benzazepines with phenols, methoxy groups, aniline, fluorinated heteroarenes and flexible alkyl linkers. These simple cyclic-amine families look conventionally makeable. Seed-2 later proposals also explore fused and bridged phenolic polycycles with greater configurational complexity. The Parent already generated strong arylpiperazines, benzazepine-linked amines and amino ketones; cyclic basic nitrogen is established chemistry in both cohorts.
liabilities: Several near-ceiling molecules have long flexible linkers and substantial hydrophobic aromatic surface. Their recorded scores do not resolve conformational, solubility or selectivity liabilities.

The fused and bridged phenolic alternatives can contain multiple unresolved stereocentres, making their synthetic and conformational interpretation less definite than the simple piperidine or piperazine examples.
Sulfonylation, acylation and direct aromatic attachment change nitrogen basicity. A low charged-SMILES rate does not mean the high-scoring neutral representations lack protonatable amines.
missing_features: No absent objective-required ring or amine motif is demonstrated: the highest-scoring proposals already contain the strongly associated cyclic aliphatic nitrogen and aromatic groups.

Configurational definition is missing from the complex saturated alternatives. There are 420 proposals with potential tetrahedral centres and zero assigned centres; the present scores do not establish whether stereochemical control would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading arylalkyl piperidine scores 0.9999999478348883, and the arylpiperazine scores 0.9999999026461167. All 218 upper-quartile proposals match the passive neutral amine heuristic requiring saturated carbon neighbours, compared with 15 of 218 lower-quartile proposals; this is a structural classification, not a pKa calculation. The cited sulfonylated piperidine/heteroaryl amide scores 1.9828327575562915e-05: having the ring nitrogen present is insufficient when it is incorporated into a sulfonamide. The nitro/carboxylic-acid heteroarene scores 1.8588450134335675e-05. The association is not an absolute requirement: a late nitrogen-free phenolic polycycle scores 0.6250165349329656. Both Parent and Child best examples already approach the observed numerical ceiling, so these records do not establish another objective-required pharmacophore as missing.

per_task.generated_character: The typical proposal has 23 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The strongest recurring chemistry is arylsulfonyl piperazine: naphthalene or indole on the sulfonyl side, with methyl, propyl, aryl, acyl or another sulfonyl group at the opposite nitrogen. The leading N-methyl naphthalenesulfonyl piperazine has 20 heavy atoms and three rings. Benzodioxane-related arylsulfonyl compounds and bis-sulfonyl piperazines add oxygenated ring environments. These motifs have familiar, plausible assembly chemistry. Broader trajectories include ordinary amides and heterocycles as well as very small acyclic species. The Child has 745 observed ring cores versus 732 in the Parent.
liabilities: Acylation or sulfonylation at the opposite nitrogen changes the molecule's ionization and hydrogen-bonding pattern. These forms should not be treated as equivalent cyclic amines.
The low tail includes an organic azide and an N-hydroxy trichloromethyl formamide, chemically unusual contexts compared with the leading arylsulfonyl series.

Multiple sulfonyl groups can add substantial polarity and mass, while small underdecorated heterocycles lose much of the aromatic attachment context; neither extreme is a reliable stand-in for the stronger combination.
missing_features: Successful joint control of aryl attachment position and opposite-nitrogen substitution remains incomplete. Piperazine and sulfonamide availability is already clear, but closely related local environments carry distinct scores.

The stronger Parent combination of heteroaryl and oxygenated aryl groups on a bis-sulfonyl piperazine is absent from the leading Child entries, although other bis-sulfonyl piperazines are generated. A universal preference for leaving one nitrogen basic is not supported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading naphthalenesulfonyl piperazine scores 0.23735633163877068; relocating the naphthalene attachment gives 0.22138416879776573 with the same heavy-atom and ring counts. Replacing the opposite N-methyl substituent with propyl gives 0.20874143036171652, while an N-acyl analogue gives 0.20421640473731204. Sulfonamides occur in 131 of 218 upper-quartile proposals and 9 of 218 lower-quartile proposals. Small urea scores 0.008404548427654986 and allyl azide scores 0.0. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-280 heteroaryl/benzodioxole bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, above the Child's leading simpler monosulfonyl example. Thus the observed preference concerns assembled aromatic/sulfonyl/nitrogen environments, not merely a free basic nitrogen or any sulfur-containing molecule.

per_task.generated_character: This is chemically heterogeneous output with median size 24 heavy atoms, three rings and two aromatic rings. The leading 26-heavy-atom molecule is a branched, fluorinated anilide/oxamide containing three amide linkages and one aromatic ring; its branched centre has no assigned configuration and its nitrogens are amidic, not a free aliphatic amine. Another strong 25-heavy-atom molecule combines a methyl benzoate, arylsulfonyl group and aryl-substituted cyclic amidine. A separate 20-heavy-atom example has a guanidine-substituted, phenyl-bearing partially saturated fused ring system. Other candidates carry nitrogen heterocycles, thioamides, esters and guanidines. These are recognizable but chemically distinct families, with more demanding or ambiguous synthesis in the complex polycyclic and peptide tail. Observed ring cores number 780 versus the Parent's 774.
liabilities: Oversized polyaromatics, lipid-like chains and peptide elaborations add extensive size or flexibility and occur among the zero-score examples.

The leading branched compound masks its nitrogen functionality as amides, while other strong examples use cyclic amidines or guanidines. These represent different ionization tendencies and donor/acceptor arrangements, rather than interchangeable nitrogen counts.
Later proposals can retain fluorinated aromatics, carbonyls and heterocyclic nitrogens yet score very poorly; these isolated motifs are insufficient evidence of the useful complete molecular context.
missing_features: Repeated production of compact molecules with a successful joint carbonyl, nitrogen and sulfonyl arrangement is missing from much of the later output. These groups are individually plentiful, while their location and chemical role vary substantially.

The branched leading anilide and the guanidine-bearing fused-ring example lack stereochemical definition. In total, 290 proposals have potential tetrahedral centres and none are assigned; objective benefit from assigning them remains unmeasured.

The strongest Parent's compact arylsulfonyl/acetylamine arrangement is absent from the Child's leading examples. The records do not justify replacing this observed assembly gap with a prescribed benchmark-specific fragment.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The branched anilide/oxamide scores 0.3085499097640706, the sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester 0.3034617343186778, and the guanidine-containing fused-ring example 0.2711448282680827. The upper recorded-score quartile has a median of 22 heavy atoms versus 31 in the lower quartile; the cited 63-heavy-atom polyaryl molecule, long-chain lipid-like molecule and peptide all score 0.0. Size alone is insufficient: the final 24-heavy-atom heterocyclic carboxylic acid/amide scores 7.082584041248927e-09. Adding fluorines to the strong sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester gives 0.18136420222115457. The Parent's seed-2 evaluation-291 best, a compact fluorinated arylsulfonyl/acetylamine arrangement, scores 0.32609684308650033; both cohorts share the Child's evaluation-87 best molecule at 0.3085499097640706. The evidence favors particular compact polar arrangements, but cannot establish one required fluorinated ring, free-amine motif or target-like scaffold from these chemically different winners.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited naphthalenesulfonyl positional isomers have identical heavy-atom and ring counts but scores 0.23735633163877068 and 0.22138416879776573. Additional fluorination of a cited sulfonyl cyclic-amidine ester changes 0.3034617343186778 to 0.18136420222115457. Free cyclic aliphatic amines characterize one high-scoring cohort, while arylsulfonyl nitrogen and largely nonbasic aromatic systems characterize others. Evaluated ring-scaffold breadth already exceeds the Parent's, so missing rings or a universal missing basic amine would misdescribe the output.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator reaches many frameworks but does not reliably reproduce the local attachment patterns that distinguish useful complete molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs chemically distinguishable choices for attachment position, bond order, carbonyl or sulfonyl connectivity, and nitrogen conjugation while changing a framework or appendage. It should retain access to both basic and nonbasic nitrogen environments and let accepted molecular feedback determine which combinations to reproduce, without a fixed preferred ring or functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A cited amidinoaryl amide scores 0.3173316605218366, while its more extensively aryl-amide-decorated relative scores 0.0004762091843102436. A compact 26-heavy-atom branched anilide/oxamide scores 0.3085499097640706, while a 63-heavy-atom polyaryl example and a long-chain lipid-like example score 0.0. At the opposite extreme, fluorine-only and small urea proposals provide little assembled organic context. Other high-scoring molecules retain longer aromatic-alkyl amine architectures, so the observations do not support one universal size optimum.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not show reliable control of complete-molecule size and polar-group assembly during elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator should support controlled additions, removals and rearrangements of appendages while maintaining a coherent full molecular context. Joint size, flexibility and polar-group combinations need to remain learnable from supplied scalar feedback; blanket shortening, a shared atom-count cutoff or indiscriminate heteroatom addition would erase distinctions visible in these trajectories.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All five digest stereocentre-marker rates are 0.0. Passive RDKit perception identifies potential tetrahedral centres in 1,145 of 4,350 Child proposals, comprising 1,950 centres, with zero assigned centres; the Parent also has zero assigned centres. The cited branched anilide/oxamide, guanidine-bearing fused-ring molecule and complex phenolic polycycles demonstrate that the absence is not explained by entirely achiral output.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit tetrahedral configuration is absent even when the generator produces constitutionally stereogenic molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic molecular representation and generation process would need to express and preserve eligible configurations and keep distinct stereoisomer identities distinguishable. This is a concrete missing chemical capability; whether using it helps must be learned or measured through ordinary feedback, without selecting a preferred configuration from hidden task identity.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent builds molecules by differentiating through a soft version of their structure. It represents each scored molecule as a graph of whole rings and individual atoms, preserves the interior, and makes the identities and presence of selected terminal units and expansion sites adjustable probabilities. A graph encoder learned from unlabeled molecules stays frozen, while a ridge readout is refitted on the current objective's accepted scores. Starting molecules are sampled with a preference for high score rank. The Parent takes bounded gradient steps that increase this readout's predicted value, retains the best relaxed state, then samples structural decisions and compatible attachments to assemble valid, distinct molecules. Accepted products enter the archive and can become later starting structures. The observed limitation is that increasing this point prediction often fails to produce a better assembled molecule.
approach.novelty: The added mechanism is ascent of a lower confidence bound on structural gain. A Gaussian posterior over the existing ridge coefficients estimates how uncertain a proposed change in the frozen graph features is. Structural ascent subtracts one posterior standard deviation of that gain, so a promising but poorly supported direction receives a smaller gradient contribution. The fitted mean remains the Parent's ridge prediction, and the resulting probabilities still drive its existing sampling and assembly process. This lineage contains only its root so far; no sibling has tested coefficient uncertainty inside structural ascent. The experiment asks whether that uncertainty changes the structural updates before sampling, and whether the resulting proposals transfer more reliably to actual improvements.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace point-estimate structural ascent with ascent of a numerically smoothed lower confidence bound on relaxed structural gain, subtracting one standard deviation computed from the full Gaussian coefficient posterior associated with the Parent's accepted-only ridge readout and differentiating that uncertainty through the frozen graph encoder.

finding_summary.headline: Uncertainty changed every relaxation, but the mean score fell from 0.3619 to 0.3079
finding_summary.insights:
This experiment establishes that coefficient uncertainty can change structural search before sampling and survive every downstream assembly step. It also shows that correcting this particular source of uncertainty is insufficient to remove prediction optimism or preserve the best final score. The strongest illustration is DRD2: 188 of 290 proposals beat their source, yet the search settled around a much lower score. The molecular assessment describes increasingly crowded polyacetals with late scores near 0.028858, while the Parent's stronger products belonged to a different biaryl/amine series. Repeated small improvements inside a weak chemical family can therefore make source-beating rates look favorable while valuable regions remain unreached.

The evidence leaves open whether the uncertainty penalty restricted productive exploration, whether early stochastic differences redirected the search, or whether structural information missing from the frozen features dominated the remaining errors. The posterior covers coefficient uncertainty conditional on an empirical noise estimate; it does not cover attachment choices, stereochemistry or the gap between a relaxed state and its assembled molecule. The generated structures still exhibit the reactive attachments and unspecified configurations identified by the molecular assessment. Preserving access to alternative core families and representing attachment environments remain worth testing. One paired seed cannot establish the repeatability of the four gains or the DRD2 loss.
finding_summary.results:
The intended mechanism ran throughout this screening replica. All 150 accepted-score posterior fits were valid, all 145 feedback updates changed the full coefficient covariance, and all 152 structural optimizations changed their retained categorical distributions relative to the same starting state's mean-only ascent. Every one of the 1,450 emitted proposals used those changed distributions. All eligible nonzero uncertainty corrections reduced the raw gradient's uncertainty directional derivative, and every optimization retained a positive confidence gain; none needed a fallback.

On the single supplied seed, macro Top-1 fell from 0.361872 to 0.307903, a loss of 0.053969. Four objectives improved: zaleplon_mpo from 0.380139 to 0.394051, deco_hop from 0.589062 to 0.602445, median_2 from 0.180051 to 0.183284, and sitagliptin_mpo from 0.234090 to 0.330875. The loss came from drd2_docking, which fell from 0.426020 to 0.028858. Both runs completed all five 300-evaluation tasks with valid, distinct batches.

Local improvement became more frequent: 447 of 1,450 proposals beat their generating molecule, compared with 380 for the Parent. Predicted improvements were realized 41.1% of the time, up from 32.4%. Their average actual score change nevertheless worsened from -0.025853 to -0.031192, and average overstatement of assembled source-relative gains rose from 0.023479 to 0.034251. Better local hit rates did not produce a better overall search result.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold series with reactive attachments; the largest products are crowded polyacetals with undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-b3517f183781, the supplied seed-0 trajectories each contain 300 distinct recorded molecules, including 290 optimizer proposals. Every proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. The main products are dihydropyrazole-thioureas, extended heteroaryl-substituted indoles, quinoline ethers linked to substituted piperidines, silylmethyl-substituted indole carboxamides, and heavily elaborated polyacetals. Rings, heteroatoms, aromatic groups and saturated amine rings are readily represented. Aromatic-atom presence rates are 1.0 for zaleplon_mpo, deco_hop and median_2, 0.9828 for sitagliptin_mpo, and 0.3379 for the predominantly saturated drd2_docking series. These are presence readings from SMILES text, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The output has many distinct decorations but narrow core families within each trajectory. Ordinary medicinal scaffolds coexist with O-F and N-F bonds, peroxides, chloromethyl ethers, sulfenyl chlorides, primary hydrosilanes and, in a late polyacetal, an explicit carbanion. The most congested polyacetals are difficult to regard as routine synthetic targets. All proposal sets have stereocentre_rate 0.0: configurations are unspecified even where the connectivity implies stereogenic carbons. This does not mean the molecules are achiral. The qualitative quality labels describe the recorded structures; no synthesis, conformer, docking-pose or new property calculation was performed. All supplied objectives are covered. The score readings below are associations in these trajectories and the Parent comparison, not proof of individual substituent effects or a missing target-specific pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: Mostly compact to moderately sized aryl-substituted dihydropyrazoles carrying a thiourea linkage. The leading series has two aryl arms, phenols, methyl substitution and small fluorinated groups; the best molecule at evaluation 277 has an N-methylated aryl-thiourea, an aryl fluoride and a fluoromethyl ether. The fluoromethyl ether has a carbon between oxygen and fluorine. Other high and late examples instead contain hydroperoxides, O-O-S or O-S attachments and aryl thiols. Mean SMILES length is 44.5, with maximum 67; aromatic and ring presence rates are both 1.0 and halogen presence is 0.6517. The core is recognizably makeable organic chemistry, while several terminal attachments have questionable stability. Relative to Parent n-0e1f7686dea8, the leading chemistry remains a dihydropyrazole family but retains the thiourea and phenolic aryl groups, where the Parent leaders used an aminomethyl-pyridyl cap and a furyloxyphenyl arm.
liabilities: Evaluation 59 contains an aryl hydroperoxide, and the final molecule contains an O-O-S chain. These introduce reactive oxygen-oxygen bonds into otherwise familiar scaffolds.
Evaluation 289 carries an aryl sulfenyl chloride. Such an S-Cl attachment is a materially different stability concern from the ordinary carbon-bound fluorine in the best molecule.

Some lower-scoring products crowd extra saturated or heteroaromatic rings around the same core. The individual fragments are familiar, but the complete attachment patterns are less convincing synthetic targets.
missing_features: Comparably successful alternative core connectivities that retain the compact polar/aromatic arrangement are not demonstrated among the leading molecules; the highest-scoring set stays with the dihydropyrazole-thiourea family.
Defined configurations at the substituted dihydropyrazole carbons are absent. The supplied records contain no comparison from which a stereochemical score preference could be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied phenolic triaryl dihydropyrazole-thiourea starts at 0.1501184006136499. The less aryl-heavy, phenol-bearing evaluation 56 reaches 0.3649319479033378, and evaluation 277 reaches 0.39405142067435733. Bulky variants carrying additional saturated amine rings or multiple heterocycles are much lower: evaluation 11 is 6.600561276614438e-07, and evaluation 36, which also lacks the thiocarbonyl, is 1.6543725850431745e-11. The visible preference is for a compact polar/aromatic arrangement within this family; it does not establish that adding halogens, thiols or peroxide bonds is generally beneficial. The final O-O-S-bearing product scores 0.3286687595331667. The Parent maximum was 0.380138751942517 with different decorations on a related core, showing another locally favorable chemical arrangement without identifying a unique required substituent.

per_task.generated_character: The leading products are extended, densely substituted indoles linked through a fluorinated benzylic amine to a phenyl-triazole-oxadiazole chain. They carry formate esters, methoxy or chloromethyl ethers and O-F groups; the best entry also replaces the indole N-H with N-F. These are large aromatic assemblies, with mean SMILES length 67.6, maximum 98, and aromatic/ring presence rates of 1.0. Halogen presence is 0.8172. The trajectory also contains the fused pyrimidinedione family seen in the Parent, so more than one supplied core is represented. The Child leaders are the indole series, whereas the Parent maximum came from a heteroaryl-decorated fused dione/benzoate series. The best molecule combines a chloromethyl ether with a formate ester. These introduce an electrophilic attachment and an additional hydrolysis site.
Dense substitution of the fused ring and the long heteroaryl arm would require substantial synthetic control; a valid-looking connectivity does not establish an accessible route.

Less extended, partly saturated alternative geometries with comparable scores are not demonstrated among the leaders; most of their variation adds or decorates heteroaromatic rings.
The stereogenic fluorinated benzylic amine linkage is left without a defined configuration. Its stereochemical contribution is untested in these records.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.5464020559680183, and the hydroxymethoxy-decorated carboxanilide at evaluation 13 scores 0.5370762711864407. The observed gradient favors this extended aromatic/polar arrangement over the simpler carboxanilides, but simultaneous substitutions prevent assignment of the gain to any single reactive bond.

per_task.generated_character: The Child trajectory elaborates a protected-sugar-like polycyclic acetal framework into exceptionally crowded polyacetals. The leading structures retain the oxygen-rich core and attach many saturated or partly unsaturated nitrogen rings, cyclic ethers, sulfur heterocycles, some aromatic azoles and a primary SiH3 hydrosilane. The Parent leaders instead use halogenated biaryl, pyrrolidine and morpholine/thiomorpholine chemistry with sulfenamide and aminal linkages.
liabilities: Multiple bulky substituents around acetal and ring-junction carbons create severe congestion and a difficult synthetic and stereochemical problem.
The primary SiH3 group is carried into the leading structures. It introduces reactive Si-H functionality without any supplied evidence about isolation or stability of these compounds.

Late products include unusual explicitly charged nitrogen environments, and evaluation 298 also has a localized carbon anion. That carbon anion is a different concern from ordinary protonation of the many amines; charge presence alone is not a defect.

A simplified scaffold presenting a limited set of polar and ionizable groups is missing from the leading polyacetal series; the nearly unchanged late scores do not establish which of its many appended groups are useful.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring products are compact to moderately sized indole carboxanilides with a fluorinated phenyl ring, phenolic or aniline substitution on the indole benzene ring, and a silylmethyl ether. The latter is an oxygen-methylene-SiH3 linkage, not a conventional oxygen-bound trialkylsilyl protecting group. This motif recurs throughout the best digest entries. The core is largely aromatic with few saturated atoms; mean proposal SMILES length is 56.1, maximum 84, aromatic presence 0.9828, ring presence 1.0 and halogen presence 0.7207. The full trajectory also samples large acetal and fused-dione derivatives with very low scores. The ordinary indole amide framework is synthetically credible, but the primary hydrosilane and some peripheral heteroatom attachments make the complete products questionable. The Parent also favored indole derivatives; its maximum combined an N-SiH3 attachment with an O-linked aziridine, whereas the Child leaders favor the silylmethyl ether.
liabilities: Primary SiH3 hydrosilanes recur across the best molecules. Their Si-H reactivity and behavior in these complete structures are unresolved by the supplied SMILES and scores.

Some high or late entries add N-S, N-F or O-F attachments, and evaluation 295 carries an explicit phenolate. These changes introduce reactive bonds or a specified ionization state that a score alone does not chemically justify.

Strongly unfavorable late products retain the core and silicon motif while adding bulky substituents. The favorable arrangement is sensitive to its surrounding chemistry; presence of the recurring motif is insufficient.
missing_features: The leading excerpt does not demonstrate a similarly successful conventional replacement for the primary hydrosilane ether. The data show association with that motif, without establishing that it is chemically required.

A comparably successful alternative core geometry retaining the modest size and polar/aromatic arrangement is absent from the leading set. Large ring additions frequently move the sampled chemistry away from that favorable region.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.00012094961439027578. The silylmethyl/phenol variant at evaluation 44 scores 0.24323049964971696, the less methoxy-decorated phenol at evaluation 110 reaches 0.3188638798296843, and its difluoroanilide counterpart at evaluation 241 reaches 0.32964789455035565. The amino-substituted indole at evaluation 131 reaches 0.3308753645714267. The visible favorable region combines modest size, the indole/anilide arrangement, small polar substitution and the silylmethyl group; it does not prove a causal benefit from silicon itself. The charged acetal at evaluation 54 scores 6.520749754415915e-65, while late indoles with extra bulky ring decoration at evaluations 296 and 297 fall to 1.3225096655844806e-12 and 1.3601291579115854e-12. The trajectory median is 4.2e-05 and the final molecule scores 0.009046134500032013, so the favorable chemical region is narrow. The Parent maximum was 0.23408968632790841 in a differently decorated, still unusual indole series.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The leading extended indole contains O-F, N-F and chloromethyl-ether chemistry. Dihydropyrazole and quinoline series contain peroxides, and a leading dihydropyrazole contains a sulfenyl chloride. Primary SiH3 groups recur in both a compact indole series and the giant polyacetals. These are concrete attachment liabilities within recognizable scaffolds; ring availability is already rich.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently maintain stable bond environments when it combines otherwise familiar fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent the full local attachment environment and provide conventional stable replacements that preserve the sampled polar and hydrophobic arrangement. Let accepted feedback test those alternatives, while distinguishing ordinary carbon-bound halogens, stable sulfur chemistry and common ionized amines from reactive heteroatom-halogen, peroxide or localized carbanion environments.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The polyacetal population has mean SMILES length 100.7 and maximum 175, with many pendant heterocycles, charged nitrogen environments and an SiH3 group. Its late reported scores lie close to 0.028858 despite substantial appendage changes. Elsewhere, compact indole and dihydropyrazole variants coexist with much lower-scoring derivatives carrying extra rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not demonstrate effective simplification of a crowded scaffold while retaining its useful polar and amine features.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide molecule-level contraction and rearrangement options as well as expansion, so a smaller scaffold can present a similar set of polar and ionizable groups. Track accumulated size and attachment congestion when proposing additional rings; task-local evidence must determine whether greater complexity is useful.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Each supplied trajectory records 300 distinct molecules, yet its leaders repeatedly retain an indole, dihydropyrazole, quinoline-ether/piperidine or polyacetal core from the supplied starting chemistry. Different input core families can appear, but much of the apparent diversity is peripheral substitution, heteroaryl extension and terminal-group exchange.
transferable_gaps.gap: Distinct proposed strings do not translate into broad access to alternative core geometry within a trajectory.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make alternative central ring connectivities and linker geometries accessible while preserving favorable functional relationships observed in accepted molecules. Assess chemical diversity at the core and attachment-topology level alongside canonical identity, allowing score feedback to choose among geometrically distinct series.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every proposal set has stereocentre_rate 0.0. The cited substituted dihydropyrazoles, fluorinated benzylic amines, substituted piperidines and crowded polyacetals nevertheless contain stereogenic connectivity. The absence is stereochemical specification, not saturated carbon or three-dimensional potential.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express defined stereochemical products even when its connectivity creates stereogenic centers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configuration and its preservation through structural changes so that emitted identities can denote individual stereoisomers. Evaluate any stereochemical preference through the same accepted-feedback process; these trajectories provide no evidence for choosing a particular configuration.

nodes.method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from an unlabeled corpus, then adapts a fresh policy independently for each objective. After every accepted batch, it trains on the best-scoring half of the current molecules and a uniformly sampled group of historical elites. Each original accepted SMILES is fitted toward the frozen prior log probability plus sixty times its observed score, with equal weight for every training sequence. Only current elites enter memory after that update; the thirty-two highest-scoring identities survive. Complete molecules are then sampled directly from the policy, validated and filtered for canonical novelty.
approach.novelty: Change only which historical elites survive in memory. Retain the best member of each molecular core before retaining second members of those cores, proceeding in score order within each round until the existing memory is full. The original uniform replay then gives every surviving family access to the same learning rule. This differs from the sibling that always replays the strongest records: it changes future availability while keeping replay sampling intact. An earlier graph-evolution experiment used similar retention, but its protected molecules never entered the narrow score bands used for breeding. Uniform replay supplies a different route from protected memory to actual learning, which this experiment will measure directly. Broader core counts alone will not establish better chemistry or scores.

nodes.hypothesis: Retain accepted historical elites by successive score-ordered rounds across Murcko cores, taking each core's best record before any core's next record, then restore descending-score/canonical order for the inherited uniform replay while preserving original accepted records and the existing memory capacity.

finding_summary.headline: Protected cores reached learning and duplicate draws fell, with little net score gain
finding_summary.insights: The earlier core-retention experiment in graph evolution failed to expose protected records to its restricted breeding sampler. Uniform neural replay opens that route: retained alternatives now enter the real loss and affect learning before later proposals. Access remains sparse, however. Only 74 of 302 protected records with a later nonterminal opportunity were drawn, and protection lasted a median of one retained snapshot after its first event. The same accepted-stream greedy comparison gives a replay reward of 0.31539, so weaker replay reward is a direct retention tradeoff rather than only a difference between generated trajectories. Broader core access and fewer duplicates did not meet the expected 0.002 mean score improvement; useful transfer from those lower-reward alternatives remains unresolved. The generated chemistry remains conventional, ring-rich aromatic amine/carbonyl chemistry with familiar leading families and no specified stereochemistry, so more core counts do not establish the precise chemical coverage the objectives need. Twenty-two protected training targets were positive and unattainable as log probabilities, another inherited limitation. The gradient evidence also has a numerical boundary: two mathematically equivalent groupings differed in combined norm by up to 0.045% under the inherited floating computation. Protected-removal signals exceeded the registered threshold by at least 86,620 times, but full vectors were not retained to establish exact numerical equivalence.
finding_summary.results: Core protection changed 216 of 435 retention decisions that preceded further proposals. Every changed local contest retained more ring cores than greedy selection. Across all 435 local contests, mean ring-core coverage was 28.71 versus 27.50. Seventy-four protected accepted records subsequently entered learning in 83 exposures across 70 updates. All seventy updates showed a measurable protected gradient contribution, and protected target mean-square error fell from 165.10 to 100.63. Summed within sessions, actual replay covered 862 distinct ring cores versus 750 in the Parent, while its mean accepted reward fell from 0.31637 to 0.27659. Duplicate raw draws fell from 30.11% to 25.51%, and batch-level novel-valid yield rose from 60.31% to 64.76%; both runs still submitted exactly 4,350 valid novel proposals. Mean final score was 0.508476 versus 0.507554, a paired gain of 0.000922. The three seed changes were -0.013399, +0.007440 and +0.008726. Median_2 improved by 0.019383 on average, while sitagliptin_mpo fell by 0.015668; the smaller remaining task changes did not produce a clear overall score gain.
