approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES language model from an unlabeled molecular corpus and begins each objective with a fresh policy copied from that frozen prior. Each accepted batch contributes its highest-scoring half. A memory keeps the thirty-two strongest earlier elites, and its strongest eligible records join the current examples with their original accepted strings and scores. Historical examples receive diminishing weights based on how many earlier fitting batches used them, while the total current and historical loss shares stay fixed. The policy minimizes weighted squared error toward frozen-prior sequence log likelihood plus sixty times accepted reward, using up to twelve clipped Adam steps and retaining the final policy. It directly samples complete SMILES, with chemical validation and canonical duplicate rejection refilling each batch.
approach.novelty: Add an individual log-probability ceiling to the fitting targets: replace only positive targets with zero. This removes the positive excess that a normalized sequence model cannot reach while keeping every nonpositive target and the Parent's exposure weights. The earlier shared-normalization sibling shifted every target in an affected batch, reversed some learning directions and lost sequence completion in two replicas. Ceiling projection never turns a capped row toward lower likelihood. The two Huber siblings bounded residual influence symmetrically; this change acts only on targets above the probability ceiling. Same-state target and gradient comparisons will test execution, and later molecular proposals will test utility. Multiple zero targets are still jointly incompatible, and collapsing distinctions among saturated targets can weaken useful exploitation.

nodes.hypothesis: Project each selected sequence's augmented likelihood target independently onto the nonpositive log-probability half-line, t_i = min(frozen_prior_log_likelihood_i + 60 * accepted_score_i, 0), while preserving the Parent's inverse-exposure historical coefficients, selected membership and squared-residual Adam update.

finding_summary.headline: Ceiling projection changed real learning and reduced duplicate draws, with an uneven gain in final score.
finding_summary.insights:
Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.
finding_summary.results:
All positive target excess was removed, and the change reached actual learning. Among 420 historical updates followed by proposals, 195 contained positive targets: 465 current and 602 historical row appearances were capped, removing 13,705.38 nats of unattainable target excess. Every affected update changed gradient direction after clipping. The three affected initialization updates did too. All 244 no-positive updates retained exactly the same local raw and projected gradient, and every one of the 450 real first backward passes matched the projected objective exactly. No capped row reversed from upward to downward likelihood pressure.

On the child's own historical training states, projection reduced the mean sum of absolute scalar learning factors from 12.795 to 6.305. Projected weighted squared error fell from 26.936 before learning to 2.984 afterward; error against the original raw targets on those same states fell from 135.072 to 97.457. Those are fitting measurements under different target definitions, not score gains. All fifteen tasks completed their budgets. Raw duplicate draws fell from 36.22% to 32.21%, and batches needing extra sampling fell from 29 to 16.

Mean final Top-1 rose from 0.517655 to 0.522705, a paired gain of 0.005050. Seed changes were -0.008594, +0.007415 and +0.016329. The gain was concentrated in deco-hop, whose task mean increased by 0.025328; docking rose by 0.001300 near its ceiling, zaleplon fell by 0.001379, and the other two tasks were unchanged. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.406769 to 0.405593, so the endpoint gain did not produce faster useful discovery overall. Terminal updates establish execution only and contribute no later proposals.

Removing individually impossible demands can alter the direction of a clipped, exposure-weighted update without reversing any capped sequence's scalar learning direction. The matched controls make this attribution unusually clear: all six sessions without a positive target reproduced the parent's complete molecular records and scores exactly, and every changed session retained its matched proposal prefix until the first positive-target intervention. This narrows the effect to active target projection under the existing replay and optimizer rules.

The mechanism satisfies only the individual probability ceiling. Two hundred of the 420 historical updates still had combined projected target probability above one. Thirty-six batches set all ten selected targets to zero, erasing their raw target distinctions. Positive raw-target appearances actually increased from 977 to 1,067 as search changed; the mechanism removes their excess when fitting, rather than preventing such opportunities. Lower projected loss also does not protect every remembered row: 905 of 2,100 historical residuals worsened, almost the parent's 906, and 1,006 historical likelihoods decreased. Every repeated training appearance was consecutive, so these records cannot establish forgetting between skipped updates.

The chemical assessment places the main gain in a more concentrated decorated quinazoline family, while overall medicinal scaffolds remain ring-rich and attachment chemistry and stereochemical definition remain unresolved. Distinct observed cores increased for zaleplon despite its slightly lower endpoint and decreased for deco-hop despite its gain. That combination rules out treating broader core counts or lower duplication as a sufficient explanation for useful search. The open question is whether the endpoint benefit persists across seeds while retaining distinctions among saturated targets and preserving useful progress earlier in the budget.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds with uneven attachment chemistry, concentrated analogue families and no specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-c2ef5c1d5a78 produces substantial organic structures, dominated by aromatic amides, decorated nitrogen heterocycles, aryl sulfonamides and cyclic amines. The digest reports 870 optimizer proposals per task; ring-closure rates range from 0.9805 to 0.9966 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.946 to 0.9931. These are fractions of SMILES strings containing the indicated features, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The passive RDKit audit finds median heavy-atom counts of 24, 33, 28, 24 and 24 in the fixed task order, with median perceived ring counts of 3, 4, 3, 3 and 3. All 4,350 accepted optimizer appearances parse, but parsing is not a synthetic-route or stability assessment. Constitutional exploration is broad: the respective distinct atom-typed Murcko scaffold counts are 540, 356, 588, 733 and 775; these counts also distinguish linker and ring-atom changes and do not establish useful diversity. The strongest subsets can nevertheless concentrate on a single decorated core. Most leading structures have recognizable medicinal chemistry, alongside very flexible, highly aromatic, reactive-handle and unusually assembled outliers. The entire panel has stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies 832 optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. Against Parent n-3462511d7ff0, two tasks have identical chemical records, while the others mainly change families or their substitution and linkage patterns. Score-gradient interpretations below are associations within recorded structures, not hidden-objective definitions, activity measurements, causal matched-pair experiments unless stated, or mechanism-activation judgements. All five task trajectories were supplied and read; tasks_without_trajectories is empty in the brief. Descriptor definitions, exact input hashes, Parent comparisons and structural receipts are saved in runs/SPIRAL2/policy/responses/r0011-06-improve-L03-molecular.audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Predominantly medium-sized, aromatic amides: anilides, benzylamides, pyridyl ethers, pyridones and indole carboxamides. The leading seed-2 ether-linked bis-pyridyl anilide has 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings; its molecular weight is 319.364. The next benzyl-pyridone/pyridylmethyl benzamide and methylamino diaryl-ether analogue have the same heavy-atom count and molecular weight. These ordinary amide and aryl-ether connections appear makeable, while the low tail includes small inorganic/ionic fragments and elaborate polycycles. The Parent also led with aromatic amides; the node changes their heteroaromatic and linker arrangements. For example, the seed-0 leading family changes from a substituted pyrrole tertiary carboxamide at recorded 0.4902347642636414 to an acetamidoindole benzylamide at 0.43351949803907636. Seed 2 instead reaches the cited ether-linked anilide at 0.5, versus the Parent aromatic amide at 0.4767312946227961.
liabilities: The low tail contains overbuilt fused/bridged polycycles with unspecified stereochemistry; their valid SMILES do not supply a practical synthesis.

A high-scoring O-benzyl hydroxamate-like amide and a sulfinamide illustrate less routine N-O and sulfur attachment chemistry; the latter has an unassigned sulfur centre. These groups require individual assessment and are not inherently invalid.
The final expanded multi-anilide retains substantial aromatic surface and extra amide burden despite its very low score.
missing_features: Reliable preservation of the moderate-sized, organized aromatic amide/ether combination during late exploration: expanded amide assemblies and fragmented outputs lose that organization.
Controlled heteroatom placement and linker topology within that composition range remain unresolved; abundant rings do not imply the required arrangement has been found.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading 24-heavy-atom aromatic amides score 0.5 or 0.4767312946227961; the isolated thiocyanate representation scores 5.670115669739515e-23, and the enlarged 44-heavy-atom multi-amide scores 3.2151129360788796e-21. Late growth to the related 35-heavy-atom multi-anilide at seed-2 evaluation 296 gives only 0.00015241757289843227. A moderate size/composition window and specific aromatic nitrogen/amide organization are therefore supported better than indiscriminate ring or amide addition. The differently connected leaders sharing molecular weight still differ in score, so size alone is not sufficient; the records do not identify a unique absent target scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are all seed-2 variants of a butoxy/dimethoxy 4-anilino-2-phenylquinazoline, with fluorine/chlorine substitutions and related alkoxy changes. The leading molecule has 35 heavy atoms, four aromatic rings, molecular weight 483.490 and nine rotatable bonds. The aryl-amino and aryl-ether connections are recognizable synthetic chemistry, although heavy decoration increases size and route complexity. Full trajectories also contain other families: a dinitrophenylhydrazone in seed 0 and a nitrogen-rich fused heteroaromatic family in seed 1. Compared with the Parent seed-2 sulfonamide/imine-decorated quinoline leader at 0.6085883514313919, the node reaches the cited quinazoline at 0.6669492630755185. The largest Murcko family grows from 71 Parent proposals to 160 node proposals; this local concentration coexists with 356 distinct node scaffolds.
liabilities: The leading family combines extensive aromatic surface, multiple halogens and flexible alkoxy substituents; solubility, conformation and synthesis remain unmeasured.
The broader stream still includes heavily nitrated hydrazones and large aliphatic ionic outliers. Their presence should not be confused with useful scaffold coverage.
No stereochemistry is specified even in branched alkoxy variants that can carry a stereocentre.
missing_features: The leading excerpt lacks alternative core architectures that retain the successful substituent arrangement: its apparent variety largely comes from decoration of one quinazoline framework.

The local score differences support more precise substituent positioning and ether connectivity, but do not identify any particular unobserved scaffold or missing functional group as the objective answer.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The strongest decorated quinazoline scores 0.6669492630755185. A difluoroaniline member scores 0.6666996765035981, whereas its same-fluorine-count positional isomer at final evaluation 298 scores 0.6362655153804642. Removing the butoxy oxygen in the cited final analogue gives 0.6316114681166585; these local comparisons support sensitivity to substitution position and linkage. Ring-rich sulfones in the worst excerpt score 0.28535067873303166 and 0.28799019607843135, while a long-chain quaternary ammonium compound scores 0.5. Thus the score is not a general measure of aromatic richness, size, or chemical plausibility.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules have accessible non-acylated amines combined with aromatic groups: benzyl/aryl piperazines, benzene-fused azepines connected through aminoalkyl chains, and aryl ketones bearing propoxy-piperidine substituents. The first digest leader has 30 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings and a saturated piperazine, with molecular weight 463.463 and calculated TPSA 6.48. The next fused-azepine leader is smaller, at 26 heavy atoms and molecular weight 360.448, but retains a flexible linker. These are recognizable medicinal scaffolds, with conventional amine/aryl chemistry in many examples. The Parent also produced cyclic amines, but its seed-2 near-ceiling leader carried an N-hydroxyaminal connection; the node supplies ketone-linked examples instead. Parent seed-0 recorded best 0.9961294199375436 becomes 0.9999997933663268 for the cited piperazine family; this is chemical comparison at an already compressed score ceiling.
liabilities: The highly aromatic first leader has little calculated polar surface, while other leaders carry long flexible linkers and multiple potentially protonatable amines; neither actual protonation nor solubility was measured.
The chloromethyl ether in a leader scoring 0.9999994163676008 is a reactive attachment requiring scrutiny even though the recorded score is high.
The final polyether-linked amide has 17 rotatable bonds and score 0.5728095677025575, showing that extensive flexible growth is still admitted.
missing_features: Some low and final proposals lose the combination of a non-acylated cyclic amine and the larger aromatic/linker arrangement; the generator can emit these features but does not preserve their chemical roles consistently.
Several high-scoring aminoalkyl families lack linker restraint. More constrained counterparts are a chemical coverage gap, with no demonstrated score benefit from the records supplied.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Free cyclic amines with suitably connected aromatic groups occur repeatedly near the score ceiling. By contrast, the N-sulfonyl piperidine example scores 1.9828327575562915e-05 and the N-acyl piperidine example 2.6715842904959654e-05: a nitrogen ring whose nitrogen is sulfonylated or acylated is chemically different from a free amine. Late seed-2 ketones retaining the propoxy-piperidine appendage score 0.9999937368364026 and 0.999988872643426, whereas the smaller amino-ketone lacking that appendage scores 0.0035116287191461495. Those are not single-change matched pairs, but support the importance of amine/aryl spacing beyond mere nitrogen presence. The many nearly identical high scores cannot establish a preferred linker length or experimental binding affinity.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger molecules combine aryl sulfonyl groups with piperazine, quinoline or benzodioxole units. The leading molecule is an unsymmetrical bis-sulfonyl piperazine linking a methylquinoline and benzodioxole: 32 heavy atoms, five perceived rings, three aromatic rings and molecular weight 475.548. Other strong examples retain N-methyl or N-aryl piperazines; the broader stream also contains amides and assorted heterocycles. Aryl sulfonamide assembly is recognizable makeable chemistry, whereas the seed-1 N-rich unsaturated ring is less routine. Every supplied node and Parent record agrees in evaluation, source, SMILES and score across all seeds for this task, so there is no molecular-output change to describe.
liabilities: Repeated sulfonyl and piperazine additions can produce large, acceptor-rich molecules without improving on the more compact leader.
The leading bis-sulfonyl piperazine has no free basic piperazine nitrogen; any intended ionization property must follow its actual substitution, not the ring name.
The low tail includes a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide and an organic azide; these are chemically distinct reactive or specialized compounds, not evidence of routine medicinal plausibility.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring proposals lack the combined aromatic/sulfonyl/piperazine organization; isolated amine or sulfonyl motifs do not reproduce the leading arrangement.

A more effective topology beyond the observed bis-sulfonamide is not identifiable from these scores. The enlarged example shows that duplicating recognizable fragments does not resolve that uncertainty.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393. The smaller quinoline sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine scores 0.2272296156064184, and the expanded structure carrying additional sulfonyl-piperazine material scores 0.2301209791058402 despite reaching 41 heavy atoms and molecular weight 628.795. Small acyclic compounds, including the cited organic azide at 0.0 and thiodiacetic acid at 0.02095188685475281, lack the combined ring/linker architecture. A late simple pyrrolylmethyl piperazine scores 0.10826206026353223, so piperazine alone is insufficient. Both nitrogens of the leading piperazine are sulfonylated: a missing free basic nitrogen is not supported as this objective's general deficit.

per_task.generated_character: The stronger excerpt remains chemically heterogeneous. It includes a butylamino-acetyl N-acylsulfonamide on a fluoro/trifluoromethyl phenyl ring, a branched oxalamide/anilide, sulfonylated cyclic amidines bearing an aromatic ester, a guanidino benzofused amine, and an acylthiourea quinolinone. The first three leaders have 23, 26 and 25 heavy atoms and molecular weights 356.341, 377.338 and 362.382; the first two each have only one aromatic ring, whereas the cyclic-amidine ester has three rings overall. Several fragments are synthetically familiar, but the varied N-acylsulfonamide, amidine, hydrazone and acylthiourea connections need individual chemical assessment. All supplied node/Parent chemical records and scores are identical across the seeds; this chemistry is inherited unchanged in the observed output.
liabilities: The high-scoring amino-acylsulfonamide combines a potentially basic amine with a potentially acidic N-acylsulfonamide; a neutral SMILES does not establish its solution microstate.
The acylthiourea and sulfonylhydrazone families introduce tautomeric or configurational questions, while the branched oxalamide is explicitly stereochemically undefined.
Large peptide-like and lipid-like outliers carry substantial size or flexibility burdens. The final stream still contains densely carbonylated or imino structures at very low recorded scores.
missing_features: Reliable compact assembly with the local polarity and substituent arrangement seen in the better examples is missing from many proposals; late carbonyl-rich and bulky structures still depart from those arrangements.

The branched oxalamide, guanidino benzofused amine and other chiral proposals lack specified tetrahedral configurations. This is a molecular-definition gap; these trajectories do not test whether stereochemical assignment changes the objective score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact amino-acylsulfonamide scores 0.32609684308650033 and the branched oxalamide 0.3085499097640706. Within the sulfonylated cyclic-amidine ester family, adding the cited aryl fluorine changes the recorded score from 0.24905607529893223 to 0.3034617343186778. Replacing the methyl ester in the unfluorinated family with an ethyl carboxamide gives 0.20841151065209942. Thus substituent identity and polar-group arrangement matter locally. The large peptide-like structures, extended lipid-like chain and heavily substituted polyaromatic examples in the worst excerpt have zero or extremely small scores. However, unfluorinated guanidino and acylthiourea leaders also score 0.2711448282680827 and 0.26424211308214746. Neither more fluorine nor more rings is a supported universal requirement, and the diverse leaders do not reveal a unique missing target pharmacophore.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Free cyclic amines recur among near-ceiling molecules, while cited N-acyl and N-sulfonyl versions of nitrogen rings occur at very low scores. Elsewhere the strongest bis-sulfonyl piperazine deliberately has both nitrogens blocked, so no universal free-amine preference is justified. Same-fluorine-count positional isomers on a decorated quinazoline score 0.6666996765035981 and 0.6362655153804642. These examples show why ring names and element counts do not determine chemical function or useful attachment geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator varies atom identities and attachments without consistently preserving the chemical role of the resulting functional group.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore functional-group roles, atom neighborhoods and substituent positions coherently, including alternatives that preserve a useful arrangement while changing one local connection. Let task-local observed feedback determine which roles matter; impose no universal amine, halogen or scaffold requirement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A 24-heavy-atom aromatic amide scores 0.5, while a related 35-heavy-atom expanded multi-anilide scores 0.00015241757289843227. A 32-heavy-atom bis-sulfonyl piperazine scores 0.2588686674995393, while a 41-heavy-atom expanded sulfonyl/piperazine structure scores 0.2301209791058402. Large peptide-like and long-chain outliers also appear at zero or negligible scores. These are observed associations, not universal molecular-size cutoffs.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably control size and polar-group growth while retaining the organization of a useful molecular family.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support compact additions, removals and replacements that vary size, flexibility and donor/acceptor organization separately enough for feedback to resolve them. Avoid assuming that duplicating a recognized group or increasing ring count preserves the useful whole-molecule arrangement.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 12 digest leaders in the decorated anilino-phenylquinazoline basin share that framework, despite extensive fluorine/chlorine and alkoxy variation. Its largest atom-typed Murcko family contains 160 optimizer proposals, versus 71 in the Parent. Across the panel ring-closure rates are already 0.9805 to 0.9966, and many distinct scaffolds occur, so the gap is not an inability to close rings or explore constitutional structures.
transferable_gaps.gap: High-scoring local exploration can become concentrated on peripheral decorations without demonstrating equivalent access to alternative core arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically coherent core and attachment rearrangements alongside decoration changes, retaining substituent roles where possible. Assess resulting molecules through ordinary feedback rather than treating scaffold counts or enforced diversity as evidence of utility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. The passive structural audit finds 832 accepted optimizer appearances with an unassigned tetrahedral centre and none with an assigned centre. The branched oxalamide scoring 0.3085499097640706 and the sulfinamide scoring 0.4531317717091581 provide digest witnesses. This absence concerns molecular identity, not proven stereochemical sensitivity of the recorded scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator has no demonstrated ability to specify the stereochemical identities of the chiral molecules it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit stereochemical alternatives when a proposed graph admits them, and preserve assigned configuration through subsequent changes. Keep any usefulness claim conditional on observed feedback; do not assume that stereochemical specification itself improves the objective.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A chloromethyl-ether arylpiperazine has recorded score 0.9999994163676008. The same panel includes an organic azide, a trichloromethyl N-hydroxyformamide, stereochemically unspecified polycycles and amino-acylsulfonamides with competing ionizable groups. All accepted optimizer structures parse, which verifies a narrower property than stability, route feasibility or a defined solution microstate.
transferable_gaps.gap: Score-compatible generation still admits reactive attachments and structures whose practical synthesis or solution form is unresolved.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain chemically coherent connection types and the ability to distinguish ordinary end-product functionality from reactive handles or unresolved microstates using general chemical context. Treat unusual N-N, N-O and sulfur chemistry individually rather than banning entire bond classes; the observed scores do not substitute for synthetic or physicochemical evidence.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).

approach.method_basis: The Parent alternates a learned molecule sampler with ordinary graph breeding. An autoregressive SMILES model is first trained on unlabeled molecules and kept as a frozen prior. Each objective gets an adaptable copy that generates one batch, followed by two batches made through graph crossover and atom or bond edits. Accepted neural samples refresh a scored population of up to sixty-four molecules, and a fresh neural sample is forced to participate in breeding at each handoff. Accepted graph descendants then train the adaptable sampler through score-ranked replay, trajectory balance with a learned normalizer, and regularization toward the frozen prior. This reciprocal loop ran repeatedly, but each valid novel graph descendant was sent directly for evaluation, and most scored below its best generating parent.
approach.novelty: Add posterior-sampling selection to the genetic phase. A Gaussian process learned from this objective's accepted scores uses molecular fingerprints to draw plausible score functions over a fresh pool of offspring from the existing graph operators. Each available evaluation slot takes the best remaining offspring under a new sampled function. The first forced neural-parent offspring at each handoff stays as in the Parent, so the reciprocal exchange remains intact. This lineage has only tested direct submission so far; the new ingredient is selection among genetic offspring before they receive real scores. A related graph-only experiment improved final best scores without improving its parent-beating rate, so the hypothesis here concerns discovering useful upper-tail outcomes within the reciprocal loop, with descendant efficiency measured separately.

nodes.hypothesis: Use a task-local fingerprint Gaussian process to choose genetic-phase evaluations by posterior-function maximization over fresh graph offspring pools, retaining the Parent's mandatory first fresh-policy offspring at each graph-cycle handoff.

finding_summary.headline: Posterior selection and reciprocal feedback reproduce across seeds; offspring efficiency remains weak
finding_summary.insights: Replication rules out missing selector execution or a broken reciprocal handoff as explanations for the weak offspring yield: both mechanisms remain active across all three seeds. It also weakens the original suggestion of improved average child-minus-parent score, which held on the screening seed but not on the two additional seeds. The selector consistently changes which offspring are evaluated, but this does not establish that uncertainty itself improves final scores. The original direct-submission Parent has only one available seed, so the earlier paired score gain of 0.005848 remains a single-seed comparison; the new results establish repeatable execution and describe score variability without establishing a paired multi-seed improvement. Prediction error in the new runs is lower than an archive-mean baseline on four of five objectives, yet nominal 95% latent intervals cover only 80.4% of selected accepted scores overall and 41.9% on sitagliptin_mpo, where prediction MSE is also worse than that baseline. These are informative but uncalibrated predictions on the selected molecules. The molecular assessment shows that ring systems and useful basic-amine chemistry are already available, while leading families still mix conventional scaffolds with reactive substitutions, complicated connectivity and unspecified stereochemistry. That narrows the remaining questions toward reliable discrimination among chemically credible alternatives and broader useful scaffold coverage. Matched Parent replicas and a same-pool mean-only or direct-order comparison are still needed to isolate score benefit, efficiency and uncertainty's contribution.
finding_summary.results: Both additional seeds reproduced the intended selection and feedback behavior. Every one of their 1,800 selected offspring maximized its reconstructed correlated posterior draw, and uncertainty changed 1,671 choices (92.8%) relative to choosing the highest posterior mean. All 190 fits used earlier accepted scores only, all 1,710 eligible fixed-molecule predictions changed after feedback, and all 100 protected neural-to-graph handoffs were preserved. There were 90 later reciprocal cycles and 4,480 nonzero graph-bearing policy updates. The two new mean final-best scores were 0.528301 and 0.517608, compared with 0.516098 in the original run of the same algorithm. Across all three seeds, mean final-best score is 0.520669 with a population standard deviation of 0.005432. The three-seed objective means are 0.458300 for zaleplon_mpo, 0.615427 for deco_hop, 0.999997 for drd2_docking, 0.204624 for median_2 and 0.324997 for sitagliptin_mpo. Only 246 of 1,900 graph descendants in the new runs beat their best generating parent (12.95%), and their mean child-minus-parent score was -0.110567. Across all three runs those quantities are 386 of 2,850 (13.54%) and -0.099708. These are below the original direct-submission Parent's single-seed parent-beating rate of 18.21%; that historical comparison is not a paired three-seed efficiency estimate.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic and cyclic-amine chemistry, with useful scaffolds mixed with reactive substitutions and unresolved stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied seed-1 and seed-2 trajectories each cover every listed objective. Each task digest contains 600 evaluated molecules, including 580 optimizer proposals. These are predominantly connected, branched, ring-bearing organic structures: the taskwise ring_closure_rate ranges from 0.9793 to 0.9948 and aromatic_atom_rate from 0.9362 to 0.9828. Those are SMILES-text presence rates, not fractions of atoms or perceived ring counts. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.0 to 69.7. The repertoire includes biaryl pyrazoles, indole carboxamides, quinoline ureas, azoles and acylhydrazones, aryl-substituted saturated amines, carbonyl-rich fused heterocycles, and triazolyl azetidines. Ring chemistry and basic amine centres are demonstrably available. The individual high-score families are more concentrated than the variety of the complete proposal sets. Conventional medicinal-chemistry building blocks coexist with oxygen- and nitrogen-halogen bonds, hydrazine/nitroso functionality, unusual short ring closures, and oversized concatenated structures. Consequently, synthetic plausibility is questionable overall and drug-likeness is mixed rather than uniformly poor. No proposed set contains explicit stereocentre annotations: every digest stereocentre_rate is 0.0, even though several depicted saturated cores can have configurational alternatives. The charge-marker rate must not be read as a basic-amine rate; neutral amine SMILES can describe protonatable centres, and nitro groups also produce charge markers. For this replication ticket, the supplied parent_trajectories and focus.parent identify seed 0 of n-cc2d839e347b itself. Comparisons below describe that prior run, not an intervention between different algorithms. Apparent score preferences are associations in the supplied molecular observations; absent chemistry is not evidence that an unobserved replacement would improve the score.

per_task.generated_character: Most proposals are aromatic, moderately sized molecules carrying amides, ureas, methoxy or hydroxy groups and frequent halogen substituents. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9793, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9569 and halogen_rate 0.7966. The seed-1 leader is an N-methyl acetanilide bearing a biaryl-linked pyrazole and a phenol. Seed 2 instead favours methoxyquinoline linked through a urea to isoindoline. Earlier proposals include substituted indole carboxamides related to the initial molecule scoring 0.3051048083696145. These recognizable cores are plausibly accessible, although many neighbouring substitutions are less convincing. Low-scoring material includes tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments and large, heavily decorated polyaryl structures. Compared with the prior seed-0 high tail of modified indole carboxamides, including unusual amide-nitrogen and cumulated-side-chain chemistry at 0.4219568943587627, the new runs supply more conventional alternative leading cores.
liabilities: The high tail includes an aryl hypochlorite and an aryl sulfur-chlorine group, which introduce reactive bonds despite favourable recorded scores.
A chloromethyl substituent occurs in a leading indole derivative. Large conjugated or multiply decorated late products add synthetic complexity without preserving the favourable score range.
The leading aromatic series carries substantial aromatic surface and limited saturated shape variation; this is a structural description, not a measured solubility or exposure result.
missing_features: Broader stable variants preserving the useful phenol, amide and heteroaryl arrangement are poorly represented relative to peripheral halogen and heteroatom substitutions in the leading families.

Controlled changes of core and linker geometry that retain the compact high-score arrangement remain incompletely explored. The observations establish distinct useful core families, but do not identify a uniquely required missing scaffold.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The phenolic biaryl-pyrazole acetanilide scores 0.5256780516063334; its otherwise corresponding unsubstituted aryl analogue scores 0.4865761385111112. The oxygen-chlorinated analogue scores 0.49263201457052164, so the observed best local substitution is an ordinary hydroxyl group. The related sulfur-chlorine structure scores 0.4686060677105447. Seed 2 reaches 0.427264458706691 with the fluoroquinoline urea, and its final hydroxyquinoline urea scores 0.4219568943587627. At the other extreme, the tiny nitrogen-fluorine fragment scores 0.0, while the large methoxy-rich sulfonamide/polyamine conjugate scores 6.660632986075464e-46. Late enlarged structures still score 0.00022579574859513555 and 0.004904478066078471. The visible preference is for a coherent aromatic core with a limited polar-group arrangement and controlled size; neither halogen addition nor continued growth is uniformly rewarded.

per_task.generated_character: The high-score molecules are conjugated, nitrogen-rich heteroaromatics rather than small aliphatic structures. Seed 2 produces a quinoline-oxadiazole assembly joined by a formamidine-like linkage to a multiply fluorinated aromatic ring; seed 1 produces substituted quinoline acylhydrazones terminating in nitro-containing diazines. Other upper examples contain fused nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles. The digest records aromatic_atom_rate 0.9828, ring_closure_rate 0.9897, mean_smiles_length 69.7 and max_smiles_length 173, consistent with extensive ring chemistry and a sizeable elaborated tail. Its charged_rate 0.3121 includes charge-separated functional groups such as nitro, and does not demonstrate a population of protonated amines. Individual azoles, aryl amides and hydrazones are recognizable synthetic motifs, but extended nitrogen linkages and reactive substitutions make the ensemble questionable. The prior seed-0 leader instead used a conjugated oxygen heterocycle with oxygen- and sulfur-containing heteroaryl appendages and scored 0.6295439524124257.
liabilities: Acylhydrazones and formamidine-like connections introduce tautomeric or configurational alternatives without corresponding geometric specification in the cited structures.
An oxygen-fluorine bond appears in both a leading quinoline derivative and a late enlarged analogue. This is different chemistry from ordinary carbon-bound fluorine.

Nitro-containing heteroaromatics, densely conjugated nitrogen-rich assemblies, and further concatenation warrant chemical-stability and synthetic scrutiny; the recorded score does not establish either property.
missing_features: Stable, geometrically specified alternatives to the imine, hydrazone and extended nitrogen linkages are not established among the supplied leaders. Short polar linkage geometry appears useful, but these observations do not identify a required replacement chemistry.

The high tail has limited evidence for useful saturated shape variation. The equal score of the aromatic and ring-expanded leading pair prevents claiming that additional aromaticity itself is a missing requirement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The quinoline-oxadiazole/formamidine leader and its fused-ring-expanded, partly nonaromatic analogue both score 0.608457551958113. The nitrodiazine acylhydrazone reaches 0.6082806347691206, and replacing the formamidine-like linkage with an enamine-like connection gives 0.606012284431845. These observations support short polar connections between heteroaromatic regions, while showing that this high-score neighbourhood does not strongly distinguish several chemically different changes. A simple fluoromethane fragment scores 0.5. The more ordinarily makeable aryl sulfone-linked amide scores 0.26999666722212967, and the sulfonylhydrazone scores 0.2969569015725102; synthetic familiarity alone therefore does not explain this gradient. A long nitrogen-rich conjugate scores 0.3298125254720826. Late extended analogues reach 0.597892888498683 and 0.5811424248155854, below the leading compact connected heteroaryl arrangements. The new best is below the prior seed-0 best despite the changed heteroaromatic families.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules combine halogenated aromatic surfaces with saturated nitrogen rings and accessible aliphatic amines. Seed 2 favours arylpiperidines connected through aminoalkyl chains to another aromatic group or to a benzodioxane-like ring system. Seed 1 includes a diaryl ether bearing linked piperidine and pyrrolidine rings. These are medium-sized, recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures, although some variants acquire imines or unusual bridged ring closures. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9948, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9793 and halogen_rate 0.7897. Its low charged_rate of 0.0121 does not mean basic centres are scarce: the neutral SMILES explicitly contain secondary and tertiary amines. The prior seed-0 leader was a more compact fused aza-polycyclic structure with an N-propyl substituent and an aryl fluoride, scoring 0.9999968262975905. The new high tail is often more extended while retaining the same broad amine-plus-aromatic character.
liabilities: Several leading structures have multiple basic centres, flexible aminoalkyl chains and heavily halogenated aromatic regions. These raise plausible physicochemical concerns without supplying measured protonation, solubility or selectivity evidence.

Some high-scoring variants contain extra short closures across an aromatic ring or unusually bridged oxygen-containing ring systems; a chemically valid graph does not establish an accessible, unstrained structure.
Late sulfur-nitrogen substitutions and imine additions can alter the electronic character of otherwise useful amines. Relevant saturated centres are not stereochemically specified.
missing_features: No additional objective-required functional group can be identified from the near-ceiling high tail; saturated basic centres and aromatic binding surfaces are already represented.

Systematically controlled linker geometry and configurationally specified saturated-ring variants are not demonstrated. Their absence limits the chemical interpretation of shape changes, but the trajectories do not establish that adding them would raise this score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The diaryl aminoalkyl piperidine reaches 0.9999986918258995, the benzodioxane-linked piperidine reaches 0.9999979836482406, and the diaryl ether with saturated amine rings reaches 0.9999966196836189. By contrast, the acylated/sulfonylated nitrogen-rich aromatic molecule scores 3.8021829379963674e-05 and the cyclic thione/carbonyl structure scores 0.0001124209367987908. A nitro-containing heteroaromatic molecule carrying a primary aminomethyl group still scores only 8.914135292267243e-05: having an amine somewhere is insufficient. A late piperidine sulfenamide scores 0.00292826144046475, while an oversized connected amine/aryl assembly scores 0.2524472505210873. These complete-molecule comparisons associate the high scores with accessible saturated amines in appropriate aryl/linker arrangements, not merely nitrogen or ring abundance. The near-ceiling upper values occur for both the prior compact core and the new extended families.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail consists largely of bulky, densely functionalized ring systems: substituted aromatic groups carry piperazine units alongside fused or rearranged nitrogen heterocycles with carbonyl and ether functionality. Seed 1 often sulfonylates a piperazine nitrogen and adds cyclopropyl or cyclopropenyl groups; seed 2 includes N-methylpiperazine-containing relatives of the initial diaryl fused dicarbonyl heterocycle. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9828, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9552, mean_smiles_length 64.1 and max_smiles_length 163. Aromatic rings, saturated nitrogen rings and heterocyclic carbonyl groups are all plentiful. Many building blocks are conventional, but the complete leading structures combine substantial size with complicated fused or contracted connectivity. Prior seed 0 also favoured carbonyl-rich polycycles, with sulfonylmorpholine-bearing aromatic appendages, and reached 0.2124137877466535. The new high families change the nitrogen-ring decoration while retaining that broad densely substituted character.
liabilities: Leading structures carry substantial molecular bulk, multiple carbonyl groups and complex ring junctions, which complicate synthesis and leave physical-property balance unestablished.
Cyclopropenyl sulfonyl groups and unusually contracted nitrogen-ring connectivity occur near the top; related simpler structures have similar scores.
Late analogues include aryl oxygen-fluorine groups. Saturated ring junctions and substituted carbonyl-containing rings lack explicit stereochemical specification.
missing_features: Less encumbered alternative cores that retain the useful nitrogen/carbonyl/aromatic relationships are incompletely represented among the leaders. The simpler high-scoring ethylsulfonylpiperazine example is direct evidence that extensive fusion is not always necessary.

Defined stereochemistry and a consistent, synthetically credible treatment of ring contraction and fusion are absent from the elaborated saturated cores. A specific missing target substructure cannot be inferred from the observed score ceiling.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial diaryl dicarbonyl heterocycle scores 0.1678386594791329. The more elaborated piperazine/sulfonyl/carbonyl assembly reaches 0.2024037172975581, while related structures with different core and sulfonyl connections score 0.2018354882632635. The seed-2 N-methylpiperazine polycycle reaches 0.1990553832983351. Crucially, the considerably simpler ethylsulfonylpiperazine attached to an aryl aza-lactam system scores 0.19835388147218586: the high tail does not require maximal fused-ring complexity. Methane and hydrazine score 0.0, and the acyclic nitrile/guanidine-like molecule scores 0.009523809523809526. A late phenolic, carbonyl-rich molecule with a piperazine-containing side chain scores 0.18925686512914505. Together these suggest useful combinations of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl environments, with only limited observed gains from extensive elaboration. The new upper values remain below the prior seed-0 best.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2 produces compact bromobenzoyl azetidines bearing a dimethyltriazole and an amino, aminomethyl or hydrazino substituent. Another family contains bridged triazole-bearing nitrogen/oxygen rings. Seed 1 instead favours carbonyl-rich imidazolone/thione and related nitrogen/sulfur-ring chemistry, often with hydrazine or nitroso functionality and a halogenated phenyl group. Thus neither nitrogen heterocycles, saturated rings, amides nor primary amines are generally absent. The digest gives ring_closure_rate 0.9845, aromatic_atom_rate 0.9362, halogen_rate 0.7552 and mean_smiles_length 46.0. Ordinary amino-substituted N-acyl azetidines are more plausible synthetic starting points than several leading N-fluorinated or nitroso-bearing variants. Prior seed 0 favoured amine-substituted unsaturated carbocycles attached to bridged nitrogen/oxygen systems and reached 0.31657990190491997. The new runs access different compact nitrogen-rich cores, while retaining problematic heteroatom connectivity in parts of the high tail.
liabilities: The leading azetidine contains both a nitrogen-nitrogen bond and a nitrogen-fluorine bond. Its relatively high score is not evidence of ordinary chemical stability.

Other high examples contain nitroso-bearing nitrogen chains, multiple adjacent carbonyl groups, sulfur-nitrogen bonds or bridged nitrogen-oxygen connectivity, all of which merit scrutiny before calling the molecules practical synthesis targets.

Several saturated cores admit configurational alternatives but contain no explicit stereocentre annotations; large late assemblies further complicate synthesis without retaining the high-score arrangement.
missing_features: Stable alternatives that preserve the successful local amino/heteroaryl/amide arrangement while replacing the reactive hydrazino or nitroso chemistry are not established at the leading score level. Conventional primary amine variants are present, so an absence-of-amines diagnosis would be false.
Configurationally specified azetidine and bridged-ring variants are missing from the emitted structures. The observations do not establish which configuration, if any, the objective would reward.
Core and substituent relocation frequently fail to preserve the narrow useful arrangement. The sampled molecules do not identify a uniquely required missing heterocycle or halogen pattern.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scores 0.3532645847815139. Its fluoromethyl-substituted hydrazino counterpart, which has carbon-bound fluorine rather than the same nitrogen-fluorine bond, scores 0.32889377886677046. The otherwise related aminomethyl and amino examples score 0.28462019114736514 and 0.27965004712778896. A separate nitroso-bearing carbonyl heterocycle reaches 0.3051477892817265. Location and connectivity matter: placing an N-fluorohydrazino substituent on the triazole while retaining the azetidine aminomethyl group gives only 0.0009072140941170833. The bulky polycyclic, polyol-containing low-tail conjugate scores 0.0, and a very large halogenated aromatic/tetrazole assembly scores 2.0625181207397576e-74. The final ring-expanded dicarbonyl/triazole structure scores 0.02556661875964576. The visible preference is for a compact and specific nitrogen/amide/aryl arrangement, with particularly sharp penalties for some elaborations; nitrogen or fluorine addition alone is not a supported rule. The pooled median is 0.001511 despite the substantially higher leading examples.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited high tails contain an aryl hypochlorite scoring 0.49263201457052164, an aryl sulfur-chlorine derivative scoring 0.4686060677105447, and an N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scoring 0.3532645847815139. Other cited examples include oxygen-fluorine bonds and nitroso-bearing nitrogen chains. Conventional phenol, amide and primary amine alternatives also occur. These examples show that reactive connectivity survives even among favourable accepted observations.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve chemically credible functional-group connectivity when modifying useful molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable functional-group replacements available while retaining the surrounding aryl, amine and carbonyl relationships. Distinguish carbon-bound halogen changes from halogenating oxygen, nitrogen or sulfur, and compare chemically coherent alternatives through the current session's accepted feedback.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited low tails include methane and hydrazine at 0.0, tiny fluorinated heteroatom fragments at 0.0, and oversized polyaryl or polyfunctional conjugates with extremely small scores. Conversely, some relatively large piperazine/carbonyl structures occupy a high tail, while a simpler ethylsulfonylpiperazine/aza-lactam structure scores 0.19835388147218586 near more elaborate relatives. The evidence supports context-dependent size and connectivity requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Control of molecular size and connectivity is uneven: useful cores are sometimes fragmented away or expanded into overly elaborate assemblies.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide growth, contraction and linker changes that preserve a coherent molecular core and useful local functional-group relationships. Explore size around accepted structures without relying on either repeated fragmentation or concatenation, and let feedback determine useful complexity for the current session.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Cited triazolyl azetidines, bridged nitrogen/oxygen cores, substituted saturated amine rings and carbonyl-rich ring junctions can have configurational alternatives. Some leading structures also contain unusually short closures across aromatic frameworks or contracted ring systems. Abundant ring-closure markers therefore establish ring presence, not well-defined or accessible geometry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks explicit stereochemical specification and provides inconsistent geometric control over new ring closures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support explicit configurational alternatives and chemically credible ring closure, expansion and contraction moves around useful molecular arrangements. Treat changes of saturation, junction geometry and linker shape as distinct chemical possibilities for feedback to assess. The present observations establish missing representation, not a demonstrated score benefit from any particular configuration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The supplied leaders repeatedly revisit related biaryl-pyrazole or quinoline-urea cores, imine/acylhydrazone-linked heteroaromatics, aryl saturated-amine architectures, piperazine-bearing carbonyl polycycles, and N-acyl azetidines. Different seeds reach visibly different core families, showing that the generator can change scaffold, but much of each leading neighbourhood consists of decoration, local ring edits or further assembly of those families.
transferable_gaps.gap: Coverage of chemically distinct useful cores remains uneven within runs, despite abundant unique molecular identities and an overall varied repertoire.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Maintain access to multiple accepted scaffold families and enable core replacements that preserve useful spatial relationships among donors, acceptors, amines and aromatic groups. Assess diversity in the chemistry of the cores and their functional-group arrangement rather than treating a new molecular string or peripheral substituent as sufficient coverage.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Accessible saturated amines in aryl/linker arrangements accompany scores such as 0.9999986918258995, while a nitro-containing aromatic molecule that also has a primary amine scores 8.914135292267243e-05. In another local family, the N-fluorohydrazino azetidine scores 0.3532645847815139, but a structure carrying that type of substituent on the triazole while retaining an aminomethyl group scores 0.0009072140941170833. These are whole-molecule observations, but they directly contradict a simple more-nitrogen or more-fluorine interpretation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Functional-group placement is not reliably conserved when exploring favourable amine and heteroaryl chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and vary functional-group attachment context, spacing and electronic environment deliberately. Make changes to a free amine, an amide nitrogen, a ring nitrogen and an imine distinct chemical operations so accepted feedback can reveal useful local arrangements without repeatedly losing them during unrelated growth.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent prior from the supplied unlabeled SMILES, always conditioning each next-token prediction on the intact preceding tokens. Its fixed holdout chooses the prior checkpoint. Each objective then starts with a fresh policy and a frozen reference prior. The best current observations train together with a uniform sample from a memory of the thirty-two strongest earlier accepted elites, preserving their original strings and accepted rewards. Bounded prior-likelihood-plus-reward updates adapt the policy, which samples complete new molecules with chemical and duplicate checks. The prior has not been trained to recover after a small amount of context information is missing.
approach.novelty: During each unlabeled training sequence, hide exactly one randomly selected content-token embedding and still predict the original unmodified targets with the existing equal-token loss. The rest of the sequence remains visible. This asks the recurrent state to use surrounding context instead of depending entirely on one local input. Clean strings and the original clean holdout still determine checkpoint selection, and online learning and generation use ordinary intact inputs. Earlier siblings changed bracket units, equivalent string views or branch loss allocation; this Child tests robustness to one missing internal context vector without changing those mechanisms. A successful robustness result still has to translate into useful valid new molecules.

nodes.hypothesis: Train the unlabeled recurrent prior to predict the unchanged original SMILES targets after zeroing exactly one uniformly selected eligible content-token input embedding per sequence, while keeping the Parent uniform token loss, clean fixed-holdout checkpoint selection and all online computations unchanged.

finding_summary.headline: Missing-context prediction improved sharply, but validity and final molecular scores declined
finding_summary.insights: The missing-vector probe measures a capability the prior successfully learned; the absolute erased-context loss improvement is much larger than the small clean-context loss degradation. Its failure to improve raw molecular validity separates this capability from tolerance of the mistakes that matter during ordinary generation. The probe leaves all later teacher-forced tokens correct and never measures recovery from an incorrectly sampled token or molecular graph. It therefore supplies no evidence that the main online error source has been addressed. Lower duplicate concentration broadened the sampled output slightly, but did not preserve the chemical arrangements needed for the strongest objectives. The molecular assessment found mostly conventional medicinal chemistry, together with extreme polar and lipophilic tails; for sitagliptin, the stronger parental polar-ring/carbonyl families were not recovered. This connects the score loss to a change in chemical coverage without identifying a single causal functional group. The evidence supports missing-context robustness as a retained capability, with a clean-language-modeling tradeoff and no demonstrated optimization gain under the tested panel.
finding_summary.results: The preparation mechanism executed on all three seeds: one eligible content embedding was erased in each of 7,613,952 training-sequence exposures per prior, with the original target strings preserved. Independent replay exactly reproduced all three training-target and erasure-mask receipts. On the entire fixed 4,096-row holdout for each seed, mean erased-downstream negative log likelihood fell from the Parent's 1.00417 to 0.53006; every seed improved. The corresponding erasure penalty fell from 0.53933 to 0.05658. This was a real improvement in prediction with missing context, although clean full-sequence NLL worsened from 0.56458 to 0.57213. Clean likelihood still selected checkpoints, and online computation used intact inputs with a frozen prior. Downstream generation did not gain validity: raw RDKit-valid draws fell from 90.43% to 89.27%. Duplicate draws fell from 30.11% to 27.51%, so the raw canonical-novel fraction rose from 60.31% to 61.76%; all 4,350 submitted proposals remained valid and unique. The final three-seed macro mean fell from 0.50755 to 0.49844, a paired change of -0.00911. Seed changes were -0.01795, +0.00012 and -0.00950. Mean zaleplon score rose by 0.03533, while sitagliptin fell by 0.08046 and lost score in every seed. The intended +0.002 macro improvement was not achieved.

molecular.headline: Mostly conventional aromatic amides, amines and sulfonamides, with extreme polar or lipophilic tails and undefined stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were read. Each current task contains 900 molecules and 870 optimizer proposals. The output is broadly diverse and mainly resembles ordinary medicinal chemistry: aryl amides and ureas, heteroaromatic amino compounds, indanol/tetralin-like alcohols, piperazines, sulfonamides, cyclic carbonyl compounds and ether-linked heterocycles. Most leading structures have plausible synthetic entry points and conventional bonding. Ring-closure rates range from 0.9793 to 0.9977 and aromatic-token rates from 0.946 to 0.992. Mean SMILES lengths range from 40.4 to 50.5, while the low tails include much larger peptides, polyamines, sugars, macrocycles and long hydrocarbon chains. Charged-token rates range from 0.0368 to 0.1299 and include ordinary nitro, azide and ammonium representations as well as occasional unusual electronic states; these rates are not a measure of solution ionization. All stereocentre-token rates are 0.0, as in the parent strings, leaving substituted saturated-ring alcohols and other stereogenic products undefined. The chemistry is generally plausible and moderately drug-like, but chemical plausibility alone does not explain the score variation, and individual reactive or geometrically difficult alternatives remain.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are moderate-sized aromatic amides or diaryl ureas, with methoxy phenyl or pyridyl groups, another aryl ring and a pyridyl or pyrimidyl carbonyl partner. Connections vary between methylene, direct biaryl and diarylamino arrangements. The molecules have recognizable amide/urea donors and acceptors, mostly ordinary aromatic substitution and little stereochemical complexity. They are generally synthetically plausible. The lowest examples are substantially larger peptide-like structures, highly hydroxylated or phosphorylated compounds, a long-ring polyamine and a very small cyanide species. Final molecules range from appropriate aromatic amides to much simpler hydrocarbons or heteroarenes that lose the polar-linker arrangement.
liabilities: Multiple aromatic rings with flexible methylene or amino links can increase conformational freedom even when the individual bonds are ordinary.
Peptide-like and highly hydroxylated proposals introduce substantial size or polarity outside the leading families.
Small charged fragments and isolated unusual electronic-state variants occur in the wider trajectories despite the conventional leading chemistry.
missing_features: Low peptide-like, polyol and macrocyclic products lack the compact aromatic and carbonyl-linker organization of the leading molecules.
The simpler low final heteroarenes lack the amide/urea arrangement retained by the stronger examples; aromatic content alone is insufficient.

The current displayed leaders do not cover the substituted indole-carboxamide arrangement of the stronger parent seed-0 molecule. That is a coverage difference rather than proof that an indole is universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Several different methoxy diarylmethyl heteroaryl amides and a methoxypyridyl/diaryl urea all score 0.48839749189747395. Related diarylamino and alternative pyridyl amides score 0.4767312946227961. These ties support a relatively compact aromatic/polar-linker balance without identifying one uniquely required ring nitrogen position or linkage. An aromatic tertiary amide in the final set scores 0.4155143263564241, whereas a naphthalene-pyridine without the amide arrangement scores 0.0019315588620192265. The large peptide-like low example scores 1.2479689558218067e-56. Parent seed 0 reached 0.5280588545286916 with a substituted indole carboxamide, while current seed 0 reaches 0.48839749189747395 with diarylmethyl amides. Current seed 1 and seed 2 reach 0.48839749189747395 and 0.4540824430539665 versus parental 0.4067656765249372 and 0.3900700429110833. The new leading chemistry is conventional, but the comparisons do not isolate a single missing pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: The best molecules are aromatic nitrogen heterocycles bearing arylamino groups, alkoxy substitution, nitrile or trifluoromethyl groups and, in the leader, a nitroanilide carboxamide. Other strong families include amino-linked fused diones, ordinary aryl sulfonamides and acylhydrazones. These are generally moderate to bulky, planar or partly planar medicinal-chemistry structures with recognizable synthetic connections. The low examples include a large ester/amide/methylsulfone assembly, an indole ether-acetamide/benzothiazole combination and a sulfone-substituted indole. Small acyclic or fluorocarbon fragments sit close to the low baseline. The output has abundant aromatic and heteroatom content but its placement matters.
liabilities: Several leading compounds carry extensive aromatic and fluorinated substitution with little saturated shape diversity.
Nitroaryl, acylhydrazone and thioether variants have distinct chemical liabilities that are not resolved by their similar scores.
A low charged nitrogen/oxygen fragment has an unusual electronic-state representation, so charge tokens should not be interpreted as uniformly ordinary ionization chemistry.
missing_features: The small low-baseline fragments lack the connected aromatic and polar-linker organization of the stronger products.

The low but synthetically plausible multiaryl structures show that merely including heterocycles, an amide or oxidized sulfur does not preserve the useful arrangement. Matched attachment-position and ring-nitrogen variants remain incompletely explored in the displayed leaders.
Less aromatic, more saturated shape variants retaining the useful polar fragments are limited among the strongest examples; their potential score benefit is not established by this set.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The nitroanilide/aza-aromatic leader scores 0.6111751890298603. Replacing that carboxanilide appendage by methoxy in the same broader scaffold family gives 0.6076219961668878; a nitrile relative scores 0.6056754360035471. Amino-linked diones with ethylthio, methoxy or propargyloxy substitution all score 0.6014089846464902, so those peripheral groups are not uniquely distinguished. An aryl sulfonamide reaches 0.5999223218699244, whereas a differently arranged sulfone-indole scores 0.31752369822101023 and an indole/benzothiazole amide scores 0.3004981574996588. This is evidence for particular heteroaromatic/linker arrangements, not a general sulfur penalty or reward. Current per-seed maxima are 0.6111751890298603, 0.5908091850309445 and 0.5784746092483299, compared with parental 0.5913471190523991, 0.61192894944948 and 0.5758665324320438. The principal families change while remaining largely conventional.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders are conventional aryl- or pyridyl-piperazines connected through ether/alkyl or aminoalkyl chains to indanol- or tetralin-like frameworks. Alcohol, methoxy, amino and aryl halogen substituents vary around the fused ring. The products combine available aliphatic amines with aromatic surface and a polar alcohol or ether. Seed 2 also produces flexible biaryl compounds with an expanded diaza ring and a nitrile-bearing phenoxyethyl connection. These are recognizable synthetic families. Low examples are amide, ester, sulfonamide or hydrazone-dominated compounds lacking the same organized aliphatic-amine framework, although one low structure does contain a primary amine.
liabilities: Flexible alkyl chains and several potentially basic centres introduce conformational and ionization ambiguity.
Unspecified alcohol and substituted-ring stereochemistry prevents the leading structures from describing single defined stereoisomers.
Other seeds include an organic azide among stronger products, so the conventional main piperazine family does not imply uniform stability across the full output.
missing_features: The low amide/sulfonamide series lacks the accessible aliphatic amine placement and hydrophobic-ring spacing of the stronger piperazine families.
The low primary-amine-containing urea shows that a basic centre without the useful overall arrangement is insufficient; matched linker geometry and ring-size comparisons are still needed.
The leading alcohol-bearing fused rings have potential stereogenic centres but no specified configurations. No stereochemical preference can be read from the supplied unlabelled molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluoroindanol/propoxy/pyridylpiperazine molecule scores 0.999998460810131; its nonfluorinated indanol relative scores 0.9999948760798478. Several aminoalkyl/tetralin-like alternatives also approach 1.0, and matched aryl fluorine/chlorine substitutions have identical recorded values of 0.9999949345268564 or 0.9999929302907594. These nearly equal values support the general aryl/aliphatic-amine arrangement but do not establish a unique halogen or fused-ring size requirement. The lowest amide-rich example scores 3.243749221679736e-05, while a primary-amine-containing but differently connected urea scores 6.812931663695377e-05; amine presence alone is not enough. Parent seed 1 already had an indole/alkyl/arylpiperazine leader at 0.9999999999666845. The present indanol/tetralin-like output changes the associated ring and linker chemistry without isolating a preferred pharmacophore from these small numerical differences.

per_task.generated_character: The leading molecules include an N-methylpiperazine sulfonamide attached to a fused benzoxazolinone-like cyclic carbamate, and a benzodioxole-sulfonyl piperazine bearing a benzodioxole acetamide side chain. Other stronger examples are a benzodioxole-substituted fused aromatic lactam, imidazole-like compounds, aromatic amides and sulfonamides. These have conventional amine, carbonyl, ether and oxidized sulfur functionality and are mostly synthetically plausible. Low products include flexible acyclic polyamines, small sulfur-containing acids, a saturated cage amide and a small carbonyl-containing oxygen/sulfur ring. The final molecules span complex sulfonamide assemblies and simpler structures lacking the same aromatic/polar arrangement.
liabilities: Large sulfonamide/amide combinations can add aromatic bulk and polarity while scoring below a simpler leader.
Some saturated or fused alternatives have undefined stereochemical relationships, although the principal piperazine leaders are achiral.
Small fragments and highly flexible charged or polyamine products can lose the aromatic organization retained by the stronger structures.
missing_features: The low flexible polyamines and small sulfur-containing acids lack the integrated aromatic/carbonyl or sulfonyl/amine arrangement found in the stronger molecules.
The displayed leaders incompletely sample matched aromatic partners and linker placements around the sulfonyl-piperazine arrangement; larger or more polar appendages are not automatically beneficial.

The trajectories do not identify one uniquely missing group beyond these observed associations. The remaining chemistry gap concerns compatible connectivity and shape rather than adding piperazine or sulfur indiscriminately.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact piperazine/fused cyclic-carbamate sulfonamide scores 0.2189839359276689, while the larger benzodioxole/sulfonyl-piperazine/acetamide combination scores 0.2160027395643138. A benzodioxole-linked aromatic lactam reaches 0.19966749769191652. Thus higher scores can occur with several carbonyl- and aromatic-containing arrangements, with a particularly clear sulfonyl-piperazine family. A flexible acyclic polyamine/polyether scores 0.0, a small sulfur-ring acid scores 0.026148818018424533, and a more complex saturated cage amide scores 0.04076048393103888. The final methoxyaryl piperazine amide reaches only 0.1411862416005035, showing that piperazine alone is not sufficient. The parent seed-2 N-methyl phenylsulfonyl piperazine scored 0.20718664161756667, versus 0.2189839359276689 for the current fused-carbamate aryl partner. Current seed 0 and seed 1 reach 0.19966749769191652 and 0.2160027395643138 versus parental 0.20090425134085538 and 0.21944544104637362.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a diarylethyl-substituted aminoguanidine hydrazone, combining aromatic hydrophobic groups with a strongly polar imino/nitrogen-rich head. Other stronger products are quite different: a pyrrolidine linked to a small sulfonylated diaza ring with an oxime-like group, an ester/amide-substituted aromatic pyridone, an oxalamide with a bridged saturated amine, and ether-linked triazole/imidazole-like heterocycles. Most fragments are familiar, but hydrazone configuration, small-ring strain and ionization remain unresolved. The lowest products are very long lipids or polyamines, highly hydroxylated sugar/nucleoside-like compounds and other bulky flexible molecules. There is no dominant shared high-scoring ring family.
liabilities: The aminoguanidine hydrazone combines a potentially strongly basic head with an unassigned imine configuration and an N-N connection.

nodes.method_name: Augmented Hill-Climb with a corpus-trained SMILES policy
nodes.method_thesis: Train a compact autoregressive SMILES prior solely on the supplied unlabeled corpus, then initialize a fresh policy from that prior for each objective. Use the initial observations and each subsequent scored batch to update only its highest-reward sequences with the Augmented Hill-Climb loss: fit policy log likelihood to frozen-prior log likelihood plus scaled observed reward. Sample complete molecules token by token from the updated policy, canonicalize them, and refill invalid or duplicate proposals by further generation. The corpus supplies language training, never a ranked molecular pool. Elite-conditioned policy updates should shift generation toward new high-scoring molecular combinations quickly enough to improve the benchmark's mean final Top-1. This is a small-budget transfer hypothesis, not a claim that published larger-budget gains carry over. The root uses the current scored batch; randomized historical replay is reserved for the first improvement. The anchor's elite augmented-likelihood mechanism is described by [Thomas et al.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13321-022-00646-z).
