molecular.headline: Sulfur-rich cages persist; a stronger aryl-amine family removes sulfur but retains strained nitrogen rings
molecular.overall_character: All supplied current and parent trajectories were inspected. Every objective has 900 entries, including 870 optimizer proposals, and none lacks trajectories. These are consistently substantial ring-containing molecules: ring-closure and branch presence rates are 1.0 throughout. Aromatic-token presence is also 1.0 on several populations, 0.9345 on the arylamide population, and 0.7184 on the sulfur-cage population. These are molecule-level text counters, not aromatic atom fractions, ring feasibility, or molecular conformations. The outputs range from recognizable indole carboxamides and aryl cyclic amines to heavily bridged N/O frameworks, long sulfur/oxygen side chains, and multiply bonded sulfur cages. Mean SMILES lengths range from 46.9 to 69.0; the main problem is not a population of trivial fragments or universally giant repeated assemblies. Rather, much of the visible variety changes decoration or connectivity within seed-specific complex families. Explicit charge and tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero, despite potentially basic amines and stereogenic carbon or sulfur connectivity. Some current chemistry differs meaningfully from the parent, especially the sulfur-free aryl-amine leader, while other leading structures and entire chemical trajectories are unchanged. Apparent synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug likeness weak because useful recognizable groups coexist with strained rings, unusual sulfur valence, reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, and undefined stereochemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The compact leaders carry aromatic rings and amide or ketone carbonyls, but they separate into chemically different families. The best combines an alkyl-substituted unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen ring system, a primary carboxamide, and an acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent benzene carbons. That last unit is a strained benzene-fused small nitrogen ring, not an ordinary anilide. Related leaders retain the same constrained amide nitrogen with benzothiophene, aminomethoxy, or chloromethyl substitution. A more conventional ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide is also near the top. The final seed instead favors pyridylmethyl ketones attached to unusual sulfur-containing unsaturated rings and a cyclobutadiene-like small ring. Ring presence is 1.0 and aromatic presence 0.9345, with mean SMILES length 46.9; ring abundance coexists with substantial chemical strain.
liabilities: The acylated nitrogen bridging adjacent aromatic carbons creates severe small-ring geometry concerns.
Multiply bonded ring sulfur with additional substituents should not be read as ordinary thiophene or terminal thiocarbonyl chemistry.
Late cyclobutadiene-like rings are highly strained, and several related products also contain N-N or N-O bonds.
Thiol and chloromethyl decorations add reactivity concerns without a consistent local score advantage.
missing_features: Ordinary amide-nitrogen and ring alternatives retaining the leading carbonyl and aromatic arrangement are not established within the strongest strained-amide series.
Stable sulfur bonding and less strained fusion patterns are underrepresented around the late pyridyl ketones.
Chemically credible matched alternatives linking the conventional indole family to the higher-scoring unusual topology are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The unusual sulfur/strained-amide leader scores 0.425403, versus 0.404974 after adding a thiol to its benzene ring and 0.385223 after adding a hydroxyl group there. Thus those extra donor groups do not improve this local series. The conventional indole carboxanilide reaches 0.399050, above the initial methoxy-rich fluorophenyl indole amide at 0.305105; high scores do not require the strained nitrogen ring. Low optimizer molecules remain substantial: a reduced, N-O-containing arylamide with a difficult heteroaryl substituent scores 0.030640, and replacing the pyridyl region of a 0.390279 ketone family with an expanded nonaromatic nitrogen ring gives 0.031675. The observed association is with the intact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement rather than ring count alone. The current seed-0 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.396663, while the conventional seed-1 leader and its supplied chemical trajectory are unchanged. The current seed-2 maximum is below the parent's 0.410039 and replaces N-chloro arylamide chemistry with a different strained sulfur/ketone family.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant leading family is relatively large and flexible: a substituted chlorophenyl imine is connected through a fluorinated amino-bearing carbon to a nitrogen-rich fused carbonyl/thione ring system. An extended chain contains successive sulfur/oxygen connections, acetal-like centres, and a terminal chlorinated group; a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur links it back toward the heterocycle. Some leaders replace an N-methyl group with direct N-bromination. Another current seed produces compact, extensively connected aza/oxygen rings with unusual sulfur triple bonding and cumulated nitrogen/carbon unsaturation. Late seed-2 molecules contain aromatic diones, sulfenyl bromides, thioether-rich branches, and unsaturated side chains. Aromatic and ring presence are both 1.0; mean SMILES length is 68.3 and maximum 95. These are complex complete molecules, with difficult stability and synthesis questions rather than missing ring content.
liabilities: Direct nitrogen-bromine and sulfur-bromine bonds are reactive functionalities, distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogen substitution.
The additionally substituted carbon-sulfur multiple bonds and sulfur triple-bond motifs are chemically unusual.
Long mixed oxygen/sulfur chains and imine connections introduce potential hydrolytic or oxidative liabilities and many conformational choices.
The cumulated-double-bond token rate of 0.0874 supports a visible population of unusual unsaturated connections, but does not establish their stability.
missing_features: Matched stable replacements for the multiply bonded sulfur connections and direct N-bromination are not established around the leading architecture.
Shorter, less labile side chains preserving the main aryl/heterocarbonyl relationship are insufficiently represented.
Independent ordinary heteroaromatic frameworks with the same functional-group relationships are underrepresented relative to complex local rearrangements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading sulfur-rich, N-brominated structure scores 0.616171 and is exactly the parent's seed-0 leader; that entire supplied chemical trajectory is unchanged. A group at 0.615507 includes extension of an aryl ethyl group to propyl, extension of a sulfur-bound methyl to ethyl, and a matched replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. The score therefore provides no local evidence that N-bromination or those chain extensions are necessary. Low optimizer examples retain complete aryl/carbonyl scaffolds at 0.526082-0.531030, versus the initial aryl dione at 0.548381. The association is with detailed heteroatom and connecting-group arrangements, not simply having more heteroaromatic rings. The current seed-1 maximum is 0.606300 versus the parent's 0.590648, with more compact but chemically unusual fused-ring/sulfur chemistry; the current seed-2 maximum is 0.589214 versus the parent's 0.609218 and carries more sulfur-rich connections. nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent starts from the best supplied molecule and walks through local graph edits. Its neighborhood includes direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen with a carbon in the same six-member ring, preserving composition. It normalizes molecular identities, rejects duplicates and uses short-lived inverse local-motif restrictions to admit the first full batch of neighbors. After real feedback it moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor, even when every neighbor is worse, and keeps a separate best archive. Equal batch maxima are currently resolved by canonical text order; memory then receives the selected transition's actual changes.
approach.novelty: Add a minimum-heavy-atom tie rule: among exact accepted batch maxima, choose the molecule with the fewest heavy atoms and use canonical order for any remaining tie. This makes measured score equality an opportunity to avoid unnecessary growth before the next neighborhood is generated. Earlier siblings changed the edit menu, chemical admissibility or inverse memory. The branch-deletion experiment established access to compact proposals but weak retention and later regrowth; this experiment changes only the choice among existing equally best accepted neighbors. No sibling in the supplied history has tested this size preference at feedback.

nodes.hypothesis: Among exact accepted-score batch maxima, select the candidate with the fewest heavy atoms before applying the inherited canonical lexical fallback, so an equally scored larger neighbor cannot become current solely because of its canonical spelling.

finding_summary.headline: Six smaller tied winners were executed, but later scores did not improve
finding_summary.insights: Canonical ordering did sometimes choose unnecessary growth at an exactly tied score, so this experiment establishes a real selection opportunity. Avoiding that growth did not preserve a permanently compact or more productive walk: every changed choice was followed by a later growth move, and the six-transition plateau containing the first seed-2 change kept its original length. Mean proposal size in the affected task decreased by only 0.30 heavy atoms, with the median unchanged at 38. Smaller also did not mean chemically simpler: one changed choice introduced a carbon-sulfur triple bond, and the molecular assessment still finds reactive heteroatom attachments and questionable complete structures. Half of the changed choices altered bonds or elements without shrinking their own source; the other half deleted one atom. The poorer later results therefore concern changed chemical neighborhoods and memory provenance, not an isolated effect of size. In the seed-2 continuation, accepted source-beating neighbors fell from 19 to nine. The evidence narrows the opportunity to sparse exact ties in one objective family and makes chemically meaningful tie preferences or persistence of compact states worth testing separately; neither has a demonstrated score benefit here.
finding_summary.results: The rule changed six of 435 accepted transitions, all on equal-score plateaus in deco_hop seeds 0 and 2. Each selected an already scored maximum with one or two fewer heavy atoms than the lexical alternative, saving 10 atoms across those same-batch comparisons. All selected identities reached the actual current state and memory update. The other 429 choices, the immediate maximum score, canonical fallback and independent archive rule passed reconstruction checks. The three-seed panel mean fell from 0.521759 to 0.520655: paired change -0.001104 against the preregistered +0.002 minimum. Deco_hop endpoints fell by 0.001632 in seed 0 and 0.014925 in seed 2; every other task/replica scored trajectory was identical. The local tie mechanism is confirmed, while its expected score benefit was not observed.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich, often sulfur-heavy molecules retain recognizable motifs but lack reliable chemical plausibility and specified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All five supplied tasks are covered; none lacks trajectories. Each has 900 recorded molecules across three seeds, including 870 optimizer proposals. These are branched, polycyclic organic graphs with substantial aromatic content, ordinary carbonyl and amine groups, and frequent sulfur and halogen substitution. Every task has string-level ring_closure_rate 1.0; aromatic_atom_rate, meaning presence of aromatic SMILES atoms rather than their atom fraction, ranges from 0.7184 to 1.0. There is no shortage of rings. Passive RDKit inspection of the supplied trajectories gives task median heavy-atom counts of 25, 38, 36, 35 and 29 in the fixed task order. All optimizer proposals parse in the matching environment. Parsing establishes graph acceptance, not stability, a synthesis route or a realizable conformation. Many later structures combine multiple bonds to sulfur, heteroatom-halogen attachments, difficult ring bridges and unspecified stereogenic centers. All five digest charged_rate and stereocentre_rate values are 0.0. This means no explicit charge or tetrahedral stereochemical notation; it does not mean the molecules cannot ionize or are achiral. Structural diversity is moderate: the observed families differ across tasks and seeds, but many distinct graphs remain decorated or distorted descendants of recognizable starting scaffolds. Relative to Parent n-abcd951ab7cc, molecule identities and recorded scores are identical throughout every seed of zaleplon_mpo, drd2_docking, median_2 and sitagliptin_mpo, and throughout deco_hop seed 1. The changed deco_hop trajectories retain the same broad imide/heteroaromatic chemistry; smaller average atom count does not establish improved chemical quality. The digest final_molecules excerpts cover only seed 2 evaluations 295-300 and are final proposals, not the best archive or a summary of every seed. All numerical graph descriptions below were passively derived from the provided SMILES; synthetic plausibility and missing chemistry are qualitative readings. Absent features have no measured counterfactual score, so an unseen objective-specific pharmacophore cannot be inferred from these records.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms, median 25, with median three perceived rings. The best seed-2 molecule at evaluation 133 is a substituted benzofuran anilide: an aromatic fused oxygen heterocycle, an N-chlorinated carboxamide, an aminophenyl group, a thiol and a carbon bearing amine and chlorine. The seed-1 high scorer at evaluation 61 is a more recognizable ethoxy/methyl/thiol-substituted indole carboxanilide; the seed-0 high scorer at evaluation 81 is a benzothiophene aryl ketone with aminomethoxy and chloromethyl substituents. Later proposals also contain bridged, partly dearomatized oxygen/sulfur frameworks. The ring and aromatic presence rates are 1.0 and 0.9563; halogen presence is 0.7552. The indole anilide looks appreciably more synthetically approachable than the N-haloamide and later bridged sulfur structures. Chemistry and scores match the Parent trajectories.
liabilities: The best example contains an N-chloroamide and a carbon bearing both amine and chlorine, while other cited examples contain N-F/N-O bonds or thiols; these raise stability and handling questions.
The final framework contains unusual sulfur multiple bonding and an N-N substituent. Complex ring connectivity and unspecified configuration reduce confidence in a straightforward synthesis.
missing_features: Reliable retention of the compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl architecture: many lower-scoring neighbors expand or dearomatize the core, or replace the carbonyl linkage.

A broad set of ordinary substituent variants around that observed high-scoring architecture without accompanying N-halogenation, labile sulfur features or elaborate bridges; such variants are not established by the top excerpt.
Specified configurations for the stereogenic substituted carbons and bridged products; the records do not establish that adding stereochemical specification would improve this score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxanilide scores 0.3051048083696145; related compact fused heteroaromatic carbonyl compounds reach 0.39905049777278273 and 0.41003927643747895. The benzothiophene ketone scores 0.393567030299894, so an amide is not obligatory within the observed high-scoring family. Low optimizer examples at 0.021532846118034143 and 0.023463222457063 have expanded/dearomatized cores despite retaining an aryl carbonyl; the evaluation-42 example that replaces the carbonyl linkage with a substituted saturated carbon scores 0.03343008011310944. The association supports compact fused heteroaromatic/carbonyl architecture more than indiscriminate ring editing. It does not isolate a causal benefit for thiols or N-halogenation. The final seed-2 sulfur-bridged hydrazine-containing proposal scores 0.3852230774700024, showing that a fairly high score can coexist with less conventional chemistry.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It makes random atom, bond and ring edits, filters invalid and previously proposed molecules, and directly evaluates the first full batch that passes its short-term memory. It then moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even if that neighbor is worse, while keeping a separate record of the best molecule found. After the selected move, it stores up to four signed local-motif changes that would reverse parts of that move. These restrictions last four completed steps, refresh on overlap and can be released in oldest-first order when they obstruct generation. At present, matching any single remembered inverse attribute vetoes a candidate, so a shared local feature can suppress a move without evidence that it reverses the rest of the remembered transition.
approach.novelty: Add a conjunction across the two inverse signs from the same remembered transition. A candidate is tabu only when it both removes at least one local motif introduced by that transition and restores at least one local motif that transition removed. A partial match remains admissible, and matches belonging to different transitions cannot be combined. This changes the meaning of a structural reversal without changing the underlying graph walk. The lineage currently contains only its root, which tested independent single-attribute vetoes; no sibling has tested this paired evidence rule. The experiment asks whether admitting partially overlapping moves exposes more useful neighbors while a smaller set of structurally supported vetoes continues to affect the walk.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace any-single-attribute tabu vetoes with same-transition bidirectional inverse-attribute matching: veto a valid novel graph edit only if its signed motif changes match at least one active positive restriction and at least one active negative restriction originating from the same selected accepted transition.

finding_summary.headline: Paired tabu matching reproduced; an identity lookup crash left one replica incomplete.
finding_summary.insights:
The narrower reversal test reproducibly changes oracle allocation and the walk while retaining active structural memory. Correct same-transition matching, intact four-step expiry and the surviving fresh-identity vetoes rule out erased memory as the source of easier admission. Most newly admitted neighbors still score below their source, so greater admissibility has not established better average neighborhood quality. The useful effects arise from a minority of admitted moves; the separate value of the remaining vetoes remains unmeasured because rejected alternatives were never scored.

The identity lookup failure previously seen only in the supplied smoke evidence now occurs in a formal replica. Its cause is localized: the generator keys pending proposals by a molecular spelling that changes when the evaluator canonicalizes it. The failing proposal was one of the newly admitted partial matches. This exposes an inherited execution limitation on the newly accessible trajectory and prevents a claim of complete or repeatable score benefit. A stable identity join and a complete replica are needed before assessing that benefit.

The molecular assessment shows that partial-overlap admission still explores recurring ring-rich families with unusual sulfur bonding, dense ring junctions and unspecified geometry. Memory selectivity does not establish chemically plausible alternatives or broad useful scaffold coverage; those limitations remain separate from the verified matching effect.
finding_summary.results:
Across the two added replicas' observed streams, the original any-match rule would veto 1,578 of 2,831 valid novel attempts (55.74%); the paired rule vetoed 121 (4.27%) on the same candidates and live memory. All 1,457 newly admitted proposals reached evaluation, accounting for 53.76% of optimizer evaluations. Of these, 141 beat their current source (9.68%), and their mean neighbor-minus-source score was -0.09247. They supplied 141 actual next-current states and 60 strict incumbent-improving observations. The remaining restrictions vetoed 112 distinct task/run molecular identities, changed 79 of 271 batches and produced nine selected next states absent from the passive unfiltered batch. Matching and memory-lifecycle checks agreed with the intended rule throughout the observed execution.

The first added replica completed all five tasks at 300 evaluations each, scoring 0.5277988 in macro final Top-1 versus 0.5180779 in the earlier screening replica of this same algorithm. The second added replica completed four tasks but crashed on zaleplon after 110 evaluations. Its completed final scores were 0.6092183 for decoration hopping, 0.9148144 for DRD2, 0.2018564 for median_2 and 0.4484554 for sitagliptin. The evaluator reports 1,310 total calls and no macro score for that replica, so there is no complete three-seed score estimate.

The crash occurred after the evaluator scored a full ten-molecule batch. The first accepted molecule's canonical spelling changed between generation and feedback, so its pending record could not be found. All ten evaluations are visible in the trajectory, but none of that batch's feedback was ingested and no next state was selected.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich neutral molecules range from recognizable aryl amides to dense sulfur cages with unusual bonding and unspecified geometry.
molecular.overall_character: Every listed objective has molecular observations. The first task has 410 evaluated molecules, including 390 optimizer proposals; its supplied trajectories end at evaluation 300 for seed 1 and 110 for seed 2. Each other task has 600 evaluated molecules and 580 optimizer proposals. The report describes only those observations. Every optimizer proposal set has ring_closure_rate 1.0 and branch_rate 1.0. Aromatic_atom_rate is 0.9872 for the first task, 1.0 for the next ring-rich families, and 0.719 for the final objective. These are text-based molecule-presence rates, not aromatic atom fractions or perceived ring counts. The molecules retain recognizable indole carboxamides, nitrogen-rich dicarbonyl heterocycles, aryl amines, esters and ethers, but often introduce unusual sulfur atoms into ring junctions or multiple bonds. Dense polycycles, bridged lactam-like systems, sulfur-nitrogen connections and sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds occur alongside ordinary thiols and thioethers. Mean SMILES lengths range from 45.1 to 70.2; the output is predominantly moderately sized to bulky multiring chemistry rather than tiny fragments or unbounded chains. Charged_rate is 0.0 throughout, which does not establish ordinary sulfur valence, synthetic accessibility or the absence of protonatable amines. Stereocentre_rate is also 0.0 throughout despite many substituted saturated centres and complex ring junctions. Chemical plausibility is mixed: conventional aryl amides are recognizable synthesis targets, whereas some sulfur-rich cages would require substantial evidence of feasible geometry and bonding before being called practical compounds. The useful high-score families remain concentrated even though the full trajectories contain numerous local topological variants. The supplied comparison trajectories are seed 0 of n-d88727c16484 itself; differences below are comparisons between runs, not evidence about activation of an algorithm change. Unobserved stable replacements or configurations have no established score benefit.

per_task.generated_character: The high tail consists mainly of neutral indole carboxanilides bearing ethoxy or methoxy, methyl and thiol substituents. Seed 2 also reaches related sulfur-substituted benzofuran carboxamides, often carrying chloromethyl or chlorohydroxymethyl groups. These are moderately sized aromatic structures with recognizable amide and heteroaromatic chemistry. The digest records aromatic_atom_rate 0.9872, ring_closure_rate 1.0, mean_smiles_length 45.1 and charged_rate 0.0. Later seed-1 structures often partially saturate the indole, introduce nitrogen-oxygen bonds, and replace the anilide ring with unusual oxygen/sulfur heterocycles containing very short closures. The prior seed-0 best, 0.3966634883331815, instead used a sulfur-containing unsaturated bicyclic aryl-ketone structure with fluorinated nitrogen decoration. The new leading amides are more recognizable chemically while occupying a similar reported score range. Coverage is limited to the supplied 410 molecules; the seed-2 final excerpt stops at evaluation 110.
liabilities: Aryl thiols can introduce oxidation and reactivity concerns; replacing the amide with a thioester changes both stability and donor/acceptor character.
Chloromethyl, chlorohydroxymethyl and sulfenamide-like substituents occur in the high or late families, adding reactive functionality to otherwise conventional cores.
Late examples contain unusual short heteroaromatic closures or cumulated bonds within rings. New saturated centres are not stereochemically specified.
missing_features: Broader chemically stable substitutions around the useful aromatic amide relationship are not established among the leaders; thiols, chlorinated alcohols and sulfur-nitrogen substituents become common local alternatives.
Independent high-scoring core families are sparsely represented relative to indole, azaindole and benzofuran carboxamide variants.
Controlled changes of saturation and ring connectivity that retain the useful arrangement are incomplete, particularly in later nitrogen-oxygen and short-closure heterocyclic structures.

nodes.method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
nodes.method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.

approach.method_basis: The Parent samples novel molecules directly from a task-local neural flow policy, then performs two graph refinement phases using accepted policy molecules and their descendants. A fingerprint Gaussian posterior chooses fresh graph offspring for evaluation while protecting the initial fresh-policy handoff. Every accepted encodable molecule retains its real score and exact token trajectory in a rank-sampled archive. Trajectory-balance updates jointly train the policy and a normalizer, with a categorical reference penalty toward a frozen prior. That prior is selected along unchanged unlabeled training by fixed-noise valid, connected, unique generation yield, using original holdout loss as the tie breaker. The present reference penalty averages token differences using the adapting policy probabilities.
approach.novelty: Reverse the direction of that one reference penalty so the frozen prior probabilities weight the token differences. This keeps a restoring gradient on a prior-supported alternative even when the adapting policy nearly abandons it, while keeping accepted-score trajectory balance and rank replay intact. The lineage has tested prior preparation, posterior selection and a scaffold replay mixture; this child instead changes how the fixed prior resists loss of its conditional token support. The test measures the changed gradient, actual reference divergence and later valid novel generation separately, because stronger retention may also weaken useful score adaptation.

nodes.hypothesis: Replace the accepted-prefix categorical reference penalty KL(policy || frozen prior) with KL(frozen prior || policy), preserving the existing coefficient, sequence normalization, score-ranked replay and trajectory-balance objective.

finding_summary.headline: Restoring gradients activated, but retained support worsened and mean score fell
finding_summary.insights:
A restoring component on nearly abandoned prior-supported alternatives was present, yet that component alone did not preserve conditional support under these joint score-driven updates. This rules out an unchanged KL orientation, a drifting prior, missing graph feedback or altered replay labels as explanations for the outcome. The registered retention-benefit falsifier is triggered even though mechanism execution is confirmed. The loss can improve while its reference-divergence component worsens; changing direction at the inherited coefficient therefore does not establish the intended protection.

The small gain in valid novel strings cannot be credited to demonstrated support retention. Its seed dependence, the missing parent prior-to-policy diagnostic and the different search histories leave that causal connection unresolved. Graph-bearing policy movement and later scaffold matches increased, which also argues against explaining the score loss as a simple shutdown of graph-to-policy learning. The molecular assessment still found a mixture of plausible compact molecules and oversized or chemically questionable assemblies. The experiment therefore narrows the next question to how joint training can retain useful conditional support without losing objective progress; changing the reference gradient alone did not settle it.
finding_summary.results:
The reference gradient changed in all 7,185 updates after the policy and prior differed; the 15 identical initial states correctly showed no gradient difference. That activation did not produce better measured retention. Across 230,400 replay occurrences, prior-to-policy KL rose from 0.473648 before updates to 0.475468 afterward, and total variation rose from 0.215919 to 0.216668. Both average changes were unfavorable in every task-seed session. The inherited policy-to-prior diagnostic was also higher than the parent overall, although the two runs followed different histories.

Raw valid novel emission increased slightly, from 7,991 to 8,050 of 12,000 draws, or 66.59% to 67.08%. Mean accepted policy-origin score increased from 0.204941 to 0.222083, and graph feedback continued to affect later generation. Nevertheless, the three-seed mean final score fell from 0.550198 to 0.543814, a decrease of 0.006384. Paired seed changes were +0.000428, -0.027151 and +0.007572. The main final-score losses were in zaleplon_mpo and median_2, whose task means fell by 0.024000 and 0.020793. All fifteen task replicas completed their 300 evaluations.

The loss can improve while its reference-divergence component worsens; changing direction at the inherited coefficient therefore does not establish the intended protection.

The small gain in valid novel strings cannot be credited to demonstrated support retention. Its seed dependence, the missing parent prior-to-policy diagnostic and the different search histories leave that causal connection unresolved. Graph-bearing policy movement and later scaffold matches increased, which also argues against explaining the score loss as a simple shutdown of graph-to-policy learning. The molecular assessment still found a mixture of plausible compact molecules and oversized or chemically questionable assemblies. The experiment therefore narrows the next question to how joint training can retain useful conditional support without losing objective progress; changing the reference gradient alone did not settle it.

molecular.headline: Compact phenolic amines coexist with oversized heteroaryl assemblies, tautomeric unsaturated rings and reactive bond motifs
molecular.overall_character: The supplied trajectories contain all five tasks and all three seeds, with 900 evaluated molecules and 870 optimizer proposals per task. All 4,350 optimizer-proposal SMILES parse with RDKit. Ring construction is abundant: digest ring-closure rates are 0.9828-0.9943 and aromatic-token rates 0.8368-0.9851. In task order, proposal median heavy-atom counts are 25, 35, 33, 32 and 24, and median ring counts are three, four, four, five and three. The output ranges from recognizable phenolic polycycles with tertiary aminoalkyl groups to partially unsaturated N/O heterocycles, large aminoheteroaryl ether/thioether assemblies, sulfonylated fused ring systems and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Unusual local bonds are not confined to negligible fragments: one task has 109 O-halogen proposals and 68 with O-O single bonds, while another has 77 C=C=N cumulene proposals, 72 contained in a perceived ring of at most seven atoms. Such graphs do not establish stable realizable compounds. Per-task nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts of 497-693 indicate substantial graph diversity, but the highest displayed molecules often occupy close analogue families. Parent chemistry already included elaborate heteroaryl assemblies, phenolic polycyclic amines and fused carbonyl systems; the current leaders change their local topology and substitution without resolving all chemical plausibility issues. No proposal has assigned stereocentres, despite 395, 227, 559, 350 and 315 proposals with unassigned centres in task order. The overall chemical reading is therefore mixed: plausible conventional subsets, substantial unresolved synthesis and geometry questions, and no experimental stability or activity evidence.

per_task.generated_character: The displayed leaders form a compact three-ring family: a central phenyl ether joins a partially unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing an aminoalkene to a cyano-substituted unsaturated oxygen ring. The top molecule has 24 heavy atoms and three six-membered rings, but only the phenyl ring is aromatic by RDKit perception. Nearby variants change ring size, replace oxygen with sulfur or carbon, alter imine/enamine positions, or add chlorine, fluorine or hydroxyl groups. This differs from the parent leaders, which included more aromatic indole-amide and fused heterocyclic systems. Full proposals remain aromatic-rich overall, with median two aromatic rings, so the single aromatic ring in this leading family should not be generalized to the whole output. Nitriles and aryl ethers are familiar chemistry; the aminoalkene/imine and unsaturated heterocycle combinations need qualification for tautomerism, geometry and synthetic access.
liabilities: Aminoalkene/imine and cyclic enol-ether-like units create tautomeric and potential reactivity questions; objective values do not establish stable solution species.
Thirty-seven proposals contain an O-O single bond and 17 contain an N-halogen bond, although those motifs are not required by the highest displayed structure.
Repeated scaffold elaboration can destroy the useful size and polar-group arrangement while preserving recognizable fragments of the original molecule.
missing_features: The leading neighborhood lacks broad, chemically established alternatives that retain its useful ether, nitrile and nitrogen placement while resolving the tautomeric unsaturated-ring architecture.
The highest structure has an unspecified stereocentre, and substituted or ring-contracted variants often add further unassigned centres; their three-dimensional configurations are not defined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top arrangement scores 0.478913. Replacing the oxygen within its cyano-bearing ring with carbon in a displayed terminal counterpart gives 0.337484, supporting the importance of that heteroatom environment within this local framework. Replacing the aryl ether link with a peroxide gives 0.443831, so the O-O bond is tolerated but is not supported as beneficial in that pair. Adding another nitrogen between the aminoalkene and ring gives 0.406646. Duplicating much of the motif in terminal products drops scores to approximately 0.000360 and 0.000660. Small species such as the isolated chlorine SMILES and fluorocyclobutane score zero, while large elaborate molecules also reach zero or vanishing values. These observations favor a specific intermediate-size heteroatom arrangement rather than maximal aromaticity, ring count or molecular growth.

per_task.generated_character: The highest family consists of extensive aminoheteroaryl ether assemblies bearing multiple aryl chlorine/bromine substituents, aminoalkyl or aminoalkenyl ether arms and quinazoline-like nitrogen heterocycles. The top molecule contains 55 heavy atoms, six aromatic rings and molecular mass 888.434. A different high-scoring family is a smaller heteroaryl thioether bearing a carbonyl nitrogen heterocycle, chloroethyl ether and imine/hydrazone-like substituents; one such molecule has 36 heavy atoms and mass 546.396. Displayed expansions reach ten or eleven aromatic rings. These are graph-valid combinations of recognizable fragments, but several whole structures are unusually large and carry chemically labile motifs. The parent also contained high-scoring extended aminoheteroaryl systems and frequent unusual oxygen connections. Current O-O single-bond proposals number 68 versus 135 in the parent, while O-halogen proposals number 109 versus 93; both remain material chemical liabilities.
liabilities: There are 172 proposals above 50 heavy atoms, with a maximum of 108; dense aromatic surfaces and heavy halogens make many high-scoring structures far larger than typical small-molecule chemotypes.
The population contains 109 O-halogen proposals, 68 with O-O single bonds, 11 acid halides and 13 carbon sites matching C(=N)-halogen, all chemically distinct from ordinary aryl halogenation.
The digest charged rate is 0.2287, with terminal nitro, anionic heteroaryl, azide and peroxide examples; formal graph validity does not settle their stability, synthesis or physical properties.
missing_features: The productive heteroaryl relationship lacks consistently economical, chemically stable whole-molecule realizations; near-equal scores occur across markedly different sizes and questionable terminal functionalities.
Imine and enamine geometries are unspecified, and stable replacements for peroxide, O-halogen and reactive imidoyl-halide connections are not demonstrated across the leading neighborhood.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 55-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.844593 and the 36-heavy-atom thioether example 0.844527, showing that the largest construction is not uniquely necessary for the displayed score. Expanding an assembly to 84 heavy atoms and ten aromatic rings gives 0.844152, and an eleven-aromatic-ring structure scores 0.839275. Additional size therefore brings no clear reward in these examples. A peroxide-containing analogue still reaches 0.842353, and an imidoyl-chloride-like substituent also appears near the maximum; the score does not establish chemical stability. Lower-scoring cyclic or acyclic sulfone-rich structures lie near 0.258-0.301, despite substantial heteroatom or aromatic content. Terminal nitrogen-rich heteroaryl structures around 0.57-0.59 show that generic heteroaryl proliferation is insufficient to reproduce the higher-score arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a phenolic dibenzocycloheptane-like framework carrying a dimethylaminoethyl substituent: 21 heavy atoms, three rings, two aromatic rings and molecular mass 281.399. Its tertiary amine is on an acyclic side chain rather than inside a saturated ring. A propyl-linked analogue and more bridged phenolic ring variants also lead. These relatively compact structures are recognizable medicinal chemistry. Other seeds supply aryl-substituted cyclic amines and substantially larger piperazine/enamine/thioketone combinations, the latter prominent in the terminal digest. The parent also had strong phenolic polycyclic amines and arylpiperazine-linked aromatics. The current compact leaders simplify some of that chemistry, even though the full proposal distribution has median 33 heavy atoms and four rings versus parent medians of 30 and four.
liabilities: More bridged ring topologies introduce stereochemical and conformational questions absent from the simpler leading structure.
Terminal piperazine structures can include thioketones, thiols, enamines and additional N-S connections; their scores do not establish the practical stability of that combined functionality.
Thirty-five proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, despite a leading conventional phenolic amine of only 21 heavy atoms.
missing_features: No additional mandatory functional group can be inferred from the near-ceiling phenolic-amine scores; broader economical coverage of the demonstrated aromatic/amine arrangements is the supported chemical need.
The highest tricycle is achiral, but bridged analogues and complex cyclic-amine products have unspecified centres: 559 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre and none assigns one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dimethylaminoethyl phenolic tricycle scores 0.999994 and the propyl-linked counterpart 0.999984. A ring-contracted aromatic analogue remains at 0.995878; adding extra halogen, amino or imino substitution does not establish a necessary improvement. The shared chemical association is a basic tertiary amine positioned with an aromatic phenolic framework. Low examples include amide/sulfonamide-rich aromatics and an acylhydrazone around 3.80e-05 to 9.56e-05, showing that nitrogen abundance alone is insufficient. A terminal piperazine/enamine/thioketone structure reaches 0.993165, but a much larger duplicated nitrogen-linked assembly drops to 0.029234. These observations support contextual amine placement and controlled elaboration, not experimentally established binding or a requirement for ring-bound nitrogen.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family combines a sulfonylated saturated nitrogen ring fused to a pyrrole- or pyrazole-like ring, a methylenedioxyphenyl substituent and a fused diazaaromatic arm. The top example has 36 heavy atoms, six rings, four aromatic rings and molecular mass 504.612; close relatives change sulfonyl alkyl length, ring nitrogen placement or the aromatic connecting arm. Sulfonylation means the saturated ring nitrogen should not be read as an ordinary basic piperidine nitrogen. Another leading family comprises densely fused N-methyl cyclic carbonyl systems, sometimes bearing an azetidine ether. The parent also produced fused cyclic carbonyl and sulfonamide-containing aromatic chemotypes. Current full proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and five rings, with 693 nonchiral Murcko scaffolds; these are abundant but often structurally elaborate ring systems.
liabilities: Many six-ring leaders approach or exceed molecular mass 500, and 55 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms, creating substantial size and synthetic-complexity burdens.
Dense fused carbonyl and aromatic systems can impose conformational or synthetic constraints that ring counts and accepted SMILES do not characterize.
Sulfonylated nitrogens, aromatic nitrogens and pyrrolic NH groups have different electronic roles; simply adding nitrogen cannot be interpreted as increasing useful basic centres.
missing_features: The leading chemical region lacks broad simpler alternatives that retain its combination of aromatic, sulfonyl and nitrogen-containing ring relationships.
Regioisomeric and stereochemical coverage is incomplete: the highest sulfonylated fused-ring molecule has an unspecified stereocentre, and 350 proposals have at least one unassigned centre.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The propylsulfonyl fused-ring example scores 0.230034 and its ethylsulfonyl counterpart 0.227223. Pyrazole-related sulfonamide variants lie near 0.220-0.226. Those nearby scores support a shared multi-ring/polar arrangement more strongly than a specific extra alkyl carbon. Adding another sulfonyl connection produces a larger 40-heavy-atom example at 0.224826, so extra sulfur/oxygen and size are not sufficient. Low molecules include methane at zero, small sulfur or oxygen compounds near 0.009 and a long-chain hydroxylated ring at 0.034939. Terminal fused carbonyl structures reach about 0.172-0.204 but do not establish that adding fusion alone supplies the missing arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The highest molecule is a compact tertiary amine joining a gem-difluorinated annulated triazole/ether system to a bridged azaaromatic ring system. It has 25 heavy atoms, five rings and one unspecified stereocentre. Other leaders contain pyridyl-substituted imino nitrogen heterocycles with methoxyamino or methoxymethylamino groups. A chemically distinct leader has an acylguanidine-like side chain and thiol attached through oxygen to a fluorinated seven-membered ring containing a C=C=N cumulene. That molecule has 23 heavy atoms and no aromatic rings by RDKit, despite aromatic-rich alternatives elsewhere in the same task. The parent leaders likewise mixed fused nitrogen heterocycles and unusual fluorinated unsaturated sulfur/nitrogen chemistry. Current proposals have median 24 heavy atoms and three rings; this is primarily a local bonding and configuration problem rather than pervasive molecular overgrowth.
liabilities: Seventy-seven proposals contain C=C=N, and 72 place that motif within a perceived ring of at most seven atoms. This is a ketenimine-like heterocumulene, not an all-carbon allene; its reactivity and ring geometry require chemical qualification.
Methoxyamino N-O bonds, thioaldehyde-like or thiol substituents, and unusual fused ring connectivity introduce different stability or synthetic-access questions in different leading families.
The highest bridged amine has unspecified configuration, and the trajectories provide no measurements of stability, physical properties or synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: The higher-score regions lack demonstrated stable ring and substituent alternatives preserving their useful compact polar arrangement, especially around the cyclic cumulene and densely bridged nitrogen systems.
Imine/enamine and heterocumulene geometry is not specified, while 315 proposals contain an unassigned stereocentre; graph connectivity alone leaves important molecular configurations unresolved.
No unique mandatory basic group, aromatic ring count or fluorinated target-like motif is justified because several chemically distinct leading families are visible.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged tertiary-amine structure scores 0.434778 and a pyridyl imino heterocycle with a methoxyamino group 0.412986. Replacing that N-O-containing substituent with the displayed N-methoxymethyl variant gives 0.407779, showing that a direct N-O bond is not uniquely required for a nearby score. The cyclic C=C=N structure scores 0.401017; related terminal structures range from 0.021065 to 0.319810 as ring nitrogen, linkage and side-chain placement change. The score therefore recognizes some compact polar arrangements while tolerating unusual local chemistry; it does not establish the realizability of a cyclic cumulene. Oversized glycosylated, peptide-like or highly elaborated aromatic examples are zero or extremely small. The full trajectory median is 0.0024005953 and exactly two rows are zero, so the distribution is weak overall without being a population of literal zeros.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal set contains 109 O-halogen motifs, 68 O-O single bonds, 11 acid halides and 13 C(=N)-halogen motifs, with a peroxide and imidoyl-halide-like functionality present near its highest scores. Another set contains 77 C=C=N cumulenes, 72 within perceived rings of at most seven atoms, including a displayed molecule scoring 0.401017. Elsewhere, the aryl ether leader scores 0.478913 while its peroxide analogue scores 0.443831, so a labile bond is not necessarily rewarded even when tolerated.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain chemically stable local bonds and geometrically credible unsaturation in useful neighborhoods.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The missing capability is dependable access to ordinary, stable alternatives preserving an observed useful arrangement of rings and polar groups. Distinguish aryl halogens from oxygen or reactive imidoyl halides, ethers from peroxides, and conventional imines from constrained heterocumulenes, without relying on any objective identity.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The five proposal sets contain one, 172, 35, 55 and five molecules above 50 heavy atoms. In one leading family, 55- and 36-heavy-atom structures both score approximately 0.8445, while expansion to 84 heavy atoms and ten aromatic rings yields 0.844152. A conventional phenolic amine reaches near-ceiling score with 21 heavy atoms, whereas a duplicated nitrogen-linked assembly in that session scores 0.029234. Duplicating another compact heterocyclic motif produces scores near 0.000360 and 0.000660.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator lacks consistent economical control of size and repetition around productive chemical cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve chemical alternatives with controlled ring fusion, linker length, appendage count and molecular mass. The output needs contextual growth around a useful arrangement, since compact and extended structures can both be productive but repeated elaboration often contributes size without an evident chemical benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: No assigned stereocentres occur among 4,350 optimizer proposals. The five sessions contain 395, 227, 559, 350 and 315 proposals with at least one unassigned centre. Leaders include partially unsaturated heterocycles, bridged phenolic systems, sulfonylated fused rings and a bridged tertiary amine. Numerous imine, enamine and heterocumulene motifs introduce further geometry questions. The simplest leading phenolic tricycle is achiral, so the issue is conditional rather than universal.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator proposes stereogenic and configurationally flexible chemistry without defining the relevant configurations.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent explicit stereoisomers and bond geometries when those degrees of freedom exist, while preserving access to achiral structures. The available feedback does not specify which unobserved configuration should be preferred, and graph validity alone does not define a three-dimensional proposal.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Per-session nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts range from 497 to 693. Nevertheless, digest leaders repeatedly vary an aminoalkene/cyano-heterocycle arrangement, large aminoheteroaryl assemblies, phenolic tertiary amines, six-ring sulfonylated systems or compact fluorinated nitrogen heterocycles. Close local changes can matter: replacing a cyano-bearing ring oxygen with carbon accompanies a decrease from 0.478913 to 0.337484. Amide or sulfonamide nitrogen environments also differ sharply from the useful tertiary-amine environment visible in another session.
transferable_gaps.gap: Many graph scaffolds coexist with narrow productive families and incomplete transfer of useful functional-group arrangements to alternative cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically distinct core and linker alternatives that preserve relevant polar-group position and electronic context, beyond repeated peripheral substitution or ring closure. Nitrogen count, aromaticity and scaffold identity are insufficient descriptions of useful chemistry; the generator needs coverage of how those features are connected.

nodes.method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
nodes.method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.

approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from the original unlabeled corpus strings and retains the checkpoint with the lowest heldout token loss. Each objective clones that prior into an adaptable flow policy and keeps the reference prior frozen. The online loop alternates a neural batch with two graph batches; accepted neural molecules refresh the breeding population and provide a protected parent at the first graph handoff. Accepted-score fingerprint posterior samples choose the other offspring from temporary pools, and accepted graph trajectories feed trajectory-balance learning of the neural policy. The same reciprocal loop is retained here. The preparation choice being questioned is its use of string likelihood alone to decide which learned prior all those components receive.
approach.novelty: Choose the prepared checkpoint by its observed yield of valid, connected, distinct molecules under a fixed ancestral sampling probe, with heldout token loss breaking ties. A separate diagnostic probe then compares that choice with the ordinary loss-minimizing checkpoint from the same training trajectory. This sibling changes checkpoint selection, whereas the previous preparation sibling changed the strings used for training. It neither combines the two interventions nor changes neural learning, graph construction or posterior allocation during an objective.

nodes.hypothesis: Select the reusable prior checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid-connected-unique molecular emission yield among unlabeled checkpoints that improve the initial holdout loss, breaking ties by lower original-string holdout NLL while preserving the Parent training and stopping rules.

finding_summary.headline: Checkpoint selection raises endpoint scores, while molecular-yield gains transfer unevenly
finding_summary.insights:
The minimum token-loss checkpoint is not the only useful prior along the same unchanged learning trajectory. This experiment cleanly separates checkpoint choice from changes to training representations, gradients or the online search algorithm. It also exposes the limitation of the selection criterion: choosing among 60 checkpoints with one fixed 256-draw sample creates a selection-sample advantage that mostly disappears on fresh diagnostic randomness in two seeds. That pattern is compatible with selection noise and supports only limited generalization of the measured yield gain. The lower online raw validity shows that valid prior sampling and useful adaptation should remain separate measurements; even the first online batch follows accepted-score policy updates.

The molecular assessment gives the same distinction a chemical interpretation. Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.
finding_summary.results:
The rule selected different prior weights in all three preparations. On the fixed selection samples, the chosen checkpoints produced 243, 245 and 238 valid, distinct molecules out of 256, compared with 232, 236 and 229 for the lowest-loss checkpoints from the same training trajectories. The independent diagnostic changed those counts by -1, +10 and 0; its pooled gain was only 9 of 768 draws, compared with 29 of 768 on the selection samples. Thus checkpoint choice and its selection-sample advantage are established, while an independent yield advantage appeared in only one seed. All training runs completed the same 29,742 updates, and the ordinary lowest-loss weights exactly matched the published parent weights, so no training-length difference explains the choice. The selected checkpoints incurred small token-loss increases of 0.001852, 0.002624 and 0.003124.

During optimization, valid terminated neural draws fell from 8,441 of 12,000 to 8,156 of 12,000, or 70.34% to 67.97%. Nevertheless, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.520669 to 0.550198, with paired gains of 0.026285, 0.051553 and 0.010747. The mean gain, 0.029528, exceeds the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin task means improved; zaleplon was nearly unchanged and DRD2 declined slightly. Every task completed the supplied evaluation panel. The new checkpoints therefore changed useful downstream search outcomes, but the score increase cannot be explained as a consistent increase in valid molecular emission.

Useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements coexist with unusual sulfur bonding, nitroso groups, peroxide bonds and unresolved stereochemistry. Valid connected uniqueness does not distinguish those liabilities, and higher endpoint scores do not establish better synthetic plausibility. The campaign now has evidence that an earlier checkpoint can improve the reciprocal search without a reliably better valid-emission rate. Whether a more representative unlabeled diagnostic can predict that downstream usefulness remains open.

molecular.headline: Rich aryl, amine and carbonyl rings coexist with triple-bonded sulfur, nitroso groups, peroxides and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: All 4,500 child trajectory rows and 4,500 corresponding Parent rows were read, including 4,350 optimizer proposals in each node. Each task supplies 900 evaluated molecules, of which 870 are optimizer proposals. The child has abundant fused heteroaromatics, saturated amine rings, aryl amides, sulfonamides and carbonyl heterocycles. Its ring-closure marker rates are 0.9816–0.9943; aromatic-marker rates are 0.7736–0.9747, with the lower value reflecting substantial unsaturated nonaromatic ring chemistry in one output set. These digest counters measure string-level presence, not atom fractions or perceived ring quality. Read-only RDKit inspection parses all 4,350 emitted child SMILES and gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 in the supplied task order. Recognizable medicinal-chemistry architectures coexist with unusually bonded sulfur, N-nitroso substituents, peroxide bonds, highly contracted unsaturated rings and oversized assemblies. All task digests have stereocentre_rate 0.0; RDKit identifies at least one unassigned tetrahedral centre in 392, 225, 563, 348 and 353 optimizer rows respectively, with assigned centres in none. The repertoire varies across seeds, while the upper tails repeatedly revisit a few related families. Chemistry quality is therefore mixed: ring and aromatic content are rich, but neither parseability nor high observed scores establish synthetic accessibility, stability or well-defined geometry. This assessment describes the output without attributing it to an algorithmic mechanism.

per_task.generated_character: The digest leaders are medium-sized heteroaryl structures. Seed 0 links a quinoline-like ring system to a fused five/five-membered aza-ring framework; its leading variants carry N–O or N–O–N attachments and an oxygen-linked carbon triply bonded to hydrogen-bearing sulfur. The leading molecule has 25 heavy atoms and four perceived rings, three aromatic. Seed 2 also provides a more conventional methoxy/cyano-substituted partially saturated quinoline-like carboxamide and a different hydroxy-nitrile/amidine series with unsaturated carbocyclic or oxygen-containing rings. Across the full optimizer output the median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, as in the Parent. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts are 577 for the child and 529 for the Parent; this counts local ring edits as distinct and is not a count of useful synthetic series. The Parent leaders included biaryl pyrazole/acetanilide, indole-amide and quinoline/urea families. Rings, nitrogen and carbonyl groups are thus not missing, but the new leading families include more problematic connectivity.
liabilities: Fifty-one of 870 child proposals contain a carbon–sulfur triple bond, versus none in the corresponding Parent task. The leading C≡S–H environment and N–O–N or O–S attachments are not ordinary medicinal functional groups, and parsing supplies no stability or synthetic evidence.

The hydroxy-nitrile and unsaturated ring families include potentially sensitive local connectivity and unassigned stereocentres. Relative stability and geometry of those proposed forms are not established by the trajectory.
Ten optimizer proposals have at most three heavy atoms. Such fragments, as well as the cited large polyfunctional assembly, lose the connected arrangement seen in the favorable examples.
missing_features: Chemically ordinary alternatives that preserve the favorable local aryl/nitrogen/substituent arrangement are not consistently established within the sulfur-rich leading family. A separate conventional nitrile/amide family is present, so the limitation is not an inability to make amides or nitriles.
Defined configurations are absent for substituted fused-ring and hydroxy-nitrile centres. The data do not establish which stereoisomer, if any, would be preferred.
Controlled core replacements preserving useful local functionality remain incomplete: some changes retain the core but sharply lose the score, while fragmentation removes it entirely.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The oxygen-linked C≡S–H structure with an N–O–N substituent scores 0.49151859442707624; the corresponding O–S substituent gives 0.46889981462810426, while the N–O version retaining C≡S–H gives 0.4509940583060807. A methoxy/N-hydroxy relative scores 0.4524187090179798. These observations show that questionable bonding is accepted among the favorable local variants, not that the sulfur motif is chemically necessary. The cyano/carboxamide alternative scores 0.46457806514522626; replacing its nitrile by methyl gives 0.31305283559478153, N-methylating its amide gives 0.4098058836024565, and replacing a methyl substituent by amino gives 0.3487840659540038. Those close-family comparisons associate the score with specific nitrile, amide and substitution relationships. The hydroxy-nitrile/amidine family reaches 0.4572645941803378. Sulfur, hydrazine, methane, a saturated sulfur-rich bicyclic structure and a large polyol/amide assembly all appear at 0.0. The pooled median is 0.177987. No uniquely required absent heterocycle follows from these whole-molecule observations.

per_task.generated_character: The upper tail is dominated by a seed-1 diaryl-ether assembly with two quinazoline-like fused aza-aromatic systems, an N-acetylpiperazinone and a carbamoyl side chain often containing sulfur and an N-nitroso group. The leader has 45 heavy atoms and five six-membered rings, four aromatic. Related high examples substitute other heteroaromatic/sulfonamide connections around the same piperazinone-bearing aza-aromatic motif. These contain recognizable building blocks but combine substantial size with sensitive terminal chemistry. Other seeds explore sulfonamides with peroxide-containing side chains and aminoalkyl heteroaromatics with anionic N–O groups. The child median is 36 heavy atoms and four rings, matching the Parent medians, but 185 of 870 proposals exceed 50 heavy atoms versus 128 Parent proposals. The digest mean SMILES length is 70.4 and charged-marker rate is 0.2356. Parent leaders used other amino/imine/acylhydrazone-linked heteroaromatics; the new high family is a different, larger arrangement rather than evidence of generally absent heteroaromatic chemistry.
liabilities: The full child set contains N–N=O connectivity in 18 of 870 optimizer proposals, versus none in the corresponding Parent task; leading examples directly exhibit that group and sometimes an additional S–N linkage.

Read-only bond counts find O–O single bonds in 135 of 870 child proposals versus five Parent proposals, and O–halogen bonds in 93 versus seven. These are structural flags requiring chemical context, not measured reaction rates or an assertion that every flagged molecule is impossible.
Large, heteroatom-rich linked assemblies and anionic N–O variants complicate synthesis and physical-property interpretation. The supplied score does not establish those properties.
missing_features: Consistently credible terminal-group alternatives preserving the useful aza-aromatic/cyclic-carbonyl arrangement remain incomplete. A favorable score is shared by nitroso, thione, N-halogenated and more conventional variants, so none of those liabilities can be inferred to be a required feature.

Independent core/linker alternatives and controlled size reduction around the useful arrangement are not established as a systematic series. Much of the high tail changes peripheral decoration on related large assemblies.
Defined geometry and stereochemistry of the more complex saturated or fused variants are absent; the current observations do not identify an objective-preferred configuration.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading N-nitroso/sulfur side-chain structure, its ring-carbonyl-to-thione relative and its chloroethyl variant each score 0.8301591128254581. A related carbon-linked side chain scores 0.8299758259468171, and a non-nitroso sulfonamide/heteroaromatic arrangement scores 0.8262461253429294. The narrow upper spread across these alternatives does not establish that nitroso, sulfur or a thione is required. Another high relative bearing N–Cl and N–F bonds scores 0.8294524481883885. By contrast, the sulfone-linked hydroxamate/styryl low example scores 0.2712455185234365, and an imide/amine/sulfone assembly scores 0.2829523943069481. A late aminoalkyl heteroaromatic N–O anion scores 0.6153794851273843. The pooled median is 0.56996. The observed preference is associated with a particular connected aza-aromatic and cyclic-carbonyl arrangement, while the scores tolerate several chemically concerning peripheral replacements.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-2 molecules are arylpiperazines joined by long carbon chains to an N-aryl five-membered nitrogen heterocycle or another aromatic group. Bromine, chlorine, fluorine, phenol and thiol substitutions recur. The leading structure has 32 heavy atoms and four rings, three aromatic, with a six-carbon linker to the piperazine; a simpler high example is a fluorophenylpiperazine with a five-carbon linker to phenyl. Other seeds explore compact but heavily bridged or fused aryl amines, including oxygen-containing polycycles. The Parent also produced arylpiperidines, aminoalkyl chains and fused saturated amines, so the broad accessible-amine/aromatic pattern is retained while the leading scaffold and linker choices change. The child median is 30 heavy atoms and four rings, compared with 28 and four for the Parent. The charged-marker rate is only 0.0103, but neutral SMILES containing secondary or tertiary amines still represent potentially basic centres.
liabilities: Long flexible linkers, repeated aromatic regions and substantial halogenation leave physical-property balance unestablished even when the accepted score is high.
Thiol-bearing or newly fused variants introduce additional chemical or geometric questions; favorable scores alone do not show oxidation stability or synthetic accessibility.

RDKit detects unassigned tetrahedral centres in 563 of 870 proposals and assigned centres in none. This includes the broader branched and bridged amine output, even though several quoted linear-linker leaders themselves have no tetrahedral stereocentre.
missing_features: No additional required functional group is identifiable from the near-limit upper tail; aromatic surfaces and accessible saturated amines are already well represented.

Controlled linker geometry and stereochemically defined alternatives to the bridged/polycyclic amine families are not demonstrated. The data establish missing specification, not a benefit for a chosen configuration.
Core and linker changes that preserve the favorable arrangement without duplicating whole large fragments are incompletely controlled.

A simpler fluorophenylpiperazine/pentylphenyl structure scores 0.9999993790262016, so extensive halogenation and the extra heteroaromatic ring are not established requirements. Parent aromatic/basic-amine examples already reached 0.9999986918258995; tiny differences near the upper limit do not identify a distinct missing chemical feature. A late duplication into a molecule with two substantial heteroaryl/amine arms scores only 0.046770493414912545. The N-acyl/sulfonyl aromatic molecule scores 3.8021829379963674e-05, the nitro acylhydrazone 4.1105044111594925e-05, and the sulfonamide/hydroxamate 5.916130606141068e-05. per_task.generated_character: The strongest example is a methylenedioxy-fused benzodiazepinone-like core attached to an aryl sulfonyl N-methylpiperazine. It has 32 heavy atoms and five rings, including a seven-membered imine/lactam ring. Related seed-1 examples instead contain bromomethyl or bromoethyl heteroaromatic lactams, biphenyl groups and the same sulfonylpiperazine motif. Seed 2 produces indole-containing oxygen rings linked through an ether to fused nitrogen/carbonyl systems; several of these have an unassigned acetal-like centre. These are recognizable amine, lactam, sulfonamide and indole ingredients, but their elaborate assembly and late heteroatom substitutions vary in plausibility. The child median is 32 heavy atoms and four rings, versus 36 and five for the Parent, whose high tail likewise combined carbonyl polycycles with sulfonylated or alkylated saturated nitrogen rings. The leading new diazepinone is more compact than several nearby brominated biphenyl relatives, illustrating useful chemical variety within that broad pattern.
liabilities: Some favorable alternatives contain alkyl bromides, while a high indole-linked relative contains a peroxide bond. These have different possible reactivity concerns and should not be treated as interchangeable decoration.

O–O single bonds occur in 50 of 870 child proposals versus 14 Parent proposals. The leading compact diazepinone does not share this liability, so the judgment is about uneven output quality rather than all members of the set.
Fused, bridged and rearranged carbonyl systems make ring geometry and synthesis uncertain, with unassigned tetrahedral centres in 348 child proposals and no assigned centres.
